## Chapter 1: Framework - AU


Framework - AU module of Temenos Transact


### 1.1  Misc


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *Accounting Unit (AU) module provides the ability to produce multiple sets of balanced financial reports for a single business entity. Although, the AU module is designed to handle multiple reporting requirements, the Singapore Asian Currency Unit (ACU) or Domestic Banking Unit (DBU) regulations are ...*
> 
> **Key Fields:** *@ID*, *Company Name*, *Company Select*, *Consolidation Mark*, *DECOMMISSION.DATE*, *Default Company*, *Financial Com*, *Financial Mne* ... +3 more
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction


#### 📖 Introduction

Related topics:

- Temenos Transact Services

Accounting Unit (AU) module provides the ability to produce multiple sets of balanced financial reports for a single business entity. Although, the AU module is designed to handle multiple reporting requirements, the Singapore Asian Currency Unit (ACU) or Domestic Banking Unit (DBU) regulations are used in this guide. For example, the Monetary Authority (MAS) in Singapore requires banks to keep separate accounting books for business operations of ACU and DBU. Accounting book is used to describe a balanced set of financial reports. MAS requires all the operations and events to be traceable either in ACU or DBU.

> **⚠️ Note:** In this User Guide, examples and setup are based on the regulations in Singapore.

All ACU and DBU activities are reported separately on a weekly and monthly basis to differentiate the activities. In Singapore, the Singapore Dollar (SGD) and Brunei Dollar (BDN) are mandatory DBU currencies and all other currencies are described as ACU. According to the basic reporting rule, any transaction involving a DBU currency must be reported in the DBU accounting books and under any circumstances, it cannot be reported in the ACU accounting books. It is permissible to allocate a non DBU currency to either ACU or DBU accounting book. Therefore, a single business entity produces two sets of balanced books when they perform transactions in the ACU and DBU currencies. The following diagram shows the Singapore operational company and the ACU and DBU accounting companies. For example, at the operational company level, interest and charges are setup. The actual accounting entries are raised in the ACU or DBU Company.


##### Product Configuration

An accounting company is setup when a Temenos Transact Company (business entity) needs to produce more than one set of financial reports with each set allocated to an accounting company. Transaction input takes place in the parent Temenos Transact Company. Accounting companies are linked to a normal Temenos Transact parent company. For example, the Singapore Company is the business entity with the following two accounting companies linked to it:

- Onshore accounting company (DBU)
- Offshore accounting company (ACU)

A set of parameter tables is used to define the rules that determines which accounting company is allocated. These rules can be setup for each relevant Temenos Transact application.

Parent Company Functionality (Business Entity):

- Configuration and parameterisation of the system is at the parent company level.
- User logs are captured in the parent company.
- Transactions are entered in the parent company.

Accounting Company:

- Accounting entries are allocated to an individual accounting company.
- Accounts and transactions are allocated to the relevant accounting company.
- Currency position records are raised for the relevant accounting companies.
- Directly signing into an accounting company is not allowed.

All accounts and contracts are entered into and owned by the parent company. The system records the accounting company for each asset and liability and profit and loss item, on the related record of the contract in EB.CONTRACT.BALANCES . According to the allocation rules, the accounting company is set to default for creating a new account. It can also be manually entered for accounts in non-mandatory currencies. For example, it is permissible to have an account in a non-DBU currency allocated to either the onshore or offshore accounting company.

The following diagram provides a simple example of a transaction being processed in the Singapore Company, with the transaction automatically allocated to the onshore (DBU) accounting company. This happens when the allocation rules are setup such that all transactions involving a mandatory onshore currency are booked into the onshore accounting company.

One of the fundamental rules of ACU or DBU is not to have DBU (onshore) currency positions in the ACU (offshore) books. Onshore currency amounts are exchanged into an offshore currency amount before using it for offshore business. The currency exchange must be initiated in the onshore accounting company, so it can be reported in the onshore books. Currency positions and P&L are raised in the accounting company allocated to the transaction.

The diagram below shows how Temenos Transact intercompany accounting works in relation to ACU or DBU using a transaction, which is debiting a USD ACU account and crediting a SGD DBU account. As an onshore (DBU) account is used, the transaction is allocated to the onshore (DBU) accounting company.

The configurations required for the Accounting Unit module is explained below.

| Field | Example value | Comments |
|---|---|---|
| @ID | SG0020100 | New business unit (lead company) code |
| Company Name | Singapore branch |  |
| Name Address | Singapore |  |
| Mnemonic | SGP | Mnemonic for this business unit (lead company) |
| Financial Com | SG0020100 | Financial code for this business |
| Financial Mne | SGP | Mnemonic for the business unit |
| Sub Division Code | 0100 | Subdivision code for the new company |
| Default Company | SG0020100 | Company code of the business unit to which the accounting unit belongs |
| Consolidation Mark | N |  |

| Column 1 | Column 2 | Column 3 |
|---|---|---|
| Rule 1 | Sector NE 900/903/904/998/999. | Book into DBU |
| Rule 2 | Sector NE 900/903/904/998/999. | Book into ACU |

## Chapter 2: Framework - BY

### 2.1  Misc

>

This can also be referred by various business modules to automate the settl...*
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Update Acct Block Closure*, *Validate Beneficiary Links*

> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction


#### 📖 Introduction

Related topics:

- APIs

The payee’s payment details are required to initiate payments. The BENEFICIARY application is used to capture payees' payment details, which could then be re-used when the customer or user makes payments to these recipients. This can also be referred by various business modules to automate the settlement process. For example, the record in BENEFICIARY can be linked to a loan or deposit pay out condition to automate the loan disbursement or to make the deposit payment at the deposit maturity.

A payee can be owned by a customer or by the bank itself. The latter being the case when the bank sets up payees for frequent suppliers like utility companies. These are exposed to all customers who can refer them while initiating payments. The payee (beneficiary) created for payment purposes can be used either on a standalone payment platform or on an embedded Temenos Transact system.

A beneficiary can be defined for a customer who is maintained on the same Temenos Transact or standalone TPH instance as the Payments Beneficiary module, in the Party MS, on a different Temenos Transact instance or on an external, third-party Deposit Demand Account (DDA) platform. If the customer is defined on a different platform, the system validates whether the beneficiary’s owning customer exists through the Master Data Access Layer (MDAL).

> **⚠️ Note:** MDAL is a framework used to access required data for a Temenos Transact application from an external system (like microservices) using REST API. Read the Master Data Access Layer section, for more information about the MDAL functionality.


##### Product Configuration

This section defines the pre-requisites and the associated applications to be configured for creating and defining beneficiaries.

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| Validate Beneficiary Links | Indicates whether the BENEFICIARY.LINKS application must be checked while amending the account in BENEFICIARY or while reversing the record in BENEFICIARY . This file is updated by AA contracts, Standing Order and Payment Order when they are using a BENEFICIARY record. When this field is set to Yes (for the first time), the system starts the ST.BENEFICIARY.LINKS.UPDATE service to update the Beneficiary Links File upon authorisation of the application. |
| Update Acct Block Closure | Indicates whether the AC.BLOCK.CLOSURE application should be updated when the account is referred in a BENEFICIARY . During the closure of the account, the system raises an override to indicate the account is referred in one or multiple records in BENEFICIARY . When this field is set to Yes (for the first time), the system starts the ST.UPDATE.AC.BLOCK.CLOSURE service to update the Account Closure upon authorisation of the application. |

If the owning customer of the BENEFICIARY record resides in another instance of Temenos Transact or in an external system, other than the BENEFICIARY application, the system needs to be configured to support the MDAL functionality. Enabling the MDAL functionality allows the system to validate through a specific MDAL Rest API that the customer defined as owning customer exists in the BENEFICIARY application.

Read the Configuring the MDAL Framework section for more information on MDAL configuration.

### 3.1  Misc


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**

> **Purpose:** *Financial institutions apply various types of charges and commissions for the services offered to their customers like payment fees and early redemption charge on deposits. Moreover, some products and services offered by the bank are also subject to various taxes.*
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction


#### 📖 Introduction

Financial institutions apply various types of charges and commissions for the services offered to their customers like payment fees and early redemption charge on deposits. Moreover, some products and services offered by the bank are also subject to various taxes.

The charges and commissions applicable to various business activities can be defined in the Charges and Fees (CG) module and can be referred by the Temenos modules when charges or commissions are linked to transactions. The CG module manages the tax definitions and rules to group customers for tax purposes along with the details of the customer group arrived at based on various grouping conditions (for example, payments, forex and letter of credits) defined in the system.

The CG module also handles the charge group assigned to each customer and provides the basic services to calculate charges and tax on charge, which are used by various Temenos modules during transaction processing.


##### Configuring Charges and Fees

Charges and Fees has no specific configuration to be set up at the parameter level.

#### 📖 Introduction

Related topics:

- T24 Services

Data Framework (DF) is a data life cycle framework that provides the Temenos Transact customers to realise the huge potential value of the transactional data generated by Temenos Transact . This is achieved by using a read-only Dimensional (DIMal) database optimised for near real-time predictive analytics and modelling tools.

DF provides the infrastructure to create and maintain a read-only database in near real time using Extract Transform and Load (ETL) process, to ensure a database which is optimised for reporting. It also provides the ability to design and execute queries against the read-only database. It leverages Temenos Transact Interaction and Integration frameworks, so that the data is available in near real-time. Read Data Framework topic for more information on the Data Framework reporting components and product configuration.

The Operational Reporting database (DB) is deployed as a series of reporting models targeting different business domain such as:

- Customer and Account Balance Reporting model (product - DA).
- Financial Reporting model (product - DZ).


##### Customer and Account Balance Reporting Model

The Customer and Account Balance Reporting model (DA) is a business domain which is available from the R15 release. It is packaged under the Temenos DA module and is licensed together with the Data Framework Reporting Model (DF) module. This model is designed specifically to:

- Query customer and account information.
- Query all the necessary information to produce the customer account balance enquries.

This query includes the history of account balances and account movements for customer accounts. The model also includes the necessary infrastructure to update read-only DB in near real-time and the ability to define and execute enquiries in the read-only DB.


##### Understanding the Components of DA Module

The following are the components of DA module:

- The DIMal Data model.
- A set of Integration Framework events.
- A set of transformation rules (execute transformation and load).
- Queries and reports.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

The topic covers the configuration of DA model components.


##### DIMal Data Model

The database (DB) model is structured using the Star schema with FACT and DIMal tables, where:

- FACT tables relate to the account movements and balance changes, the underlying data for the FACT tables come from the Temenos Transact Transactional DB like: FACT_ACCOUNTMOVEMNT (for account movements from STMT.ENTRY ) FACT_BALANCE (for account balance from ACCT.ACTIVITY )
- DIMal tables hold relatively the non-volatile sets of attributes that enables the query constraining and filtering. For example: DIM_ACCOUNT (for the account details - ACCOUNT ) DIM_PARTY (the customer details - CUSTOMER )

| Table Name | Table Description | Domain/Support Table | FACT/DIM | Corresponding Temenos Transact Table |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| FACT_ACCOUNTMOVEMENT | This table contains the movements that have affected an account, as a result of a completed transaction event. Every record occurrence in this table represents one movement that has affected the account balance | Domain | FACT | STMT.ENTRY / STMT.ENTRY.DETAIL |
| FACT_BALANCE | This table contains the after image of the balances of an account as a result of movement to that account, generated by an underlying transaction There are two types of balances recorded: Booking - Based on when the balance is reflected in the general ledger. Value - When the balance is used for interest calculation. Every record occurrence in this table represents the after image of the balance for an account with the corresponding balance type, balance date and timestamp at which the balance is updated | Domain | FACT | ACCT.ACTVITY / ACCT.BALANCE.ACTIVITY |
| DIM_ACCOUNT | This table contains the details for each ACCOUNT record. This could be a customer account, nostro/vostro, or an internal account. Each occurrence in this table represents the after image of any change in an account (creation, change or closure) | Domain | DIM | ACCOUNT |
| DIM_TRANSACTIONTYPE | This table contains the details of the transaction code as held in each occurrence of the FACT_ACCOUNTMOVEMENT table | Domain | DIM | TRANSACTION |
| STATEMENT | This table contains the basic details of an account in a statement | Domain | DIM | ACCOUNT.STATEMENT |
| PARTY_RELATIONS_MASTER | This table contains the basic details of the customer relationship between Temenos Transact customers or Temenos Transact customer to person or an entity. Each occurrence defines a type of relationship | Domain | DIM | CUSTOMER.RELATIONSHIP |
| PARTY_RELATIONS_DETAIL | This table holds the details of each relationship type. These are the actual relation of the corresponding party and role | Domain | DIM | CUSTOMER / ACCOUNT / SEC.ACC.MASTER |
| DIM_PARTY | This table contains the customer details. Each occurrence of a record in this table is the after image of a change to a customer | Support | DIM | CUSTOMER |
| DIM_COMPANY | This table contains the details of each financial entity. Each occurrence holds the after image as a result of a change to the company detail | Support | DIM | COMPANY |
| DIM_OFFICER | This table contains the details of the authorised bank officers | Support | DIM | DEPT.ACCT.OFFICER |
| DIM_CURRENCY | This table contains the basic details of the currency definition | Support | DIM | CURRENCY |
| CURRENCY_DESCRIPTION | This table contains the basic details of the currency description | Support | Snowflake | N/A |
| DIM_CHANNEL | This table contains the basic details of the channels defined in the system | Support | DIM | EB.CHANNEL |
| CHANNEL_DESCRIPTION | This table is an extension of the CHANNEL table, as the description is multi-valued and language related | Support | Snowflake | EB.CHANNEL / LANGUAGE |
| BANKING_DATE | This table contains the system date of the financial entities within the database. Each occurrence is the after image, as a result of a change in the date for each financial entity | Support | DIM | DATES |
| LANGUAGE | This table contains the reference to the language codes available in the system and the corresponding description | Support | Reference | LANGUAGE |
| TARGET | This table contains the list of target codes defined and assigned to CUSTOMER records, to indicate how the customer fits in with the bank's overall marketing strategy | Support | DIM | TARGET |
| TARGET_DESCRIPTION | This table is an extension of the TARGET table, as the description is multi-value and language related. Each occurrence of the record is the language related description | Support | Snowflake | TARGET / LANGUAGE |
| CUSTOMER_STATUS | This table holds a list of customer status that may be assigned to CUSTOMER records, which allows the bank to classify their customers on any kind of criteria defined locally | Support | Reference | CUSTOMER.STATUS |
| CUSTOMER_STATUS_DESCRIPTION | This table is an extension of the CUSTOMER_STATUS, as the description is multi-value and language related | Support | Snowflake | CUSTOMER.STATUS / LANGUAGE |
| INDUSTRY | This table holds the list industry codes that may be assigned to each CUSTOMER record which identifies the industry in which the customer is trading | Support | DIM | INDUSTRY / LANGUAGE |
| INDUSTRY_NAME | This table is an extension of the INDUSTRY table which holds the description for each language defined | Support | Snowflake | INDUSTRY / LANGUAGE |
| SECTOR | This table holds the list of codes that may be assigned to each CUSTOMER record which identifies the economy segment in which the customer is trading | Support | DIM | SECTOR |
| SECTOR_DESCRIPTION | This table is an extension of the SECTOR table which holds the description for each language defined | Support | Snowflake | SECTOR / LANGUAGE |
| USER | This table holds the list of users that are allowed to access Temenos software | Support | Reference | USER |


##### Integration Framework Events

The Integration Framework (IF) events are published at run-time for the business event from core banking. For the DA model, the business events includes the following:

- Whenever an attribute from a Dimension (DIM) table and the data model is created or modified in the Core Banking. For example, a new ACCOUNT record is created or any attribute of the ACCOUNT application is changed.
- A transaction that raises an entry to an ACCOUNT and the updates in account balance affects the business event of the FACT tables.

The data contained in the IF events is in XML format. These events are exposed and consumed by any ESB, even without the module for the corresponding Reporting model.


##### Transformation Rules

The DA model contains a set of transformation rules which converts the data from the IF events. That is, from an XML format into SQL format and then load this into the Reporting DB. The transformation rules are available only if the DA module is licensed.


##### Query and Reports

The DA model is designed to provide full query capability for the accounts held in Temenos Core Banking. This data model provides the following details on which the queries and reports are built:

- The complete details of historic balances for both booking dated and value dated.
- The complete details of customers which includes the relationships with other customers.
- The details of the account static data and history of the account statement production.
- The complete details of all the account movements.

The standard Model Bank includes some pre-defined queries to interrogate the DF database and some metadata definitions, which allows creation and customisation of other enquiries. These are available in the DA module.

These queries provide more flexibility than the current Core Banking query capability. For example, it is possible to search for a movement with a specific amount, reference, narrative or transaction reference, without the need to specify the account number and date period. The DA queries provide the following capabilities:

- To query movements across accounts on a number of different criteria such as date, time, amount and type of transaction.
- To determine and reconcile the balance at any given date for the accounts based on the movements and viewed by booking date or value date.
- To show key data from the underlying business transactions.
- To query static details of the customer, customer relationships, accounts and related data historically.
- To query across multiple companies (access permitting) and multiple customers.

All static data is held by date, which creates a view that shows the state of the customer account and relationships at any given date and time.


#### 🔧 Working With

The topic covers the workflow of DA model.


##### Exit Points for DA Model

An exit point is the point in the system at which an event is triggered to load the data from the core banking system. However, static and dynamic tables have different exit points. At the exit point, the Integration Framework (IF) event is triggered and the IF run-time publishes the data in the IF.EVENTS.INTERFACE table.

The exit point for tables that are relatively static or non-volatile (such as the DIM and Reference tables) is when a record in the table is authorised (which includes both new records and changed records).

FACT tables (FACT_ACCOUNTMOVEMENT and FACT_BALANCE) contain the business facts and are fast changing. The exit point for these tables is within the core financial component service. The component service triggers an event with the account movement and the after-image of the account balances as a result of the transaction, for example, Funds Transfer (FT).

The account movements are contained in the Temenos Transact Transactional database (DB) tables, such as the STMT.ENTRY and STMT.ENTRY.DETAIL application. The entries are loaded near real-time, whenever the transaction is authorised and these movements are mapped into the FACT table (FACT_ACCOUNTMOVEMENT) in the read-only reporting DB.

An account may have consolidated accounting entries in Temenos Transact Transactional DB. However, the entries are loaded at the lowest level of detail into read-only reporting DB.

When a transaction is reversed, the core accounting process retrieves the original entries posted to the account, and creates a set of entries based on a copy and changes the sign of the entry setting in the Reversal Indicator field. At the same time, the status of the original entry and the new entry is set to REVE. This indicator is used to suppress the entry from a customer statement.

For such a reversal, both the original amended entry with the status set to REVE, the new reversal entry with the Reversal Indicator field set and the status set to REVE are published in the read-only reporting DB at the time of the reversal.

Temenos core banking maintains a historic series of account balances in the ACCT.ACTIVITY table for Temenos Transact legacy accounts and in the ACCT.BALANCE.ACTIVITY table for accounts created by the AA module. These tables hold the booking-dated and value-dated balances of the account.

The booking-date balance is the date on which the account balance is updated and is reflected in the general ledger. The value-date of accounting movement is important as it is used when calculating interest and charges for the account. The value-dated balance forms the basis for interest calculations. The after-image of the balances affected by the authorised transaction are loaded and time-stamped, to indicate the order in which the balances are updated.

Account balances are mapped into the FACT_BALANCE table with the account ID, balance type (booking or value), company ID, processing time (the time stamp when the balance is loaded) and balance date.


##### Initial Load Service

An initial load service is available for Temenos users though the DA model. It provides the ability to load the historic data from Temenos core banking into the DF reporting database, so that the bank has the correct view of the FACT and DIM tables within the data model.

The initial load service has a mechanism to automatically trigger the events to load the historical data for IF Dimension tables such as:

- DIM_COMPANY
- DIM_CURRENCY
- DIM_CHANNEL
- DIM_PARTY
- DIM_ACCOUNT
- DIM_TRANSACTIONTYPE
- PARTY_RELATION_MASTER
- BANKING_DATE

The DA.STMT.ENT.TAKEON service is run to trigger the initial load of the account movements into the DF database.

The historical account movements that are loaded into the DF are the ones that are from the live table and which are not archived. This service uses the entry information in STMT.PRINTED table to capture the underlying STMT.ENTRY records. If the entry is consolidated, it gets the underlying detailed entries from the STMT.ENTRY.DETAIL table.

The DA.ACCT.ACTIV.TAKEON service is run to trigger the initial load of the account balances into the DF database. Historical records are not available for each ACCT.ACTIVITY and ACCT.BALANCE.ACTIVITY updates in Core Banking, hence the initial load process only the ACCT.ACTIVITY and ACCT.BALANCE.ACTIVITY records that exist from the live table.


##### Handling High Volume Transaction Accounts

An account that is flagged for High Volume Transaction (HVT) does not have a balance update in real time. This is done to avoid a locking contention when processing the core banking transactions, since these accounts are frequently updated by multiple transactions. Entries are raised in real time for HVT accounts from the core financial component, but the balance updates are deferred and handled by the background service (HVT.MERGE.SERVICE).

For DF, both the entries and the account balance updates for HVT accounts are published from the HVT.MERGE.SERVICE and not from the financial component. This implies that the entries are not loaded in near real-time, but with a slight delay.


##### Enquiries and Views

Each reporting model is delivered with a set of standard enquiries and views that provides the capability to query the reporting DB. These views are available only in the DA module for the DA model.

| Views | Description |
|---|---|
| DF.VW.CUSTOMER | This view retrieves the details relating to the customer from the DIM_PARTY table, to allow customer search. |
| DF.VW.CUST.RELATION | This view retrieves the information relating to customer relationship from the DIM_PARTY, PARTY_RELATIONS_MASTER and PARTY_RELATIONS_DETAILS tables. |
| DF.VW.ACCOUNT | This view retrieves the details relating to account from the DIM_ACCOUNT table. |
| DF.VW.AC.STMT.SUMMA | This view retrieves the details relating to account and the statements from the DIM_ACCOUNT and STATEMENT table. |
| DF.VW.ACCOUNT.MOV | This view retrieves the details relating to value-dated account movements from FACT_ACCOUNTMOVEMENT table. This provides few details. |
| DF.VW.ACCT.MOV.DTL | This view retrieves the details relating to account movements from FACT_ACCOUNTMOVEMENT and DIM_ACCOUNT tables. This provides more details of the account movement. |
| DF.VW.AC.BOOKDT.BAL | This view retrieves the details relating to account booking dated balance from FACT_BALANCE (with balance type as BOOKING) and DIM_ACCOUNT tables. |
| DF.VW.AC.VALUDT.BAL | This view retrieves the details relating to account value dated balance from FACT_BALANCE (with balance type as VALUE) and DIM_ACCOUNT tables. |
| DF.VW.AC.BOOKDT.MOV | This view retrieves the details relating to the account movements, based on the processing date from the FACT_ACCOUNTMOVEMENT and DIM_ACCOUNT tables. |
| DF.VW.AC.VALUDT.MOV | This view retrieves the details relating to the account movements, based on the processing date from the FACT_ACCOUNTMOVEMENT and DIM_ACCOUNT tables. |

The list of enquiries that are built from the metadata definitions are explained in the below table.

> **⚠️ Note:** Temenos Transact is restricted to define relationships between customers owned by the same entity and only where the customer table is shared.

| Description | Enquiry Name in Temenos Transact | Enquiry Properties | Metadata Definition used in Temenos Transact Enquiry |
|---|---|---|---|
| CUSTOMER search - Search for matching customers. | ENQ.DIM.CUSTOMER.SEARCH | This query allows the user to search for customers across the enterprise and provides summary information about the customer, including the company, name, type of customer and status. Search options based on partial addresses and names are provided. From this base query, a number of subsequent queries are run for each customer that is found. | DF_VW_CUSTOMER |
| Customer Relationship search - Search for related customers. | ENQ.DIM.CUS.REL.SEARCH | This query allows the user to search for related customers. For a specified customer, expressed either as a number or name, the query shows all the related customers and the nature of their relationship. The user can restrict the search to relationships of a specific type. Temenos Transact is restricted to define relationships between customers owned by the same entity and only where the customer table is shared. | DF_VW_CUST_RELATION |
| Account search - Search for matching accounts. | ENQ.DIM.ACCOUNT.SEARCH | This query allows the user to search for accounts across the company. The user can search for a specific account matching the account number (including external account numbers) or the account title. The user can search for accounts owned by a customer, with optional additional criteria such as product and currency. As a result the query presents a list of all accounts found. | DF_VW_ACCOUNT |
| Account Statement summary - Shows the account statement dates and the opening and closing balances for matching accounts. | ENQ.DIM.ACC.STMT.SUM | This query is provided to show dates on which an account has produced an account statement, and the closing balance that is shown in the statement. The user can select accounts either based on a specific account number or for a specified customer criteria, in which case multiple accounts are shown. The search can be narrowed by supplying a range of dates to be considered. | DF_VW_AC_STMT_SUMMA |
| Account Movement search - Search for specific movements over specified accounts/customer and time. | ENQ.DIM.ACC.MOVEMENT | This query allows the user to search for specific movements that were posted to a Temenos Transact account. The search criteria allows the user to search across multiple accounts, and the user can refine the search by specifying the details of the customer and currency of the account. Search capability is possible using the details provided in the accounting entry such as, amount, local amount, type of movement, quoted reference and narrative information. | DF_VW_ACCOUNT_MOV DF_VW_ACCT_MOV_DTL |
| Account Booking dated balance - Shows the booking-dated balance for account(s) over a specified period. | ENQ.DIM.ACC.BKDATED.BALANCE | This query shows the booking dated balance for an account on any specified date or range of dates. The user can search for one or more accounts, either by a specified ID, account title, customer name or number. A date is specified and the booking-dated account balance on that date (or the last movement date before that date) is shown for the requested period. The booking-dated balance is the balance that the account holder is shown in their account statement. It is updated on the processing date of an underlying account movement. | DF_VW_AC_BOOKDT_BAL |
| Account Value dated balance - Show value dated balances for account(s) over a specified period. | ENQ.DIM.ACC.VDDATED.BALANCE | This query shows the value-dated balance for an account on a specified date or range of dates. The user can search for one of more accounts, either by specified account, account title or customer name or number. A date must be specified and the value-dated account balance on that date (or the last movement date before that date) will be shown for the requested period. The value-dated balance is the balance that is the basis for all interest calculations on an account. It is updated using the value date of an underlying account movement. | DF_VW_VALUDT_BAL |
| Account Statement - Show open and closing booking dated balance and movement details for an account over a specified period. | Composite screen: DIM.ACCOUNT.STATEMENT Enquiries: ENQ.DIM.ACCOUNT.STATEMENT | The query provides complete details of movements across an account or accounts between specified dates, showing the booking-dated balance on the start date and the end date. Details of the movement include the movement amount, value date, transaction with other references and the transaction narrative. Full movement details and the underlying common transaction information are available, allowing customised views with the different types of detail to be included. The query allows selection of multiple accounts for one or more customers in different companies. | DF_VW_AC_STMT_SUMMA DF_VW_AC_BOOKDT_BAL DF_VW_ACCOUNT_MOV |
| Account Value dated statement - Show open and closing value date balance and movement details for an account over a specified period. | ENQ.DIM.VDATED.STATEMENT | The query provides full details of movements across an account or accounts between specified value dates, showing the value-dated balance on the start date and on the end date. Details of each movement shown include the movement amount, the processing date, the transaction and other references and the transaction narrative. Full movement details and the underlying common transaction information are available, allowing customised views with different amount of detail to be included. The query allows the selection of multiple accounts for one or more customers in different companies. | DF_VW_AC_STMT_SUMMA DF_VW_AC_VALUDT_BAL DF_VW_ACCOUNT_MOV |


##### Data Model Diagrams

This topic explains the data models in DA module with diagrams.

Common Reference Data is a common set of tables across the entire reporting DB, that serves as a reference for information held within the reporting DB. These tables include both Global Reference Data (such as, country and currency), and Temenos specific Reference Data (such as, transaction types and channels). They are used to support and provide meaning to the Temenos Transact information held within the reporting DB.

The language a description is in, the currency an amount is in or the industry a customer has an occupation in.

The Customer Account Reporting subject area depicts all the objects and capabilities of the DF database that records the customer account transactions. It provides a clear view of all the information associated with a customer transaction in the form of FACT and DIM, where a customer transaction is represented as a FACT and all the significant information associated with it are represented as DIM. The purpose of this representation is to provide clarity on what parameters or dimensions are used to find a specific customer transaction or a group of customer transactions.

The customer number, account number, officer and channel.

The Account Balance Reporting depicts the various objects and capabilities of the DF database which records the account balance information. It provides a clear view of all the information associated with the balance generated as a result of a transaction with an account in the form of FACT and DIM, where the balance itself is represented as a FACT and the significant information associated with it (such as, the company code and account number) are represented as DIM. The purpose of this representation is to provide clarity on what parameters or dimensions are used to find a specific balance value.

The account number and company.

Customer reporting depicts the various objects and capabilities of the DF database that records the customer information and the relationships between them. This subject area expands on the customer dimension which provides a variety of information (such as, address, contact details and occupation). This is related to both the customers and the relationships between the various customers held within the DF database.

Data Framework (DF) is a data life cycle framework that provides the Temenos Transact customers to realise the huge potential value of the transactional data generated by Temenos Transact . The Operational Reporting database (DB) is deployed as a series of reporting models targeting different business domain such as:

- Customer and Account Balance Reporting model (product - DA).

##### Financial Reporting Model

The Financial Reporting model (DZ) is a business domain and is available from 201612. This model is packaged under the Temenos DZ module and is licenced together with the Data Framework Reporting Model (DF) module.

This model is designed specifically for the purposes of querying the information of general ledger movements, all necessary information to produce financial reports and queries. This includes a full history of journal movements, contract and general ledger balances, with capability to drill down from general ledger to the underlying movement or contract balance. The model also includes the necessary infrastructure to support the update of the read-only database in near-real time, and the ability to define and execute enquiries in the read-only database.


##### Understanding the Components of the DZ Module

The DZ module consists of the following components.

- The Dimensional (DIMal) data model.
- A set of Integration Framework (IF) events.
- A set of transformation rules (execute transform and load).
- Query and report.

It leverages the Temenos Transact Interaction and Integration frameworks, so that the data is available in near real-time.

The below diagram represents the components of Data Framework reporting.

The Temenos Transact transactional database contains the current (live) and aged (historical) data. The historical data is non-volatile and is used mainly for query and reporting purposes. Hence, this data can be moved to a Reporting database (DB) which is then used for querying purposes. This also leads to the reduced size of Temenos Transact Transactional database to a greater extent which improves the turnaround time of the transaction processing during online and Close of Business (COB).

The data life cycle management performs the following activities:

- Processes the business event initiated in Temenos Transact transactional database and updates the relevant tables in Temenos Transact Transactional database.
- As business events occur, the data is collected and stored in the Integration framework event table.
- Data captured by the Integration Framework is extracted (no ESB) into the staging area.
- Mappings are defined between the source data structure and reporting model, including transforms where required.
- Data is picked up from the staging area, transformed into reporting model format (organised) and then loaded into the model in the Reporting DB in near real time.
- Each Business Reporting model covers one or more business functions or domains.
- A DIMal data model is created which identifies this as selectable data (optimised for fast read).
- Data is stored with full history of change at the lowest level of detail possible.
- Views, queries and reports can be created in the read-only operational Reporting DB for near real-time predictive analytics.

The Operational Reporting DB is deployed as a series of reporting models targeting different business domain such as:

- Customer and Account Balance Reporting model (product - DA).
- Financial Reporting model (product - DZ).


##### Product Configuration

The DIMal data model consists of tables grouped into Domain and Support tables.

- Domain tables relate to specific business Domain and Support tables provide additional details to the business domain, and is common across all the other business domains.
- Some attributes of the Domain and Support tables are volatile in nature while the others are non-volatile.
- The volatile attributes are stored in FACT tables, like account movements and balances. The non-volatile attributes are stored in Dimension (DIM) tables, like customer, currency and account officer.

The database also consists of Reference tables and Snowflake schema tables:

- Snowflake schema - Since some attributes of certain DIMal tables are multi-valued, these DIM tables are normalised into multiple related tables in a Snowflake schema.
- Reference tables - Some tables are added into the DB model to provide additional description or values to a field(s) defined in the DIM or FACT tables.

Each Business Reporting model has their own FACT and DIM tables depending on the nature of the data being used for the model.

Framework - DC module of Temenos Transact


### 5.1  Misc

DC module allows a bank’s financial control department to correct period-end financial reporting, by creati...*
>

> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction


#### 📖 Introduction

Related topics:

- Temenos Transact Services

Data capture is the most basic method of moving balances and generating accounting entries. It allows the users to post transactions to customer accounts, internal account and profit and loss. DC module allows a bank’s financial control department to correct period-end financial reporting, by creating journal entries. Some banks refer to DC as journaling facility.

DC’s flexibility makes it versatile. It is widely customised by clients for multiple accounting purposes. For example, creating a transaction in customer account for an uncollected fee.

Use of customized screens created with the VERSION application can make this general application specific to particular accounting requirements.

DC groups the credit and debit transactions in batches and each batch must be balanced. If the batch is unbalanced during input, the system automatically balances the batch by creating a balancing accounting entry and posting it to a suspense account. This is done during the COB processing.


##### Product Configuration

This topic covers the configurations required for Data Capture. Unlike other applications in Temenos Transact where a single transaction may create multiple accounting entries, Data Capture operates by creating each accounting entry as a single transaction which, when combined with other transactions, form a batch.

The DC.PARAMETER application contains the category for each of the suspense accounts used by DATA.CAPTURE when either an entry needs to be moved to suspense account or a difference in a batch needs an adjustment entry. As DATA.CAPTURE is allowed to post entries to accounts which are in Position Type other than (as well as) TR, the CATEGORY details entered are set to each FX.POS.TYPE used.

The following screenshot shows how to define the CATEGORY for each type of suspense and Position Type .

As each entry is posted individually in the batch, it is important to keep track of the Position Type for each one as it is not permissible to have a mix of Position Type entries in the same batch. This file keeps track of each entry and is used to inform the user if the next entry matches the details of those previously entered for the batch.

This file is used by most Temenos Transact applications where a specific CATEGORY , ACCOUNT or CUSTOMER type is specified.

The SUSPENSE record contains the category for DATA.CAPTURE items to use when the close of business is in process and batches have been left unauthorised. During the close of business processing, all items that have not been authorised are replaced by suspense entries.

Additionally, a balancing item is generated if a batch is found to be out of balance. The internal account number for this is found by reference to a record identified as difference on the ACCOUNT.CLASS application.

TRANSACTION codes are low-level codes used by applications when creating accounting entries. These can indicate whether an entry:

- Is a debit or credit
- Incurs transaction charges
- Is a reference to be used on statements.

DATA.CAPTURE uses codes for balancing items of:

- 98 for Credit
- 99 for Debit

The DC.ADVICES application contains only one record and it is used to control the printing of advices from the DATA.CAPTURE module. The production of advices is requested via input in a Local Ref field at the transaction level during DATA.CAPTURE input. This item specifies which of the Local Ref fields has to be used to request the production of an advice, which will subsequently record the delivery reference for the advice produced.

The following screenshot shows the DC.ADVICES application.

The Dc Balanced field allows the user to control whether a batch may be left unbalanced. The options in this field enable authorisation of all items in the batch to occur consistently so that all items of the batch will have the same status after the batch has been authorised. The following options are available for this field:

- YES – The batch may be left unbalanced and the user may proceed further with input, delete or hold.
- LOCK – The batch cannot be left unbalanced to move on to other tasks. The user must balance the input. Otherwise, the user is prompted with the option to delete, hold the batch or continue the process until the batch balances.
- NULL – This is the default value, similar to NO, that is, the batch cannot be left unbalanced . The user must balance the batch before exiting it or abandoning the input.

If a batch is unbalanced, the DC processing at end-of-the day processing will automatically balance the batch and post the balancing entry to a suspense account configured for DC.

The following record in ACCOUNTING.PARAMETER application shows how to treat a batch as one transaction.

A suspense account is used to pass debit or credit entries when the system cannot find the right account to post to during the COB processes. When the entries generated by DC cannot find the right account to post to, an internal suspense account, specifically configured for DC, will be used so that the COB processing can continue.

Default categories for the suspense accounts to be used by DC are defined in the ACCOUNT.CLASS application, which instructs the system on the account category to be used. The SUSPENSE record contains the category for DATA.CAPTURE items to be used when the end-of-the-day is in progress and batches have been left unauthorised or unbalanced. During the close of business processing, all items that have not been authorised are replaced by suspense entries.

The following screenshot defines a SUSPENSE account record.

Additionally, a balancing item is generated if a batch is found to be unbalanced . The internal account number for this is defined in the DIFFERENCE record in the ACCOUNT.CLASS application.

> **⚠️ Note:** Non-zero balances in suspense accounts indicate issues and it is recommended that the bank investigates this immediately.


##### Illustrating Model Parameters

This section covers the high-level parameterisation setup, which allows the definition to pass debit and credit entries related to a transaction as a batch.

| S.No. | Parameter | Description |
|---|---|---|
| 1. | DC.PARAMETER | It allows the user to define the category required for the suspense account when a suspense entry or an adjustment entry needs to be parked. |
| 2. | ACCOUNT.CLASS | It allows the user to define the default suspense accounts when the correct internal account is not known and the default account category is defined for the SUSPENSE record of ACCOUNT.CLASS application. |
| 3. | TRANSACTION | It allows the user to define the information of transaction code details for each Temenos Transact application for creating accounting entries. Data Capture uses the codes for balancing the debit entry and credit entry. |
| 4. | DC.ADVICES | It allows the user to define the record to control the printing of advices in the Data Capture Module. |
| 5. | ACCOUNT.PARAMETER | SYSTEM record of this application provides an indicator field ( Dc Balanced ), which helps the DATA.CAPTURE application to identify whether any batch can be left unbalanced. If the field is set to Yes, the batch may be left unbalanced. The user may either process further with input or delete or hold the batch. |

Data Framework (DF) is a data life cycle framework that provides the Temenos Transact customers to realise the huge potential value of the transactional data generated by Temenos Transact . ##### Customer and Account Balance Reporting Model

The Customer and Account Balance Reporting model (DA) is a business domain which is available from the R15 release. It is packaged under the Temenos DA module and is licensed together with the Data Framework Reporting Model (DF) module. This model is designed specifically to:

- Query customer and account information.
- Query all the necessary information to produce the customer account balance enquries.

This query includes the history of account balances and account movements for customer accounts. The model also includes the necessary infrastructure to update read-only DB in near real-time and the ability to define and execute enquiries in the read-only DB.


##### Understanding the Components of DA Module

The following are the components of DA module:

- The DIMal Data model.
- A set of Integration Framework events.
- A set of transformation rules (execute transformation and load).
- Queries and reports.

#### 📖 Introduction

Related topics:

- T24 Services

Data Framework (DF) is a data life cycle framework that provides the Temenos Transact customers to realise the huge potential value of the transactional data generated by Temenos Transact . This is achieved by using a read-only Dimensional (DIMal) database optimised for near real-time predictive analytics and modelling tools.

DF provides the infrastructure to create and maintain a read-only database in near real time using Extract Transform and Load (ETL) process, to ensure a database which is optimised for reporting. It also provides the ability to design and execute queries against the read-only database. It leverages the Temenos Transact Interaction and Integration frameworks, so that the data is available in near real-time. Read Data Framework topic for more information on the Data Framework reporting components and product configuration.

The Operational Reporting database (DB) is deployed as a series of reporting models targeting different business domain such as:

- Customer and Account Balance Reporting model (product - DA).
- Financial Reporting model (product - DZ).


##### Financial Reporting Model

The Financial Reporting model (DZ) is a business domain and is available from 201612. This model is packaged under the Temenos DZ module and is licenced together with the Data Framework Reporting Model (DF) module.

This model is designed specifically for the purposes of querying the information of general ledger movements, all necessary information to produce financial reports and queries. This includes a full history of journal movements, contract and general ledger balances, with capability to drill down from general ledger to the underlying movement or contract balance. The model also includes the necessary infrastructure to support the update of the read-only database in near-real time, and the ability to define and execute enquiries in the read-only database.


##### Understanding the Components of the DZ Module

The DZ module consists of the following components.

- The Dimensional (DIMal) data model.
- A set of Integration Framework (IF) events.
- A set of transformation rules (execute transform and load).
- Query and report.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

The topic covers the configuration of DZ model components.


##### DIMal Data Model

The DIMal data model consists of tables grouped into Domain and Support as shown in the below screen shot.

- The Domain tables relate to the specific business domain for Financial Reporting (for example, Profit and Loss (PL) movements, contract balances, contract balances which are FACT tables, customer relationship which is a DIMal tables).
- The Support tables provide additional details to the business domain and that is common across all other business domains (for example, country, sector).

This database model is structured using the Star schema with FACT and DIM tables. These tables are explained in detail in the below sections.

These tables hold the reporting information of the business events from Temenos core banking relating financial movements and general ledger (GL) balances. The data for the FACT tables are from the Temenos core banking tables:

- FACT_CONTRACTMOVEMENT (with movement details from RE.CONSOL.SPEC.ENTRY ).
- FACT_PLMOVEMENT (with movement details from CATEG.ENTRY ).
- FACT_CONTRACTBALANCE (with asset balances from EB.CONTRACT.BALANCE ).
- FACT_GLBALANCE (with GL balances from RE.STAT.LINE.BAL ).
- FINANCIALDETAILS (relates to the FACT tables, financial movements and contract balances with enrichment of GL line, cash flow details and post-closing details). The enrichment of the financial details is based on the configuration in RE.FIN.DETAILS.PARAM .

The following tables hold the financial details for each corresponding FACT_TABLE:

- FINDETAILS_ACCOUNTMOVEMENT (GL lines for account movement).
- FINDETAILS_CONTRACTMOVEMENT (GL lines for contract movement).
- FINDETAILS_PLMOVEMENT (GL Lines for PL movement).
- FINDETAILS_CONTRCT_BALANCE (GL lines for contract balance).
- FINDETAILS_PL_POSTCLOSING (enrichment with post-closing details for PL adjustment).
- FINDETAILS_ACCT_POSTCLOSING (enrichment with post-closing details for account adjustment).
- FINDETAILS_CONT_POSTCLOSING (enrichment with post-closing details for revaluation adjustment).
- CASH_FLOW_FIN_DTLS (enrichment of account movements with cash flow details).

These tables hold relatively non-volatile set of attributes that enable query constraining and filtering. The examples of DIM tables are:

- DIM_CONTRACT (with static details relating to the contract, from EB.CONTRACT.BALANCES ).
- DIM_PRODUCT (with the product details from CATEGORY ).
- DIM_GL_REP_LINE (GL line definition details from RE.STAT.REP.LINE ).
- DIM_GL_REP_HEAD (GL report definition details from RE.STAT.REPORT.HEAD ).
- DIM_CONTRACTTXNTYPE (list of transaction codes for contract movement from RE.TXN.CODE ).
- DIM_BAL_TYPE (list of balance types from AC.BALANCE.TYPE ).

The DB also consist of Reference tables and Snowflake types tables.

Some tables are added into the DB model to provide additional description or values to a field(s) defined in the DIM or FACT table. The following is a list of Reference tables as part DZ model.

- INDUSTRY (list of industry definition from INDUSTRY ).
- LANGUAGE (list of language definition from LANGUAGE ).
- PC_PERIOD (list of post-closing periods from PC.PERIOD ).
- SECTOR (list of sector definitions from SECTOR ).
- TARGET (list of target definitions from TARGET ).
- CUSTOMER_STATUS (list of possible CUSTOMER.STATUS ).

Since some attributes of DIM tables are multi-valued, those DIM tables are normalised into multiple related tables in a Snowflake schema.

To ensure that the journal reports are aligned with GL reports for drill down capability, all the FACT tables have an additional field named Reporting Date . This is to ensure that only this field is used to report the movements and GL balances.


##### Integration Framework Events

The Integration Framework (IF) events are published at run-time from the business event.

For the DZ model, the business events include the following:

- Whenever a record from the DIM table of the model is created or modified.
- Whenever a business event that affect any of the FACT table. For example, a transaction that raise an accounting entry and updates the account or contract balance.

The data contained in the IF events is in XML format, these events are exposed and can be consumed by any ESB even without the DZ module.


##### Transformation Rules

The DZ model contains a set of transformation rules which converts the data from XML into SQL format, and then loads this into the reporting DB.


##### Query and Reports

The DZ model is designed to provide full query capability on financial related data held in the Temenos core banking.

The Data model provides the following details on which the queries and reports are built:

- Full details of real time and historic financial movements that affect the GL.
- Details of the contract static data.
- Full details of historic contract balances by asset type and date.
- Full details of all account, contract and PL movements are available.
- Full details of GL lines definition (chart of accounts).
- Option to include additional financial details with : Enrichment of GL lines for all financial movements and contract balances. Enrichment of cash flow details for account movements. Enrichment of post-closing details.

The standard Model Bank includes pre-defined queries to interrogate the DF database and some metadata definitions to create and customise other enquiries.

These queries provide more flexibility than the current core banking query capability. For example, it is possible to query a movement with a specific amount, reference, narrative or transaction reference without the need to first specify the account number and date period.

The Financial Reporting queries provide the following capabilities.

- Ability to query all financial movements on a number of different criteria (for example, date, time, amount and type of transaction).
- Ability to generate a journal report for any given date (based on the data loaded into the database) for contingent and non-contingent movements.
- Ability to show key data from the underlying business transaction.
- Ability to generate GL over historical dates, with drill down capability to underlying movements and contract balances.
- Ability to generate multi-GAAP reporting.
- Ability to view post-closing adjustments.

The queries can take place across multiple companies (access permitting) and multiple customers.


#### 🔧 Working With

The topic covers the workflow of Financial Reporting model (DZ).


##### Exit Points for DZ Model

An exit point is the point in the system at which an event is triggered is to load the data from the core banking system, the exit points for static tables and dynamic tables are different.

At the exit point, the Integration Framework (IF) event is triggered and the IF run-time publishes the data to the IF.EVENTS.INTERFACE table.

The following are the main exit points for the DA model.

- Application level for static tables.
- Core accounting for financial movements, account and contract balance update.
- HVT merge service for accounts flagged as high volume.
- Background service for enrichment of additional financial details.
- To handle special processing with financial accounting, such as Asset and Liability (AL) revaluation, post-closing (PC), GL line rebuild, Central Reporting Files (CRF) rebuild.

The below screen shot shows the main exit points from the Temenos core banking for the Financial Reporting model.

For tables that are relatively static, such as the Dimension (DIM) and Reference tables, the exit point is when a record in the table is being authorised, that includes any new or changed record.

The financial FACT tables contain business facts and are fast changing, the exit point for these is a component service within the core accounting processing. For non-HVT accounts, the component service (AccountingEventsService-extractDfEntryContractBalance) is called once at the transaction authorisation. The component service to emit the following reporting information as an event through the use of IF and the details are exposed in XML format.

- All the financial movements raised from the transaction.
- Account balance update as a result of the transaction.
- Contract balance update as a result of the transaction.

The financial movements consist of the account movements, contract movements and PL movements.

- The account movements are contained in the Temenos core banking STMT.ENTRY table, the reporting information is loaded into the FACT_ACCOUNTMOVEMENT table.
- The contract movements are contained in the Temenos core banking RE.CONSOL.SPEC.ENTRY table, the reporting information is loaded into the FACT_CONTRACTMOVEMENT table.
- The PL movements are contained in the Temenos core banking CATEG.ENTRY table, the reporting information is loaded into the FACT_PLMOVEMENT table.

For performance reason, an account can be defined to generate consolidated accounting entries in the core banking. However, the entries are loaded at the lowest level of detail into DF database. For this the reporting information is taken from the STMT.ENTRY.DETAIL , RE.SPEC.ENTRY.DETAIL and CATEG.ENTRY.DETAIL tables.

Temenos core banking maintains a historic series of account balances in the ACCT.ACTIVITY tables for standard accounts and in the ACCT.BALANCE.ACTIVITY tables for the accounts created by AA module. These tables hold the booking-dated and value-dated balances for the account.

The booking-date balance is the date on which the account balance is updated and is reflected in the GL.The value-date of accounting movement is important as this is used in calculating the interest and charges periodically for account. The value-dated balance is the basis for interest calculations.The after-image of the balances affected by the authorised transaction are loaded and are time-stamped to indicate the order in which the balances are updated.

The account balances are mapped into the FACT_BALANCE table with the following details:

- Contract ID
- Balance type (booking or value)
- Company ID
- Processing time (the time stamp that the balance is loaded)
- Balance date
- Balance

Temenos core banking maintains the contract balances in the EB.CONTRACT.BALANCE table for each asset balance type and date. This is the balance sheet balances at the contract.

The after-image of the balances affected by the authorised transaction are loaded and are time-stamped to indicate the order in which the balances are updated. The contract balances are mapped into the FACT_CONTRACTBALANCE table with the following details.

- Contract ID
- Balance Type (corresponding asset type)
- Company ID
- Processing time (the time stamp that the balance is loaded)
- Balance date
- Balance
- Credit and debit movements
- Position type

For HVT accounts, the component service - AccountingEventsService-extractDfEntryContractBalance is called during the HVT merge service, to update all financial movements of the transaction and account balances.

An HVT account denotes high volume transactions and the bulking of entries is extended to HVT accounts. The bulking can be configured using the AC.HVT.PARAMETER application by setting up the bulk size in the Ent Per If Event field.

Based on the number provided in this field, entries are grouped and published as individual IF events that have a common identifier. The IF events published for the bulk are followed by an event carrying the account or contract balance details. If the Ent Per If Event field is not configured, then all the entries and the balances are published as one IF event.

The below example screen shots shows the IF events for an HVT account from the HVT merge service. The IF event are updated with details of the account movements and account balance.

There is an option to enrich all the financial movements and contract balance updates with the corresponding GL lines as defined in the Temenos core banking and the ability to enrich the account movements with the corresponding cash flow related activity.

To trigger the enrichment of the financial details, the logic with the core accounting checks if the field to provide the financial details is set. The Fin Details Req field must be set to Yes in the ACCOUNT.PARAMETER application, to expose the financial details to the operational reporting database.

The choice of which financial details enrichment to expose in the operational reporting database is parameter driven. The RE.FIN.DETAILS.PARAM application can be defined at the lead company level with the following details:

- Selection of GL report(s) for which the corresponding GL lines are used to enrich the financial movements and contract balances.
- The logic to be applied to enrich the account movements with the corresponding cash flow activity.

The Financial Report field is a multi-value field to define the CRF report(s) which are used to generate all the financial reports in the operational reporting database. Each financial movement and contract balance update is enriched with the corresponding GL line for each of the reports specified, based on the report definition in core banking

> **⚠️ Note:** For performance reasons, tt is not recommended to define many reports.

Rules can be defined on how to classify the cash based movement ( STMT.ENTRY ) in order to produce a statement of cash flow, using the rules engine in CASHFLOW.RULE (the key to the EB.RULES.GATEWAY record) or plug-in an API in the Cashflow Api field in the RE.FIN.DETAILS.PARAM application.

Since the financial details enrichment requires the details outside the transaction context, it cannot happen within the transaction boundary, as it affects the performance of online transaction.

Instead, the core accounting process checks if the Fin Details Req field in ACCOUNT.PARAMETER is set to YES, a temporary financial detail internal table (AC.ACCOUNTING.DTLS.UPD) is updated for each transaction with enough details for a background service to provide the financial details enrichment.

A background service is run to use the financial details internal table and fetch the financial details, which the financial movements and contract balances are mapped to as a result of a transaction.

It computes the corresponding GL line based on the report line definition in the transactional system or executes the rules engine or API, to get the corresponding cash flow classifications. Then the component service is called to publish the financial details into the IF.EVENTS.INTERFACE.TABLE . Then the details are transformed and loaded into the following Data Framework tables:

- FINDETAILS_ACCOUNTMOVEMENT (GL lines for account movement).
- FINDETAILS_CONTRACTMOVEMENT (GL lines for contract movement).
- FINDETAILS_PLMOVEMENT (GL lines for PL movement).
- FINDETAILS_CONTRCT_BALANCE (GL lines for contract balance).
- CASH_FLOW_FIN_DTLS (enrichment of account movements with cash flow details).

Apart from the core accounting, there are other processes within core banking that generate financial movements and contract balance updates. These are special processes and includes the following:

- Asset and liability revaluation.
- Post-closing adjustment.
- Rebuild of GL lines as a result of a change in line definition.
- Rebuild of CRF key, which can result in balances and movements being mapped to different GL lines.

The component exit points for these special processes are also optional.Tthey are triggered only if the Fin Details Req field in ACCOUNT.PARAMETER is set to Yes.

The foreign currency Asset and Liability (AL) revaluation is done at the CRF (GL) level within Temenos core banking and the revaluation adjustment entries are posted at the GL level. The purpose of the operational reporting database is to record details at the lowest level, if any aggregation is done from the reporting database.

If the Fin Details Req field is set to Yes, a background service job - EOD.RE.CONTRACT.REVALUATION is triggered. Then the core banking revaluation process:

- Calculates the new local equivalent amount of the FCY balances for each foreign contract based on the current revaluation rate.
- Updates the EB.CONTRACT.BALANCES application with the new local equivalent.
- Calculates the revaluation adjustment entries at contract level.
- Publishes these entries at contract level in the IF.EVENTS.INTERFACE.TABLE , through the component service.

These details are transformed and loaded in the FACT_CONTRACTBALANCE and FACT_CONTRACTMOVEMENT.

> **⚠️ Note:** The revaluation adjustment entries in the core banking still remains at the GL level.

The post-closing module provides the capability to post accounting adjustments, which will affect an earlier accounting period. The Financial Reporting model has the required information to build a post-closing adjusted report with drill down capability, to the underlying adjustment movements and contract balances. The following are the information in the report:

- The movements raised by the post-closing module as a result of a post-closing adjustment.
- Enrichment of the GL line and the post-closing period to these movements.
- List of accounting periods to which post-closing adjustments are made in the transactional system and an option to drill down to the adjustments made.

An exit point is setup at the application level when the PC.PERIOD is created in core banking, to publish the accounting period ( PC.PERIOD ). Through the Data Framework transformation rules, it is loaded into the PC_PERIOD reference table.

When a PC adjustment is made through Funds Transfer (FT) or Data Capture (DC), the core accounting raises the movements and these are loaded into the FACT_ACCOUNTMOVEMENT or FACT_PLMOVEMENT tables. The background service responsible for the financial details enrichment also executes the component service routine, to publish the PC details for each PC adjustment entry. Then these are transformed and loaded into the following tables:

- FINDETAILS_PL_POSTCLOSING (PC details for PL adjustment).
- FINDETAILS_ACCT_POSTCLOSING (PC details for adjustment to accounts).

These tables have the following details:

- Processing date Time - The time-stamp details when the entry is loaded.
- Pc Period - The accounting period for which adjustment is made.
- Entry Id - The unique identifier to the entry.
- Company Id - The unique identifier to the company where the entry is booked.
- GL Line - The GL report line, where the entry is mapped to (at this stage the GL line is calculated based on the line definition in the current live database).

When a PC adjustment is made, the PC database is updated through the PC.UPDATE.DATABASE process, which updates the GL and performs any revaluation (if required).

The foreign currency revaluation happens, if there is a change in the exchange between the date of the accounting period and the date of the adjustment. Then the local equivalent balance is adjusted at the CRF level and a special entry is raised for the CRF level revaluation adjustment. A component exit point is setup within the PC.UPDATE.DATABASE process, to perform the following action:

- Publish the CRF movement for the CRF revaluation adjustment.
- Publish a dummy contract record for the CRF being revalued, as the revaluation is done at the CRF level and in the operational reporting database, each entry must have a corresponding contract.
- Publish the PC details and financial details for all PC adjustment movements, based on the GL line definition in the PC database. These details are then loaded into the following tables: FINDETAILS_CONT_POSTCLOSING (enrichment with PC details for revaluation adjustment). FINDETAILS_PL_POSTCLOSING (enrichment with PC details for PL adjustment). FINDETAILS_ACCT_POSTCLOSING (enrichment with PC details for account adjustment).

If there is any change in the GL report line definition or in the components of the CRF key, it has an impact on the GL line to which a movement and contract balance is mapped. A component exit point is built within the core job that recalculates the GL report line. It is triggered only if the modified report is specified in the RE.FIN.DETAILS.PARAM . Then the component service publishes all the affected contracts with the new GL line, as a result of the GL line rebuild.

The RE.DF.RECALC.ENTRY.LINE background service is built to recalculate the new GL line with all of current bank day’s account and contract movements. Then the entry IDs are published with the new GL line. If the GL line change is related to PL items, all the PL movements from the first day of the financial year to current bank day are loaded with only the entry ID and the new GL line.

A mechanism is built within the core process that recalculates the CRF key for each contract and PL movement, to save the temporary financial details triggered in the internal table (AC.ACCOUNTING.DTLS.UPD) with the details required to calculate the new GL line.

Then the background service that process the financial details enrichment executes the component service, to publish the contract balances and the PL movements with the new GL line. The financial details are transformed and loaded into the following tables in the operational reporting database:

- FINDETAILS_ACCOUNTMOVEMENT (GL lines for account movement).
- FINDETAILS_CONTRACTMOVEMENT (GL lines for contract movement).
- FINDETAILS_PLMOVEMENT (GL lines for PL movement).
- FINDETAILS_CONTRCT_BALANCE (GL lines for contract balance).


##### Initial Load Service

The initial load service is available for existing Temenos users taking the Reporting model. It provides the ability to load the historic data from Temenos Core Banking into the Data Framework reporting database. Hence, the bank may have the correct the view of the FACT and DIM tables within the data model.

The initial load service has a mechanism to automatically trigger the events, to load the historical data for the IF dimension and static tables such as:

- TARGET (list of target codes)
- SECTOR (list of sector codes)
- INDUSTRY (list of industry codes)
- AC.BALANCE.TYPE (list of soft balance types)
- RE.TXN.COODE (list of transaction codes for contract movements)
- CATEGORY (list of category codes)
- RE.STAT.REP.LINE (list of line definitions)
- PC.PERIOD

The RE.FIN.REPORTING.TAKEON service job is run, to trigger the initial load of the FACT tables and system defined balance types into the DF database.

The RE.DIM.DATA.TAKEON job gets the list of system defined balance types. These are loaded into the DIM_BAL_TYPE table in the operational reporting database.

The historical account movements that are loaded into the DF are from the live table and not archived.

- The RE.PL.MVMT.TAKEON service job is run to publish the historical PL movements from the CATEG.ENTRY records. If the entry is consolidated, then the job gets the underlying detailed entries from the CATEG.ENTRY.DETAIL table. These are loaded into the FACT_PL_MOVEMENT table in the operational reporting database.
- The RE.CONTRACT.MVMT.TAKEON service job is run to publish the historical contract movements from the RE.CONSOL.SPEC.ENTRY records. If the entry is consolidated, then the job gets the underlying detailed entries from the RE.SPEC.ENTRY.DETAIL table. These are loaded into the FACT_CONTRACT_MOVEMENT table in the operational reporting database.

Run the RE.GL.BALANCE.TAKEON service job, to publish the historical GL line balances from the RE.STAT.LINE.BAL records. These are then loaded into the FACT_GLBALANCE table in the operational reporting database.

> **⚠️ Note:** The LOCAL and PROFIT records are not loaded.

Run the RE.ECB.BALANCE.TAKEON service job, to publish the current contract balances from the EB.CONTRACT.BALANCES records. Since, core banking does not maintain historical records of the contract balances, only the records that are current in the core banking system alone are published.

The static information are loaded into the DIM_CONTRACT table. The asset balances are loaded into the FACT_CONTRACTBALANCE table with the following details:

- Processing date time
- Contract ID
- Currency
- Company ID
- Balance type
- Balance Date
- Reporting date
- Position Type (used for multi-GAAP reporting)
- Balance (foreign amount and local equivalent)
- Credit movement (foreign amount and local equivalent)
- Debit movement (foreign amount and local equivalent)
- Reporting type (contingent or non-contingent)


##### Multi-GAAP Reporting

The Position Type field in Temenos core banking allows reporting under different Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (GAAP):

- TR: This is used for all movements and balance updates from the core banking functionality.
- IF: This is used for all delta movements and balance updates from the IFRS module. The delta is the difference between IFRS method and core banking.
- IA: This is used for all delta movements and balance updates from the International Accounting (IA) standards module.
- XX: This is used for all delta movements and balances updated for each country’s local GAAP. For example, GB for UK, US for USA and FR for France.

The financial movements, contract balances and GL balances loaded into the reporting database are tagged with the Position Type . Hence, the capability to generate financial reports based on Position Type is provided. For example, the below screen shot shows the journal summary by Position Type .


##### Enquiries and Views

The following standard enquiries and views provide the capability to query the read-only reporting database for the Financial Reporting model. These views are available only when the DZ module is installed.

| Views | Description |

| DF.VW.CNTRCT.MVMT$DIM | This view retrieves the details relating to account movements from FACT_CONTRACTMOVEMENT, FACT_ACCOUNTMOVEMENT and DIM_ACCOUNT tables. This provide more details on the AL movements |

| DF.VW.GL.MVMT.SRCH$DIM | This view retrieves all the movements from FACT_ACCOUNTMOVEMENT, FACT_CONTRACTMOVEMENT, FACT_PLMOVEMENT and FIN_DETAILS tables, to provide from the GL lines to the underlying movements |
| DF.VW.TRANS.SEARCH$DIM | This view retrieves the details from the FACT_ACCOUNTMOVEMENT, FACT_CONTRACTMOVEMENT and FACT_PLMOVEMENT tables, to allow the search from an underlying transaction or other selected criteria |
| DF.VW.TRANS.SUMMARY$DIM | This view retrieves the details from the FACT_ACCOUNTMOVEMENT, FACT_CONTRACTMOVEMENT and FACT_PLMOVEMENT tables. It provides a summary by reporting date, position type, reporting type (contingent or non-contingent), system ID and company ID |
| DF.VW.CONTRACT.BAL$DIM | This view retrieves the details relating to contract balances from the FACT_CONTRACTBALANCE |
| DF.VW.PL.BAL.LIST$DIM | This view retrieves the details relating the PL movements from the first day of the required financial year and makes a summary of PL balances. |
