##### Financial Data Model Diagrams

This topic explains the data models in DZ module with diagrams.

Common Reference Data is a common set of tables across the entire reporting database that serves as reference or lookup for information held within reporting database. These tables include both global reference data (like, country and currency) and Temenos specific reference data (like, transaction types and channels).

They support and provide meaning to the core banking information held within the reporting database. For example, what language a description might be in, or what currency an amount might be in or what industry a customer might have an occupation in.

The contract subject area depicts the various objects and capabilities of a contract within the DF database. It provides a clear view of all the information associated with and forms a contract within Temenos core banking.

The contract movement subject area depicts all the objects and capabilities of the DF database that record a contract transaction. It provides a clear view of all information associated with a contract transaction in the form of FACTS and DIM, where a contract transaction is represented as a FACT and all the significant information associated with it are represented as DIM.

The purpose of this representation is to provide clarity on the parameters such as customer number, currency and transaction type that can be used to find a specific contract transaction or a group of contract transactions (FACT).

The profit and loss reporting subject area depicts all the objects and capabilities of the DF database that record a PL transaction. It represents the information associated with a PL entry in the form of FACTS and DIM, where a PL transaction is represented as a FACT and all the significant information associated with it are represented as DIM.

The purpose of this representation is to provide clarity on the parameters, such as customer number, currency and transaction type that can be used to find a specific or a group of PL transactions (FACT).

Contract balance subject area depicts the various objects and capabilities of the DF database in terms of representing a balance generated, as a result of a transaction related to a contract. It shows a contract balance value and its attributes as a FACT and all the other significant associated information (such as, contract and company) as its DIM.

The purpose of this is to understand the various parameters (DIM) that can be used to get to a specific or a group of contract balance records.

Temenos core banking and in effect the DF database holds each of the GL reports in the form of templates generating the GL report automatically when needed. The GL financial details subject area depicts the association between an accounting transaction and a GL report line template item.

This allows the user to identify all the accounting transactions that are part of a GL report line or vice versa. The objects contained within this subject area aim to provide clarity on which GL report lines or GL reports are affected by an accounting transaction immediately after an accounting transaction is recorded and even before a GL report is generated.

The GL balance subject area depicts the various objects associated with a balance generated, as a result of an accounting record that form a part of the financial statements. It provides a clear view of the capabilities of the DF database in terms of being able to extract a GL balance value or a group of GL balance values in the form of FACTS and DIM. The GL balance value is represented as a FACT and the possible means to get to one or more general ledger balance values are represented as DIM.

The post-closing subject area depicts the effects of a post-closing action on all the associated accounting transactions, as well as how it translates the entries within a GL report.

Cash flow details represents the various objects within the DF database that are used to detail the cash flow activity associated with a customer transaction.

### 6.3  Misc


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *Data Framework is a data life cycle framework that provides the Temenos Transact customers to realise the huge potential value of the transactional data generated by Temenos Transact . This is achieved by using a read-only Dimensional (DIMal) database optimised for near real-time predictive analytic...*
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction


#### 📖 Introduction

Related topics:

- Temenos Transact Services

Data Framework is a data life cycle framework that provides the Temenos Transact customers to realise the huge potential value of the transactional data generated by Temenos Transact . This is achieved by using a read-only Dimensional (DIMal) database optimised for near real-time predictive analytics and modelling tools.

Data Framework provides the infrastructure to create and maintain a read-only database in near real time using Extract Transform and Load (ETL) process, to ensure a database which is optimised for reporting. It also provides the ability to design and execute queries against the read only database. It leverages the Temenos Transact Interaction and Integration frameworks, so that the data is available in near real-time.

The below diagram represents the components of Data Framework reporting.

The Temenos Transact transactional database contains the current (live) and aged (historical) data. The historical data is non-volatile and is used mainly for query and reporting purposes. Hence, this data can be moved to a Reporting database (DB) which is then used for querying purposes. This also leads to the reduced size of Temenos Transact Transactional database to a greater extent which improves the turnaround time of the transaction processing during online and Close of Business (COB).

The data life cycle management performs the following activities:

- Processes the business event initiated in Temenos Transact transactional database and updates the relevant tables in Temenos Transact Transactional database.
- As business events occur, the data is collected and stored in the Integration framework event table.
- Data captured by the Integration Framework is extracted (no ESB) into the staging area.
- Mappings are defined between the source data structure and reporting model, including transforms where required.
- Data is picked up from the staging area, transformed into reporting model format (organised) and then loaded into the model in the Reporting DB in near real time.
- Each Business Reporting model covers one or more business functions or domains.
- A DIMal data model is created which identifies this as selectable data (optimised for fast read).
- Data is stored with full history of change at the lowest level of detail possible.
- Views, queries and reports can be created in the read-only operational Reporting DB for near real-time predictive analytics.

The Operational Reporting DB is deployed as a series of reporting models targeting different business domain such as:

- Customer and Account Balance Reporting model (product - DA).
- Financial Reporting model (product - DZ).


##### Product Configuration

The DIMal data model consists of tables grouped into Domain and Support tables.

- Domain tables relate to specific business Domain and Support tables provide additional details to the business domain, and is common across all the other business domains.
- Some attributes of the Domain and Support tables are volatile in nature while the others are non-volatile.
- The volatile attributes are stored in FACT tables, like account movements and balances. The non-volatile attributes are stored in Dimension (DIM) tables, like customer, currency and account officer.

The database also consists of Reference tables and Snowflake schema tables:

- Snowflake schema - Since some attributes of certain DIMal tables are multi-valued, these DIM tables are normalised into multiple related tables in a Snowflake schema.
- Reference tables - Some tables are added into the DB model to provide additional description or values to a field(s) defined in the DIM or FACT tables.

Each Business Reporting model has their own FACT and DIM tables depending on the nature of the data being used for the model.

### 7.1  Converting Sys Base Euro


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *Temenos Transact users with a local currency, that is one of the In-currencies must convert the base currency to EUR during the transition phase. The Euro module provides a utility that allows this conversion to take place.*
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Batch Sessions*, *Conv Cont Susp Cat*, *Conv Lcy Susp Cat*, *Conv Lcy Txn Code*, *Conversion Date*, *Converted Lcy*, *Fixed Start Date*, *Lccy Conv Rec* ... +4 more
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

Temenos Transact users with a local currency, that is one of the In-currencies must convert the base currency to EUR during the transition phase. The Euro module provides a utility that allows this conversion to take place.


##### Timing of the Conversion

The conversion can be run as soon as the fixed rates apply and it takes place during the COB process immediately preceding the start date. The conversion process runs in the COB after all the standard COB processing and reports have been processed, just before the date is cycled to the next working day.

The COB process halts just prior to the start of the actual conversion, when the normal COB processing is complete. In this stage, a backup should be taken, as this is the last point the system will be in National Currency Unit (NCU). If the conversion is run at the end of a financial period, which is likely to be the case, the backup taken at this point can be restored in another area to allow additional reports and enquiries to take place on the old base currency.


##### Preparation of the Database

The local currency conversion converts many files. The ACCOUNT.FILE.STATS process should be run and the results should be analysed before the conversion preparation. Any poorly sized files should be resized as they can adversely affect the performance of the conversion.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

This section explains the configuration of Conversion of System's Base Currency to Euro.


##### Configuring the System Ready for Conversion

The conversion process can result in rounding errors, which can be corrected by posting any difference to a difference suspense account. For this purpose, an internal account with CATEGORY in the range of 10000 – 19999 should be created.

When contracts are converted, the early maturity of the NCU contract and draw-down of the EUR contract are made through the suspense accounts. A new category should be created for this suspense in the range of 10000 – 19999.

A different suspense account should be opened in EUR for the category created in the above steps. The user must open an account in each company, which shares the CURRENCY application.

A transaction code should be created for any movement created to adjust conversion differences.


##### Configuring the Batch Process

The run date should be set for the adhoc jobs for the following batch records:

- EU.BASE.VERIFY
- EU.BATCH.INTERRUPT
- EU.PRE.BASE.CONVERT
- EU.RUN.BASE.CONVERT
- EU.POST.BASE.CONVERT
- EU.BASE.CONV.CRB.RECALC
- EU.BASE.CONV.REPORTING
- EU.BASE.CONV.REPORTS2

In a multi-company environment, these jobs run for each currency-level company. The dates should be set only for those companies to be converted. The EU.BASE.VERIFY job will set the run dates for the remaining EU batches.


##### ConfiguringEU.PARAMETER

The EU.PARAMETER application contains details for each company that should be converted. The user must convert each company sharing a CURRENCY application and one record is required for each company. The user must be in the correct company to input the record as the file is keyed by the company code.

The following information should be input in the EU.PARAMETER application to run the conversion:

- Converted Lcy – Denotes the currency to convert to, that is, EUR.
- Conversion Date – This is the date on which the conversion is run. This date cannot be before the Fixed Start Date for the Converted Lcy . The date can be entered prior to the start date of the currency provided it is the working day before the start date. If the user wants to run the conversion on 1st January 1999, the Conversion Date will be 01/01/99 and the system date will be 31/12/98.
- Conv Lcy Susp Cat – The category created for the difference entry should be entered in this field
- Conv Cont Susp Cat – The category opened for contract suspense accounts should be defined in this field
- Conv Lcy Txn Code – The transaction code created in the previous steps should be defined in this field
- Lccy Conv Rec – The record ID to the EU.CONVERSION.PROCESS file should be specified in this field. The released records, EURO.LCCY.1 and EURO.LCCY.2 should be defined here. User should not add additional records without Temenos approval.

The following screenshot shows how to set up the EU.PARAMETER for base currency conversion.

The linked EU.CONVERSION.PROCESS records list the specific EU.CONVERSION.PARAM items that are run and the correct order of processing.


#### 🔧 Working With


##### Multi-Threading of Base Currency Conversion

The user can run the base currency conversion with multi-threading functionality, which should make greater use of processor availability and improve performance and conversion times during end-of-day. Here the user should make minor changes to use the full functionality of the multi-threading.

The EU.BASE.RUN.CONVERT routine should be specified as the JOB.NAME in the batch EU.RUN.BASE.CONVERT. This job is run when the base currency is converted from the In-currency to Euro.


##### Setting Parameters and Processes for Multi-Threading

Once the batch base currency conversion record is set to run in multi-thread, the user must specify the records that should be converted, and the conversion thread by which it should be converted. Following are the three stages of the conversion:

- The records that should be converted should be identified on the EU.CONVERSION.PARAM table and where necessary, these may need to be amended to suit local requirements.
- The identified records are divided into sets on the EU.CONVERSION.PROCESS file.
- The divided sets must be applied to the overall EU.PARAMETER record.

The records that should to be converted for the base currency conversion will be provided by Temenos through the released EU.CONVERSION.PARAM records. Each record specifies the field names, which should be converted for that application. In many cases, user intervention may not be required. However, some files have to be changed to suit local requirements. For example, if large files have been split into distributed files (for example, CATEG.ENTRY table), in the Voc File Name field of the EU.CONVERSION.PARAM application, the VOC name for that file should be specified.

Once all EU.CONVERSION.PARAM applications have been set up, they should be added to EU.CONVERSION.PROCESS groups. Two records, EURO.LCCY.1 and EURO.LCCY.2 which contain all the records that need to be converted for the EU base conversion process, is already released by Temenos Transact . However, to enable multi-threading, new EU.CONVERSION.PROCESS records should be set up, to split out the number of these records evenly across each process. These records should then be included in EU.PARAMETER application.

> **⚠️ Note:** It is important that there are at least as many EU.CONVERSION.PROCESS records listed in EU.PARAMETER application, as there are batch sessions to be run during the COB (as specified in the Batch Sessions field in the SPF SYSTEM record). If there are fewer records in the Lccy Conv Rec field than the number of batch sessions, the system will automatically assume that it must run in single-thread mode.


##### Running Local Currency Conversion

Once the items in the previous steps have been configured, the batch can be started, which converts the local currency. The COB runs normally until the EU.BATCH.INTERRUPT is reached.

| Percentage spread | Percentage difference in mid-rate |
|---|---|
| 5% | 0.225% |
| 0.5% | 0.0025% |
| 0.05% | 0.000025% |

When the batch halts, a backup of the system should be taken.

The batch can be restarted by taking the AUTO BATCH option. The batch will then continue as normal.


#### 📋 Tasks

There are no Tasks available for Converting the System's Base Currency to Euro feature.


#### 📊 Outputs

There are no Outputs available for Converting the System's Base Currency to Euro feature.

### 7.2  Displaying Euro Equivalents


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *Temenos Transact will allow the Euro equivalent to be displayed for In-currency amounts throughout the system including:*
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Amount*, *De Message*, *Enrichm Char*, *Field Name*, *Fixed Rate*, *Fixed Start Date*, *Type*
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

Temenos Transact will allow the Euro equivalent to be displayed for In-currency amounts throughout the system including:

- Display of all amounts in all applications. An additional enquiry conversion option to display the amount in enquiries.
- Conversion option is available to display the amount in DE.FORMAT.PRINT and DE.FORMAT.TEMPLATE applications.

Euro equivalents are displayed whenever a Fixed Rate is specified for a CURRENCY regardless of whether the Fixed Start Date is reached. This will allow the Euro equivalent to be shown on customer output for information purposes prior to the start date.


#### 🔧 Working With


##### Displaying EURO Equivalents in Applications

Once the Fixed Rate is specified in a CURRENCY record, the system will automatically display the Euro equivalent as an enrichment wherever possible.

The Euro equivalent will not be displayed if:

- The field is already enhanced.
- A version is used and the number of enrichment characters ( Enrichm Char in the VERSION record) for the field is not set.

If existing versions do not show the enrichment against an Amount field, the version should be amended accordingly. Foreign currency amount fields where the related currency is an In-currency, displays the equivalent; similarly, local currency fields where the local currency is ‘In’.


##### Displaying EURO Equivalents in Enquiry

There are three conversion types in Temenos Transact Enquiry, which allows Euro equivalents and related information to be displayed for any amount. These conversions are:

| Input | Amount fields |
|---|---|
| Format | UTIL FIXEQU, ccy name Where, Ccy name is the name of the enquiry field containing the value of the currency. |
| Result | If Ccy name is an In-currency, the Euro Equivalent calculated at FIXED.RATE. If Ccy name is an out currency, a null value is returned. |

| Input | Not required |
|---|---|
| Format | UTIL FIXCCY, ccy name Where, Ccy name is the name of the enquiry field containing the value of the currency. |
| Result | If Ccy name is an In-currency, the fixed currency, that is, EUR. If Ccy name is an Out-currency, a null value is returned. |

| Input | Not required |
|---|---|
| Format | UTIL FIXRTE, ccy name Where, Ccy name is the name of the enquiry field containing the value of the currency. |
| Result | If Ccy name is an In-currency, the fixed conversion to the currency. If Ccy name is an Out-currency, a null value is returned. |


##### Displaying the Euro Equivalent in Printed Delivery Output

Three conversions are available in the applications DE.FORMAT.PRINT and DE.FORMAT.TEMPLATE , which can be used to display Euro equivalents, and Euro related information. These can be added to the existing customer output as required.

The specification and use of the conversions is identical in both applications.

| Input | Amount field |
|---|---|
| Format | FIXEQU*ccy name Where, Ccy name is the name of the De Message field containing the value of the currency. |
| Result | If Ccy name is an In-currency, the Euro Equivalent calculated at FIXED.RATE. If Ccy name is an Out-currency, a null value is returned. |

| Input | Not required |
|---|---|
| Format | FIXCCY*ccy name Where, Ccy name is the name of the De Message field containing the value of the currency |
| Result | If Ccy name is an In-currency, the fixed currency, that is, EUR. If Ccy name is an Out-currency, a null value is returned. |

### 7.3  Euro and Pos Mgmt


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *The Position Management application has additional functionality built in for use with the Euro.*
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Base Country*
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

The Position Management application has additional functionality built in for use with the Euro.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

This is covered as part of module configuration. There is no specific configuration for this feature.


#### 🔧 Working With


##### Defining a Calendar for the Euro

The Euro has only two holidays (Christmas and New Year), so settlement is possible even on non-working days for the local country. The user may want to view some of the positions held in the position management system based on the possible settlement dates, rather than based on the local holiday definitions. The PM.CALENDAR application allows dates to be calculated based on specific countries and/or regions.

The Base Country field allows the specific country or region to be defined. Combinations can be specified by expanding the multi-value, if a combination is used as a common working day and is obtained when calculating the calendar dates. Existing PM.CALENDAR definitions may be modified, or the user can create new calendars.

### 7.4  Exchange Rate Calc Involving Euro


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *Although the euro can be considered as a regular currency in certain circumstances, when In-currencies are involved, additional rules will apply for the calculation of exchange rates. The Euro module allows the exchange rate regulations to be applied for all rate calculations in Temenos Transact .*
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Blocked Date*, *Fixed Ccy*, *Fixed Rate*, *Fixed Start Date*, *Forward Premium*, *Start Date*
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

Although the euro can be considered as a regular currency in certain circumstances, when In-currencies are involved, additional rules will apply for the calculation of exchange rates. The Euro module allows the exchange rate regulations to be applied for all rate calculations in Temenos Transact .


#### ⚙️ Configuration

This section covers the configuration required for exchange rate calculations involving the euro.


##### Fixing In-currencies to the EURO

The fixed rates and dates for In-currencies should be applied when available.

Use of Expected Fixed Rates:

The expected rates will be published and can be specified before the fixing date. If rates are specified before the fixing date, the fixed rate calculations described in the section Exchange Rate Calculations will not be used in transaction calculations until the fixing date is reached.

On the fixing date, the user must ensure that the rates of fixed In-currencies are set to be equal to the fixed rate for the currency with zero spread.

Adding Rates to an In-currency:

The fixed rate should be added to the CURRENCY record for each In-currency. Rates are fixed by specifying the value of 1 euro in the Fixed Rate field. The Fixed Ccy field should be defined as EUR, the date at which the fixed rate applies should be defined in the Fixed Start Date field.

Setting Expiry Date for a Currency:

At the end of the transition phase, the National Currency Unit (NCU) will cease to exist. To prevent transactions being raised after this date, the Blocked Date field should be specified in the CURRENCY record. Any transaction raised with a value date after this date will generate an override.

> **⚠️ Note:** In the below example XEU should be blocked from 01/01/99 as it is officially replaced by EUR on this date.

A summary of the currencies linked to a fixed currency can be obtained by viewing the EU.FIXED.CURRENCY table.


##### Forward Exchange Rates

Once the Euro begins, the conversion rate is fixed. There will be no forward premium or discount for any of the In-currencies against the euro. If the local currency of the system is either an In-currency or the euro, the FORWARD.RATES table should be modified to set the Forward Premium to be zero from the euro Start Date .

If forward rates are built automatically from the PERIODIC.INTEREST application, this feature should be disabled for each of the In-currencies in the above situation. If the local currency is out, Forward rates will be required for EUR in the same way as any other currency. For the In-currencies, the rates will need to be derived from the Euro rates.


##### Interest Rates

When European Monetary Union (EMU) starts, the base interest rates will be the same for each In-currency, since each In-currency is a different expression of the euro. Currently, interest rates will be different for each currency. However, these should converge towards a common rate towards the end of 1998. The interest rate applications ( PERIODIC.INTEREST and BASIC.INTEREST ) are used to record the rates.

Interest rates used for accounts ( GROUP.DEBIT.INT and GROUP.CREDIT.INT ) needs to be reviewed for each product.


#### 🔧 Working With

Fixed exchange rates or triangulation means that once fixed, each National Currency Unit (NCU) should be considered as a different expression of the Euro, rather than as a separate currency. Since there is a fixed conversion rate between each NCU and the Euro, it is possible to convert from any In-currency to another or to the Euro and always receive the same result.

The rules for performing calculation and rounding, under Article 235 regulation can be summarised as follows:

- The conversion rates shall be adopted as one Euro expressed in terms of each of the national currency units of the participating countries to six significant figures (the number of decimal places varies from one national currency to another).
- The conversion rates will not be rounded or truncated during conversions.
- When rounding monetary amounts to be paid or accounted for after a conversion, these must be rounded up or down to the nearest sub-unit (or in the absence of a sub-unit to the nearest unit) or according to national law or practice to a multiple or fraction of the sub-unit (or unit) of the national currency unit. If the result is exactly halfway, the result shall be rounded up.
- The conversion rates shall be used for conversions in either direction between the Euro and its national denominations.
- Inverse rates derived from the conversion rates shall not be used.
- Conversion between one national currency and another must be done through the Euro – referred to as triangulation.

In Temenos Transact , the fixed conversion rates are held in the CURRENCY application in the Fixed Rate field. The currency against which the rate is fixed (that is, EUR), is held in the Fixed Ccy field, the date the fixed rate applies from is held in the Fixed Start Date field. Any transaction involving an In-currency on or after the fixed start date follows the above rules. The details of the calculation methods are described below.


##### Temenos TransactConversion of In-currency to In-currency

As mentioned above, conversions from one In-currency to another must always be performed through the Euro module (after the Fixed Start Date has passed). This is frequently referred to as triangulation.

- An In-currency amount is converted to the Euro amount by dividing the In-currency amount by the Fixed Rate to the Euro.
- The intermediary Euro value is held to six decimal places.
- The intermediary Euro amount is converted to the other In-currency amount by multiplying by the Fixed Rate .
- The resulting amount is rounded and formatted to the number of decimals of the currency.


##### Temenos TransactConversion of In-currency to Euro

Conversions from an In-currency to the Euro always use the fixed conversion rate (after the Fixed Start Date has passed).

- An In-currency amount is converted to the Euro amount by dividing the In-currency amount by the Fixed Rate to the Euro.
- The resulting Euro amount is rounded and formatted to the number of decimals of the currency.


##### Temenos TransactConversion of Euro to In-currency

Conversions from the Euro to an In-currency always use the fixed conversion rate (once the Fixed Start Date has passed).

- A Euro amount is converted to an In-currency amount by multiplying by the Fixed Rate .
- The resulting In-currency amount is rounded and formatted to the number of decimals of the currency.


##### Temenos TransactConversion of In-currency to Out-currency

Conversions of In-currency amounts to Out-currency amounts are performed through the Euro.

- The In-currency amount is converted to a Euro amount by dividing it by the Fixed Rate .
- The result is limited to the applicable six decimal digits.
- The Euro amount is converted to the out currency using the standard rate conversion.
- The resulting Out-currency amount is rounded and formatted to the number of decimals of the currency.


##### Temenos TransactConversion of Out-currency to In-currency

Conversions of Out-currency amounts to In-currency amounts are performed through the Euro.

- The Out-currency amount is converted to a Euro amount using the standard rate calculations.
- The result is held to six decimal places
- The Euro amount is converted to the In-currency by multiplying it by the Fixed Rate .
- The resulting In-currency amount is rounded and formatted to the number of decimals of the currency.


##### Use of Different Rates between In-currencies and Euro

Applications that allow the entry of exchange rates, allow entry of rates that differ from the fixed rate or the derived cross-rate (using the fixed rates). In this case, an override is generated by the system if the rate entered differs from the fixed cross rate by more than 0.001%.


#### 📋 Tasks

There are no Tasks available for Exchange Rate Calculations Involving the Euro feature.


#### 📊 Outputs

There are no Outputs available for Exchange Rate Calculations Involving the Euro feature.

### 7.5  Local Clearing


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *Many In-Country local clearing systems allow payments to be made in Euro and in the local currency. During the transition period, payments can be sent in both EUR and NCU.*
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Allow Fcy Debit*, *Brnch Nostro Bc*, *Brnch Nostro Bd*, *Brnch Nostro Bi*, *Payment Ccy*, *Request Type*
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

Many In-Country local clearing systems allow payments to be made in Euro and in the local currency. During the transition period, payments can be sent in both EUR and NCU.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

This is covered as part of module configuration. There is no specific configuration for this feature.


#### 🔧 Working With


##### Allowing Payment in EUR

Prior to the introduction of the Euro, outgoing local clearing payments could only be made through the Temenos Transact FUNDS.TRANSFER application in the local currency. To allow transactions in EUR and NCU, the FT.BC.PARAMETER parameter for the local clearing system should be modified.

To allow a non-local currency account to be debited when sending an outgoing payment, the Allow Fcy Debit field should be set to YES.

The Payment Ccy field is used to control the currencies in which the payment can be sent to the clearing institution. If there is no value specified, the system will assume that only the local currency is valid. Payment will only be allowed in the currencies defined in this field if defined.

The following screenshot shows the field names and details in FT.BC.PARAMETER application.

Additional clearing accounts will be required for each additional currency specified in the Payment Ccy field. Each additional account should be added to the system record in FT.LOCAL.CLEARING, in the Brnch Nostro Bi , Brnch Nostro Bc , Brnch Nostro Bd fields, before they can be used in a local clearing FUNDS.TRANSFER transaction.


##### Layout of Local Clearing Files

If the local clearing system allows payment in EUR in addition to NCU, the record layout of the clearing files to be sent and received is likely to be different. The changes required will depend on each local system. The local Temenos client services area will be able to give further information regarding the required changes.


#### 📋 Tasks

Before the introduction of Euro, outgoing local clearing payments are made through the Temenos Transact FUNDS.TRANSFER application in the local currency. To allow transactions in EUR, the FT.BC.PARAMETER for the local clearing system should be modified.


##### Workflow

In Local Clearing, the user can perform the below activities:

This enquiry allows the user to capture reversal requests for a Clearing Transaction. After the record is committed, the authoriser can Delete or Authorise the record.

To initiate a Booking Request, follow the below steps:

1. Initiate Booking Request .
2. In the Initiate Booking Request tab, enter values in the following fields: Request Type is captured as Reverse by default. Original Txn Id Contra Txn Code Reason
3. Click the Validate icon to check for errors and overrides.
4. Click the Commit icon to submit the record.

This enquiry allows the user to authorise or delete the booking requests created through the initiate booking request screen. The user also have the options to view the booking request and original transactions by using the drilldown options.

To view a booking request, perform the following steps:

1. Authorise/Delete Booking Requests .
2. Click the View Booking Request icon of a corresponding record.
3. In the Initiate Booking Request screen, verify the record details.

To authorise a record, perform the following steps:

1. Authorise/Delete Booking Requests .
2. Click the Authorise Booking Request icon of a corresponding record.
3. In the Initiate Booking Request screen, click the Authorise icon.

To delete a record, perform the following steps:

1. Authorise/Delete Booking Requests .
2. Click the Delete Booking Request icon of a corresponding record.
3. In the Initiate Booking Request screen, click the Delete icon.

To view the Original Inward Entry , perform the following steps:

1. Authorise/Delete Booking Requests .
2. Click the View Original Txn icon of a corresponding record.
3. In the AC.INWARD.ENTRY screen, verify the record details.

This enquiry displays all the inward batch entries, which are further used to initiate the booking requests. Clearing Batch contains parent and child entries. The user have the options to view the child entries and original transactions by using the drilldown options.

To view the child entries, perform the following steps:

1. Clearing Batch Messages .
2. Click the View Child Entries icon of a corresponding record.
3. In the AC.INWARD.ENTRY screen, verify the record details.

To view the original transaction entries, perform the following steps:

1. Clearing Batch Messages .
2. Click the View Entry icon of a corresponding record.
3. In the AC.INWARD.ENTRY screen, verify the record details.

The AC.IN.SUSP.FT.ENTRY enquiry displays all the inward Funds Transfer entries to perform the local clearing and it fetches the data from AC.INWARD.ENTRY application. The user have the options, such as, View Entry, Modify FT, Delete FT and Reversal Booking Request to action the records.

To view an entry, perform the following steps:

1. Interface Transaction List .
2. Click the View Entry icon of a corresponding record.
3. In the AC.INWARD.ENTRY screen, verify the record details.

To modify a FT entry, perform the following steps:

1. Interface Transaction List .
2. Click the Modify FT icon of a corresponding record.
3. In the AC.INWARD.ENTRY screen, verify the record details.

There are no Outputs available for Local Clearing feature.

### 7.6  Misc


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *The Single European Currency (Euro) was introduced on 1 January 1999. The Euro module was introduced in Temenos Transact to support countries converting from national currency units to Euros. The Euro module is a set of additional functionality across all applications and utilities designed to suppo...*
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Available Date*, *Base CCY Rank*, *Base Ccy Rank*, *Build Fwd Rate*, *Converted Lcy*, *Fixed Ccy*, *Fixed Rate*, *Fixed Start Date* ... +3 more
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction


#### 📖 Introduction

Related topics:

- APIs
- Temenos Transact Services

The Single European Currency (Euro) was introduced on 1 January 1999. The Euro module was introduced in Temenos Transact to support countries converting from national currency units to Euros. The Euro module is a set of additional functionality across all applications and utilities designed to support the new requirements of the single currency and to provide a smooth conversion from the national currency. Although this module was designed to work with the introduction of the Single European Currency, this module supports additional functionality. For example, when there is a requirement to perform a conversion of the system base currency.

> **⚠️ Note:** Any reference to euro in this document can equally apply to any currency irrevocably fixed to another. If there is a requirement to change the base currency to a currency that is not used as the base for usual exchange quotation rates, then a slight change to the conversion will be required.

Following are the terminologies used in this document to explain the Euro conversion process:

| Term | Description |
|---|---|
| Article 235 | The council regulation (EC), which governs conversion and rounding rules for euro conversion. |
| EMU | European Monetary Union. |
| NCU | National Currency Unit – a general term for existing national currencies. |
| In-currency | A currency that is converting to EUR. |
| Out-currency | A currency that is not a member of EMU. |
| Triangulation | The process of converting one In-currency amount to another through the euro. |
| Re-denomination | Process of converting an In-currency transaction to the euro equivalent of something, which is at the fixed conversion rate. |
| Transition Phase | The phase where both NCU and EUR can be used. ERI (Euro Related Information) is added to SWIFT messages where the amount is converted from NCU to EUR. |


##### Product Configuration

The euro is a new currency that must be defined just as any other currency in Temenos Transact .

> **⚠️ Note:** Although the exchange rate between the existing ECU (code XEU) and the euro is defined as 1, the XEU must be treated as a separate currency.

The following tables should be configured to set euro as a new currency (code EUR).

Europe must be defined as a country in the COUNTRY application before the currency can be specified. There is probably already a code XE, used for the XEU. However, the euro will need its own country code (EU) to be defined.

The user can also define a Geographical Block to hold all In-countries.

The common characteristics of the euro should be defined in the CURRENCY.PARAM application. The user should set the Base Ccy Rank and a standard interest day basis should be agreed for the euro.

The CURRENCY record can now be defined for EUR. User must ensure that the correct Quotation Code is used. The Fixed Ccy , Fixed Start Date and Fixed Rate fields should not be used for the EUR currency.

The euro is defined as a currency before it is due to come into existence. However, financial movements can be generated with value date before this date (that is, 01/01/99). The Available Date field should be set to the start date of the currency. The system will generate an override message, if any entry is posted across an account with a value date prior to the Available Date.

Post this process, the euro is an existing currency and does not need an available date.

The value of Base Ccy Rank is defaulted to the value in CURRENCY.PARAM and cannot be amended directly. If a change is required, the underlying CURRENCY.PARAM record should be amended. The next amendment to the CURRENCY record will update this field.

EU should be defined in the HOLIDAY table. Settling process happens on all the day except Christmas and New Year holidays.

The PERIODIC.INTEREST table ‘01’ should be defined with the forward euro interest rates. The foreign exchange forward rates for this currency can be calculated automatically if required, by using the Build Fwd Rate field.

The user must check the BASIC.INTEREST application for existing base rates for the local currency and each of the In-currencies. A euro rate is required for each base rate used by existing contracts and accounts, which may be re-denominated in euro.

Account Conditions should be defined for each condition group that EUR accounts are expected to be opened in. Account group conditions are defined in the below applications:

- GROUP.DEBIT.INT
- GROUP.CREDIT.INT


##### Illustrating Model Parameters

This section covers the high-level parameterisation setup required to work with Single European Currency (Euro). This module helps the user to setup additional functionalities across all applications and utilities designed to support the requirements of single currency.

| S.No. | Parameters | Description |
|---|---|---|
| 1. | COUNTRY | This application allows the user to define the code EU as Euro need its own country code. In addition, Geographical Block field must be defined from the available dropdown geographies. |
| 2. | CURRENCY | This application allows the user to define the currency record for EUR. In addition, user must ensure that correct quotation code is defined. User must not define Fixed Ccy , Fixed Rate and Fixed Start Date for EUR Currency. |
| 3. | CURRENCY.PARAM | This application allows the user to define the common characteristics of Euro. In addition, Base CCY Rank must also be defined. |
| 4. | FORWARD.RATES | This application allows the user to define the premium or discount expected for the exchange rate of the Euro against the local currency when it is Out- Currency. However, if involved currency is In-Currency type, premium or discount must not be applied for the Euro. |
| 5. | HOLIDAY | This application allows the user to define the public holidays for EU, for the calendar years over which the bank's current business is spread. |
| 6. | PEIRODIC.INTEREST | This application allows the user to default the interest rate for any time period, which can be used by applications like foreign exchange on forward contracts using interest revaluation method or loans and deposits applications to perform automatic rollover. For Euro module, periodic interest must be defined with forward euro interest rates. |
| 7. | BASIC.INTEREST | This application allows the user to define floating rates – Base Rate, Prime Rate and Overnight Rate. Whenever there is a change in the rate, user must define the interest rates for the currency with the date on which it becomes active. A record must be defined for Euro with the applicable rates along with effective date. |
| 8. | EU.PARAMETER | This application allows the user to define the following: Company code – Code of the company where local currency is converted. Routine to calculate the new Euro account number. Default category for internal suspense accounts when converting contracts from one currency to fixed currency. Internal account category code to be used for posting adjustment entries in the new local currency after the conversion of the base currency has taken place. Transaction code used for all adjustment entries posted by the conversion process. The rate used to convert local currency amounts from Original Lcy to Converted Lcy . |
| 9. | PM.CALENDAR | This application allows the user to define a calendar in which possible settlements is allowed for Euro. |

### 7.7  Quotation of Rate Involving Euro


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *The user should understand the rules that apply when quoting exchange rates involving the euro for the In-currencies and the likely market convention to be applied when quoting Out-currencies against the euro.*
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Base Ccy Rank*, *Base Ccy Rank,*, *Quotation Code*
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

The user should understand the rules that apply when quoting exchange rates involving the euro for the In-currencies and the likely market convention to be applied when quoting Out-currencies against the euro.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

This is covered as part of module configuration. There is no specific configuration for this feature.


#### 🔧 Working With

The Temenos Transact CURRENCY application continues to express exchange rates against the system local currency. If the local currency is ‘In’, there may no longer be a market rate quoted for the local currency against out currencies after the Euro starts; a euro rate is quoted instead. To update the CURRENCY application in this scenario, the rates should be derived from the quoted Euro rate.


##### In-Currencies

All In-currencies are quoted as ‘1’ Euro to ‘n’ NCU. This might result in an exchange rate of less than 1.


##### Out-Currencies

Although there is no definitive ruling, it is expected that market practice also follows the ‘1’ euro to ‘n’ NCU quotation method. In the UK, this is expected to be the practice, which does not follow the standard UK quotation method (1GBP: n Fcy).


##### Quotation Code

When defining the EUR currency, the user must ensure that the Quotation Code is correctly defined in order to follow the recommended practice.

- If EUR is not the local currency, the quotation code should be ‘0’.
- If EUR is the local currency, quotation code for other currencies must be null.


##### Base Currency Rank

The usual rule for defaulting the base currency of a deal is to use the currency that yields a rate greater than 1. From the rules for quoting euro rates, this may not be the case for certain currencies against the euro (for example, GBP), where the current rule would result in an inverse rate being defaulted. Base Ccy Rank parameter is used to resolve this. The correct setting of this value can be used to force a currency to be the base currency instead of the usual rule, where the currency that yields a rate greater than 1 is used. A value in the range 1 to 99 can be specified. Whenever the system attempts to default the base currency, this value is tested. If a value is present, that currency is the default base currency. If both currencies have a value, the currency with the lowest value is the default base.

If the euro is not the local currency, it is important to set this value for the EUR currency to ensure that euro is taken as the default. It is recommended that a value greater than 1 (for example, 5) is used to allow for additional currencies, which should be the base when dealing with the euro. If EUR is the local currency, or the system has been converted to euro, the user needs to set the Base Ccy Rank, where there are existing exchange rates quoted less than 1 involving the local currency (for example, IEP or GBP). In this case, the rank should additionally be set for the old local currency. The most likely requirement is to enforce the sequence of EUR, GBP and USD. This could be done by setting the values as follows:

| Currency | Base Rank |
|---|---|
| EUR | 5 |
| GBP | 10 |
| USD | 15 |

Refer to the Help text in CURRENCY and CURRENCY.PARAM for further details and examples.


#### 📋 Tasks

There are no Tasks available for Quotation of Rate Involving Euro feature.


#### 📊 Outputs

There are no Outputs available for Quotation of Rate Involving Euro feature.

### 7.8  Redenoim Accounts


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *The account currency conversion converts many files. The ACCOUNT.FILE.STATS process should be run and the results should be analysed before the conversion preparation. Any poorly sized files should be resized as they can adversely affect the performance of the conversion.*
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Ac Txn Code*, *Auto Close Acct*, *Auto Closure Date*, *Auto Pay Acct*, *Bal Transfer Type*, *Charge Types*, *Comm Types*, *Convert Sto* ... +8 more
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction


##### Preparation of Data

The account currency conversion converts many files. The ACCOUNT.FILE.STATS process should be run and the results should be analysed before the conversion preparation. Any poorly sized files should be resized as they can adversely affect the performance of the conversion.


#### ⚙️ Configuration


##### Timing of conversion

The conversion can be run as soon as the fixed rates apply. The conversion process can be run in the following scenarios:

- If the Batch Stage is COB – The conversion can be run during the batch, if the BATCH.STAGE is SXXX (system wide), after all the standard COB processing, just before the reports are processed. When accounts should to be re-denominated to another currency the actual processing takes place in the system wide stage of the COB. Thus, in the balance sheet the amounts are shown under the new currency. The Conversion of the contracts take place online, but the accounts used in the contracts should have been converted already. Under this set up, the accounts have to be converted on a different day to the contracts.
- If the BATCH.STAGE is Start of Day – The conversion can be run during the batch if the BATCH.STAGE is DXXX. This allows the contracts to be converted online during that day and thus both the accounts and contracts can be shown in the balance sheet under the new currency.

This decision is made by the bank to decide at which stage of the processing during the batch, that they require the accounts to be converted.

> **⚠️ Note:** Once the conversion process has begun and an account has been converted, it is not possible to switch between the two options.


##### Batch Process

In a multi-company environment, the BATCH record EU.ACCT.CONVERSION is run for each financial level company. All the jobs in the batch are set with the frequency as ‘A’ – Adhoc, as shown in the screen below:

- The Next Run Date of the jobs in the batch must be set to the conversion date, so the jobs are executed on the respective conversion date.
- The job EU.ACCT.CCY.CONVERT enables the multi-threading of account conversions
- The job AC.HVT.MERGE should be run to handle the merging of transactions for the HVT accounts before conversion. This job must be added, if not already available in the BATCH for EU.ACCT.CONVERSION and SOD.EU.ACCT.CONVERSION batch records. The default frequency is ‘A’ - Adhoc and the user must configure the Next Run Date of the batch records to the conversion date.
- The job EU.CONV.PARAM.FILES improves the performance of the conversion processing. It must be added, if not already available in the BATCH for EU.ACCT.CONVERSION and SOD.EU.ACCT.CONVERSION batch records, after the job EU.ACCT.CCY.CONVERT with frequency as A (Ad-hoc) and Next Run Date as conversion date.

The AC.HVT.MERGE job must be added as the first job with frequency as ‘A’ – Adhoc, in the BATCH for EU.BASE.CONV.REPORTING record, as shown below:


##### Report

The BATCH job EU.ACCT.CONVERSION is configured to produce a report ( EU.AC.CCY.CONV.FAILED enquiry) after the conversion process. The report is a list of all failed account conversions. The following screenshot shows the Failed Account Conversion enquiry.


#### 🔧 Working With


##### Conditions Verified Prior to Conversion

The following criteria are verified prior to conversion, for all types of accounts:

- The account cannot have Auto Pay Acct set to pass accounting entries to another account.
- The Currency of the account must be one of the In-currencies . Note: This is denoted by a Fixed Rate field defined in the CURRENCY record for the existing currency of the account.
- Interest and charge conditions must be defined from the start of the current capitalisation period of the EUR currency.
- The account cannot be a Passbook account. Passbook accounts must be opened under a new key for EUR.
- The new renumbered account number must be valid and consistent with the existing old account number. Hence, internal accounts must follow internal account number formats and for external accounts, the INTERCO.PARAMETER application must be cross-checked if it exists.
- The Bal Transfer Type field must be of type beginning with AC.
- Posting Restrict must be in the range 90-99 for account closure.
- No unauthorised AC.PENDING records should exist for the account.
- The account cannot be set for Nostro Reconciliation.
- If the account is set for closure after the conversion, the following checks are verified: If the account is not an Interest Liquidation Account. If the account is not an Interest Compensation Account. If the account does not have any Direct Debit Mandates. If the account is not a part of securities portfolio.


##### Preparation of Accounts

To prepare accounts to be converted on a specific date, a conversion request must be recorded in the AC.CCY.CONVERSION application. This following details are included in the application:

- The account number to be used for the In-currency account when it is renumbered ( Renumber Ac No ).
- Whether the renumbered account should be closed ( Auto Close Acct ).
- If closure is required, the date of closure (default next interest payment) and posting restriction code to be used ( Auto Closure Date and Posting Restrict ).
- Whether the mnemonic for the account is to stay with the converted EUR account or with the renumbered In-currency account ( Keep Mnemonic ).
- The type of AC funds transfer to be used to transfer the balance between the In-currency and EUR account ( Bal Transfer Type ).
- Whether the standing orders are to be converted to the EUR ccy account or to be renumbered to the new account number ( Convert Sto ).

Before the conversion request can be entered, a structure for allocating a new account number for the national currency account must be decided. This account number does not have to meet the existing CHECKDIGIT (number of characters) requirements, so a simple structure can be followed, such as, replacing the leading ‘0’ of the number with a 9 or adding a ‘1’ to the number. EU.AC.NEXT.ID renumbering subroutine is available with this module for adding ‘1’ to the existing number.

In case of multi-company installations, the INTERCO.PARAMETER record should be adjusted to include the new range of numbers as valid for each company, if the above first structure is followed. For example, if accounts beginning ‘001’ are valid for company A, this should now additionally allow accounts beginning ‘901’.

Individual records may be entered in this application for an account, or may be created automatically through the bulk conversion EU.CCY.CONVERSION application. This application allows a selection criteria to be specified (that is, all accounts in DEM for a particular customer), with a general set of conversion conditions. When ‘verified’, this application should create individual AC.CCY.CONVERSION records for accounts.


##### Redenomination of Accounts Using Bulk Conversion Utility

The EU.CCY.CONVERSION application is a utility used to perform multiple contract and account conversions to EUR. The options specified are used to create AC.CCY.CONVERSION records for each account to be converted and similarly to create EU.CONTRACT.CONVERSION records for contracts, as explained in the Redenomination of Contracts section.

This utility provides the ability to convert accounts dependent upon user defined selection criteria. A selection can be entered for the ACCOUNT application (for example, customer, currency, and category), which also includes the following information:

- Renumber routine, the routine to return the account number to be used for the national currency account
- Keep mnemonic
- Convert standing orders
- Automatic closure required
- Conversion date
- Type of funds transfer required to perform balance transfer

In the following screenshot, once the record has been verified, the bulk utility selects all accounts denominated in DEM currency and sets them for re-denomination into EUR. This is achieved by creating a record in AC.CCY.CONVERSION for each account selected therefore preparing the account for conversion. In essence, the bulk utility enables the creation of AC.CCY.CONVERSION records without the user having to enter each one individually.


##### Account Conversion and Cash Pooling

Cash pooling operates on a single currency basis; whether foreign or local, all the accounts in a group must be in the same currency. When one of the accounts in the group is subject to an account conversion to change the account to EUR currency (and at the same time renumbering the original account) this can complicate the cash pooling operation.

To prevent any cross-currency complications of having mixed currencies in a group, which has values, based on the group currency it is essential that the integrity of the group be maintained.

As part of the EU conversion, any client who has cash pooling records in the currency being converted to EUR should activate the BATCH record EU.ACCP.GROUP.PARAM and set the run date to the current date.

EU conversion of cash pooling is closely tied to the account conversion process. After the account is converted, the cash pool COB procedures verifies whether the account is part of a cash pool group. If it is, the group may be flagged as inactive as a precaution. This is done by setting the Eucc Process field value to Yes. This prevents any records in the group being modified and excludes the group from the cash pool processing until it is made active again. The following example screen shot shows a Cash Pooling blocked for a partially converted group.

Once all the accounts in the group are converted the cashpool records ( AC.CASH.POOL ), which have been placed on hold, can be amended (for example, to use more logical rounded Euro amounts, rather than the unrounded exact equivalents) and authorised for the cash pool processing for the group can resume.

Certain sweeps are configured to make sweep during the COB and return the funds the next morning.

All surplus funds on a current account are swept up to a savings account each night to attract interest, but the balance is returned the next morning to provide a working balance. In this scenario, the return of the funds is redirected to the new EUR account.


##### Conversion of Accounts with Sub-Accounts

There is no automatic process for the conversion of master accounts with sub-accounts. In order to convert these accounts, follow the below manual process:

1. Remove the link between the master account and the sub account. In the ACCOUNT record of the sub account, the value in the Master Account field must be removed. In the ACCOUNT record for the master account, the value in the Max Sub Account field must be removed.
2. After the transaction is completed, transfer the balance of the sub account to the master account to ensure the balance of the sub account is zero.
3. Set up an ACCOUNT.CLOSURE record for the sub account, this can either be set to close online or in the COB.
4. Create an AC.CCY.CONVERSION record for the master account and convert the account by following the normal account conversion process.
5. Once the Master account is converted to the new currency, edit the ACCOUNT record and populate the Max Sub Account field. This will allow the system to generate new sub accounts under the new currency when required.


##### Conversion Process

When an account is converted automatically, the account number is maintained and the account is converted to EUR. The original account in the national currency is renumbered as stated in the AC.CCY.CONVERSION record, thereby ensuring that the full history is maintained. The Original Acct and Auto Pay Acct fields in the ACCOUNT records maintain a link between the two accounts.

The conversion of the account balance to EUR from the existing currency is performed by the automatic creation of a funds transfer between the fields original account, and the existing (now EUR) account number. A special account transfer transaction type can be created for the account, which allows the creation of a specific advice, and charges to be taken if required using standard functionality. This is retrieved from the Bal Transfer Type field in the AC.CCY.CONVERSION record.

However, if the company does not have the Funds Transfer module installed, the accounting entries are created to transfer the funds from the renumbered original account to the existing (now EUR) account. A special account transfer transaction type can be created and set in Ac Txn Code in the relevant company record (in EU.PARAMETER ), to be used for any accounting entries that are raised during the transfer of balance.

Temenos Transact does not generally allow accounts of a different currency to be used for settlement of contracts denominated in another currency. Conversion of existing accounts to EUR may create situations where this arises. Since the original account will be renumbered and will remain in contract currency when the account is converted, contracts using the account for settlement are also converted so that the settlement account is the renumbered account.

If required, a charge can be levied for converting an account to EUR. This is controlled by the FUNDS. TRANSFER application, which is used to perform the transfer between the national currency account and the EUR account created by the conversion process. An account conversion charge can be defined in either FT.COMMISSION.TYPE or FT.CHARGE.TYPE applications and subsequently specified in Comm Types or Charge Types fields in the FT.TXN.TYPE.CONDITION record used for the transfer. New transaction codes can also be created for the Euro conversion, which should then be specified in the FT.TXN.TYPE.CONDITION record.


#### 📋 Tasks

There are no Tasks available for Redenomination of Accounts feature.


#### 📊 Outputs

There are no Outputs available for Redenomination of Accounts feature.
