#### 📖 Introduction

After the fixing of currency exchange rates it may be necessary to convert any contracts, which have a maturity beyond the end of the life of the NCU.

In Temenos Transact , the following modules are supported for contract conversion subject to certain restrictions:

- LD Loans and Deposits
- MM Money Markets
- MG Mortgages
- SW Interest Rate Swaps

To achieve conversion we essentially early mature the NCU contract to suspense, and raise a new contract in EUR through the following process:

- General set-up for contract conversion
- Set the conversion conditions for the contract either individually or through the bulk utility
- Input to the contract using the appropriate version. This sets the NCU contract to early mature, and raises the new EUR contract in HLD status
- Authorise the early maturity of the NCU contract
- Input/Authorise the new EUR contract
- Resolve any created Funds Transfer (under certain circumstances FTs are raised to handle contract events)


##### ConfigureEB.API

Ensure that the EB.API file contains details of the following records for contract conversion:

- EU.LD.CREATE.UNAUTH.DEAL
- EU.MG.CREATE.UNAUTH.DEAL
- EU.MM.CREATE.UNAUTH.DEAL
- EU.SW.CREATE.UNAUTH.DEAL

record for contract conversion.


##### Suspense Account

Although it can be changed at the group or individual contract level, it is necessary to set-up a default suspense category and accounts for the balance transfer.

A new category for the suspense accounts used in the contract conversion process should be created. This should be a standard internal account category in the range 10000 to 19999.

Contract Conversion Suspense Category:

This default category should be entered on the EU.PARAMETER record.

The above example shows the contract conversion suspense account in EU.PARAMETER . A Euro suspense account should be opened for the category created earlier. The last four digits should be 0001.

The following screenshot shows the contract conversion suspense account.

Similar accounts should be opened for each of the In-Currencies where conversions take place. There are two accounting options for these accounts:

Auto Pay:

If the Auto Pay Acct for each In-Currency account is defined as the EUR suspense account, then all entries raised from the conversion process wash through the same account; the net result being zero balance.

Manual:

If the auto pay is not set, then the total value of the early matured contracts of the National Currency Unit (NCU) is held in each of the NCU suspense accounts, and the total value of the new EUR contracts is held in the EUR suspense accounts. This option is required if a check on these totals is necessary. The amounts can then be transferred manually to net off the balances as required.

The following screenshot shows the In-currency contract conversion account using auto- pay.

If different suspense categories and accounts are required for different contract types or for the suspension of interest where conversion takes place on a non-interest date, these should be set-up in a similar manner. However, they do not require specification on the EU.PARAMETER record. The following screenshot shows the category for suspension of accrued interest.

The following screenshot shows the EUR account for LD Interest Suspense.

The following is an example of an In-currency account for LD Interest Suspense.


##### Creating DummyLIMIT.REFERENCE

As a result of the process of early maturing the NCU contract and opening a new EUR contract, there is a time where both contracts affect the limits system. To avoid the double exposure on the limit, the maturing NCU contract is moved from the customer limit to a dummy limit under a separate Limit Reference. The new EUR contract uses the original limit and Limit Reference.

> **⚠️ Note:** This process is different for LD Commitments and their drawdowns; refer to the relevant user guide section for more information.

A minimum of one LIMIT.REFERENCE should be created. This should be a non-reducing type and does not require overrides, specified by defining the Default Check field as No.

The following screenshot shows a dummy LIMIT.REFERENCE for contract conversion.

The Limit Reference should be added to the LIMIT.PARAMETER application as an additional Product No for each application (example, LD.LOANS.AND.DEPOSITS , SWAP , MM.MONEY.MARKET and MG.MORTGAGE ) where conversion takes place, and for each set of decision fields relating to contract conditions for contracts due to be converted.

When the contracts are converted, the necessary dummy LIMIT records are automatically created.


##### Bulk Conversion Utility –EU.CCY.CONVERSION

The settings for conversion of contracts is held in the EU.CONTRACT.CONVERSION file, where each record is keyed by the individual contract ID. A bulk conversion utility, EU.CCY.CONVERSION , assists in the creation of these records, where sizeable volumes of contracts are converted under the same conditions.

The utility allows the user to make selections from the contract files, based on any criteria on those files, and set the conversion conditions. When the record is verified, the related EU.CONTRACT.CONVERSION records are created. If there are no errors or overrides, the records are created fully authorised, otherwise they are created in HLD (hold) status to allow the user to correct the settings prior to conversion.

> **⚠️ Note:** This utility and the EU.CONTRACT.CONVERSION do not execute the contract conversion, they just set the parameters.

This utility is also used for bulk selection of accounts for conversion, but the fields in terms of contract conversion are as follows:

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| Id | The file has a free format key. |
| Application | Set to the appropriate application for the desired conversion: ACCOUNT LD.LOANS.AND.DEPOSITS MG.MORTGAGE MM.MONEY.MARKET SWAP |
| Select Field; Operand; Value | These fields specify the conditions of the contracts (or accounts), which are to be converted using the parameters of this record. The Select Field must be from the above application. |
| New Ccy | The currency for the new contract, that is, EUR. |
| Renumber Routine | Only used for account conversion. |
| Conversion Date | This field is optional for contracts. If entered, this date will be passed to the Conversion Date field in the created EU.CONTRACT.CONVERSION records. If not input, Conversion Date will be defaulted to the next interest schedule date, unless the Non Int Conv flag is set, in which case, the field will be defaulted to the current day. |
| Auto Clos Ac; Ac Post Restrict; Keep Mnemonic; Bal Transfer Type; Convert Sto | Only used for account conversion. |
| Ncu Limit Ref | The dummy LIMIT.REFERENCE record to be used on the maturing NCU contracts to avoid double exposure on the customer limit. Loans under commitment use different functionality in this regard, explained in the relevant section of this User Guide. |
| Ncu Susp Cat | The suspense category to be used for the early maturity of the NCU contract and the creation of the new EUR contract. This can be different from the setting in EU.PARAMETER , if required. |
| Ac Transfer Type; Ot Transfer Type | The internal and external FT.TXN.TYPE.CONDITION record to be used for any Funds Transfers that are created to account for principal schedules taking place on the conversion date. |
| Auth Records; Hold; Records; Ignored Records; Error Details | These system fields hold the results produced when this record is verified. They note the number of records that have been fully created, placed on hold due to override or error conditions, and have been ignored (if a EU.CONTRACT.CONVERSION record already exists for the contract), and any associated error messages. |
| Non Int Conv | If this flag is set to Yes, then contracts converted under this selection can be converted on a non-interest settlement date. Currently, this flag can only be set for LDs and MMs. |
| Int Transfer Type | The FT.TXN.TYPE.CONDITION record for the future dated FT created to post the suspended interest, if the Conversion Date is not an interest settlement date. |
| Int Susp Cat | The category of the suspense account to be used for the suspension of interest, if the Conversion Date is not an interest settlement date. |
| Local Ref | Standard system local reference field. |

The following screenshot shows Bulk Conversion of all CHF loans with category 21051.


##### Contract Conversion Settings –EU.CONTRACT.CONVERSION

The EU.CONTRACT.CONVERSION record holds all the settings for the conversion of an individual contract, and records the results of the conversion for any post-conversion reconciliation and checking.

> **⚠️ Note:** It does not execute the conversion itself.

It can be input directly for an individual contract or created through the EU.CCY.CONVERSION utility.

The fields are as follows:

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| Id | The transaction reference number of the contract to be converted. |
| Application | System Field holding the application of the contract to be converted. |
| Conversion Date | The value date at which the NCU contract is matured, and the new EUR contract starts. The Conversion Date defaults to the next interest settlement date, unless the Non Int Conv flag has been set to Yes, either from the EU.CCY.CONVERSION record or by using a version to pre-populate it, in which case the Conversion Date defaults to the current day. If the Non Int Conv flag on this record is set to Yes through direct user input, the Conversion Date is not automatically updated from its initial default value, but can be updated manually. |
| Old Ccy | No input field, recording the NCU currency. |
| New Ccy | Automatically populated with the fixed currency (that is, EUR). |
| Old Limit Ref | System Field recording the original LIMIT.REFERENCE record from the NCU contract. This will then be used on the new EUR contract. |
| New Limit Ref | The maturing NCU contract is updated to use this limit reference, so this should contain the dummy LIMIT.REFERENCE record. Loans under commitment use different functionality in this regard, which is explained in the relevant section of this user guide. |
| Bal Susp Cat | The suspense category to be used for the early maturity of the NCU contract and the creation of the new EUR contract. This defaults from the Ncu Susp Cat field. This record is created from EU.CCY.CONVERSION or from Cont Conv Susp Cat in EU.PARAMETER , but it can be updated to an alternative valid category, if required. |
| New Contract | After a conversion has been run, this system field is updated with the transaction id of the new EUR contract. |
| Actual Conv Date | This System Field records when the conversion was executed. The conversion takes place on an interest date, which can be before the Conversion Date (value date). |
| Original Amount | This System Field records the principal of the NCU contract prior to conversion. |
| Converted Amt | This System Field records the principal of the new EUR contract. If there has been a principal payment on the conversion date, then this will not be the EUR equivalent of the Original Amount . |
| Ac Transfer Type; Ot Transfer Type | The internal and external FT.TXN.TYPE.CONDITION record that is to be used for any funds transfers that are created to account for principal schedules taking place on the conversion date. |
| Repayment Ft; Repayment Amount | The ID and amount of any funds transfer raised to account for a principal schedule taking pace on conversion date. |
| Error Msg | This field holds any error message encountered during the creation of this record from EU.CCY.CONVERSION , or during the execution of the conversion. |
| Local Ref | Standard system local reference field. |
| Commit No |  |
| Drawdown Amt | This field holds the principal of the drawdown in the currency of the commitment when an LD drawdown under commitment is converted. |
| Non Int Conv | If this flag is set to yes, then Conversion Date can be set to any working day, not just the next interest settlement date. Currently, this flag can only be set for LDs and MMs. |
| Int Transfer Type | The FT.TXN.TYPE.CONDITION record for the future dated FT created to post the suspended interest, if the Conversion Date is not an interest settlement date. |
| Int Susp Cat | The Category of the suspense account to be used for the suspension of interest, if the Conversion Date is not an interest settlement date. |
| Interest Ft; Interest Amt; Int Value Date | These are system fields updated with the ID, amount and value date of the funds transfer created to post the suspended interest, if the Conversion Date is not an interest settlement date. |


##### Timing of Conversion

In Temenos Transact , contract conversion can take place at any time after the rate fixing date and is independent of both the local currency conversion and account conversion processes, although it is preferable to convert contracts after customer accounts, so that the customer EUR accounts default onto the new EUR contracts.

The preparation of the EU.CONTRACT.CONVERSION records can take place prior to the conversion date. This is recommended for any sites where all the Euro conversions are due to take place over a short space of time.

For contracts, which are converting on an interest settlement date, it is possible to run the conversion prior to the Conversion Date (value date for maturity of NCU contract and start of EUR contract). However, it is advisable to keep the gap between the run date and the conversion date as short as possible, as any subsequently entered information or events against the NCU contract is not automatically reflected in the EUR contract. The conversion must be run on the Conversion Date if the contract is being converted on a non-interest settlement date.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

This is covered as part of module configuration. There is no specific configuration for this feature.


#### 🔧 Working With

This section explains the working of Redenomination of Contracts.


##### Euro and Derivatives

The Euro conversion of derivatives should be regarded as two separate processes:

- Firstly, the closing and cash settling of all open DX.TRADE .
- Secondly, the conversion of all related reporting and static data records.

The closing and cash settling of all open DX.TRADE can be performed online or as part of close of business (COB). However, the conversion of all related static data can only be performed within the COB.

Cash settlement for the purpose of this functionality has been defined as:

- For futures contracts, the effective realisation of any profit and loss due to involved parties.
- For options contracts, the payment of any outstanding option premium.

Conversion does not occur to individual transactions where any of the following conditions exist:

- Unauthorised Deals
- Unauthorised Closeouts
- Diary Events Pending
- Open Orders
- Partially Filled Orders
- Unauthorised Orders
- Unauthorised records in any DX application
- Partial Closeout

The EU.DX.CONVERT.CCY COB process has been created in batch and is run daily to convert derivatives contracts and customers as per settings in the DX.EU.PARAMETER application.

The dates, on which particular exchanges need to be converted, along with the conversion date for the customer reporting currency are set up in the new DX.EU.PARAMETER application. The Psn Cnv Date , Psn Cnv Ccy and Psn Cus Exch related fields correspond to derivatives contract conversion, and the Cus Cnv Date and Cus Cnv Ccy related fields correspond to the customer reporting currency conversion.

> **⚠️ Note:** For both sets of fields, more than one currency can be specified for each run date.

However, it should be noted that by utilising this methodology, ALL contracts registered against the selected exchanges are converted and any associated open DX.TRADE cash settled unless the user exempts the contract from conversion by setting Settlement Allowed to No in the relevant DX.CONTRACT.MASTER record.

If it is required that only particular trades that relate to the same contract are converted, and not all trades, then the user needs to select specific trades for conversion by utilising the online enquiries provided (see later). User must ensure that trades that are NOT to be converted are not subsequently captured by the COB conversion.

The following screenshot shows DX.EU.PARAMETER with input fields.

Any derivatives contracts where either or both the Currency and Delivery Currency are in the converting, currency is made inactive by setting the Last Valid Date to the conversion date. Subsequent to performing the conversion, it is no longer possible to enter into any new transaction in the converted contracts.

The following screenshot shows DX.CONTRACT.MASTER record prior to conversion:

However, where new contract definitions are required, which are based on existing terminated contracts (for example, where an exchange provides a newly denominated equivalent contract to aid the conversion process), the user can copy the DX.CONTRACT.MASTER record of the originating contract definition and substitute new field definitions where required ,for example, Currency . Any DX.CUSTOMER records where the Reporting Ccy is in the converting, currency is converted so that the Reporting Ccy becomes the new currency.

The following screenshot shows the DX.CUSTOMER record prior to conversion:

All deals held in, or delivering into the conversion currency, should be cash settled prior to the Euro conversion date.

Having run the converting COB, all transactions meeting the selection have their status marked as CLOSED, the corresponding DX.REP.POSITION records are reversed, future profits and losses realised and/or outstanding option premiums paid and updates passed to all other relevant DX records.

Users may prefer to individually select transactions to settle. To enable this, the Derivatives Positions to Close and Euro Mature Transactions enquiries can be used to identify and perform the cash settlement of individual transactions online, where either the delivery currency or the trade currency is the same as the local currency that is to be converted. It should be remembered that if this method is utilised, it is necessary to settle both sides of a transaction uniquely, that is, this is NOT a back-to-back process.

> **⚠️ Note:** From the above screenshots both sides of the position can be seen separately and have to be settled individually.

The user can select View Transaction from the results of the Derivatives Positions to close enquiry. This launches the Euro Mature Transactions enquiry, which in turn displays the individual DX.TRADE that compose the position and from here the user can select Mature, which allows the user to settle the transaction. The following screenshot shows the Euro Mature Transactions enquiry.

The following screenshot shows setting a Future Trade to settle after selecting ‘Mature’ in Euro Mature Transactions enquiry:

It is envisaged that this is not always a preferred method to convert trades when there are a large number of transactions involved. Where only particular trades that relate to the same contract are converted is required and not all trades for a given contract, then the user needs to use this method to select specific trades for conversion. User must ensure that the trades that are not to be converted are not subsequently captured by the COB conversion.

Having matured both sides of the selected transactions and their status marked as CLOSED, the corresponding DX.REP.POSITION records are reversed, future profits and losses realised and/or outstanding option premiums paid.

It should be remembered that the online process does not perform any changes to the static data held in the DX.CONTRACT . MASTER or DX.CUSTOMER files. These conversions occur only when a subsequent related COB is run where the DX.EU.PARAMETER record is configured to do so.

Following the Euro Conversion Date (ECD), the account balances for the converted accounts are maintained in EUR, and recorded in the Asset Management (AM) Valuation and Performance files.

Historic valuation and performance data continue to have the old currency accounts. For example, if a DEM account is converted to EUR, the historic valuation and performance in the tables AM.VEH.MM, AM.INST.VEH.MM and AM.INST.PERF.DETAIL continue to hold DEM account balances.

The procedure for converting accounts is described in the Redenomination of Accounts section in this document.

The following example illustrates the effect of an account conversion on AM Valuations. The EU.CONVERSION.PARAM record AM.VALUATION.ACCOUNT should be recorded in EU.CONVERSION.PROCESS.

The following screenshots display the EU.CONVERSION.PROCESS .

The valuation for Portfolio 1006-1 (Account no. 21733) prior to conversion is as follows.

Account 21733 is set to be converted to EUR.

After the account has been converted, the valuation for 12/6/03 is recorded in DEM, under the renumbered account number. The valuation after the account conversion is recorded in EUR under the pre-existing account number. The following screenshot shows the AM Historic Valuation enquiry.


##### Euro and Securities

- Changing the Reference Currency of Portfolios – SC Application
- Group Specification of Reference Currency Change
- Changing the Reference Currency of Portfolios – AM Applications
- Automated Creation of New Securities
- Re-denomination of Securities – Both SC and AM applications

Temenos Transact allows the reference currency of a portfolio to be changed to a different currency, where a fixed rate exists between the two currencies. That is, the currency can only be changed to the currency identified in the Fixed Ccy field of the currency record of the initial reference currency. The change to the reference currency will be facilitated by the addition of a new field that allows the new reference currency to be entered. As the ‘no compulsion – no prohibition’ principle applies, individual portfolios will be re-denominated at different times during the transition period. However, towards the end of the transition period, it will be necessary to convert any remaining portfolios in one go. Therefore, in addition to manual input in the new reference currency field, a conversion record will be required to select portfolios and add the new reference currency to a group of portfolios (selected by current reference currency for example).

When the portfolio reference currency is changed, there will still be a requirement to reprint historical valuation reports in the original portfolio reference currency. Therefore, the original reference currency will be stored. Also, as the historical values of the portfolio are required, the historical valuation totals, contributions, withdrawals and invested capital amounts need to be recorded in the original reference currency as well as the converted values in the new reference currency. New fields are added to store the values in the original reference currency with the existing fields for contributions, withdrawals and so on containing amounts that have been converted at the fixed exchange rate to the new reference currency (that is, the Euro).

The details of individual items for historical portfolio reports are held internally in Temenos Transact in twelve files – SC.CASH.FLOW01, SC.CASH.FLOW02, and SC.CASH.FLOW12 (where the number at the end signifies the month number). These files will not be converted to the new reference currency, but instead will be populated with new historical data over the year following the conversion of the reference currency, thus facilitating the production of historical valuation reports.

As the value of a portfolio can be re-calculated online, the portfolio can be valued in the new reference currency, immediately when the conversion takes place. However, in addition to the portfolio data, Temenos Transact uses the reference currency of the portfolio to calculate the cost of position. The cost of a security position is held in the SECURITY.POSITION table. The individual security movements that gave rise to that position are contained in the SECURITY.TRANS table. Both these tables contain a cost amount in the portfolio reference currency, where the SECURITY.POSITION figure is calculated from the figure contained in SECURITY.TRANS .

Therefore, as part of the process of converting the portfolio reference currency, Temenos Transact needs to convert the cost amounts to the new reference currency on all the individual SECURITY.TRANS records and then rebuild the SECURITY.POSITION figure from them using the recalculation of cost of position functionality in Temenos Transact . If the SECURITY.TRANS records are converted and the SECURITY.POSITION record rebuilt, this will eliminate the possibility of rounding errors between the SECURITY.POSITION record and the total of the SECURITY.TRANS records.

The conversion of the reference currency takes place during the COB. It will be done by the EOD.SC.CONV.REF.CCY process that normally runs in the application COB. It is suggested that a portfolio be converted to Euro immediately after the production of a portfolio valuation report that has been sent to the customer informing them of the change. This program will use a list of portfolios that have been flagged to change the reference currency and process each portfolio in turn.

First it will copy across all the historical figures in the SEC.ACC.MASTER record, then converts all the SECURITY.TRANS records for that portfolio and rebuilds the cost of position in the Reference Currency on each SECURITY.POSITION record of that portfolio. Once this is done, the SC.FUND.FLOW table will be converted (which contains details of all contributions and withdrawals for the portfolio) and the contributions and withdrawals figures on the SEC.ACC.MASTER record will be recalculated. The other total figures on the SEC.ACC.MASTER file will be converted at the fixed rate and finally the current value of the portfolio is recalculated using the online portfolio revaluation that already exists in Temenos Transact .

The following screenshot shows a SEC.ACC.MASTER record for which a request is made to change the reference currency to EUR.

> **⚠️ Note:** The Reference Currency field is set to ITL in this screenshot.

The above screenshot is an example of a Portfolio before conversion.

> **⚠️ Note:** The New Reference Ccy field has been set to EUR on this screen with an effective date of 01 JAN 1999 set in the New Rfccy Eff Date field.

The following screenshot shows the SEC.ACC.MASTER record after conversion of the reference currency.

> **⚠️ Note:** The Reference Currency field for this portfolio has been changed to EUR and the Old Reference Ccy field has been set to ITL.

The SC.ACC.MASTER.CONV utility program can be used to define a new reference currency for a group of portfolio IDs linked by a logical relationship. There are fields in the file that can be used to specify the logical relationship. The application works out a list of portfolios that have been selected as a result of the relationship. These portfolios are converted in the COB processing by the EOD.SC.CONV.REF.CCY program EOD.SC.CONV.REF.CCY that runs in the SC.BATCH.APP batch suite.

An example of this is shown in the screenshot that follows.

> **⚠️ Note:** It is assumed that the system has been prepared in advance to enable the completion of the above processes. If not, refer to Configuring the System ready for the Conversion in this document.

Changing the reference currency of individual portfolio (SEC.ACC.MASTER) records is done exactly the same way as in the SC application instructions in the previous section. This is performed by updating both the New Rfccy Eff Date and New Reference Ccy fields with the effective date of the change to the currency specified.

EU.SC.CONVERT BATCH job includes an additional trigger to update the portfolio details for the SEC.ACC.MASTER records undergoing reference currency conversion in a Temenos Transact internal concat file, AM.CONV.SAM.REF.CCY.

In addition, additional processing is required to trigger the conversion of reference currency amounts that exist in various AM tables that are used in enquiries and reporting.

These are AM tables:

- AM.VEH (Historic Portfolio Valuation)
- AM.INST.VEH (Instrument Valuation)
- AM.INST.PERF.DETAIL (Instrument Performance)

Before performing COB, the AM.PARAMETER application should have the Conv Hist Val field set to Y to indicate that historical valuation data should undergo conversion to the new reference currency, where appropriate.

Just like in the SC application, the running of a COB performs the necessary updates.

After the COB, various enquiries can be checked to ensure the integrity of the newly reported EUR reference currency.

The changing of the reference currency affects certain enquiries and reports that detail the current reference currency equivalents.

The following extracts show a number of example enquiries after the setting of the change of reference currency.

It is possible to create SECURITY.MASTER records from feeds at some Temenos Transact sites. However, a utility is required to select the SECURITY.MASTER records and copy them to new Euro denominated securities.

The SEC.MASTER.CONV application allows users to select the SECURITY.MASTER application (using any field in the SECURITY.MASTER and STANDARD.SELECTION record).

The usage of this application has been described in the Re-denomination Process Guidelines section.


##### Realisation of In-currency Forex Profit and Loss

At the start of the transition period, the exchange rate between member currencies are irrevocably fixed. As a result, the profit or loss due on deals involving two in-currencies can be realised immediately. According to national convention, it may be required to realise this figure in the year balance sheet for the year end, immediately prior to the start of the transition period (that is, the end of 1998).

In Temenos Transact , the facility to realise the profit and loss due is available on an individual contract basis, depending on the type and use of contract.

The REVALUATION.PARAMETER table allows Profit and Loss (P&L) category codes to be defined for each product, for use when P&L is to be realised immediately. Internal account category codes can also be specified for posting exchange adjustment entries for realised Profit and Loss.

The following screen shot shows the REVALUATION.PARAMETER table.

Fixed profit and loss categories should be specified for the Application Id of FX, FX.SP and FX.RB.

The Realise Fix Pl field in the FOREX application is used to denote whether or not the profit or loss should be reported as realised when the deal involves two in-currencies. The date of this realisation is recorded in the new Fix Pl Realised field.

Each contract to be realised should be updated with a Y in this field. The selection of contracts to be realised can be performed prior to the start of the transition period.

The following screen shot shows the Realisation of an FX contract

The COB revaluation process performs the realisation of profit and loss for the flagged contracts. Realisation only takes place when both currencies of the contract are fixed, and the system is either the working day immediately prior to the Fixed Start Date or after this date.

If realisation is to take place, existing unrealised profit and loss is posted to the FIX P&L categories. If the contract performs accruals (for REVALUATION.TYPE SL, IN, IH and SF), the accruals are completed for the life of the contract.

No further accrual or revaluation takes place for these contracts until maturity is reached.

A daily report EU.PL.REALISED.TODAY shows the P&L realised.


##### Redenomination ofAC.CASH.POOL

Cash pooling operates on a single currency basis; whether foreign or local, all the accounts in a group must be of the same currency. When one of the accounts in the group is subject to an account conversion to change the account to EUR currency (and at the same time renumbering the original account), this can complicate the cash pooling operation.

To prevent any cross-currency complications of having mixed currencies in a group, which have values, based on the group currency it is essential that the integrity of the group is maintained.

As part of the EU conversion, any client who has cash pooling records in the currency converted to EUR needs to activate the EU.ACCP.GROUP.PARAM BATCH record and set the run date to the current day.

EU conversion of cash pooling is closely tied to the account conversion process. Once an account is converted, the cash pool EOD procedures check whether the account is part of a cash pool group. If it is, then as a precaution, the group can be flagged as inactive. This is done by setting the Eucc Process field to Yes. This will prevent any records in the group from being modified and will exclude the group from the cash pool processing until it is made active again. Once all the accounts in the group are converted, the cash pool records (AC.CASH.POOL) that were placed on hold can be amended or authorised, and the cash pool processing for the group can resume.

There are two basic scenarios in the conversion process:

- Full account conversion
- Partial account conversion

Full conversion means that either all the accounts are converted in group or in respect to cash pooling, all the accounts in a cashpool group are done at the same time. Depending on volumes of cashpool records in use, a full selection of the cashpool accounts is the best option. In larger volumes, it may be required to convert group by group.

An SRP2 group is selected, where the currency is ‘old’ currency CHF and has a working sweep.

Check the accounts used in the group including those such as the Main Master, which may not be in any sweep record.

The following screen shot shows that the group currency is changed to EUR after COB.

> **⚠️ Note:** The AC.CP.GROUP.PARAM record has been changed to EUR but the Eucc Process field is not marked as Yes, indicating that the group can be input to, modified and authorised.

All the AC.CASH.POOL group records were then amended and authorized ready for the next COB. Doing a whole group at once reduces the impact and can have the group up and running in less time.

Partial account conversion relates to the actions where one or more accounts are converted; this creates a group, which has both old currency and EUR accounts. As the group is suspended when this condition occurs and no sweeps are made until the group is re-activated, the conversion of the remaining accounts needs to be prioritised.

##### Redenomination of Loans and Deposits

After the EU.CONTRACT.CONVERSION records have been set up, the standard workflow to execute the LD conversion is as follows:

- Input the early maturity of the NCU contract (this creates the EUR contract in HLD status).
- Authorise the early maturity of the NCU contract.
- Input and authorise the new EUR contract.
- Input and authorise any resulting fund transfers relating to principal schedules and suspended interest.

> **⚠️ Note:** The workflow for LD commitments and their drawdowns is a little more complex.

To early mature the NCU contract, input to the main contract through the LD.LOANS.AND.DEPOSITS,EUCC version.

After making an entry into the record through this version, the associated routines:

- Check that the settings in the EU.CONTRACT.CONVERSION are valid.
- Set the maturity date on the NCU contract to the Conversion Date.
- Change the principal liquidation account on the NCU contract to an NCU suspense account based on the category specified in the Bal Susp Cat field in the EU.CONTRACT.CONVERSION record.
- If conversion takes place on a non-interest settlement date, the associated routines set the interest liquidation account on the NCU contract to the NCU suspense account based on the category specified in the Int Susp Cat field in the EU.CONTRACT.CONVERSION record.
- Set the limit reference in the NCU contract to the dummy reference New Limit Ref from the EU.CONTRACT.CONVERSION record.

After committing the contract record through the version, the associated routines create a new EUR contract in HLD status, based on the terms and schedules of the NCU contract, and:

- Sets the principal on the EUR contract to be the fixed equivalent of the outstanding balance on the NCU contract less any principal payments due to be made on the conversion date itself.
- Sets the value date on the EUR contract to the conversion date.
- Sets the draw down account on the EUR contract to be the EUR suspense account, based on the category specified in the EU.CONTRACT.CONVERSION record.
- Sets the limit reference to that of the original NCU contract, that is, the Old Limit Ref from the EU.CONTRACT.CONVERSION record.
- Sets the reference number of the new EUR contract in the Link Reference field of the original contract and vice versa.
- Creates FTs, as appropriate, for principal schedules and suspended interest.
- Update the EU.CONTRACT.CONVERSION record with details of the conversion.

> **⚠️ Note:** Note: No history records from the NCU contract are converted.

Warning: Any changes made to the NCU contract after this time does not affect the new EUR contract, and so should be made with careful consideration. In particular, changes should not be made again through the LD.LOANS.AND.DEPOSITS,EUCC version, as this could have intended results.

- Authorising the Early Maturity

The NCU contract set to early mature should be authorised. For standard contracts, this can be done through any version (or none). However, for commitments and loans under the commitment, the LD.LOANS.AND.DEPOSITS,EUCC version must be used.

- Completion of the EUR Contract

The new EUR contracts have been created in HLD status, which need to be input and authorised to make them live. With the exception of drawdowns under commitment, no particular version is required for this.

- Completion of Created FT Records

If the conversion creates any funds transfer records for principal repayments or suspended interest, then these also require input and authorisation. No particular versions are required.

If a principal repayment is scheduled to take place on the conversion date, it is not possible to transfer this schedule to the new contract. Therefore, after committing the conversion through LD.LOANS.AND.DEPOSITS,EUCC, the system raises a funds transfer for the principal. The funds transfer debits the original principal liquidation account (for a loan) and credits the suspense account used for early maturity (based on the category in the Bal Susp Cat in the EU.CONTRACT.CONVERSION record). Entries will be vice versa for deposits.

The transaction codes and other settings for the funds transfer are taken from FT.TXN.TYPE.CONDITION specified in the Ac Transfer Type field for internal transfers, or the Ot Transfer Type field for external transfers.

As the funds transfer is created in HLD status, it will require input and authorisation to complete the transaction.


##### Redenomination of Money Market Contracts

After EU.CONTRACT.CONVERSION has been populated with details of the individual contracts to be converted, conversion can be performed using the version record provided. In the case of Money Market contracts, the MM.MONEY.MARKET,EUCC allows the conversion to run online. The following list is a more detailed explanation of each of the conversion processes.

> **⚠️ Note:** The version calls an EU.MM.CREATE.UNAUTH.DEAL input routine, which should be set up as an EB.API record.

- Converting MM contracts on a Non-Interest Date
- Early maturing the existing MM contract
- Creation of the new EUR MM contract
- Creation of a Funds Transfer for MM repayments
- Creation of Funds Transfer for Suspended Interest
- Validation and Authorisation - Contracts and FT's
- Example - Conversion of a MM on a non-interest date

It is possible to convert term and call notice loans and deposit type transactions on a non-interest settlement date. If the Non Int Conv flag is set to Yes, then the Conversion Date specified in the EU.CONTRACT.CONVERSION record can be any working day. If the flag is set through EU.CCY.CONVERSION or via a version used to input the EU.CONTRACT.CONVERSION , then the Conversion Date defaults to the current day. However, if the flag is set by direct user input to the EU.CONTRACT.CONVERSION record, then the Conversion Date would have already defaulted to the next interest settlement date, and needs to be updated manually to the required conversion date.

Because of the processing for the interest accrual, conversions set to take on a non-interest date, must be executed on the Conversion Date itself.

Functional Limitations for MM Conversion on a Non-interest Date:

Rollover and Principal Increase Information

As it is not possible to input rollover information on initial input of a contract, this information will not be carried over to the EUR deal and is lost in the conversion.

- CAPITALISATION (for fixed maturity contracts)
- ROLLOVER.MARKER
- ROLLOVER.DATE
- NEW.INTEREST.RATE
- NEXT.INT.AMOUNT
- NEXT.PRIN.AMOUNT
- PRIN.INCREASE
- INCR.EFF.DATE

If the contract has the Auto Rollover and associated fields set, then these will be maintained correctly, and will populate the above fields as normal during COB processing.

Deferred Interest:

Presuming that the Liq Defer Interest field is not set to D. If interest should be deferred, then this will require manual adjustment of the Fund Transfer (FT).

Capitalisation:

For fixed maturity contracts, capitalisation is only applicable on a rollover. So, as mentioned above, the setting will be lost along with the other rollover information. The interest accrual is processed on the assumption of settling the interest to the customer’s account on the next interest date.

For Call or Notice contracts, the user can maintain the setting in capitalisation for future interest events. However, the processing of the interest accrual will not be correct. The interest accrual FT is raised with the posting to the customer’s account, rather than capitalising the interest onto the contract. It is recommended that users follow the procedure of removing these FTs and manually entering the EUR equivalent onto the contract as a principal increase, which is scheduled for the next interest date.

Early maturity of a Money Market contract takes place as soon as the contract is INPUT through the relevant version and involves the following:

- Set the maturity date to be the next interest payment date to flag the contract for conversion. This will, in effect, be the conversion date.
- The principal liquidation account is set as suspense account (this may be an internal account with a Bal Susp Cat category).
- Set the limit reference to be New Limit Ref (as defined in EU.CONTRACT.CONVERSION). In the case of a loan contract, the limit reference should be amended to a dummy reference of a non-reducing type. This avoids the old and new contracts both appearing under the same Limit Reference and the apparent double exposure. It also ensures that if the loan was taken under a reducing Limit, the Limit is not reduced again when the new EUR contract starts.
- Care must be taken to ensure that any principal repayment on the conversion date still takes place.

When conversion is taking place on a non-interest date, the conversion will also:

- Set Int Liq Acct in the NCU contract to the suspense account in the NCU currency based on the category defined in Int Susp Cat in the EU.CONTRACT.CONVERSION record.

After committing the contract record through the version, the associated routines create a new EUR contract in HLD status, based on the terms and schedules of the NCU contract, and also:

- Sets the principal on the EUR contract to be the fixed equivalent of the outstanding balance on the NCU contract, less any principal payments due to be made on the conversion date itself.
- Sets the value date on the EUR contract to the conversion date.
- Sets the draw down account on the EUR contract to be the EUR suspense account, based on the category specified in the EU.CONTRACT.CONVERSION record.
- Sets the Limit Reference to that of the original NCU contract, that is, the Old Limit Ref from the EU.CONTRACT.CONVERSION record.
- Sets the reference number of the new EUR contract in the Link Reference field of the original contract and vice versa.
- Creates FTs, as appropriate, for principal schedules and suspended interest.
- Update the EU.CONTRACT.CONVERSION record with details of the conversion.

> **⚠️ Note:** No history records from the NCU contract are converted.

Warning: Any changes made to the NCU contract after this time does not affect the new EUR contract, and should be made with careful consideration. In particular, changes should not be made again through the LD.LOANS.AND.DEPOSITS,EUCC version, as this can have intended results.

Any principal increase or decrease scheduled to take place on the conversion date does not take place because the contract fully matures on this date through a suspense account. A manual repayment is therefore required in these cases, which is automatically created by the conversion utility at the same time as the EUR denominated contract, and is set to ‘hold’ (that is, status of FHLD). The funds transfer debits the original principal liquidation account (for a loan) and credits the suspense account used for early maturity. Entries will be vice versa for deposits.

The following is an example of a funds transfer for repayments.

Once the new contract and funds transfer transactions have been created, the associated EU.CONTRACT.CONVERSION record is updated with New Contract, Actual Conv Date, Original Amount, Converted Amt, Repayment Ft and Repayment Amt, as demonstrated above.

Validation and Authorisation of EUR contracts:

Once the contract has been validated, the original contract needs to be authorised and the new contract that has an IHLD status needs to be validated and authorised.

Validation and Authorisation of Funds Transfer Transactions:

If a funds transfer transaction is generated to satisfy a scheduled principal repayment and/or suspended interest, the new funds transfer transaction, which also has an IHLD status needs to be validated and authorised.

In the case of an funds transfer for suspended interest, this can be value dated further forward than normally permitted, by the settings on the relevant EB.DATES record. In this case, the EB.DATES settings should be temporarily changed to allow these transactions to be input and authorised, before returning it to its normal settings.

| Interest Dates | Interest Amount |
|---|---|
| Original Committed Interest up to 26th April | 250.00 PLN |
| Suspended Interest for period up to 21st April | 388.89 PLN |
| Interest for new contract 21st Aug to 26th April | 138.89 PLN (=26.17 EUR) |


##### Redenomination of Mortgage Contracts

Once EU.CONTRACT.CONVERSION has been populated with details of the individual contracts to be converted, conversion may be performed using the VERSION record provided. In the case of mortgage, the MG.MORTGAGE,EUCC version allows the conversion to run online. Listed below is a more detailed explanation of each of the conversion processes.

- Early maturing the existing MG contract
- Creation of the new EUR MG Contract
- Creation of a Funds Transfer for MG Repayments
- Validation and Authorisation of various records

Early maturity of a mortgage contract takes place as soon as the contract is Input through the relevant version and involves the following:

- Mortgage contract are early matured by the creation of an MG.PAYMENT record for the outstanding principal.
- Set the value date and the transaction date to the required next interest payment date to flag the contract for conversion. This will be, in effect, the conversion date.
- The transaction type is set to CLOSURE.
- The payment account is set as suspense account (this can be an internal account with a category of Bal Susp Cat).
- Set the limit reference to be New Limit Ref (as defined in EU.CONTRACT.CONVERSION). The limit reference should be amended to a dummy reference of a non-reducing type. This avoids the old and new contracts both appearing under the same limit reference and the apparent double exposure. It also ensures that if the loan is taken under a reducing limit, the limit is not reduced again when the new EUR contract starts.

Care must be taken to ensure that any principal repayment on the conversion date still takes place.

After the early maturity VERSION is validated, an additional routine creates the new EUR denominated mortgage contract based on the original contract and sets it to ‘hold’ (that is, with an IHLD status). The following is an outline of this creation process:

- The original contract is used as the basis for the creation of the new EUR denominated contract.
- The outstanding balance at the conversion date is converted to EUR to become the principal on new EUR contract.
- The Value Date of the new contract is the conversion date.
- The Drawdown Account is set to the suspense account (that is, the internal account created from Bal Susp Cat in EU.CONTRACT.CONVERSION).
- The limit reference is set to the limit reference of the original contract (that is, the limit reference held in Old Limit Ref in EU.CONTRACT.CONVERSION).
- The reference number of the new contract is held in the Link Reference field of the original contract and vice versa.

> **⚠️ Note:** No history records from the original contract are converted.

Any scheduled repayment due to take place on the conversion date does not take place because the contract fully matures on this date through a suspense account. A manual repayment is therefore required in these cases, which is automatically created by the conversion utility, at the same time as the EUR denominated contract, and is set to ‘hold’ (that is, IHLD status). The funds transfer debits the original mortgage account and credits the suspense account used for early maturity.

Once the new contract and funds transfer transactions have been created, the associated EU.CONTRACT.CONVERSION record is updated with New Contract, Actual Conv Date, Original Amount, Converted Amt, Repayment Ft and Repayment Amount as shown below.

Validation and Authorisation of MG.PAYMENT Records:

Following the conversion process, the MG.PAYMENT record created to early mature the mortgage contract needs to be validated and authorised.

Validation and Authorisation of EUR Contracts:

Once the contract has been validated, the original contract will need to be authorised and the new contract that has an IHLD status needs to be validated and authorised.

Validation and Authorisation of Funds Transfer Transactions:

If a scheduled principal repayment has taken place and a new funds transfer transaction is created, that also has an IHLD status, then this needs to be validated and authorised.


##### Redenomination of Swap contracts

Early maturity of a swap contract takes place as soon as the contract is INPUT through the relevant version and involves the following:

- Set the maturity date, asset frequency and liability frequency (for maturity date schedules) to the required conversion date.
- The account number for a principal repayment is set as suspense account (this can be an internal account with a Bal Susp Cat category).
- Set the limit reference to be New Limit Ref (as defined in EU.CONTRACT.CONVERSION). In the case of a loan contract, the limit reference should be amended to a dummy reference of a non-reducing type. This avoids the old and new contracts both appearing under the same limit reference and the apparent double exposure. It also ensures that if the loan is taken under a reducing limit, the limit is not reduced again when the new EUR contract starts.
- Care must be taken to ensure that any principal repayment on the conversion date still takes place.

After the early maturity VERSION is validated, an additional routine creates the new EUR denominated swap contract based on the original contract and sets it to ‘hold’ (that is, with an IHLD status). The following is an outline of this creation process:

- The original contract is used as the basis for the creation of the new EUR denominated contract.
- The outstanding asset and liability principal amounts at the conversion date is converted to EUR to become the respective principal amounts in the new EUR contract.
- The value date of the new contract is set to the early closure date and the maturity date is set to the original maturity date.
- The draw down account is set to the suspense account (that is, the internal account created from Bal Susp Cat in EU.CONTRACT.CONVERSION).
- The limit reference is set to the limit reference of the original contract (that is, the limit reference held in Old Limit Ref in EU.CONTRACT.CONVERSION).
- The reference number of the new contract is held in the Link Reference field of the original contract and vice versa.

> **⚠️ Note:** No history records from the original contract are converted.

Any principal increase or decrease scheduled to take place on the conversion date does not take place because the contract fully matures on this date through a suspense account. A manual repayment is therefore required in these cases, which is automatically created by the conversion utility, at the same time as the EUR denominated contract, and is set to ‘hold’ (that is, FHLD status ). The funds transfer debits the original principal liquidation account (for a loan) and credits the suspense account used for early maturity. Entries will be vice versa for deposits. IRS Swap contracts have a notional principal for which, decreases will not be passed through accounts.

Once the new contract and funds transfer transactions have been created, the associated EU.CONTRACT.CONVERSION record is updated with New Contract, Actual Conv Date, Original Amount, Converted Amt, Repayment Ft and Repayment Amount as shown in the following screenshot:

Validation and Authorisation of EUR Contracts:

Once the contract is validated, the original contract needs to be authorised and the new contract, which has an IHLD status, needs to be validated and authorised.

Validation and Authorisation of Funds Transfer Transactions:

If a funds transfer transaction is generated to satisfy a scheduled principal repayment, then this new funds transfer transaction, which has an FHLD status needs to be validated and authorised.


##### Redenomination Process Guidelines

If testing is done onsite, then it is cautioned that the Eucc Process group field is set if one or most of the accounts are converted. If all accounts are converted, the cash pool records are on hold and need amending and authorising, and the field will be empty. The presence of the field makes the group inactive.

The IT department needs to do the following to use the guidelines explained here.

- Set up Local Reference fields in the LOCAL.TABLE application. Sample records for these are provided in the EURO.SEC.TOOL data library. The following screenshots give instructions for setting up these records (all instructions are for amending the GB Description field):

LOCAL.TABLE for Cash Rounding.

LOCAL.TABLE for Par Value Rounding.

Linking the LOCAL.TABLE records to the SECURITY.MASTER application.

- Set up the addresses for the local reference fields added in the above step in the EU.PARAMETER record. This has been illustrated in the screen shot below:

Defining the local reference locations on the EU.PARAMETER record

The back office needs to do the following to use the guidelines explained here.

- Use SEC.MASTER.CONV in the TEST stage. This has been illustrated in the screenshot shown below.

### 7.10  Settlement NCU Contracts


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *During the transition period, the principle of ‘No compulsion, No prohibition’, that is, a customer or the bank may choose to accept NCU payment in EUR or to remain in NCU. The bank must be able to handle the conversion between NCU and EUR, as required. Most applications in Temenos Transact require ...*
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Auto Pay Acct*, *Auto Pay Categ*, *Auto Rec Ccy*, *Dc Aut Pay Txns*, *Orig Ccy Payment*, *Subs For Txn List*
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

During the transition period, the principle of ‘No compulsion, No prohibition’, that is, a customer or the bank may choose to accept NCU payment in EUR or to remain in NCU. The bank must be able to handle the conversion between NCU and EUR, as required. Most applications in Temenos Transact require that settlement accounts are in the same currency as the contract. As settlement of NCU amounts can be made in EUR or NCU, this restriction requires a manual process to settle through a suspense account on the underlying contract, and create a funds transfer (or similar) from the NCU suspense to the correct EUR account.

While this practice may be acceptable for small numbers of Euro settlements, it would obviously be a large operational overhead and also prone to operator error in any site with a reasonable volume of transactions.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

This is covered as part of module configuration. There is no specific configuration for this feature.


#### 🔧 Working With

The Euro module allows automatic conversion of NCU amounts to EUR for any nominated Account. The user can follow one of the below process:

- Auto Payment Account – Here an existing NCU account is linked to a EUR account. Many NCU accounts can be linked to the same EUR account, all the transactions across the linked NCU accounts are converted to EUR, and posted to the EUR account. Any related payments are also converted to EUR.
- General Suspense Account – Here a suspense account of a specific category is used for settlement from the contract. A customer who has only a EUR account nominates that any deal in a specific NCU should be settled to the EUR account. The system checks any posting made across the general suspense account to see if the customer has a nominated EUR account, if available, the entry will be converted and posted to the EUR account.


##### Settlement Using Auto Pay Account

This section explains the ability to settle NCU through EUR for individual accounts. Read the Redenomination of Accounts section for details about the automated process of converting an account from NCU to EUR.

To explain the use of the auto pay account, the bank deciding to settle NCU through the Euro is used an example in the below screenshots.

Settlement in IEP currency should be made through a EUR nostro maintained with the same bank. The following screenshot shows the EUR Nostro account:

The IEP ACCOUNT record should be linked to the Euro Nostro using the Auto Pay Acct :

Once the Auto Pay Acct is defined (refer to the above screenshot), the following process is followed:

- Accounting entries raised to the IEP Nostro (with the exception of certain entries through the DATA.CAPTURE application, refer to the DATA.CAPTURE if needed) is converted to EUR and posted to the EUR Nostro.
- Forward accounting entries to the IEP Nostro is converted to EUR and posted to the EUR Nostro. Any forward entries, which exist prior to establishing the link with the auto pay account is converted to EUR entries in the COB processing. For this reason, it is recommended that the Nostro be linked at the end of the working day.

Any payment message (for example, MT100/202) for the IEP Nostro is also converted to EUR. The original IEP amount appears in the message as Euro Related Information (ERI) if the payment is sent through SWIFT.

If there is a requirement that the payments must still be sent in the original currency and not converted, the Orig Ccy Payment field of the account is set to YES. In this case, the payment remains in NCU and no ERI information is displayed.

The NCU account should continue to be used for deals in NCU, if defined as a default Nostro. If applicable, the account continues to default. Any further postings and payments to the account is converted automatically as described above (Converting Payment Messages Using the Auto Pay Account).

As mentioned, once the link is established, all further postings are directed to the EUR Auto Pay Acct . If an adjustment should be posted to the NCU account, this must be posted through the DATA.CAPTURE application, which can be used to force the entry to the NCU account. When entry is forced to the NCU account an override is required.

The following screenshot shows the adjustments made through DATA.CAPTURE application:

By default, the DATA.CAPTURE application posts entries to the specified account, so that when an NCU account that is linked to an Auto Pay Acct is used, the posting is made to the NCU account and is not converted.

The DATA.CAPTURE application has many functions and this rule may not be appropriate always, there may be a requirement to post to the Auto Pay Acct in the same way as the other applications. For example, the user may use the application to post transactions raised in another system and any postings should be converted to a linked Euro account.

The automatic posting to the auto pay account can be controlled by setting the Dc Aut Pay Txns and Subs For Txn List fields in the EU.PARAMETER application, which is defined at company level. Individual Transaction codes, which should or should not be posted to a linked auto pay account, should be specified in the Dc Aut Pay Txns field. The Subs For Txn List field indicates whether the Transaction codes specified should or should not convert.

In the below example screenshot, any transactions raised using codes 1 and 51 is posted to the Auto Pay Acct , if defined:

The following setting (in the screenshot) results in all transactions except for 1 and 51 being posted to the Auto Pay Acct , if defined:


##### Settlement Using General Suspense Account

The Auto Payment Account is the best method used for linking Nostros to EUR and linking nostros to customers with existing NCU accounts. However, if a new customer created in the system wants todeal in NCU, but settle through a EUR account, the general suspense account should be used.

This method does not require the customer to have an NCU account. Instead the EUR account record defines which NCU currencies can post to the account. NCU contracts should use a general suspense account for settlement.

A new category in the range of 10-000 to 19-999 should be allocated for the general suspense account.

An internal account should be opened for each In-currency. The general suspense account has an ID in the below format:

- - , where nnnnn is the category defined in the previous step. The following screenshot shows the General Euro Suspense account.

The general suspense category must be added to the ACCOUNT.PARAMETER application (ID of System) before it can be used.

> **⚠️ Note:** Once the ACCOUNT.PARAMETER record is authorised, users must login again to Temenos Transact to use the updated setting.

The following screenshot shows the Auto Pay Categ .

The customer’s Euro account should be linked to the general suspense account to be used for settlement of contracts. In order to do this, the NCU currencies that can be settled by the account should be specified in the Auto Rec Ccy field.

The CUST.ACC.CCY.REC application displays details about particular customer accounts that should receive NCU payments.

The general suspense account defaults as the settlement account, if the customer has specified that Euro should be used to settle the particular currency of the deal. Entering the general suspense account for a particular NCU can also specify the account.

The user must exercise precaution if the suspense is specified for a customer who does not have a EUR account, which can receive NCU. Here, the movement is not posted to the EUR account and remains in the suspense account.

Once the Auto Rec Ccy is defined as shown above:

- Accounting entries raised to the IEP and DEM suspense accounts for the customer is converted to EUR and posted to the EUR current account.
- Forward accounting entries to the IEP and DEM suspense accounts for the customer is converted to EUR and posted to the EUR current account. Any forward entries, which exist prior to establishing the link, is converted to EUR entries in the COB processing.

### 8.1  Asst Ent Oper Units


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *Fixed Asset Management module provides the ability to tag and track the operational units (branch or department) of the bank where the fixed asset is physically deployed or linked throughout its lifecycle. Operational units are independent of the banks Company or Organisation structure maintained in...*
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Auto Account Sequence*, *Auto Open FA Acct*, *Dept Acct Officer*, *Short Description*
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

Fixed Asset Management module provides the ability to tag and track the operational units (branch or department) of the bank where the fixed asset is physically deployed or linked throughout its lifecycle. Operational units are independent of the banks Company or Organisation structure maintained in Transact. These operational units are module-specific and the scope is limited to Fixed Asset Management module only. Banks can choose the Company Book or Branch under which the journal entries and the financials of the fixed assets pertaining to an operational unit are reported.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

This is covered as part of module configuration. There is no specific configuration for this feature.


#### 📋 Tasks

Fixed Asset Management module allows the user to tag and track the operational units (branch or department) of the bank where the fixed asset is physically deployed or linked through-out its life cycle.


##### Workflow

In Asset Entity and Operational Units, the user can perform the following activities.

This enquiry allows the user to capture a new asset entity and to view or amend the existing asset entity records.

To create Asset Entity, follow the below steps:

1. Input/Amend Asset Entity .
2. In the Contract screen, click the Create New Record (New Deal) icon.
3. In the Asset Entity screen, provide ID and click Enter .
4. In the Asset Entity screen, enter required values in the below fields: Short Description Auto Open FA Acct Auto Account Sequence Dept Acct Officer Enter values for Asset Class and related Account numbers fields if Auto Open FA Acct is set to No.
5. Click the Validate icon to check for overrides and errors.
6. Click the Commit icon to create the record.

To view an Asset Entity record, follow the below steps:

1. Input/Amend Asset Entity . Enquiry displays the authorised asset entity records.
2. In the List of Asset Entity Records screen, click the View icon corresponding to a record.

To amend Asset Type record, follow the below steps:

1. Input/Amend Asset Entity . Enquiry displays the authorised asset entity records.
2. In the List of Asset Entity Records screen, click the Amend icon corresponding to a record.
3. Click the Validate icon to check for overrides and errors.
4. Click the Commit icon to amend the record.

### 8.2  Fixd Asst Clssfcation


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *Fixed Asset Classification enable banks to group their fixed assets based on the asset characteristic nature, purpose and legal or depreciation requirements. Fixed Asset Classification is established as a two-tier structure.*
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Asset Category*, *Asset Class*, *CWIP Categ*, *Capital Allowance*, *Depreciate to Zero*, *Depreciation*, *Depreciation Allowed*, *Depreciation Categ* ... +18 more
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

Fixed Asset Classification enable banks to group their fixed assets based on the asset characteristic nature, purpose and legal or depreciation requirements. Fixed Asset Classification is established as a two-tier structure.


##### Asset Class

- Asset Class is the top level of grouping or classifying fixed assets.
- It is possible to define common accounting rules and configurations that apply for the assets grouped under the asset class.


##### Asset Type

- Asset type is the sub-level of grouping or classifying fixed assets under asset class.
- It is possible to define common depreciation rules and cost type configurations that apply for all the assets grouped under the asset type.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

This is covered as part of module configuration. There is no specific configuration for this feature.


#### 📋 Tasks

Asset Class is a high-level classification of fixed assets based on their characteristics.

This enquiry allows the user to capture a new asset class and to view or amend the existing asset classes.


##### Workflow

In Fixed Asset Classification, the user can perform the following activities.

To create Asset Class, follow the below steps:

1. Input/Amend Account Based .
2. In the Contract screen, click the Create New Record (New Deal) icon.
3. In the Asset Class screen, provide ID and click Enter .
4. In the Asset Class screen, enter required values in the below fields: Description Asset Category Provision Category Write Off Depreciation Category Depreciation Capital Allowance Depreciate to Zero CWIP Categ Profit Categ Loss Categ Payables Acct Categ Receivables Acct Categ
5. Click the Validate icon to check for overrides and errors.
6. Click the Commit icon to create the record.

To view an Asset Class record, follow the below steps:

1. Input/Amend Asset Class . Enquiry displays the authorised Asset Class records.
2. In the List of Asset Class Records screen, click the View icon corresponding to a record.

To amend an Asset Class record, follow the below steps:

1. Input/Amend Asset Class . Enquiry displays the authorised asset class records.
2. In the List of Asset Class Records screen, click the Amend icon corresponding to a record.
3. Click the Validate icon to check for overrides and errors.
4. Click the Commit icon to amend the record.

Asset Type is the sub-level grouping of fixed assets under asset class that exhibit similar characteristics and are subject to the same depreciation factors

### 8.3  Fixd Asst Lifcycle


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *Fixed Asset Management helps to capture the lifecycle events of a fixed asset from acquisition through depreciation and disposal of the asset. As a part of recording the lifecycle event in the system, one or more of the following processes are triggered online.*
> 
> **Applications:** `EB.LOOKUP`, `FIXED.ASSET.TYPE`

> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

Fixed Asset Management helps to capture the lifecycle events of a fixed asset from acquisition through depreciation and disposal of the asset. As a part of recording the lifecycle event in the system, one or more of the following processes are triggered online.

- Payment initiation to the supplier or vendor of the asset.
- Posting journal entries to reflect the asset balances on the General Ledger.
- Updating status of the asset based on the event performed.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

This section explains the configurations associated to Fixed Asset Management Lifecycle activities.


##### Customise Fixed Asset Lifecycle Activity

Fixed asset lifecycle activity name and description can be customised to the bank requirements. Fixed assets activities are managed through the EB.LOOKUP application (Virtual Table). The following table shows the fixed assets activities involved in the asset lifecycle.

> **⚠️ Note:** The EB.LOOKUP items customise the fixed asset activity name and description only. The user cannot add new or remove existing fixed asset lifecycle activities from the EB.LOOKUP application.


#### 📋 Tasks

This section explains the tasks related to Fixed Asset Lifecycle.


##### Workflow

In Fixed Asset Lifecycle, the user can perform the following activities.

This screen allows the user to register the fixed asset details. Cost details are optional input and depreciation details can be fetched from FIXED.ASSET.TYPE definition.

Asset registration is the first and user-initiated activity in the life cycle of the asset to on-board the asset in the system.

1. Register Asset .
2. In Register Fixed Asset tab, enter the required values in the below fields. Asset Description Asset Class Asset Type Asset Entity Economic Life Supplier Beneficiary Reference Dept Account Officer
3. In Cost Details tab, enter required values in the below fields. Currency of Asset Original Value of Asset Cost of Asset Cost Type Cost Type Amt Recoverable Cost Residual Value (calculated as 0 if not provided)
4. In Depreciation Details tab, enter required values in the below fields. Depreciation Allowed Depreciation Method Depreciation Frequency Depreciation Rate
5. Click Validate icon to check for errors and overrides.
6. Click Commit icon to submit the record.

> **⚠️ Note:** Pending Registrations . This lists the assets from asset catalog where the asset purpose is defined as either own purpose or finance. The user can complete the registration of asset using the drilldown.

Capital Work in Progress (CWIP) represents costs incurred on a fixed asset which is still under construction. The Capital Work-In-Progress (a user-initiated activity) provides an ability for banks to record WIP cost incurred on an asset and initiate the payment to supplier or vendor as work-in progress payments.

This screen allows the user to initiate capital WIP payment to supplier.

1. Capital Work in Progress Payments .
2. In CWIP Transfer screen, enter required values in the below fields. Asset ID Capital Work in Progress Amount Date of Invoice Invoice Reference Cost Type Cost Type Amount Recoverable Cost
3. Click the Validate icon to check for overrides and errors.
4. Click the Commit icon to amend the record.

This user-initiated activity confirms if the asset is received and deployed. The asset can now be reported in the books of the bank and payment can be initiated to the third-party vendor or supplier.

Date of purchase and cost details of the assets are defaulted upon validating the record if the same is captured during register activity.

This screen allows the user to initiate purchase activity of the asset.

1. Purchase Asset .
2. In Purchase Fixed Asset screen, enter required values in the below fields. Asset ID Original Value Cost Type Cost Type Amt Recoverable Cost Cost of Asset Residual Value Date of Purchase Depreciation Rate
3. Click the Validate icon to check for overrides and errors.
4. Click the Commit icon to amend the record.

Capital Improvement is a user-initiated activity which improves the lifetime of the fixed asset with additional cost.

This activity can be performed on assets with Status Asset as Acquired/Purchased only.

This screen allows the user to initiate purchase activity of the asset.

1. Capital Improvement .
2. In Capital Improvement screen, enter required values in the below fields. Asset ID Supplier Beneficiary Reference Capital Improvement Date Capital Improvement Cost Economic Life extension Depreciation Rate
3. Click the Validate icon to check for overrides and errors.
4. Click the Commit icon to amend the record.

Transfer of an asset is a user-initiated activity which allow banks to record the transfer or movement of fixed assets between the organisation units of the bank. Transfer activity is allowed only for assets with Status as either Registered or Work-In-Progress or Purchased

This screen allows the user to perform transfer of an asset.

### 8.4  Migration Fxd Asset


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
>
