### 11.5  IBAN Structure Directory


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *SWIFT is the formal registrar of IBAN under the current standard ISO 13616-2:2007. The IBAN structure files downloaded from SWIFT are processed and the information uploaded into relevant tables in Temenos Transact .*
> 
> **Applications:** `IN.IBAN.STRUCTURE`
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Field A*, *Field B*, *Field C*, *Field D*
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

SWIFT is the formal registrar of IBAN under the current standard ISO 13616-2:2007. The IBAN structure files downloaded from SWIFT are processed and the information uploaded into relevant tables in Temenos Transact .

SWIFT is discontinuing support for this directory by Nov 2026. The SWIFTRef FORMAT-CTRY file replaces the IBAN Structure file.

Read SWIFTRef Identifiers Directory to find how the IBAN Structure are uploaded and managed in the system.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

This section explains the IBAN Structure application.

The IN.IBAN.STRUCTURE records contain the IBAN structure information downloaded from SWIFT. This application holds information such as the length of IBAN along with the position identifiers for bank, branch, and BIC codes.

This section details how the information from the IBAN Structure file is recorded in IN.IBAN.STRUCTURE using the following fields. The value in the Modification Flag field indicates if there is a change to the existing record since the last release of the IBAN structure file. The field contains one of the following values.

- A (Addition) – A new IBAN structure record is introduced.
- M (Modification) – An existing IBAN structure record is modified.
- D (Deletion) – An existing IBAN structure record is no longer in use is deleted.

The uploaded records are handled according to the modification flag:

- If the record does not exist and the modification flag is A, a new record is created.
- If the record exists and the modification flag is M, then the record is updated.
- If the modification flag is D, then the Modification Flag field will be updated as D and the record will be reversed.

- The values for the fields shown in the below screenshot, from Tag to Iban Total Len , are updated from the IBAN file.

- The values from the Iban Country Code to Iban Total Len fields shown in the above screenshot form the IBAN number per country.
- The fields shown in the below screenshot hold the information related to the application and fields from the respective applications from where the values will be retrieved. These values will form a part of the Basic Bank Account Number (BBAN) that will generate for a particular company in Temenos Transact .

> **⚠️ Note:** It is possible to use values from a local table to be included in IBAN.

When the SFRD25 is licensed then the following details are captured on upload of the SWIFTRef FORMAT-CTRY file:

| Field Name | Description |
|---|---|
| Field A | This field captures the IBAN NATIONAL ID POSITION attribute in the Formats file. The field indicates the start position of the IBAN National ID within the IBAN format. |
| Field B | This field captures the IBAN NATIONAL ID TYPE attribute in the Formats file. The fields indicate the ID TYPE of the IBAN National ID. |
| Field C | This field captures the DOMESTIC ACCOUNT NUMBER POSITION attribute in the Formats file. The field indicates the start position of the Domestic Account Number. |
| Field D | This field captures the DOMESTIC ACCOUNT NUMBER LENGTH attribute in the Formats file. The field indicates the length of the Domestic Account Number. |

### 11.6  Misc


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *The International Banking Account Number (IBAN) is an international standard that allows to uniquely identify bank accounts across national borders. Based on the IBAN, it is possible to identify both the country and the bank where the account is maintained.*
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction


#### 📖 Introduction

Related topics:

- APIs
- Temenos Transact Services
- Uploading IBAN Directories
- Centralised Reference Data

The International Banking Account Number (IBAN) is an international standard that allows to uniquely identify bank accounts across national borders. Based on the IBAN, it is possible to identify both the country and the bank where the account is maintained.

In Temenos Transact or Standalone TPH, the IBAN module (IN):

- Manages the IBAN Structure rules for the countries that have adopted the IBANs.
- It optionally handles the IBAN National Identifiers
- Provides a set of REST APIs through which the IBAN reference data can be accessed

A set of public methods are available under the System Table (ST) module to access or validate the IBAN-related data against the reference directories.

SWIFT provides the IBAN-related data as part of the following directories:

- SWIFTRef IBAN Plus – This directory includes the IBAN structure rules for the countries that adopted IBAN, the IBAN National Identifiers used in the countries and their corresponding BIC, and the list of IBAN National Identifiers that cannot be used in Payments. From November 2026 SWIFT discontinues support for this directory, which is replaced by the SWIFT Identifiers All
- SWIFTRef Identifiers All – This directory includes all the entity identifiers. This includes BIC, LEI, IBAN National IDs, and national IDs which are not used in IBANs.

SWIFTRef IBAN Plus Upload

- Temenos supports the upload of the SWIFTRef IBAN Plus directory published by SWIFT. The upload processes for the SWIFTRef IBAN Plus files into the Temenos IBAN Structure, IBAN Plus, and Exclusion List are part of the Centralised Reference Data module (RD).
- Clients upgrading from a release before 201907 who have already licensed Delivery (DE) or IBAN module (IN) in the prior release, can get the RD license code at no additional cost. Before starting the upgrade, the customers should request the license code of the RD module from their account manager.
- From November 2026, SWIFT discontinues support for this directory. SWIFT clients can upload the SWIFTRef Identifiers All which replaces SWIFT IBAN Plus

SWIFTRef Identifiers Directory

- Temenos supports the upload of the Identifiers All directory published by SWIFT. The upload of the SWIFTRef Identifiers files is part of the Temenos SWIFTRef Identifiers Directory (SFRD25) module.
- From R25 clients that have licensed the Centralised Reference Data module (RD) will automatically receive the SFRD25 module
- Upgrading clients to R25 which have licensed SFRD25, will automatically receive the RD module
- Based on the configuration of the RD module:
- The IBAN National IDs can be referred from the IBAN Plus or from the Centralised Bank Directory
- The upload process can optionally update the IBAN National ID into the IBAN Plus Directory

Read SWIFTRef Identifiers Directory user guide for more information.

### 12.1  Consolidated Company CRF Report


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *The system generates individual company general ledger reports such as the Balance Sheet and Profit and Loss reports for all the companies within a group.*
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

The system generates individual company general ledger reports such as the Balance Sheet and Profit and Loss reports for all the companies within a group.

If a consolidated view of the group is required, COMPANY.CONSOL functionality may be used.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

This topic explains the system configuration of the feature.


##### Consolidated Company Reporting Parameters

The COMPANY.CONSOL application holds the descriptions and details of companies to be consolidated. The consolidation tool has the flexibility to consolidate one or more existing companies into an existing lead company or create a separate company solely for consolidated reporting purpose.

A bank as 3 business units X, Y and Z all set up as companies in T24. Y and Z can be consolidated into X. Or it can create a reporting company W into which it can consolidate X, Y and Z.

Each record is independent of the others and there is no hierarchical relationship between them.

The default currency for any report produced can be specified. Special currency exchange rates can be used or the standard rates from the currency record(s) can be used.

When producing a combined report, the local currency amount or the local currency equivalent amount is converted into the reporting currency. The original currency figures are not used. Therefore, it is necessary to enter some default conditions on these records. The default conditions are:

- The currency to be used when the rates are to be taken from one currency record.
- When there are two or more currency records for the same local currency, which company’s currency record must be used.


##### Special Currency Rates for Combined Reporting

The RE.RPT.CCY.RATE application holds the details of the exchange rates used for producing combined reports.

The key to the records on this file are the reporting currency followed by a 'sequence' number thus allowing more than one set of rates to be loaded per reporting currency. This is used in cases where the rate required is different for head office from current market rates used for daily transactions.

When converting to the reporting currency, the 'local' currency amount field is the one converted but not the foreign currency (original currency) field.

This means that only rates between the reporting currency and the local currency for each company must be loaded. When one or more companies share the same local currency, then the exchange rate between the local currency and reporting currency will be shared by all the companies with the same local currency. It is not possible to load different rates per company.

> **⚠️ Note:** It is not possible to load different rates per company.


#### 🔧 Working With

This topic covers the workflow of this feature.


##### Combined Currency Report Requests

The RE.CONSOL.REQUEST application produces CRF reports for consolidated companies. This application holds details of the requests for different reports.

These requests can be run as part of the end of day processing, in the EB.CONSOL.PRINT batch process or on-line using the ‘V’ (Verify) function for this application.

The following details are included in a request:

- The CRF report
- The level of the report
- The currency of the report
- The consolidation group
- Where and which the exchange rates to be used.

It is the local currency amounts, from the CRF base, that are converted into the reporting currency. The original currency amounts are not considered for combined reporting.

For each local currency, one rate is determined and the same is used for all the companies with that local currency irrespective of whether there are different set of exchange rates for each company.

The exchange rates can be taken from:

1. A record in the RE.RPT.CCY.RATE application. This option is referred as the SPECIAL level rates.
2. The CURRENCY application for each local currency. If more than one currency is used as a local currency, then the currency to be used is specified in the COMPANY.CONSOL application. This option is referred as the COMPANY level rates.
3. One of the CURRENCY applications. This application is specified in the COMPANY.CONSOL application. These rates are considered as the DEFAULT rates.

If a particular rate is missing from the level requested it is obtained using the next level down or by using the master company's CURRENCY application and calculating cross rates when required.


##### CRF Reporting

In a multi-branch environment the CRF key are identified by the company suffix which is attached to the key by the system. It is the last attribute in the CRF key.

EXAMPLE: The following CONSOLIDATE.ASST.LIAB shows the same type of customer current accounts in two different branches. AC.1.TR.GBP.1001.2800.32.GB.........GB0010101

AC.1.TR.GBP.1001.2800.32.GB.........GB0010201

The following CONSOLIDATE.PRFT.LOSS shows the interest accruals in three different branches.

PL.53001.20000..10.........GB0010101

PL.53001.20000..10.........GB0010201

PL.53001.20000..10.........GB0010202

The CRF reporting data applications, where necessary, include the company code in the key.

The CRF reporting is restricted to reporting at the company (branch) level, unless the standard method of consolidating company reports is used, that is, through RE.CONSOL.REQUEST .


#### 📋 Tasks

#### 📊 Outputs

#### 📖 Introduction

This topic illustrates an example of the process to create two book type companies in a single company Model Bank (MB) environment.

> **⚠️ Note:** This topic is for guidance only.

The following should be decided outside Temenos Transact , before creating an MB area.

- The digits of account number that will be used to identify the company to which the ACCOUNT belongs (identifies starting from the first position till the fourth position). This is populated in the INTERCO.PARAMETER application.

- Allocation of the sub-division code for identifying each COMPANY. These are 022 and 033 respectively for each book, which is populated into the records in COMPANY when they are created.

### 12.3  Creating Multi-Company Environment


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *Before creating a company, it is important to decide the structure of the company. It is possible to setup a system in Temenos Transact that combines all types of company.*
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

Before creating a company, it is important to decide the structure of the company. It is possible to setup a system in Temenos Transact that combines all types of company.

- Classic multi-company – A set of lead companies, which can share various data type applications.
- Simple multi-branch – A set of branches linked to the master company sharing the master company’s application with the exception of financial reporting (FRP) applications.
- Combined – A set of lead companies, which can share various data type applications, where each lead company may also have a set of branch companies linked to it (if required).
- An Accounting company can be linked to any of the combinations above.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

- A multi-branch structure is setup when there is a need of client’s business operations. Typically the client may have a head office operation managing multiple branches and subsidiary companies. They may share the same local currency and customer records and there is no requirement for separate COB processing (global processing) for different groups of companies. This provides a much more efficient system than multi-company structure that are independent of each other.
- A multi-company structure setup is required if there is more than one local currency or if the Customer Information (CIF) is unique for different entities of the company, that is, several entities of the bank cannot share the same customer database and manage their own CIF.
- Combined structures may be necessary for a more complex bank with multi-national presence with companies and branches within these companies.
- If a bank operates over a large geographical area with different time zones, then it may be necessary to install one lead company for each time zone (or group of time zones), so that separate COB processing can take place for each group of branches, even though all branches may be part of the same financial group and the lead companies share the same customer and currency files.
- If a bank operates in different countries with different local currencies, each country can be set up with a separate lead company, with its own branch structure. It is possible for each lead company to share the same CUSTOMER application but have a separate CURRENCY application.


#### 🔧 Working With

This topic outlines the steps to setup a new company. The following are the main steps:

- Actions outside Temenos Transact .
- Creating a new record in COMPANY .
- After creating the record in COMPANY .


##### Actions OutsideTemenos Transact

The following must be agreed before setting up or changing to a multi-company environment:

- The company number and mnemonic.
- The local currency.
- The financial year-end.
- The sub-division number.
- The level of the files to be shared or not shared.
- The applications to be run under the company.
- The applications requiring the auto ID function.
- The name and address of the company.
- The type of rate and tolerance data to be loaded from other company records.
- The account number check-digit type and format from other company records.
- The digits of account number to be used that identifies the company to which the account belongs.
- The category code for inter-company accounts.
- The transaction codes for the inter-company transactions.
- Usage of the company group number and sequence number in the company key.
- Allocation of the company digits in the account number for each company.
- Allocation of the sub-division code for identifying each company.


##### Creating a New COMPANY record

Follow the below steps to create a new company in Temenos Transact :

- Ensure that you are the only user in the system.
- Create a new record in the COMPANY.GROUP application (if required), if the company number contains a new group number.
- Check if the IBLC.TODAY and SYSTEM.END.OF.DAY4 records exist in the BATCH.NEW.COMPANY application. . The IBLC.TODAY and SYSTEM.END.OF.DAY4 records are obsolete and should be reversed.
- Run the COMPANY.CREATE application.

This enables the creation of a company using a special service through the COMPANY application, with zero authorisers.


##### Understanding theCOMPANY.CREATEApplication

COMPANY.CREATE is a ‘W’ type application. It cannot be run in Browser mode.

The workflow of this application is as follows:

- Populates the record in COMPANY.CREATE with appropriate details for the new company.
- It creates all the required applications and tables, generates the records in BATCH in the unauthorised application and copies the requested records in the FILE.SETUP.DETAIL application in the respective unauthorised applications in IHLD status.

The objective is to simplify the creation of a new company using the following methods:

- Reduce the amount of data to input into the new company record.
- Default as much data as possible into the new company record, from an existing company record.
- Automate the creation of authorised records for the new company as much as possible.

There are basically two types of company in Temenos Transact :

- Lead company – This type of company owns a full set of financial level data and is exactly the same as a company in a multi-company environment. The master company (usually BNK) can be defined as a lead company with some additional features not relevant to this application. The various non-financial application types, that is, not FIN can be shared with other companies, usually the master company exactly as in a standard multi-company environment. A full set of data files are created for the new company and any data records are created unauthorised.

- Branch Company – This type of company is linked to a lead company and shares all application types with it. A branch company can produce an independent set of financial books. The only new files created for a new branch are the financial reporting type (FRP). This type of file is generally related to REPGEN work files. All data records created for the new branch are automatically authorised.

If the company to be created shares the following file type with an existing lead company and is in the same geographical time zone, then it is more efficient to create a branch:

- INT – Installation
- CUS – Customer
- CST – Customer Table
- FIN – Financial
- FTD – Financial Table Descriptive
- FTF – Financial Table Financial
- CCY – Currency
- NOS – Nostro

When creating a new company the minimum amount of information required is input in this application, that is, name, address, mnemonic and sub-division code. The Financial Com field determines whether a lead or branch company is being created. If the Financial Com field value is not the same as the @ID of the created company, then a branch is created, otherwise a new lead company is created.

The Default Cust Com field value is used to identify the record in COMPANY application that provides the data to default values into the new company record created. When creating a new branch, all fields apart from those input into this application are taken from the lead company. When creating a new lead company, the default company can be used to reduce the amount of data that is input into the new company.

If the new lead company that is being setup has similar applications and table type structure as an existing company, then the new record is populated with data from the default. Then, when the control is passed to the

application, the relevant fields can be modified, rather than filling all the fields.


##### After Creating the COMPANY record

When creating a new branch, the relevant data records are created in the authorised state, so the amount of work required is minimised to setting up the users for the new branch.

The following steps must be performed before letting other users back onto the system:

1. Modify the records in USER , so that access to the new company is allowed.
2. Input and authorise the records in DATES for the new company. On this record, the Run Date and Next Working Day fields must be the same as on the first company created.
3. Create an abbreviation for changing to new company.
4. Update the company related fields in the SYSTEM record in the INTERCO.PARAMETER , if a new lead company is created.
5. The above is done before signing onto the new company. It is necessary to sign-off and on again, to obtain use of the modified details to the records in USER and INTERCO.PARAMETER .
6. Create a record in the REVALUATION.PARAMETER application with the parameters setup for the following: AL – Asset and Liability revaluation FX – Forex FX.SP – Forex spot revaluation FX.RB – Forex rebate revaluation

1. Input and authorise the data on the following files (the below list is assumed to have shared customer and Nostro records), if the files are created for new lead company. For these files, the data has to be written to the unauthorised file.

1. Input and authorise the data on the following files (the below list is assumed to have shared customer and Nostro records), if the files are created for a new lead company. For these files the data must be entered.

Other Interest and Charges applications.

##### Close of Business

The COB processing in the extended multi-company works as follows:

- The application level jobs run at lead company level, that is, all branches linked to a particular lead company are processed together.
- The core batch control routine determines the correct company to load the relevant record being processed.
- Reporting jobs are run separately for each company including branches.
- Global processing option is restricted to lead companies, that is, all branches in the same group are processed together but different groups of branches can be processed separately.

### 12.4  Inter-company Accounting


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *Inter-company accounting is an important part of the configuration in a MCMB functionality. This is to accommodate balance movements between:*
> 
> **Applications:** `ACCOUNT.PARAMETER`, `INTERCO.PARAMETER`
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Retain Orig Accting Sys*, *Val Date By Cat Sys 1.1*, *Val Date Sys Id 1*
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

Inter-company accounting is an important part of the configuration in a MCMB functionality. This is to accommodate balance movements between:

- Branch companies
- Branch companies and its lead company


#### ⚙️ Configuration

INTERCO.PARAMETER is used for configuring the intercompany accounting. It is also used to decide the structure of the internal accounts for the intercompany accounting.

The INTERCO.PARAMETER application is a SYSTEM level file, that is, there is only one instance of the file shared across all companies. If the SYSTEM record is missing, then Temenos Transact assumes that a single company accounting environment exists.

It contains the details of types on intercompany accounting, that is, multi-company, multi-branch or both.. It helps to identify the company number for each company. In a multi-branch system, the branches always follow the rules set by their lead company.

If the user requires inter‑company accounting, then the user must input and authorise the SYSTEM record before creating the second company.

> **⚠️ Note:** Before authorising the SYSTEM record for an inter‑company accounting environment, the INTERCO record must be present in the ACCOUNT.CLASS application.

There must be portion of the account number from which the lead company can be determined. This is called the branch code and is used to identify the branch. Each branch code must be assigned to a company. as postings to accounts can only be made by transactions of the company to which the account belongs (except for inter-company postings for which special rules apply). If an account has a branch code which is not assigned to a company, then postings cannot be made to it. If the account belongs to the master company or one of its branches, then it is not necessary to have a branch code in the account number. Normally, master company account number lengths differ from those of other lead companies.

When installing a multi-branch system, the conversion of the existing internal accounts is automatic. When an entry is passed to an internal account, a new internal account is opened, the old account is set for closure and is set to auto pay into the new account.

The intercompany accounts require a special structure depending whether it’s a multi-company or a multi-branch set-up or a mixture.


##### Structure of Internal Account for inter-company accounting

Internal accounts maintain the bank’s general ledger (GL) accounts which are identified using the branch or sub-division code, based on the configuration of the company to which it belongs.


#### 🔧 Working With

The standard format of a Temenos Transact internal account is CCYCATEGNNNN, where:

- CCY is a three alphabetic character currency code.
- CATEG is a five numeric character category code.
- NNNN is a four numeric character identifier, which is a sub-division code in case of inter-company accounts.

In a multi-branch setup, as all internal accounts for all branches are stored on the same table, there is an additional four numeric character sub-division code of the company that owns the account. If an entry is passed from Company A to Company B, the inter-company account in Company A has the following format:

- CCY is the currency code.
- CATEG is the inter-company category code.
- SUBDIV B is the sub-division code of the company being posted to.
- SUBDIV A is the sub-division code of the company being posted from.

This topic covers the different accounting options for inter-company.


##### Head Office Inter-Company Accounting Options

Inter-company accounting entries can be passed through a defined single company. This increases the number of entries for an inter-company transfer from four to six, with two additional entries in the designated company, but considerably reduces the number of inter-company accounts required where there are large numbers of companies in the system.

This option allows a unit to define if an inter-unit account is held within the unit for each branch or if the inter-unit accounts are maintained with the head office (or some central unit).

If inter-unit accounts are held at the head office, it means that each unit must only raise an inter-unit entries with the head office only and a single inter-unit account is maintained in each unit for inter-unit transactions.

The head office maintains a single inter-unit account with each unit.

In the scenario of 1,000 branches, there are:

- 1,000 inter-unit accounts held at head office.
- 1,000 inter-unit account with head office held at each branch multiplied by 1,000.
- Total of 2,000 accounts instead of 1,000,000 accounts.

> **⚠️ Note:** The assumption is that only local currency is used. If different currencies are used, then an inter-unit account is required for each currency.

To enable this functionality, the Intercomp Co field in the SYSTEM record of the INTERCO.PARAMETER application should be input with the company ID of the company that is created or configured as the head office.


##### Inter-Company Accounting and PL

The multi-company and multi-branch intercompany accounting use the same mechanism where the books are balanced by passing the entries through internal inter-company accounts.

The user must be signed in to the relevant company or branch to input a transaction. However, in multi-branch, a user can be automatically switched from one branch to another before entering a transaction, which is controlled at the version level.

| Company A |  |
|---|---|
| Debit account A | Credit account A to B inter-company account |

In an extended multi-company, the sub-division code of the owning company is appended to the key of internal accounts. This is an automatic process and the conversion of existing internal accounts is not required.

As in current multi-company functionality, all Profit and Loss (PL) are booked in the company where the transaction takes place.


##### Retaining Original Accounting System for Interco entries

Based on the configuration set in the ACCOUNT.PARAMETER that is relevant to the Intercompany account product category, the Retain Orig Accting Sys in the INTERCO.PARAMETER determines whether inter-company accounting entries must follow the accounting system of the original PL entry or default.

If the field is set to,

- Yes - The inter-company accounting entry aligns with the accounting system of the originating PL entry.
- No - The accounting system for the inter-company entry is the configurations in ACCOUNT.PARAMETER , as applicable to the intercompany account product category.

This distinction ensures consistency in processing accounting entries and supports accurate financial reporting and compliance.

The system sets the ACCOUNT.PARAMETER for the Val Date Sys Id 1 = SCSP-SEC TRADE to follow the Trade Dated GL (TDGL) accounting system. It also configures the PL commission category to follow the Trade Dated, with the Val Date By Cat Sys 1.1 set to No in the accounting system.

For an SEC.TRADE transaction, when the user books a commission from one company to another, the system performs the below.

- PL entry is generated for the receiving company with the accounting system as Trade Dated.
- Raises corresponding inter-company accounting entries to balance the books across the companies.

If Retain Orig Accting Sys is set to,

- Yes - The inter-company accounting entries adopt the originating PL entry’s accounting system. For example - Trade Dated.
- No - The inter-company accounting entries follow the accounting system applicable to the Interco product category, based on the definition in the ACCOUNT.PARAMETER . For example - TDGL.


#### 📋 Tasks

There are no Tasks available for Inter-company Accounting feature.


#### 📊 Outputs

There are no Outputs available for Inter-company Accounting feature.


> **Related Applications:** `ACCOUNT.PARAMETER`, `INTERCO.PARAMETER`

### 12.5  Misc


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *Temenos Transact architecture supports the set-up of multiple company in one instance of Temenos Transact . The companies can operate independently or can share record types and certain files. Companies can also share the operation of Nostro accounts and Security Management System (SMS) in Temenos T...*
> 
> **Applications:** `BATCH`, `COMPANY`, `COMPANY.CREATE`, `INTERCO.PARAMETER`
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Deactivate*, *Default Company*
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction


#### 📖 Introduction

Related topics:

- Temenos Transact Services

Temenos Transact architecture supports the set-up of multiple company in one instance of Temenos Transact . The companies can operate independently or can share record types and certain files. Companies can also share the operation of Nostro accounts and Security Management System (SMS) in Temenos Transact , which maintains the security of access at company level. All these are covered separately in this guide.

The following types of company exists in the MCMB set up.

- Master Company – This is the first company setup in a Temenos Transact installation (normally BNK) and it owns a complete set of data tables. The master company can also be a lead company. The master company is present in all types of Temenos Transact environment.
- Lead Company – Sometimes called Parent Company. A lead company is defined on installation by indicating that the financial tables are to be owned by the company being created. Typically a Lead Company is used to represent a legal entity in the real world. It can have its own base currency and COB. It can be set up to share (or not) certain data sets with other companies. However, it will store all financial level data in its own set of tables.
- Branch Company – Sometimes called Book Company, is a typical Temenos Transact Company. It is always linked to a Lead Company. A branch always shares Lead Company’s Base currency, batch holiday table and COB. In a multi-branch set-up, all financial level data is held in the same single physical database as the Lead Company; although logically they are separated by the branch ID. For example, if there are 10 branches with the same Lead Company, there will be one Account table whereas if 10 branches are set up as lead companies, they will have 10 Account tables. A Branch can be linked to only one Lead Company. One Branch Company cannot be linked to another Branch Company. A branch always shares its local currency and batch holiday table with its lead company.

- Accounting Company – also called Accounting Unit. AU is an optional module and has a user guide of its own therefore not covered fully in this guide. The AU Functionality allows separate financial books to be maintained in a company or a branch. For example, a bank can produce books for individual business lines operating while still maintaining company as a whole. It shares the same currency, batch holiday table and COB similar to Branch company.

Transactions can take place between accounts in different companies using intercompany accounting functionality. Consolidated reporting, combined companies, can be produced using the consolidation functionality.


##### Sharing Information between Companies

The decision on what to share needs careful consideration as once set up, it cannot be changed. These decisions are taken when the system is initially installed before the system build begins.

The system classifies applications by the application type and are an inherent part of the system when installed. The classifications enable share/not share decisions when MCMB is set-up.

- The sharing options are available to lead companies.
- Branch companies will always share the files of the lead company.
- New companies can be added and existing companies can be decommissioned.
- Classification of the applications is delivered as part of the system build.

The following list explains each Application Type.

> **⚠️ Note:** Before installing the system, the decision to share information between the companies must be reached with the bank. The file classifications can then be adjusted through FILE.CONTROL.

| Application Type | Description |
|---|---|
| INT - Installation level | There is only one copy of installation level application in a Temenos Transact database, so the actual application name does not include a company mnemonic. The following are the examples of INT level application: COMPANY USER VERSION ENQUIRY |
| CUS - Customer level | The CUSTOMER and related applications includes the customer number in the key. Examples of CUS level application: CUSTOMER.DEFAULT LIMIT This type of application can be shared between lead companies. |
| CST - Customer tables | Parameter tables related to customer examples include INDUSTRY and SECTOR, together with parameter tables for limits, collateral and position management. This type of table can be shared between lead companies. |
| FIN - Financial | There is always one copy of a financial application for each lead company. All branches linked to a lead company share the same financial application. The following are the examples of FIN applications: ACCOUNT FUNDS.TRANSFER TELLER |
| FRP - Financial reporting | There is one copy of a financial application for every company in the system. For example, the COB job list applications and REPGEN work files (like RGP.TRANS.JOURNAL2). |
| FTD - Financial application definitions | Financial parameter applications that does not contain data with amounts or rates linked to a particular local currency. For example, GEN.CONDITION type tables and BASIC.INTEREST . This type of application can be shared between lead companies. |
| FTF - Financial application data | Financial parameter applications that contain financial data, often contain local currency amounts. The following are the example of FTF application: GROUP.DEBIT.INT GENERAL.CHARGE TAX This type of TAX application can be shared between lead companies. |
| CCY - Currency applications | Contains currency related information, for example, CURRENCY and PERIODIC.INTEREST . This type of application can be shared between lead companies. |
| NOS - Nostro applications | Applications related to Nostro accounts. For example, AGENCY and NOSTRO.ACCOUNT . This type of application can be shared between lead companies. |


##### Facilitating MCMB Environment

Facilitating MCMB environment requires a number of functions to be in place. These are:

- Grouping structure
- Intercompany accounting
- Branch Holiday
- Global Processing for COBs

Temenos Transact uses company codes to identify companies (if it is a lead company, a branch company or an accounting company). The format of the company code is CC GGG LLLL, where:

- CC is the country code.
- GGG is the company group code.
- LLLL is the local code.

> **⚠️ Note:** Local code must be different for each location or branch within one country, even if the processing is run in different environments.

The system facilitates grouping of operating companies into reporting groups. For example, a bank has operations in different countries and want to group them by these jurisdictions. Another bank wants to set up a regional group for all its branches in South of England and one for all its branches in North of England.

The group code is part of the 'T24 Company’ key and as such helps in identifying a particular operating company of 'T24 Companies’ that have been set up.

Thus for each of the T24 Company forming part of the same operating company, the group must be the same. Therefore, the same group codes need to be created at each of the locations where the organisation is operating the Temenos Transact system.

Thus, the COMPANY.GROUP code forms the centre portion of the individual records in COMPANY , for example, GB0010001.

Inter-company accounting is an important part of the configuration in an MCMB environment. It facilitates the accounting between companies set up in the environment - be it lead companies or branch companies.

When there are a large number of branches, multi-book accounting needs a large number of internal accounts, as each company needs an account with other company, potentially in many currencies. For this type of environment, it is better for the inter-company accounting to go through the head or regional office. So, only the head office holds an account with each branch so that an intercompany transaction is channeled through the Head Office. For example, Branch 1 has business with Branches 2, 3 and 4 in different currencies with each. Instead of Branch 1 having intercompany accounts with each of 2, 3 and 4 branches, it just has one account with its Head Office, which will channel the transactions to the other branches. Thus, reducing the number of intercompany accounts required.

In a multi-branch environment, there are possibilities that all branches might not follow the working practices of the lead company. For example, the head office may not work at weekends, whereas the branches may be working. This is facilitated in the COMPANY application and the following fields are available:

- Official Holiday – Indicates the business holiday table for the local country.
- Branch Holiday – Indicates the business holiday table for this company.
- Batch Holiday – Indicates the holiday table that controls the days on which the COB processing occurs.

For example, it is possible to setup the system to run the COB processing 365 days per year, with some branches open on weekends for restricted business activities.

> **⚠️ Note:** If a branch is open on an official holiday, then applications can be restricted at VERSION level.

Global processing allows the Close of Business (COB) processing in a multi-company environment to be run independently at the lead company or lead company group level. If the lead companies in a Temenos Transact instance are located in a variety of time zones, then the COB processing takes place at a convenient time for the relevant group or company, while the other members of the group are still online.

The global processing module also provides the following functionalities:

- Full transaction management in the end of day process.
- A resilient fault-tolerant end of day process (the system does stop due to an error with a contract).
- Use of online backups rather than traditional backup.
- Global processing functionality is restricted to lead companies, that is, all branches linked to a lead company are processed together.
- Ability to post accounting entries to companies that are offline from a company that is online.


##### Deactivation of Company

This functionality allows the users to deactivate a company in the Transact. To deactivate a company, the Deactivate field in the COMPANY application must be set to ‘Y’ in the respective COMPANY record at the database level by special IT maintenance operation team and the field is not available for manual input through any screen or API. Before deactivating a company, the bank needs to make sure,

- There should not be any cross-company transactions. All future dated transactions posted before the deactivation of the company does not take place once the company is deactivated.
- All background services and BATCH jobs must be shut down.
- No active users can log in into the system during the deactivation process.


###### Implications of Lead Company Deactivation

The restrictions, errors, and impact of deactivating a lead company in Transact are listed below:

- Users cannot create new transactions, contracts, accounts, customers, or arrangements and generate accounting for deactivated companies.
- Creating new data items, new tables and installing new products for deactivated companies are not allowed.
- When a lead company is deactivated, the branches of the lead company are automatically deactivated, and all services are stopped.
- Inter-company transactions and interfaces involving deactivated companies are restricted.
- Users cannot configure references to deactivated companies in the INTERCO.PARAMETER application.
- Automated services like OFS or user-initiated services and signing into deactivated companies are restricted.
- For transactions with a settlement account belonging to the deactivated company or its branches, an error message is triggered during validation or record commitment, preventing the transaction.
- During the creation of a new company in the COMPANY.CREATE application, if the Default Company field is set to the deactivated company, the system triggers an error message during validation or record commitment, preventing the creation of the new company.
- Upon receiving OFS instructions using the deactivated company code, the system returns an error message, rejecting the transaction.
- New records cannot be created using the mnemonic of the deactivated company in the BATCH application. The system triggers an error message and prevents the creation when trying to create a new record using the deactivated company mnemonic.
- Running COB for the deactivated company is not possible. The system does not initiate the COB process for the company, ensuring no batches or services are run. Any existing batch and service for a deactivated company will not run.
- When the user runs COB for all companies, the system runs batches or services only for active companies, skipping the deactivated company.

Read Multi Company Closure and Data Cleardown for more information on closure of one or multiple companies within a multi-company.


> **Related Applications:** `BATCH`, `COMPANY`, `COMPANY.CREATE`, `INTERCO.PARAMETER`

### 12.6  Nostro Accounts


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**

#### 📖 Introduction

In a multi-company or multi-book setup, the lead companies can share the Nostro accounts if the inter-company accounting is switched on. In this scenario, there will be a lead Nostro company. The NOSTRO.ACCOUNT application is maintained at the Nostro company level.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

There is no configuration content for this feature.


#### 🔧 Working With

Physical records in NOSTRO.ACCOUNT can be created in other company records in addition to the Nostro company.

BNK is the Nostro company, for Singapore and Switzerland branches. This means that all external payments go through the BNK company Nostro accounts. However, the other branches require the ability to have their own individual Nostro accounts in the local currency, to enable them to make local payments, which can include salary, expenses or payments to the Central bank. A sample local Nostro account is shown in the below screen shot.

The CCY.NOSTRO.ACCT application is updated with the new Nostro account.

When a local Nostro account is created, it should be added to the NOSTRO.ACCOUNT application in the Nostro company.

There are no restrictions in the system that prevent the use of local Nostro accounts by another company. However, this can be achieved by setting up FT version records as explained below:

- The FT version records specific to the individual companies can be created with unique records in FT.TXN.TYPE.CONDITION .
- Within the versions, the local Nostro account should be defaulted.
- These version records should be subsequently added locally to the relevant user menus.

### 12.7  Position Management

#### 📖 Introduction

Position management information is stored at different levels in different tables, as follows:

- At contract level in PM.TRAN.ACTIVITY table.
- At lead company level in PM.DLY.POSN.CLASS table.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

There is no configuration content for this feature.


#### 🔧 Working With

The key to PM.DLY.POSN.CLASS table is based on the following attributes:

- Position class
- Currency market
- Dealer desk
- Position type (fixed at TR)
- Currency
- Value date

A position management enquiry normally displays the information consolidated at lead company level. However, it is possible to combine the information from several lead companies in the same enquiry, if configured to do so.

Standard functionality is not available currently, to enable a position management enquiry to display the data consolidated at branch level, or it not possible to drill down to the data consolidated at branch level.

### 12.8  Transfer Contracts between Companies


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *Transfer of Accounts and Contracts is possible from one Branch to another or from one company to another provided they are part of the same group structure.*
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

Transfer of Accounts and Contracts is possible from one Branch to another or from one company to another provided they are part of the same group structure.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

There is no configuration content for this feature.


#### 🔧 Working With

This process is handled by EB.COMPANY.CHANGE . The user specifies the contract using its contract key and defines the new company to which they wish to be moved to. The actual movement is performed as part of the next COB process when all selected transactions, related records and live accounting entries are moved from the one company to the another company. Subsequent to moving a transaction from one company to another, the transaction will still be maintained and administered by the system as per the normal functionality associated with the contracts.

If an accounting event is generated by a transaction that has been moved between companies and if the account being called remains in the originating company, the system automatically raises INTERCO accounting entries.

In case of a maturing MM.MONEY.MARKET, an INTERCO credit is raised in the new company and a matching INTERCO debit is raised in the originating company along with the subsequent final credit to the depositories account.

The user should create a record in the STANDARD.MAPPING application for MM.MONEY.MARKET and FRA.DEAL. This defines the reference to the relevant transactional records, for example, by @ID and link any associated records that may also need to be moved between companies. That is, in case of MM.MONEY.MARKET the associated MM.PAYMENT.ENTRY, MM.RECEIPT.ENTRY and LMM.SCHEDULES applications are also moved. The Cont Move Chk Rtn field can be used to restrict the transaction movement of a specified type by applying a routine, for example, where MM.MONEY.MARKET transaction is the child of a REPO deal and transaction movement to another company is not possible.


#### 📋 Tasks

There are no Tasks available for Transfer of Contracts feature.

There are no Outputs available for Transfer of Contracts feature.

> **📇 Quick Reference Card**

#### 📖 Introduction

Temenos Transact architecture enables the setup of multiple companies within a single instance, allowing them to operate independently or share records and specific files as required.

The MCDCLR (Multi-Company Closure and Data Cleardown) feature ensures the secure closure of one or multiple companies within a multi-company Transact environment, followed by the removal of relevant data after a configurable retention period.

The key aspects of the functionality are:

- Data Retention with Controlled Access - During the retention period, the system allows optional restricted read-only access for authorised users.
- Regulatory Compliance - Efficiently addresses data privacy and compliance requirements by ensuring the timely removal of inactive company data, minimizing the risk of non-compliance.
- Cost Optimisation - By removing obsolete data and company instances, the feature reduces unnecessary storage costs, particularly in SaaS environments.

This functionality is particularly valuable in Business-as-a-Service (BaaS) or Software-as-a-Service (SaaS) implementations, where it ensures proper company deactivation and effective data management when agreements come to an end.


##### Clearing Down of Companies Marked as Deactivated

Previously, Temenos Transact did not have a dedicated module for managing company closures and data. Instead, an existing mechanism allowed users to manually set the Deactivate field to Y in the COMPANY application, rendering companies inactive. This process prevented further contracts or updates from being processed for the deactivated entities.

The Company Closure functionality allows the system to automate the update of the Deactivate field. This field is updated automatically when the system processes a Closure Request, replacing the need for manual intervention


##### Business Events

When the Emit Business Event field in MS.PARAMETER is set as Yes, the business events representing the state change are emitted.

The following business events are emitted for Static Information data or Reference data tables.

| Business Event | Description |
|---|---|
| ReferenceData.closeCompany.companyClosureRequestApproved | Event to be emitted when a Company Closure Request is authorised. |
| ReferenceData.closeCompany.companyClosureRequestCancelled | Event to be emitted when a Company Closure Request is reversed. |
| ReferenceData.closeCompany.companyClosureRequestModified | Event to be emitted when a Company Closure Request is modified. |

### 13.1  Cleardown of ClosedCompanies


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *The Cleardown process in Transact involves:*
> 
> **Applications:** `BATCH`, `COMPANY`, `DE.ADDRESS`, `MCDCLR.APPLN.CLEARDOWN`, `MCDCLR.COMPANY.DEACTIVATE`
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Data*, *Deactivate*, *Exc Cleardown*
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

The Cleardown process in Transact involves:

- Worklist Generation - Upon expiration of the retention period, an automated service generates a worklist of files to be cleared. This list includes all the files that are owned by the deactivated companies.
- Cleardown Execution - The system processes the worklist with the invocation of database scripts and file deletion process to remove the specified files.
- Auditing and Logging - Every step of the cleardown is logged, providing a detailed audit trail for compliance verification.
- Error Handling - If discrepancies or errors occur during the process, they are flagged, and logged for action by the administrators.

Currently, the files that are owned by the respective deactivated companies are allowed to be cleared down. This includes FIN, FTD, FRP,CUS,CST, FTF, and FTD file types.

The MCDCLR.APPLN.CLEARDOWN application in the MCDCLR module allows to exclude any file from the above types in case one wants to retain it for various reasons. The cleardown of closed companies is a vital process in:

- Ensuring regulatory compliance and data security
- Optimising storage costs in cloud-based architectures
- Enhancing the system performance by removing redundant data


#### ⚙️ Configuration

This section describes the configuration of clear down exclusions and alerts in TAFJ.


##### Configuring Cleardown Exclusions

The fields in the MCDCLR.APPLN.CLEARDOWN are as follows:

> **⚠️ Note:** @ID – The record is keyed by the file name.

Currently, any file type other than FIN, FRP, FTD, CUS, CST, FTF is not allowed.

This is not a mandatory parameter required for the cleardown process. The bank can choose to configure this table in case any file is required to be retained within the database.

| Field Name | Description |
|---|---|
| Exc Cleardown | The field denotes whether the Transact table is excluded from the cleardown process. Allowed option is Yes. |


##### Configuring Alerts in TAFJ for Company Cleanup

This section describes the configurations that needs to be done for the warning message to be raised upon successful creation of the worklist for a Company Closure Request.

In the TAFJ.properties (or the required properties file), set the property temn.tafj.runtime.enable.custom.logger=true .

1. In the TAFJTrace.properties, append the loggers ALERT_COMPANYCLEANUP,DIAGNOSTIC_COMPANYCLEANUP to the existing ones and set the log level to DEBUG.
2. Add company_cleanup in the appender and set the path as shown below to capture the log..


#### 🔧 Working With

As mentioned in the configuration section, once the company closure request is authorised, a future dated trigger is updated in the system to schedule the company's deactivation on the specified deactivation date.

During the deactivation day COB, the system safely closes the company (or companies within the request) and marks the Deactivate field in COMPANY application to Y.


##### Worklist Queue Generation

After the deactivation date has passed and the company/companies have been safely closed, the MCDCLR.COMP.DEACTIVATION.FILE.LIST service must be run to generate the worklist queue in MCDCLR.COMPANY.APPLN.WORKLIST.

This service identifies and collates a list of files that need to be removed from the database for all companies included in the request. The worklist can only be generated after the deactivation date to ensure the company has been safely deactivated and can now be cleared down.

Each worklist ID is uniquely identified by the following structure:

Company Code – Deactivation Date – Cleardown Date – Request ID

The worklist contains a comprehensive list of files for deletion, including all applicable file types such as $NAU, $HIS, $SIM, $DEL, $ARC, and the live file itself. All the files of the type FIN, FRP, FTD, CUS, CST, FTF for a company are included in this list by default unless specified in MCDCLR.APPLN.CLEARDOWN as excluded.

The generated worklist is non-modifiable, that is, no changes can be made to the file list once the queue is updated and the list is updated based on the configuration available in the system at the time of running of the service.

Once the worklist is created for all the companies in a request, the system generates a TAFJ log (available only with the configuration mentioned above), notifying that the list is ready for cleardown on the specified cleardown date.

The generated worklist is then fed into a database script for execution. This script handles the deletion of files as per the details in the worklist and needs to be executed separately.

For a single company closure request, it is possible to have multiple worklists keyed by the Company ID. The below enquiry aids in tracking and management of files across different companies included in the request based on Company or Request ID or Cleardown date

File Cleardown Worklist

Drilldown further to view the worklist. Note that this contains only the list of files that are fed to the database script for clearing.


##### Cleardown Execution

Data cleardown happens at two levels in this process. First, purge services in Transact clear records from shared INT files. Then, the database script deletes company specific files such as FIN, FRP, FTD, CUS, CST, and FTF. It is recommended to run the purge services first, followed by the database script, to ensure consistent and complete removal of data.

| Parameters | Description |
|---|---|
| Execution Status | Indicates whether the process passed or encountered issues during execution. |
| Company Code | Indicates the code of the company whose files are being cleared. |
| Cleardown Date | Indicates the date when the files are eligible for deletion based on the retention policy. |
| Total Files Selected | Indicates the total number of files identified for deletion during the process in the worklist |
| Total Files Deleted | Indicates the total number of files successfully removed from the system. |

The below end-of-process services from Delivery Module are reused to remove company specific records from inward and outward files.

- DE.EOP.INWARD
- DE.EOP.OUTWARD

In addition to the above files, records with sensitive information such as DE.ADDRESS are also deleted during the company data purging process.

These services are manually triggered using the MCDCLR.COMPANY.DEACTIVATE Request ID in the Data field of the respective BATCH records as shown below.

- The Company Closure functionality uses Request ID instead of Purge Date for triggering the purging services for company closure functionality.
- Both Request ID-based purging (for Company Closure) and Date-based purging (for generic file archiving) cannot be used together.
- Multiple Request IDs can be given in one go (by multivaluing the Data field) while running the service provided the cleardown date for all the requests have passed.
- After successful execution of the service, the processed request IDs are removed from the batch record by the system. If there are any errors or a request ID is not processed because the cleardown date is not passed, then the request ID is retained in the Data field of the BATCH record.

As part of the company closure functionality, these services also remove data from the archived $ARC tables, if available. If the cleardown date has not passed, no records are removed, and exception logs are raised (with the appropriate setup in SPF).

The service execution logs are available in the default COMO folder for reference.


##### Cleardown of Already Deactivated Companies

Read Company Closure Request for Deactivated Companies to initiate clearing down of already deactivated companies by raising a Company Closure request.

The process flow is the same after the Company Closure Request is created.


#### 📋 Tasks

There are no Tasks available for the Cleardown of Closed Companies feature.


#### 📊 Outputs

### 13.2  Closing of Company


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *The deactivation date marks the point at which the specified company or companies become inoperable in the system. On this date, the system automatically enforces various restrictions and operational changes to ensure that deactivated companies no longer interact with active processes or data flows.*
> 
> **Applications:** `COMPANY`, `PROTOCOL`
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Deactivate*
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

The deactivation date marks the point at which the specified company or companies become inoperable in the system. On this date, the system automatically enforces various restrictions and operational changes to ensure that deactivated companies no longer interact with active processes or data flows.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

There is no specific configuration for this feature.


#### 🔧 Working With

This section helps the user to understand the working of closing or deactivating companies.

During the COB on the deactivation day, the system safely closes the company (or companies within the request) and marks the Deactivate field in COMPANY application to Y. The system allows the COB to be finished for the day after which no changes including date cycling takes place in the deactivated companies.


##### Permanence of Deactivation

Once a company is deactivated, it cannot be reactivated. The system prevents new contracts or updates from being made in the deactivated company. It also blocks new data releases and restricts access to the company using OFS or GAI. Mechanisms for upgrades, updates, and product installations ensure that no data is released in the deactivated company.


##### Disabling Background Services

Once the deactivation date is reached, background services linked to the deactivated company automatically stop. The user cannot create records in BATCH, TSA.SERVICE, or TSA.SERVICES.COB for the deactivated company. Services linked to the deactivated company cannot be set to START/AUTO.

The COB (Close of Business) process running on the deactivation date will continue to completion. However, after COB completion, auto services for the deactivated company will no longer run, and the service control is set to STOP.


##### Restricted Access During the Retention Period

During the retention period, the system permits GET APIs with restricted access but disallows PUT/POST for updating tables belonging to the deactivated company. Access to records from the deactivated company through enquiry is also restricted.

The READONLY attribute in the USER profile allows users requiring restricted access to deactivated companies during the retention period. Only users with the READONLY attribute can log into deactivated companies during this period.

Users with the READONLY attribute can perform the following functions:

- E (Exceptions)
- L (List)
- S (See)
- P (Print)

The system strictly prohibits the Input, Validate, Audit, Authorize, Copy, Reverse, or Delete actions, even for users with the READONLY attribute. Any attempts to perform these actions are logged in the PROTOCOL application for audit purposes.


#### 📋 Tasks

There are no Tasks available for the Closing of Company feature.


#### 📊 Outputs

There are no Outputs available for the Closing of Company feature.


> **Related Applications:** `COMPANY`, `PROTOCOL`

### 13.4  Scheduling of Company Closure


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *The Company Closure application, MCDCLR.COMPANY.DEACTIVATE is the primary tool to initiate and manage the closure process in a Transact multi-company environment.*
> 
> **Applications:** `COMPANY`, `COMPANY.DEACTIVATE.TRIGGER`, `MCDCLR.COMPANY.DEACTIVATE`
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Assoc Companies*, *Comp
 Deactivated*, *Comp Deactivated*, *Data Cleardown Date*, *Data Ret Period*, *Deactivate*, *Deactivation Date*
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

The Company Closure application, MCDCLR.COMPANY.DEACTIVATE is the primary tool to initiate and manage the closure process in a Transact multi-company environment.

Key features of the Company Closure application are:

| Feature | Description |
|---|---|
| Closure Scheduling | Selects the companies to be closed and specify the date from which they will become inactive. |
| Retention Period Configuration | Sets the duration for which the company’s data should be retained before permanent deletion. |

The MCDCLR.COMPANY.DEACTIVATE application ensures a smooth and compliant execution of the company closure process by enabling efficient scheduling and data retention management.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

This section details the fields in MCDCLR.COMPANY.DEACTIVATE used for configuring the setup.


##### Configuring Companies for Deactivation

The table below lists the fields required to configure companies for deactivation.

| Field Name | Description |
|---|---|
| Comp Deactivated | Enter the lead company or companies to be deactivated in this field. It supports adding multiple companies to the same list. Refer the Working With section for more information on the business validations of this field. |
| Assoc Companies | This informational field updates automatically to display the branch companies associated with the lead company or companies specified in the Comp Deactivated field. |

> **⚠️ Note:** @ID – The record is keyed by a unique reference.


##### Configuring Date and Retention Period

The table below lists the fields required to configure the date and retention period.

| Field Name | Description |
|---|---|
| Deactivation Date | Specifies the date after which the company (and associated companies in the request) becomes inoperable. |
| Data Ret Period | Denotes the retention period for which data in the deactivated companies are retained. The default value is 1M (one month), and valid inputs must follow the format for months or years (for example, 3M, 5Y). |
| Data Cleardown Date | This non-editable field represents the calendar date calculated by applying the retention period to the deactivation date. After this date, the system removes the data for the specified companies, making it unavailable. |


#### 🔧 Working With

The system permits the closure of a company within the Transact Multi Company environment under the following conditions:

- The company must be a valid lead company that is not designated as a MASTER company.
- All associated branch companies (or accounting companies) within the lead company are automatically included in the closure list by default.
- The company can be closed if it operates independently, without sharing its customer table or currency table with another active company.
- If multiple companies share the customer or currency table, they must all be included in the same closure request.
- In case of companies sharing financial files and descriptive files, like FTF, FTD, CST, the system allows deactivation of the companies using the file separately or together with the company holding the file itself. However, the main company holding the file cannot be closed separately as the sharing companies refer to it. Having said that, the system still allows closure of the main company if all the companies sharing its file are fully deactivated and not just scheduled for closure.
- The company must not be part of any Intercompany (Interco) accounting setup or definition.
- For all companies in the request, the deactivation date must be greater than today's date.
- For companies already marked as deactivated, a deactivation date of TODAY is permitted, as the request is only to capture the deactivation for future cleardown.


##### Creating a Company Closure Request

Company Closure Request , and follow the steps below:

1. Click the new deal icon for a system-generated record (ID).
2. Enter the relevant details as shown below.
3. After entering all the relevant data, commit the request and send it for authorisation. The unauthorised requests are available in the Authorise/Amend/Delete Closure Request tab for authorisation, amendment or deletion. The authorised requests that have not reached the deactivation date are available in the View/Modify Scheduled Closure Request tab for modification or cancellation. Reversing or amending a request is allowed only before the deactivation date. Once the deactivation date has passed, no further changes to the request are permitted.
4. Once a request is successfully authorised, the system creates a future-dated trigger in the COMPANY.DEACTIVATE.TRIGGER file. On the specified deactivation date, the system picks up this trigger to initiate the deactivation process for the listed companies.


##### Creating a Company Closure Request for Deactivated Companies

The cleardown process for companies marked as deactivated (where the Deactivate field in COMPANY is set to Y), can be triggered using the MCDCLR.COMPANY.DEACTIVATE application.

The user can specify a deactivation date, which can either be the current date (the date of capture), or a future date greater than today. The cleardown process will begin once the deactivation date is set and the specified data retention period has passed.

In the below example, the company GB0020001 has already been deactivated by the old method of setting the Deactivate field in COMPANY to Y.

The user can still submit a closure request for these companies to clear the data. In such cases, the system allows a deactivation date of TODAY (for example, 17th May) or any date greater than today.


#### 📋 Tasks

There are no Tasks available for the Scheduling of Company Closure feature.


#### 📊 Outputs

There are no Outputs available for the Scheduling of Company Closure feature.

### 14.2  Daily Position Class


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *PM.DLY.POSN.CLASS is a system created file, which is a breakdown of each PM.TRAN.ACTIVITY record into individual activities. The record key comprises of a key, equal to the related PM.POSN.CLASS ID, along with the currency market, dealer desk, position type, currency and value date.*
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Booking Date*, *Value Date*
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

PM.DLY.POSN.CLASS is a system created file, which is a breakdown of each PM.TRAN.ACTIVITY record into individual activities. The record key comprises of a key, equal to the related PM.POSN.CLASS ID, along with the currency market, dealer desk, position type, currency and value date.

Asset and liability splits the data held in each record, along with and also has amounts, rates (where Fixed), or a pointer to the relevant rate table, and a rate/amount calculation. For each activity with the same key, totals are accumulated and consolidated into a single record.

- If individual activities have stored rates, values are consolidated and an average rate is calculated.
- If activities have rate indicators, it is consolidated only by similar indicators.

As each movement is added to the enquiry, the transaction reference is appended to each record and provides a reference to each of the PM.TRAN.ACTIVITY records.


#### 🔧 Working With

The process after generating PM.TRAN.ACTIVITY is to split the records, so that each of the activities is created as a single PM.DLY.POSN.CLASS record. Records with identical keys are consolidated into a single record as part of the splitting process.

All matured data is removed from the PM.DLY.POSN.CLASS , after checking the value date on the record key and deleting the record when the value date is less than the next working day. Transactions input into Temenos Transact during the COB have a booking date of the next working day. The booking date is included in the key, and checked whether the booking and value dates are less than the next working day.

Below is a list of PM.DLY.POSN.CLASS record IDs along with an individual record with a booking date:

PM.DRILL.DOWN is a key-only file to hold the drill down data for the PM.DLY.POSN.CLASS records. This key is made up of the first six elements of the PM.DLY.POSN.CLASS key followed by the transaction key. The booking date is shown in this key for non-stop transactions booked during the COB.

In the example below, the Value Date is 8th and Booking Date is 10th.


#### 📋 Tasks

There are no Tasks available for Daily Position Class feature.


#### 📊 Outputs

This topic helps the user to view the enquiries and reports of Daily Position Class feature.


##### Enquiries and Reports

This section allows the user to view the below list of enquiries and reports:

Discounted P&L Analysis

This enquiry determines the Net Present Value (NPV) of Profit or loss, assuming that Placing and Taking across different time buckets are closed out at the market rates.

Duration Analysis

This enquiry determines the ASSET, LIAB and NET duration of the cash flows in different time buckets with the total of net durations across different time buckets.

Forex Position and Break Even Analysis

This enquiry displays the buying and selling average rates with the break-even exchange rate for the net foreign currency position displayed across different time buckets.

Interest Mismatch (GAP) Position

This enquiry displays the asset and liability average interest rate with the break-even interest rate for the currency across different time buckets.

Net Present Value Analysis

This enquiry displays the NPV of cash flow by using the,

- Appropriate rates from different time bucket
- Concept of time value of money.

It also provides the actual total cash flow and the present value of the actual cash flow.

Position Movements Today

This enquiry displays the position movement entries for a selected currency for the day. The user has options to view the details.

Position Movements Yesterday

This enquiry displays the Position Movement entries for the previous working day for a selected currency. The user can view the individual transaction records which hit the position.
