### 16.19  Misc


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *The Transaction Recycler provides the ability to retry failed financial transactions again at regular intervals. This is a generic retry mechanism which can be consumed by any Temenos Transact application. The Transaction Recycler is available for Arrangement Architecture (AA) and Interest and Charg...*
> 
> **Applications:** `AA.PARAMETER`, `MS.PARAMETER`, `RC.CONTRACT.PRIORITY`
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Aa Product*, *Aa Product Group*, *Attribute Type*, *Attribute Value*, *Create Retry Trigger*, *Custom Priority Rank*, *Date Convention*, *Def Prev Settle* ... +33 more
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction


#### 📖 Introduction

Related topics:

- Temenos Transact Services

The Transaction Recycler provides the ability to retry failed financial transactions again at regular intervals. This is a generic retry mechanism which can be consumed by any Temenos Transact application. The Transaction Recycler is available for Arrangement Architecture (AA) and Interest and Charged (IC) modules (R13 release and above). Read Transaction Cycler section under Settlement Property Class for more information related to Arrangement Architecture.

The Transaction Recycler service handles the retry of failed transactions. This service will run as a COB job at a specific stage during both End of Day (EOD) and online phases. This job will retry the transactions on scheduled dates until the transaction is settled or number of retry attempts allowed have been exhausted or retry end date is reached.

During each retry, the Transaction Recycler will take the amount available in the settlement account for settling the transaction amount in full or partial, based on the Transaction Recycler retry configuration. The RC can retry the settlement based on pre-defined priority order as defined by the bank. In case of an AA loan repayment, the RC.CONTRACT.PRIORITY application allows the user to define sorting priority criteria based on custom values - the bill type or the aging status of bill.

The transactions handed over to Recycler (RC), if settled outside the RC framework are not excluded from further processing by RC and is marked with a specific status.

The following chart shows the transaction recycler process:

The Transaction Recycler acts as a framework and the processing required for retrying an AA payment or IC charges is built as a plug-in. In the above flow chart, the core plug-ins are generally represented as the payment processor, and the RC processes further, when there is an AA payment or an IC payment pending. The Transaction Recycler recognises that two different types of payments should be processed and the respective payment processor invoked is parameterised. This design enables the addition of new activity types (including any client-specific local activities) to be retried while using the same Transaction Recycler framework to orchestrate the recycling.


##### Product Configuration

The following chart shows the Transaction Recycler module components:

| Core Routine Fields | Description | Routine Name |
|---|---|---|
| Pre processor | Used to define whether a message specific core routine needs to be called to pre-process a message. | RC.PREP.RC.TYPE – For example, RC.PREP.IC.CHARGE |
| Prioritise | Used to define the message-specific core routine called by the Transaction Recycler to perform transaction grouping and sorting. | RC.PRTY.RC.TYPE – For example, RC.PRTY.IC.CHARGE |
| Processor | Used to define the message-specific core routine called by the Transaction Recycler to process the Transaction Recycler transaction, or transactions if they are grouped. | RC.PROC.RC.TYPE – For example, RC.PROCE.IC.CHARGE |
| Post process | Defines the message-specific API routine called by the Transaction Recycler to perform processing after the transaction has been completed. | RC.POST.RC.TYPE – For example, RC.POST.IC.CHARGE |

The RC.PRIORITY application is a highest level prioritisation parameter that allows to setup priority of transactions at the company level by EB.SYSTEM.ID or AA.PRODUCT.GROUP . This application is used in conjunction with RC.PRODUCT.PRIORITY and RC.CONTRACT.PRIORITY to create the rules regarding which type of transaction takes priority when there is more than one outstanding transaction against a settlement account. It ranks by EB.SYSTEM.ID , by AA.PRODUCT.GROUP or by a custom RC.PRODUCT.PRIORITY record and the ID to this application can be either a master or a lead company.

In the RC.PRIORITY application, the order of priorities are defined in the descending order (for example, the first definition has the highest priority and so on).

- In the above screenshot, the system is set up to consider the transactions in the following order, if multiple retry requests are posted against the same account:First: Products defined in the RC.PRODUCT.PRIORITY application in the PRIORITY+ONE record (direct debits sent by TPH with transaction code 125).

- Second: Products defined in the RC.PRODUCT.PRIORITY application in the MORTAGES record (MORTGAGE AA Product and then MORTGAGE.CASHBACK AA Product).

- Third: Products defined in the RC.PRODUCT.PRIORITY application in the PRIORITY +TPH record (direct debits sent by TPH with transaction code 213).

- Fourth: Request posted by the PAYMENT.ORDER application, irrespective of the request type.

When using as a priority, either a System ID (an EB.SYSTEM.ID record), the system does not require a correspondent RC.PRODUCT.PRIORITY record. If the RC.PRODUCT.PRIORITY record is not defined, it will process all retry transaction requests posted by the application in a default order, considering the oldest one received by the recycler first.

> **⚠️ Note:** The system allows only one option for each priority to be entered. This can either be an EB.SYSTEM.ID, an AA.PRODUCT.GROUP or a Product Priority (custom RC.PRODUCT.PRIORITY ID ).

Def Prev Settle is a filtering rule that means if, out of a list of ‘n’ pending transactions, one of transactions could not be settled (during retry), then all subsequent pending transactions in that list will be abandoned. It could be set to either Yes or No or left blank. If selected, it is applicable for EB.SYSTEM.ID , AA.PRODUCT.GROUP or Product Priority. This field is mutually exclusive with Prev Settle field.

The Prev Settle field can be set as Yes or No. If set to Yes, during retry of ‘n’ transactions, all transactions must be settled. Even if one of the transactions fail for some reason, then none of the remaining transactions will be considered for settlement.

The RC.CONTRACT.PRIORITY application is used in conjunction with RC.PRIORITY and RC.PRODUCT.PRIORITY to create the rules regarding the type of transaction that takes priority when there is more than one outstanding transaction against a settlement account. The RC.CONTRACT.PRIORITY is used to set the ranks at transaction level for the same type of retry request. It is used to set priority by value date, transaction amount or by a custom setting, for example by bills overdue status sent to Recycler by Arrangement Architecture (AA).

For example, if there are several transactions for the same product type against the settlement account, then the transactions have to be prioritised.

- The oldest transactions are processed first.
- If there are more than one transaction due for the same date and type, then prioritise by the largest amount first.

The RC.CONTRACT.PRIORITY application allows the user to define sorting priority criteria based on custom values. For example, based on the bills’ status issued by AA in case of loans repayments. To perform this, set:

- Due Type - Sort By Priority Attribute
- Due Rule - Custom

The Priority Rank Type field in RC.CONTRACT.PRIORITY accepts the following three options:

- Aging Status - Enables prioritisation based on the aging status of bills generated for each arrangement.
- Bill Type - Enables prioritisation of bill ( RC.DETAIL ) records based on the bill type of the arrangements.
- Blank – The value is used if the prioritization is by Aging Status of the bills.

It is not possible to set the prioritization by both Aging Status /Blank and Bill Type in the same record.

The multi-valued Custom Priority Rank field must contain custom values in the order which they must be sorted. Based on the Custom Priority Rank the Custom Priority Rank field must contain valid EB.LOOKUP record values from AA.OVERDUE.STATUS or from AA.BILL.TYPE .

In the example below, the custom values represent the overdue bill’s status based on aging / bill type as they are sent by AA to Recycler, to process the retry requests.

> **⚠️ Note:** It is not possible to set the prioritization by both Aging Status / Blank and Bill Type in the same record.

The overdue status is shown in the RC.DETAIL record after the request is settled.

> **⚠️ Note:** The AA Payment Rules setup must be in sync with the setup done in the Recycler priority setup tables. For example, if the oldest bill setup is done in AA Payment Rules, the same setup must be done in the recycler.

For example, if the Payment Rules are setup to consider the oldest bill first for an AA Product, and for the same AA Product, the contract priority rule is setup to consider the largest amount first (different setup than in Payment Rules), the system works as follows:

- If two bills are issued for the same contract on the same date, the system settles the bills by date (oldest one first) ignoring the ‘By amount’ setup in the recycler.
- If two bills are issued for the same contract on different dates, the system settles the bills considering the ‘By amount’ setup in the recycler.
- If two bills are issued for different contracts on different dates, the system settles the bills considering the ‘By amount’ setup in the recycler.
- If two bills are issued for different contracts on the same date, the system settles the bills by date (oldest one first) ignoring the ‘By amount’ setup in the recycler.

The user can define product priorities based on contract custom criteria using the RC.PRODUCT.PRIORITY application. If the user wants to define such priority, the Rank Based Priority field must be defined with the RC.CONTRACT.PRIORITY custom name. If this is set, the order defined in RC.CONTRACT.PRIORITY is applied to all products setup in RC.PRODUCT.PRIORITY . For example, it is possible to define custom priority criteria based on bills overdue status and based on product type. The bills overdue status should be setup first in the RC.CONTRACT.PRIORITY application as a custom record (read the RC.CONTRACT.PRIORITY for more details).

In order to sort the retry request based on the setup in RC.CONTRACT.PRIORITY and the one in the product order defined in RC.PRODUCT.PRIORITY , Priority Execution field must be defined. The values in this field are ’Rank Then Product’ and ’Product Then Rank’.

If the value ’Rank Then Product’ is selected, if more than one retry request is posted against the same account, the system orders requests based on the rank (status) defined in RC.CONTRACT.PRIORITY first and then by the product as defined in RC.CONTRACT.PRIORITY . If the value ’Product Then Rank’ is selected, the system orders the requests by product first and then by their rank from the RC.CONTRACT.PRIORITY application.

The following screenshot shows the RC.PRODUCT.PRIORITY is created with the value ’Rank Then Product’.

The RC.CONTRACT.PRIORITY custom record ‘MORTGAGELOANS’ has the setup as shown in the below screenshot.

The RC.PRODUCT.PRIORITY record is setup to order the requests according to the rank (status) first and then according to the product order (MORTGAGE.LOANS.USD and then MORTGAGE.LOANS.1Y), if more than one request has the same rank (status).

In case the RC.PRODUCT.PRIORITY record has a custom ID and if the Priority Execution field is defined with the value ’Rank Then Product’, the Aa Product Group field will become multivalued, allowing the definition of priorities based on products which are part of different AA PRODUCT GROUPS in the same record.

The input of Aa Product Group field is mandatory in case any Aa Product are defined. The Aa Product definition is not mandatory if the Aa Product Group is entered. If only the Aa Product Group is defined, the system considers all the retry requests posted by any product type within the product group and orders them by date (the oldest one is considered first). It is not possible to define a duplicate combination of Aa Product Group and Aa Product of the same type in the same record.

The online recycler checks for the following:

- New triggers on the accounts with active retry requests.
- Retry request for which the cut off time has passed.

The RC.PARAMETER application controls the retry trigger and the Create Retry Trigger field can have one of the following options:

- Any Credit – The system creates a retry trigger ( RC.RETRY.TRIGGER table application) for any credit posted on the account.
- Credit Balance – The system creates a retry trigger only if the new credit makes the account balance positive.

In the OVERRIDE record, ACCT.UNAUTH.OD, the Susp Appln field and Fwd Acct Mode should to be configured, as shown in the example below:

| Scenario 1 Schedule Initiation on Holiday parameter is configured | Scenario 2 Schedule Initiation on Holiday parameter is not configured |
|---|---|
| Transaction Recycler retries the transaction to settle the bill. System checks the value date when the settlement account received the funds. As it is backdated, RC settles the bill with value date on Saturday. Penalty interest accrued for Saturday and Sunday is reversed, and only one day of penalty interest is applied to the contract. Bill is settled & Contract status = Current, as of Saturday. | Transaction Recycler retries the transaction to settle the bill. System checks the value date when the settlement account received the funds. As it is backdated, RC settles the bill with the value date on Saturday. Age Overdue activity is reversed and not replayed. Total amount for which the customer is charged = Instalment amount + One day’s penalty. Due to the reversal of the ageing activities, the penalty interest is posted to UNC/remainder activity. |


##### Business Events

When the Emit Business Event field in MS.PARAMETER is set as ‘Yes’, the business events representing the state change are emitted.

The following business events are emitted for Transaction Recycler.

| Business Event | Description |
|---|---|
| settlementService.transactionRetry.currentRetry | Event to be emitted when the transaction retry is moved to current status |
| settlementService.transactionRetry.fundRecovered | Event to be emitted for a transaction retry when the funds are recovered successfully |
| settlementService.transactionRetry.fundReserved | Event to be emitted for a transaction retry when the funds are reserved successfully |
| settlementService.transactionRetry.manuallyApproved | Event to be emitted when a transaction is manually approved |
| settlementService.transactionRetry.retryCancelled | Event to be emitted when the transaction retry is cancelled |
| settlementService.transactionRetry.retryCompleted | Event to be emitted when the transaction retry is completed |
| settlementService.transactionRetry.retryCreated | Event to be emitted when the transaction retry is created |


> **Related Applications:** `AA.PARAMETER`, `MS.PARAMETER`, `RC.CONTRACT.PRIORITY`

### 16.20  Processing Block Funds Using Tran Recycler


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *The feature to capture and recover the locked amount from the account using Transaction Recycler mechanism is enabled for both manual and automatic block of funds.*
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Block Funds*, *Def Block Funds*, *From Date*, *Id*, *Retry End Date*, *System*, *To Date*
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

The feature to capture and recover the locked amount from the account using Transaction Recycler mechanism is enabled for both manual and automatic block of funds.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

The Def Block Funds field is an optional field maintained at the product level to decide if AC.LOCKED.EVENTS record has to be created, when Transaction Recycler captures a debit transaction for retry on later date. This displays values of Yes or No or blank (no values).

- When the field is set to NO, the AC.LOCKED.EVENTS is not created during capture process. The default value is NULL and this is same as NO.
- When the field is set to YES, the AC.LOCKED.EVENTS is created during capture process for the transaction amount. The From Date field is updated with the transaction date and To Date field is updated with Retry End Date from the RC.DETAIL table.

The Block Funds is a multi-value field associated with System Id field. It is an optional field that helps determine if a failed transaction captured by RC is required to create an AC.LOCKED.EVENTS record, if the transaction’s EB.SYSTEM.ID application matches with the one defined in the RC.CAPTURE application. This field can be set to YES, NO or left blank.

- When the value is set to Yes, the AC.LOCKED.EVENTS record is created when a captured transaction’s EB.SYSTEM.ID matches with the one defined in RC.CAPTURE .
- When the value is set to No, the AC.LOCKED.EVENTS record is not created. The default value is null, same as No value.


#### 📋 Tasks

There are no Tasks available for Processing Blocked Funds using Transaction Recycler feature.


#### 📊 Outputs

There are no Outputs available for Processing Blocked Funds using Transaction Recycler feature.

### 16.21  Retry Online Processing Based on Account Triggers


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *When processing retry requests, the Recycler online service checks for the triggers created for accounts that have pending Retry request to recover the unpaid bills. The triggers for accounts are created when a credit is received in the account or if a locked amount is released, decreased or expired...*
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Create Retry Trigger*
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

When processing retry requests, the Recycler online service checks for the triggers created for accounts that have pending Retry request to recover the unpaid bills. The triggers for accounts are created when a credit is received in the account or if a locked amount is released, decreased or expired.


#### ⚙️ Configuration


##### Configuring Credit Triggers in Accounts

The RC.PARAMETER application controls the retry trigger and the Create Retry Trigger field can have one of the following options:

- Any Credit – The system creates a retry trigger (in the RC.RETRY.TRIGGER application) for any credit posted on the account.
- Credit Balance – The system creates a retry trigger only if the new credit makes the account balance positive.

The setup is done at Temenos Transact Company level.


##### Configuring for Locked Amount Release, Decrease or Expiration

Configuration is not required as the system creates this trigger whenever a release, decrease or expiration of a locked amount is posted for an account using the AC.LOCKED.EVENTS application, which has pending retry requests.


#### 📋 Tasks

There are no Tasks available for Retry Online Processing Based on Account Triggers feature.


#### 📊 Outputs

There are no Outputs available for Retry Online Processing Based on Account Triggers feature.

### 16.22  Retry Processing from Multiple Account


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *When multiple pay-in accounts are defined for a loan arrangement and the retry condition is indicated, the system tries the settlement of the unpaid bill amounts from each settlement account, according to the defined rules. If the recycler condition is enabled for an account, the settlement is hande...*
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Update Pending Retry*
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

When multiple pay-in accounts are defined for a loan arrangement and the retry condition is indicated, the system tries the settlement of the unpaid bill amounts from each settlement account, according to the defined rules. If the recycler condition is enabled for an account, the settlement is handed off to the recycler process when the bill is due.

The recycler tries to recover the funds for the unpaid bills from the first settlement account and if there are no sufficient funds, the recycler continues with the next settlement account until the bill is fully recovered.

The user can add, remove or make a change in the order of the settlement accounts defined in the settlement property. This functionality can be applied to both newly created retry requests and existing ones, which are in pending for recovering unpaid bills.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

For the recycler to be able to retry the requests for the same bill from multiple accounts, the accounts must be defined at the arrangement level in the pay-in side, in the order in which they should be considered for processing.

The accounts that are defined as settlement accounts must be opened in the same Transact Company as the loan arrangement. The settlement rule must be set to Partial and the amount or percentage is not defined.

> **⚠️ Note:** The AA Payment Rules setup must be in sync with the setup done in the recycler priority setup tables. For example, if the oldest bill setup is done in AA Payment Rules, then the same setup must be done in the Recycler.

If a change of the settlement accounts is required, this can be done by updating the AA Settlement activity. If the change should also be applied for the retry requests that are already created in the system for that arrangement, the Update Pending Retry field should be set to Yes. The retry option is applicable for both the Partial and None rules, which is defined at the level of the AA Arrangement and only if the effective date is a back date or is equal to the current business date.


#### 📋 Tasks

There are no Tasks available for Retry Process for Multiple Settlement Accounts feature.


#### 📊 Outputs

There are no Outputs available for Retry Process for Multiple Settlement Accounts feature.

### 16.24  Transaction Cycler Service


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *This section contains the examples on how the Transaction Cycler service executes the various types of transactions considering the priority of execution and how it processes retry requests based on back value dated transactions.*
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Monday - 4 Jan*, *Priority Execution*, *Tuesday - 5 Jan*
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

This section contains the examples on how the Transaction Cycler service executes the various types of transactions considering the priority of execution and how it processes retry requests based on back value dated transactions.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

This is covered as part of module configuration. There is no specific configuration for this feature.


#### 🔧 Working With

The following screenshot shows example on how the system will prioritise and executes the retry recycler requests based on transaction code sent by the TPH:

- An record in RC.CONTRACT.PRIORITY application is setup to sort the request by date, considering the oldest request first.

- The RC.PRODUCT.PRIORITY application is created with a custom ID and setup to consider the direct debit request sent by TPH with transaction code 1 .
- The RC.PRIORITY is created, if more than one retry request is posted against the same account, to consider first the Direct Debit (DD) request sent by TPH with transaction code ’1’ (the custom record in RC.PRODUCT.PRIORITY ), then the requests from Payment Order (PI) and all other request sent by TPH (PP). If there are other requests posted by other business applications they will be considered last, ordered by date (oldest one has priority).

- A payment order transaction of USD 750 to be debited is posted against the account 10015151506. Since the account does not have a balance, a record in RC.DETAIL is created for this amount.

- A direct debit transaction of USD 458.50 with transaction code ’1’ is posted by TPH against the same account 10015151506. Since the account does not have a balance, a record in RC.DETAIL is created for this amount.

- A debit transaction of USD 288.20 with the transaction code ’1’ is posted by TPH against the same account 10015151506. This transaction is not a DD. Since this account does not have a balance, a record in RC.DETAIL is created for this amount.

A credit transaction of USD 700 is posted against the same account 10015151506. Since this account received a credit, an entry in RC.RETRY.TRIGGER is created.

- The Online Recycler process is triggered. For the first priority setup in RC.PRIORITY application, the DD transaction sent by TPH with transaction code ‘1’ is settled first.

> **⚠️ Note:** Because the remaining funds are not sufficient, all other retry requests remain pending.

A credit transaction of USD 750 is posted against the same account 10015151506. Since this account received a credit, an record in the RC.RETRY.TRIGGER is created.

The Online Recycler process is triggered. For the second priority setup in RC.PRIORITY application, the payment order transaction is settled next.

The second debit transaction sent by TPH remains pending due to insufficient funds, as shown in the below screenshot.

A credit transaction of USD 289 is posted against the same account 10015151506. Since the account received a credit, a record in the RC.RETRY.TRIGGER is created. The Online Recycler process is triggered. For the third priority setup in RC.PRIORITY application, the other debit transaction sent by TPH is settled next.

The following screenshots show example on how the system will prioritise and execute retry recycler requests based on bills status sent by AA in case the definition is ’Product then Rank’.

- The RC.CONTRACT.PRIORITY record is setup to sort the request by bills status, in the following order.

- One request from PAYMENT.ORDER application.

As per the system setup in RC.PRIORITY , the first requests which will be settled are the ones from the NORTHSHORE.LOANS. As there are no requests from this product type, the system will jump to the next priority. The second priority are the requests from the custom record in RC.PRODUCT.PRIORITY .

Since, there are multiple requests from the same products, the system will order them first by product as defined in the record in RC.PRODUCT.PRIORITY and as they were sent to Recycler:

- MORTGAGE.LOANS.USD - Status NAB
- MORTGAGE.LOANS.USD - Status OD1
- MORTGAGE.LOANS.USD - Status GRA

- MORTGAGE.LOANS.1Y - Status OD1
- MORTGAGE.LOANS.1Y - Status GRA
- MORTGAGE.LOANS.1Y - Status DUE

As there are more than one request from the same product, the system will order them by status as defined in RC.CONTRACT.PRIORITY:

- MORTGAGE.LOANS.USD - Status NAB
- MORTGAGE.LOANS.USD - Status OD1
- MORTGAGE.LOANS.1Y - Status NAB
- MORTGAGE.LOANS.1Y - Status OD1

> **⚠️ Note:** The remaining requests with other status than the ones in the RC.CONTRACT.PRIRORITY will be processed last (after the third priority).

- MORTGAGE.LOANS.USD - Status GRA
- MORTGAGE.LOANS.USD - Status DUE
- MORTGAGE.LOANS.1Y - Status GRA
- MORTGAGE.LOANS.1Y - Status DUE

The third priority are requests from the AC.LOCKED.EVENTS application. A credit of USD 500 is posted on the account 02000000016. The system created a record in the RC.RETRY.TRIGGER application.

The Online Recycler process is triggered. As funds are sufficient, the bills for MORTGAGE.LOANS.USD with status NAB is settled first.

A credit of USD 500 is posted on the account 02000000016. The system has created a record in the RC.RETRY.TRIGGER application

The Online Recycler process is triggered. As funds are sufficient, the bills for MORTGAGE.LOANS.USD with status OD1 is settled.

- A credit of USD 500 is posted on the account 02000000016.
- The system has created a record in the RC.RETRY.TRIGGER application.
- The online recycler process is triggered.
- As funds are sufficient, the bills for MORTGAGE.LOANS.1Y with status NAB is settled.

A credit of USD 500 is posted on the account 02000000016. The system has created a record in the RC.RETRY.TRIGGER application

The Online Recycler process is triggered. As funds are sufficient, the bills for MORTGAGE.LOANS.1Y with status OD1 is settled next.

- A credit of USD 50 is posted on the account 02000000016.
- The system has created a record in the RC.RETRY.TRIGGER application.
- The Online Recycler process is triggered.
- As funds are sufficient, the request from AC.LOCKED.EVENTS is settled next.

If a credit transaction is received in the account, the requests from MORTGAGE.LOANS.USD (with status as GRA) and MORTGAGE.LOANS.1Y (with status as DUE), and the request from payment order will be settled next in the date order (the oldest one will have precedence).


##### Process Retry Requests based on Back Value Dated Credit Transactions

The Recycler can be setup to track any back value dated credit transactions posted to a customer’s account for which there are pending retry requests handed off by a business application.

This enables the system to process the retry request with a value date equal to the credit transaction’s back value date. For example, a retry request is handed off to Recycler on a Friday, and the customer does not have enough funds into his account. The close of business job moves the business day to Monday but on Saturday a credit is received on the customer’s account. In this case, the Recycler recovers the funds on a Monday (business date) but with Saturday’s value date.

For the system to track the back value dated credit transactions, the Track Back dated credit txn field must be enabled in the RC.PARAMETER application.

The back value credit transactions are consumed only if, for the respective account, there are pending retry requests ( RC.DETAIL records) created by a business application.

Once the Recycler recovers the necessary amount of a specific back value credit transaction, this will not be considered on the next retry. Recycler considers all back value dated credit transactions posted on the funding accounts and processes the retry requests for each day, starting with the date set up as retry start date or retry takeover date in RC.DETAIL record, until T-1 (Today (current date)-1). For current date, funds will be recovered considering the working balance minus any locked event.

The funds are recovered if value dated balance for the respective day is available to cover the pending requests based on the full or partial condition and if the balance is still available for the current booking date. When funds are recovered, the system initiates Funds Transfer records with credit and debit value dates as respective back date for which the retry is being performed.

| Bills/Account | Bill Retry Start Date/Takeover Date |  |  |  |  |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
|  | Friday - 1 Jan | Saturday - 2 Jan | Sunday - 3 Jan | Monday - 4 Jan | Tuesday - 5 Jan |
| Bill 1 | 500 | 500 | 500 | 500 | 500 |
| Account 1 working - locked balance | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| Account 1 value dated balance | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 |

### 16.25  Transaction Recycler Process


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *The Transaction Recycler is a generic framework that interfaces with the core and local API routines to perform a message-specific processing. The Transaction Recycler service is set up to run either online or at pre-determined points during COB. The transactions are captured from accounting entries...*
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

The Transaction Recycler is a generic framework that interfaces with the core and local API routines to perform a message-specific processing. The Transaction Recycler service is set up to run either online or at pre-determined points during COB. The transactions are captured from accounting entries through a generic capture mechanism using system-level capture definitions.

- Debit entries that can put an account into overdraft.
- Payments against arrangement accounts that would put the settlement account into debit are captured through a direct interface from the AA module. The Transaction Recycler service selection routine ensures that all transactions due against a settlement account are processed together.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

This is covered as part of module configuration. There is no specific configuration for this feature.


#### 📋 Tasks

The transaction recycler provides the ability to re-initiate (retry) failed recurring financial transactions at regular intervals. This is a generic re-initiation mechanism which can be consumed by any Temenos Transact application. This service runs as a COB job at a specific stage during both End of Day (EOD) and online phases.

### 17.1  Centralised Bank Directory


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *The Temenos centralised bank directory contains the BIC and national ID related data for the financial institutions. It is also referred as bank directory plus as it is uploaded from SWIFTRef bank directory plus file.*

 File*, *Archive File
 Location*, *Clr Sys Acrynm*, *Country*, *Delimiter*, *File Location*, *File Nam*, *File Name* ... +15 more
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

The Temenos centralised bank directory contains the BIC and national ID related data for the financial institutions. It is also referred as bank directory plus as it is uploaded from SWIFTRef bank directory plus file.

The RD module provides an upload mechanism for the SWIFT Bank Directory Plus into the RD Centralised Bank Directory.

SWIFT is discontinuing support for this directory by Nov 2026. The Identifiers All is their new SWIFTRef product which replaces both Bank Directory Plus and IBAN Plus. Read SWIFTRef Identifiers Directory User Guide for more information.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

This section defines the configuration required for Centralised Bank Directory.


##### Reference Data Parameter

The RD.PARAMETER allows the bank to indicate if the Reference Data (RD) module is the main reference data referred and used for BIC validation.

The RD.PARAMETER allows the bank to capture the following information:

The Validate Bic field indicates if BICs should be validated against the directory or just its format should be validated:

- Yes – Validates the BIC against the directory.
- No – It does not validate the BIC against the directory.

The Reference Data field indicates if RD is the main reference data checked by the BIC validation routine.

- Yes – indicates that the RD.CENTRAL.BANK.DIR is used as the main reference data.
- No – indicates that the legacy BIC directory DE.BIC is used as the main reference data.

Based on the above setup, the existing BIC APIs refer either to the new centralised bank directory or the legacy BIC directory.

> **⚠️ Note:** TPH uses the centralised bank directory to refer to BIC and national IDs and therefore is important to have this as the main reference data for other applications as well.

Non-TPH customer, which have local developments that refer directly, DE.BIC can continue to use the legacy directory. Temenos recommends its customers to plan the amendment of the existing local code to refer the BIC reference data through the published APIs to make use of the benefits introduced by the RD module.


##### Upload Parameter

The RD.BANK.DIR.UPLD.PARAM application stores the centralised bank directory upload parameters, which govern the upload of the SWIFTRef bank directory plus files. The structure and purpose of this application is explained below.

| S.No. | Field Name | Description |
|---|---|---|
| 1. | Upld Param Id | This field must be set to SYSTEM. |
| 2. | Description | This field represents a standard Temenos Transact alphanumeric field and allows the bank to assign a description. |
| 3. | Action | This field uploads the file from SWIFT. It holds the following values: If set to OVERWRITE, the existing records in the table are cleared. If set to UPDATE, the existing records are not cleared and the information is just updated. |
| 4. | Upload Type | This field indicates if the uploaded file is the one indicated by the user or the process can pick the file(s) automatically based on the upload rules. This field holds the following values: Automated – The system checks the available files and starts uploading them according to the upload rules. Either the File Name Format or File Name Format Api is mandatory when this option is chosen. Manual – The system only uploads the file indicated by the user. The File Nam e is mandatory for this option. |
| 5. | File Type | This field indicates the type of file to be uploaded and is applicable for automated uploads. This field holds the following values: Daily Delta Monthly Full Monthly Delta |
| 6. | File Location | Indicates the path where the file is held. |
| 7. | File Name | Indicates the name of the file to load. |
| 8. | Delimiter | This field distinguishes the data contents within the file. |
| 9. | Action On Miss File | This field indicates the actions taken by the process when a file is missing. It holds the following values: Stop – If the next file is not found then the upload process stops. Skip – If the next file is not found then the upload process continues with the next available file. |
| 10. | File Name Format | This field indicates the naming convention of the file(s), which must be uploaded. This field is in line with the option in the File Type and match with the pattern provided by SWIFT to identify the publication date. |
| 11. | File Name Format Api | This field indicates the Local API to determine which file(s) must be picked. |
| 12. | Last Publication Date | This field indicates the date of the last publication file which was uploaded. Only the files after this date are considered for automatic upload. |
| 13. | Archive File Location | This field indicates the path where the processed files are moved. The absence of this path deletes the processed file from database. |
| 14. | Local Mapping Api | This field allows the CMB or local layers to indicate an upload or mapping logic to map details from the uploaded file in the directory. |


##### Country National System Identifiers

The RD.CTRY.NAT.SYS.IDENTIFIER application allows the bank to capture the details of the various national clearing system identifiers used in various countries.

The RD module refers to this parameterisation table to identify the BIC for a particular national identifier and to determine the national identifier associated with a specific BIC.

Temenos does not provide a file upload for this configuration table. Temenos recommends clients to consult the NATIONALIDFORMAT file, which is part of the SWIFTRef Bank Directory Plus, and update the model bank records released in this application.

The table below explains the use of the fields in the RD.CTRY.NAT.SYS.IDENTIFIER application:

| Field Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| id | Indicates a unique identifier of a national clearing system formed by a country code followed by ‘.’ and a sequence number Some countries use more than one national identifier (for example, in the US, both ABA and Fedwire are used. |
| Country | Indicates the country code of a national clearing system |
| Iso Clearing Sys Id | Indicates the ISO identifier of the national clearing system. It should be populated with the value prefixed by “ISO5:” and before the next “,” (comma) in the FIELD B of the NATIONALIDFORMAT file. If the FIELD B is populated with ISO5:GBDSC, ISO2:SC, then use GBDSC |
| Swift Clr Sys Id | Indicates the clearing prefix used in the SWIFT MT message. It should be populated with the value prefixed by ISO2 in FIELD B of the NATIONALIDFORMAT file. If the FIELD B is populated with ISO5:GBDSC, ISO2:SC, then use SC |
| Clr Sys Acrynm | Indicates the NATIONAL ID LOCAL ACRONYM in the NATIONALIDFORMAT file |
| National Id Format | Indicates the format of the National Id. It should be populated with the value of the REGEX FORMAT field in the NATIONALIDFORMAT file |
| National Id Type | Indicates the National Id Type specified. It should be populated with the value of the NATIONAL ID TYPE IN BDP field of the NATIONALIDFORMAT file |

The setup in RD.CTRY.NAT.SYS.IDENTIFIER is important, especially for Foreign National Ids (identifiers to a foreign bank in another national clearing IDs).

A German bank that has a national id in the Great Britan Domestic Clearing system). In such cases, the records uploaded from the SWIFTRef Bank Directory have the country code identifying the country where the institution is registered (Germany), and the national id type indicates the clearing code in which the respective national id can be used (SC – which identifies the GB Domestic Clearing system).

The bank must run the RD.UPDATE.NAT.CTRY.CONCAT service to ensure that the files are correctly updated if there is any changes in the RD.CTRY.NAT.SYS.IDENTIFIER application after uploading the SWIFTRef Bank Directory Plus.

> **⚠️ Note:** If the SFRD module is installed, then the upload to RD.CTRY.NAT.SYS.IDENTIFIER is supported. Records in the FORMATS-CTRY file that have the RECORD STRUCTURE as “ID FORMAT” and the RECORD CONTENT TYPE as “D” are uploaded to the RD.CTRY.NAT.SYS.IDENTIFIER . Read Upload of SWIFTRef Formats and Identifier Directory User Guide for more information.

### 17.2  Misc


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *The Centralised Reference Data module handles the upload of reference data in Temenos Transact . This module has its own license code (RD). This module provides the following:*
> 
> **Applications:** `DE.BIC`, `MS.PARAMETER`, `RD.PARAMETER`
>

>

#### 📖 Introduction

Related topics:

- APIs
- Temenos Transact Services

The Centralised Reference Data module handles the upload of reference data in Temenos Transact . This module has its own license code (RD). This module provides the following:

- The centralised bank directory is the Temenos standard solution for managing BICs and National IDs. It replaces the existing DE.BIC , as well as Temenos Payments Hub (TPH) own directories.
- An automated and manual process to upload SWIFTRef bank directory plus to the Temenos centralised bank directory.
- An automated and manual process to upload SWIFTRef IBAN directories to the Temenos IBAN-related directories that are part of the IBAN module (IN). The upload of the IBAN structure is manual.
- Enhanced capabilities to handle future date changes are published in the SWIFTRef bank directory plus and in the IBAN plus directories.
- Tracks the bank directory plus, IBAN plus and exclusion list upload (stores the name of the source file, create deleted records before moving them to history) and eliminates the exceptions (Unauthorised records are not present for modified or deleted records).
- Separate data for master (created and maintained through upload) and custom reference data (created and maintained manually by the bank).
- A mechanism to restrict reference data to specific companies or exclude reference data for specific companies.

SWIFT is discontinuing support for the Bank Directory Plus and IBAN Plus directories by Nov 2026. The Identifiers All is thier new SWIFTRef product which replaces both Bank Directory Plus and IBAN Plus. Read the SWIFTRef Identifiers Directory User Guide for more information.


##### Reference Data Usage

The RD and IN modules are available to new and migrating customers.

A one-time service 'RD.COPY.DE.BIC' is provided to existing customers to migrate data from the Temenos BIC directory ( DE.BIC ) to the centralised bank directory, or the customer can proceed with a complete upload of the latest bank directory plus file to the centralised bank directory.

For non-TPH customers with existing local developments that refer to the legacy BIC directory directly and not through the published methods, a parameterisation option (the Reference Data set to No in RD.PARAMETER ) allows them to indicate if th BIC validation API (DE.VALIDATE.SWIFT.ADDRESS* method) considers the RD centralised bank directory or the legacy BIC directory as the main reference data.

Temenos recommends its customers to plan for the amendment of the existing local code to refer to the BIC reference data through the published methods to leverage the benefits introduced by the RD module.

> **⚠️ Note:** The Temenos BIC directory is the legacy solution for BIC, moved to care and maintenance. Temenos still supports this but will not improve this further.


##### Product Configuration

This section covers the configuration of Upload Principles for Directories and Reference Data Parameter

| File Type | Frequency | Description |
|---|---|---|
| Daily full | Once a month | The daily full file is only required for an optional data resynchronisation. The daily full file is published as a separate file along with the daily delta. |
| Daily delta | Every day, including weekends | This file contains only the changes of the previous day. |
| Monthly full | Once a Month | The file contains full details. |
| Monthly delta | Once a month | The file contains the changes from the previous month. |

When a record is created, modified or deleted from the RD Centralized Bank Directory, first-class business events are emitted.

The MS Event subscription for the RD Centralized Bank directory and the IBAN Plus directory reference data is by default set as Yes, which indicates that the business events are emitted by default when records are created, modified or deleted in these directories.

However, the considering the volume of records in the directories, the bank may choose to unsubscribe the reference data events for the RD Centralized Bank directory and the IBAN Plus directory by disabling the flag in the Subscribed field of the respective event.

If the user does not prefer to emit any business event, then this can be configured by setting the Emit Business Event field as Null in MS.PARAMETER .

### 17.4  Structured Creditor Reference


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *Structured Creditor Reference is an International Business Standard based on ISO 11649. According to the ISO standard, the Structured Creditor Reference is an alphanumeric string with the letters ‘RF’ at the beginning. A company can identify customer invoices using the Structured Creditor Reference....*
> 
> **Key Fields:** *creditorReference*, *generateOrValidateOption*
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

Structured Creditor Reference is an International Business Standard based on ISO 11649. According to the ISO standard, the Structured Creditor Reference is an alphanumeric string with the letters ‘RF’ at the beginning. A company can identify customer invoices using the Structured Creditor Reference. A company can add the Structured Creditor Reference to its invoices and at the time when a customer pays the invoice quoting the Structured Creditor Reference, the company can match the payment with the invoice using the Structured Creditor Reference. By validating the Structured Creditor Reference provided as part of the payment details, the bank can improve the level of confidence on the accuracy of the supplied data, and therefore, reduce the need for manual intervention during the reconciliation process for their customers. Real or Unique Creditor Reference is country specific. It is an alphanumeric string with maximum 21 digits and does not contain any special characters, whereas Structured Creditor Reference is also an alphanumeric string with the letters ‘RF’ and two check digits (XX) at the beginning of the supplied Real or Unique Creditor Reference.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

The payment system interacting with Temenos Transact can send a request to either generate or validate the Structured Creditor Reference. The API request in turn invokes an enquiry, ENQ RD.API.STUCTUREDCREDITORREFERENCE.1.0.0, to either generate or validate the Structured Creditor Reference. To generate Structured Creditor Reference, the user must enter the Real or Unique Creditor Reference in the creditorReference field and the value ‘GENERATE’ in the generateOrValidateOption field, as shown in the screenshot below:

Similarly, to validate the Structured Creditor Reference, the user must enter the Structured Creditor Reference in the creditorReference field and the value ‘VALIDATE’ in the generateOrValidateOption field, as shown in the screenshot below:

### 17.5  SWIFT Gpi Directory


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *The SWIFT global payments innovation (SWIFT gpi) is a SWIFT service that addresses the cross-border payments with the purpose of increasing their speed, transparency and end-to-end tracking.*
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Act As Intermediary*, *Action*, *Allowed Company*, *Cbd Recordkey*, *Ccy Code*, *Channel Type*, *Country*, *Country Code* ... +31 more
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

The SWIFT global payments innovation (SWIFT gpi) is a SWIFT service that addresses the cross-border payments with the purpose of increasing their speed, transparency and end-to-end tracking.

The gpi directory provided by SWIFT contains the complete list of financial institutions that act as gpi participants. It provides the following details on these financial institutions:

- Participation and reachability, including details such as the currencies for which they participate to the gpi service.
- The channels through which they can be reached.
- Related cut-off times.

The gpi directory enables identification, routing and monitoring which is hosted and supported by SWIFT.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

The Temenos SWIFT gpi directory is maintained in the RD.SWIFT.GPI.DIR application and contains all the related information about the financial institutions that are GPI participants.

The Temenos SWIFT GPI directory allows the bank to capture the following information.

| S.No. | Field Name | Description |
|---|---|---|
| 1. | Flag | Indicates if there is a change in the record, since the last release of the SWIFT gpi Directory structure file. This field holds the following values: A – Addition since last SWIFT gpi Directory file. D – Deletion since last SWIFT gpi Directory file. M – Modification since last SWIFT gpi Directory file. |
| 2. | Source Key | Indicates the identifier of the record in the SWIFT gpi Directory file. |
| 3. | Cbd Recordkey | Indicates the corresponding record key of the participant in the Temenos Transact Centralised Bank Directory, containing the participant's details. |
| 4. | Platform | Indicates the service platform. |
| 5. | Service | Indicates the Service type identifier. For example, the value of field is 111 in block 3 of the gpi MT103. |
| 6. | Service Name | Indicates the name of the service. |
| 7. | Participant Id | Indicates the participant's routing ID, at which it is reachable for receiving gpi payments. For example, it can be a BIC8 followed by XXX, a BIC8 followed by a three-character branch code, or a clearing code ( National Id ) of the non-FIN PMI (payment market infrastructure not on FIN). |
| 8. | Id Type | Indicates the type of the identifier used for the Participant Id , such as the BIC or a National Id of a non-FIN PMI (Payment Market Infrastructure not on FIN). |
| 9. | Participant Name | Indicates the institution name of the participant. |
| 10. | Country | Indicates the two character ISO country code of the participant. |
| 11. | Ccy Code | Indicates the three character ISO currency code. |
| 12. | Cut off time | Indicates the participant's public gpi cut-off time for gpi payments in this currency. |
| 13. | Cut Off Day | Cut-off day can be empty (same day cut-off time) or can contain the value ‘D-n’ (where n can be a value between 1 and 9). |
| 14. | Local Time Zone | Indicates the time zone of the participant. |
| 15. | Act As Intermediary | Y (Yes) or N (No) flag specifying whether the participant acts as the gpi Intermediary Agent for gpi payments in a given currency and over a given reachable through channel (in Reachable Through field ). |
| 16. | Reachable Through | Indicates the channel through which the participant is reachable for gpi payment instructions for one of its gpi currencies. |
| 17. | Channel Type | Indicates the type of the Reachable Through channel. This field holds the following values: Intermediary FIN-PMI (payment market infrastructure on FIN) D-C (direct or cover) NON-FIN-PMI (payment market infrastructure not on FIN) |
| 18. | Start Date | Indicates the future date when the record becomes valid (including this day itself, if it is a business day). |
| 19. | Stop Date | Indicates the future date until the record is valid (including this day itself, if it is a business day). |
| 20. | Ssi Record Key | Indicates the record key of the Standing Settlement Instruction (SSI) in SWIFTRef's SSI plus directory for this participant and currency. |
| 21. | Delegated To | Indicates the BIC which forwards the payment or updates the tracker on behalf of the participant ID. It is a valid BIC of eight characters. |
| 22. | Source Name | This field is populated because of the upload process with the File Name of the SWIFT gpi Directory, through which the record is created, amended or deleted in the system. |
| 23. | Entry Type | This field is set by the system and indicates if the record is created or maintained through an upload or manually. It holds the following values: Upload – The record is created through upload. Custom – The record is created manually. |
| 24. | Status | This field indicates the status of the record. |
| 25. | Allowed Company | This field indicates that the record is available only for those companies that are mentioned. |
| 26. | Excluded Company | This field indicates that the record is available for all the companies, but not for the one excluded. |

> **⚠️ Note:** Temenos provides an upload process through which this directory is populated based on the SWIFT gpi Directory published by SWIFT. The upload process is part of the Centralised Reference Data (RD) module.


#### 📋 Tasks

The SWIFT global payments innovation (SWIFT GPI) is a SWIFT service that addresses the cross-border payments with the purpose of increasing their speed, transparency and end-to-end tracking. The Temenos SWIFT GPI directory is maintained in the RD.SWIFT.GPI.DIR application and contains all the related information about the financial institutions that are GPI participants.


##### Workflow

The user can perform the following activities:

| Swift GPI Directory | Enter values in the following fields: Participant ID Country Code Currency Code Source Key Click the Validate icon to check for errors and overrides. Click the Commit icon. |

| SCREENS | WORKFLOW |

|  | GPI Directory Upload Parameter . |

### 17.6  Uploading IBAN Directories


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *The SWIFTRef IBAN Plus is downloaded by the bank from SWIFT. The following files part of this directory can be uploaded in Transact/Standalone Temenos Payments Hub:*
> 
> **Applications:** `IN.EXCLUSION.LIST`, `IN.IBAN.PLUS`, `IN.IBAN.STRUCTURE`
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

The SWIFTRef IBAN Plus is downloaded by the bank from SWIFT. The following files part of this directory can be uploaded in Transact/Standalone Temenos Payments Hub:

- The IBAN Structure file can be uploaded into the Temenos IBAN Structure application ( IN.IBAN.STRUCTURE )
- The IBAN Plus file can be uploaded into the Temenos IBAN Plus application ( IN.IBAN.PLUS )
- The IBAN Exclusion file can be uploaded into the Temenos IBAN Exclusion application ( IN.EXCLUSION.LIST )

SWIFT is discontinuing support for this directory by Nov 2026. The SWIFTRef Identifiers All is the SWIFTRef product which replaces both the SWIFTRef Bank Directory Plus and IBAN Plus. The SWIFTRef FORMAT-CTRY file replaces the IBAN Structure file.

Read SWIFTRef Identifiers Directory to find how the IBAN Structure and IBAN reference data are uploaded and managed in the system.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

There is no specific configuration for Upload of IBAN Plus Directory.


#### 📋 Tasks

There are no Tasks available for Upload of IBAN Plus Directory feature.


#### 📊 Outputs

There are no Outputs available for Upload of IBAN Plus Directory feature.

### 18.1  Misc


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *SWIFT’s new IDENTIFIERS-ALL directory replaces the existing SWIFTRef Bank Directory Plus (BDP) and SWIFTRef IBAN Plus (IBP) directories.*
> 
> **Applications:** `IN.IBAN.PLUS`, `RD.PARAMETER`
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Iban Reference
 Data*, *Update IBAN Plus*, *Update Legacy
 Bic*
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction


#### 📖 Introduction

SWIFT’s new IDENTIFIERS-ALL directory replaces the existing SWIFTRef Bank Directory Plus (BDP) and SWIFTRef IBAN Plus (IBP) directories.

The SWIFTRef Identifiers Directory (SFRD25) module supports key structural changes in these files compared to the previous directories and enables seamless data upload in Transact and Standalone TPH.

- The IDENTIFIERS-ALL file contains the BIC, National IDs, IBAN National IDs, Legal Entity Identifier (LEI) for the entities involved in payments across the SWIFT network, various regional or local RTGS-es, and regional or local clearings. The difference from the previous directory is that each line in the directory represents an identifier and one entity can have more than one identifier or line in the directory file. In the SWIFTRef Bank Directory Plus and IBAN Plus, one line represented one entity, and it included its identifiers.
- The FORMATS-CTRY file contains the definitions of account numbers, IBAN structure, identifier types. The SFRD25 module handles the upload of the records related to the IBAN structure into the Temenos IBAN Structure directory and the identifier types (ID TYPE) into the RD Country National System Identifier directory. Records in other formats are ignored.

The SFRD25 module includes:

- The SWIFTRef Identifiers Directory, a landing application that stores the uploaded records.
- A Camel based component which handles the upload of: The national identifier records from the FORMATS-CTRY file into the Temenos Country National System Identifier directory. The IBAN records from the FORMATS-CTRY file into the Temenos IBAN Structure Directory. The IDENTIFIERS- ALL records into the Temenos SWIFT Identifiers Directory.
- An online process which updates the RD Central Bank Directory, and optionally IBAN Plus and Legacy BIC Directory based on the details stored in the landing SWIFT Identifiers Directory.
- A housekeeping process to remove obsolete records (such as, deleted records, and records from previous full file uploads).

From R25 onwards:

- The system updates the RD Centralised Bank Directory and based on parameterisation, continues to update IN.IBAN.PLUS and legacy BIC directories. Depending on the parameterisation, IBAN APIs can reference either IBAN Plus directory or the RD Centralised Bank directory.
- The Bank Directory Plus and IBAN Plus upload processes included in the RD module are still available for new/upgrading clients as the timeline for the existing directories is November 2026, however the recommendation is to use the IDENTIFIERS directories.
- Ensure that once the bank decides to move to IDENTIFIERS-ALL, it continues with the upload of these files and does not upload BDP and IBP files further on.

The diagram below describes the upload process of the SFRD Directory:


##### Product Configuration

The following configuration in RD.PARAMETER helps to update the Legacy BIC and legacy IBAN Plus directories. Moreover, it allows the use of RD as the main reference data for IBAN, as the IDENTIFIERS-ALL includes the IBAN National Id along the other identifiers:

| Field Name |  |
|---|---|
| Iban Reference Data | Indicates the main directory for IBAN. The options are: Yes - The RD Central Bank Directory is the main reference data for IBAN and therefore the IBAN APIs refers to the RD Central Bank Directory. None or No- The RD Central Bank Directory is not the main reference data for IBAN and therefore the IBAN APIs continue to refer to the IBAN Plus Directory. |
| Update Legacy Bic | Indicates if the legacy BIC needs to be updated along with the RD Central Bank Directory. The options are: No- Only the RD Central Bank Directory is updated. Legacy BIC is not updated. Yes- Both the RD Central Bank Directory and Legacy BIC are updated from the landing application. |
| Update IBAN Plus | Indicates if the IBAN Plus Directory must be updated along with the RD Central Bank Directory. The options are: No- No changes are reflected in the IBAN Plus directory. Yes- IBAN-related changes are reflected in the IBAN Plus directory. |


> **Related Applications:** `IN.IBAN.PLUS`, `RD.PARAMETER`

#### 🔧 Working With

This section describes the key elements of the IBAN FORMAT, ID FORMAT and IDENTIFIERS records.


###### Key Elements in IBAN FORMAT Records

- Record Key- These are unique within the file and across different types of files. It starts with a two- letter prefix that represents the file name. For the records in IDENTIFIERS, the Record Key begins with FO.
- IBAN Country Code- It is the two-letter country code included in the IBAN.
- Reused by: The list of countries that use this IBAN structure is mentioned in this element.
- IBAN National ID Type: The Id Type of the IBAN National ID that appears as the IBAN National ID within SwiftRef Portfolio Evolution files, such as the IBAN ID within the IDENTIFIER Record Structure.


###### Key Elements in ID FORMAT Records

- Country Code- It is the two-letter country or territory code owned and applied to the ID of this type.
- ISO CLC Type - The ISO clearing code type is used to cross-reference between the Iso Clc Type and the Id Type used in the IDENTIFIERS file.
- Regex Format - A structured expression of the ID format, suitable for automated validation.
- ID Type - The SwiftRef proprietary acronym for a set of identifiers/clearing codes listed in the IDENTIFIERS file. The syntax (except for the BIC and LEI) is: - .


###### Key Elements in IDENTIFIERS

- Record Key - It is a unique number allocated by SWIFT to each record. It starts with a two- letter prefix that represents the file name. For the records in IDENTIFIERS, the Record Key begins with ID.
- EID - The Entity Identifier (EID) is a unique SWIFTRef identifier (assigned by an external source) of the organisation that owns the identifier to cross-reference legal entities like head offices, subsidiaries, or branches.
- ID - The identifier assigned to the entity can be a BIC, LEI, National ID, and so on, depending on the corresponding ID Type.
- ID Type- The type of the identifier. The Id Type can be fixed (BIC11, BIC8, LEI), for national identifiers it follows the format: - .
- ID Usage- Indicates the context in which the IDENTIFIER can be used. It indicates how the identifier is used in payments, whether a BIC is connected to the Swift network, whether the ID is used in IBANs, and so on.

Consider the following example:

| Attribute in IDENTIFIERS-ALL | Values | Fields in SFRD.IDENTIFIER.DIRECTORY |
|---|---|---|
| Record Key | ID0000000XYZ | ID and Source Key |
| Eid | 0123ABC | Entity Id |
| Id | DEUTDEFFXXX | Identifier |
| Id Type | BIC11 | Identifier Type |
| Id Usage | FIN,FINPLUS | Id Usage |

The below screenshot shows the SFRD.IDENTIFIER.DIRECTORY record with the key elements mentioned above.

The SWIFTRef Identifiers Directory component (SFRD25_SFRDUpload) is a Camel-based component which monitors a certain folder.

, where:

- - Can be FORMATS-CTRY, FORMATS-SEPA, IDENTIFIERS-ALL, IDENTIFIERS-SEPA
- - Can be either F (Full file) or M (delta file)
- - Is in the format yyyy-MM-ddd
- - Can be either xml or txt

If the component detects a new file with the name matching this format, then:

- A file in the SFRDOutputFolder with a .inprogress extension is updated. This indicates that the upload of the file is in progress.
- Once the file is processed, it is deleted from the SFRDInputFolder and in SFRDOutputFolder .inprogress file is changed to .uploaded. These .inprogress and .uploaded files are status indicators with no data in them. If any exception is observed in any of the records in a file, the exception message is recorded in the .error file in SFRDOutputFolder and the failed record is moved to DeadLetterFolder.
- . The OFS XML layer picks the message and creates a record in the SFRD landing application namely, SFRD.IDENTIFIER.DIRECTORY .
- before it processes the next batch.

If the file name does not match the file format, the XSLT file is missing or has invalid header details, an exception is raised and the file is not processed further. In the SFRDOutputFolder, .inprogress file is changed to .failed file and the exception message is recorded in the .error file and the file is deleted from the SFRDInputFolder.

For example, if the user tries to upload a file with the file name IDENTIFIERS-ALL-V1-F-2019-10.xml, the file is not processed as the date component is not in the format of YYYY-MM-DD. This file is moved to the folder identified by the SFRDOutputFolder property as IDENTIFIERS-ALL-V1-F-2019-10.error. The error is updated as shown below.

If an error occurs in a particular record, once the file is processed the following two files are created in the SFRDOutputFolder.

- .uploaded extension - Has details regarding the successfully uploaded records
- .error extension - Has the details about the records which are not processed due to some exceptions

| Operation Name | Frequency | Details |
|---|---|---|
| Initial Full FORMATS file upload | Initial | Uploads the IBAN FORMAT records into IN.IBAN.STRUCTURE . Uploads the ID FORMAT records into RD.CTRY.NAT.SYS.IDENTIFIER . Review any record in the IN.IBAN.STRUCTURE which does not have an Id Type ( Field B ) blank and manually reverse them. |
| Initial Full IDENTIFIERS-ALL file upload | Initial | Uploads the IDENTIFIERS ALL into the SFRD.IDENTIFIER.DIRECTORY . |
|  |  | Automatically starts SFRD.UPDATE.SERVICE when the file upload finishes. Updates the details from SFRD.IDENTIFIER.DIRECTORY to: RD.CENTRAL.BANK.DIR IN.IBAN.PLUS , if IBAN Reference Data is set to Yes DE.BIC , if Update Legacy BIC is in RD.PARAMETER is set to Yes It is recommended to set IBAN Reference Data to No and Update Legacy BIC to No before the first upload. |
| Monthly Delta FORMATS file upload | Monthly, after the delta files are published | Uploads the IBAN FORMAT records into IN.IBAN.STRUCTURE . Uploads the ID FORMAT records into RD.CTRY.NAT.SYS.IDENTIFIER . It is recommended to upload the files each month. In case of exceptional issues, if more than one file must be uploaded, it should be done in the date order, starting with the oldest. |
| Monthly Delta IDENTIFIERS-ALL file upload | Monthly, after the delta files are published | Uploads the IDENTIFIERS ALL into the SFRD.IDENTIFIER.DIRECTORY . |
|  |  | Automatically starts SFRD.UPDATE.SERVICE when the file upload finishes and updates the details from SFRD.IDENTIFIER.DIRECTORY to: RD.CENTRAL.BANK.DIR IN.IBAN.PLUS , if IBAN Reference Data is set to Yes DE.BIC , if Update Legacy BIC is in RD.PARAMETER is set to Yes |
| Housekeeping process – push the future dated updates into the directory and remove the deleted records ( Status = Delete) from the directories | Daily, after midnight | Start SFRD.UPDATE.SERVICE. |

### 19.1  BIC Database Upload


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *The Bank Directory Plus file must be downloaded from SWIFT. This file is uploaded into the Temenos Transact system and is accessible to all applications for verification. Series of applications are provided to facilitate the smooth transfer of this data from its native source into the Temenos Transa...*
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction


#### 📖 Introduction

The Bank Directory Plus file must be downloaded from SWIFT. This file is uploaded into the Temenos Transact system and is accessible to all applications for verification. Series of applications are provided to facilitate the smooth transfer of this data from its native source into the Temenos Transact system. The Temenos Transact applications will allow the setting of default parameters, generating an automatic ID, uploading of the database and maintaining new or existing records on the BIC file within the system.

> **⚠️ Note:** Every effort needs to be made to ensure that Temenos’ release instructions are current with the latest Bank Directory Plus product, it is always advisable to read the instructions supplied with it, however unlikely, SWIFT may have included alterations without notice.

---


### 19.2  Customer Address in Delivery Output


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *The content of the customer address is configurable by defining rules. The system allows the Country Model Bank or implementations layers to define the rules that describe how the system handles the addresses in the delivery output.*
>

#### 📖 Introduction

#### 📖 Introduction

Temenos Transact allows Email and SMS as message carriers within the Delivery module, so that any existing message supported by the Delivery module can be additionally or singularly sent through Email and/or SMS. In addition, the secure messaging functionality integrated with the Delivery module can be linked. This enables the usage of standard message routing facilities to generate a secure message thereby ensuring that all customer messaging is configured and sent through a central utility.

For sending Email, SMS and secure messages, an extensible markup language (xml) format of the message should be generated and sent to the customer using the interface.

### 19.9  EndPeriodProcessing


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *The delivery end of period processing consolidates all statistical data. It clears the application of deleted, acknowledged and printed messages. The delivery end of period processing is independent of the Temenos Transact close of business (COB) and is run whenever required by the user.*
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction


#### 📖 Introduction

The delivery end of period processing consolidates all statistical data. It clears the application of deleted, acknowledged and printed messages. The delivery end of period processing is independent of the Temenos Transact close of business (COB) and is run whenever required by the user.

> **⚠️ Note:** It is suggested to run the processing weekly. However, it is up to the user to decide when they find it best to run and how often to process.

Running the delivery end of period removes the messages, for which processing is complete and places them in the HISTORY tables. Therefore, regular running of end of period keeps the LIVE tables in a reasonable size and therefore improves the processing time within delivery.

### 19.11  Generation of MX Message using ISOMX Carrier


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *This functionality provides Business Applications a framework to forms the business message. The Business Applications hands off the message data to Delivery, Delivery maps the message and issues the details to the Integration Framework which applies the transformation to the final formal. The Deliv...*
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction


#### 📖 Introduction

This functionality provides Business Applications a framework to forms the business message. The Business Applications hands off the message data to Delivery, Delivery maps the message and issues the details to the Integration Framework which applies the transformation to the final formal. The Delivery Carrier associated to this processing is ISOMX.

To use the full benefits of the Delivery Transformation layer and the capabilities to handle headers please consult the Support MX messages through SWIFTNet Interact services section.

ISO 20022 MX is a new message type expressed in XML syntax, which is more flexible and easier to implement than the previous generation of message types (MT). These message types are developed in accordance with the ISO 20022 standard.

The current syntax format is xxxx.nnn.aaa.bb, where:

- xxxx is an alphabetic code in four positions (fixed length) identifying the business process.
- nnn is an alphanumeric code in three positions (fixed length) identifying the message functionality.
- aaa is a numeric code in three positions (fixed length) identifying a particular flavour (variant) of message functionality.
- bb is a numeric code in two positions (fixed length) identifying the version.

TREA.001.001.02, where:

- TREA refers to Treasury.
- 001 refers to NDF opening (notification).
- 001 refers to the variant.
- 02 refers to the version message format, in this case, version 2 of NDF opening type.


##### SWIFT Standards for MX Messages

| MX Identifier | Description |
|---|---|
| acmt.xxx.xxx.xx | Account Management |
| admi.xxx.xxx.xx | Administration |
| camt.xxx.xxx.xx | Cash Management |
| defp.xxx.xxx.xx | Derivatives |
| pacs.xxx.xxx.xx | Payments Clearing and Settlement |
| pain.xxx.xxx.xx | Payments Initiation |
| reda.xxx.xxx.xx | Reference Data |
| seev.xxx.xxx.xx | Securities Events |
| semt.xxx.xxx.xx | Securities Management |
| sese.xxx.xxx.xx | Securities Settlement |
| setr.xxx.xxx.xx | Securities Trade |
| trea.xxx.xxx.xx | Treasury |
| tsmt.xxx.xxx.xx | Trade Services Management |

### 19.14  Interbank Statement Request


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *Banks send a request message to their correspondent requesting information related to their accounts (or accounts maintained for their customers, where a prior agreement is in place).*
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction


#### 📖 Introduction

Banks send a request message to their correspondent requesting information related to their accounts (or accounts maintained for their customers, where a prior agreement is in place).

Incidentally an MT920 request message is sent to the account servicing institution to transmit one or more MT940 Customer Statements, MT941 Balance Report(s), MT942 Interim Transaction Report(s), or MT950 Statement Message(s) containing the latest information available for the account as identified in the message. This message has a multiple sequence consisting of account(s) for which the information and required message type(s) is requested. The MT920 message requires implementation of special procedures and its use is governed by bilateral agreements between correspondents.

---


### 19.15  Interim Intraday Transaction Report


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *The interim transaction report (MT942) should contain detailed and summary information about the entries debited or credited to the account since:*
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction


#### 📖 Introduction

The interim transaction report (MT942) should contain detailed and summary information about the entries debited or credited to the account since:

- The last statement (MT940 or 950) or balance report (MT941) or
- The last interim transaction (MT942) report (sent in the period since the last statement or balance report).

The interim report can be generated manually on an ad hoc basis or automatically through the Temenos Transact service.

MT942 is an intra-day transaction report, which is used to transmit detailed information about entries debited or credited to the account since:

- The last statement or balance report.
- The last interim transaction report (sent in the period since the last statement or balance report).

MT941 and MT942 message types are not linked and therefore the statement for these message types is generated independently, that is, the entries to be reported in the statement for the message type 942 do not depend on the last MT941 statement.

> **📇 Quick Reference Card**

> **Purpose:** *This topic explains the Delivery (DE) module that manages the flow of all messages from Temenos Transact , such as confirmations, payments and advices which gives full control over formatting and language of presentation to the users.
