### 19.42  Customer Risk Group


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *The user can create customer groups of related parties for different business operational purposes, where the customer groups for risk purpose is used for limit allocation.*
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

The user can create customer groups of related parties for different business operational purposes, where the customer groups for risk purpose is used for limit allocation.

Operational groups are constructed by utilising defined relationships between customers.

To create a new group:

- The user specifies a single customer or party.
- The system retrieves all customers or parties that are related to that customer with specific types of relation code. The system filters the relationships to be uploaded depending on the configuration (in CUST.GROUP.PURPOSE ) of the rules for this specific group purpose.
- The system automatically defaults the group relationship type, that is, Economic Dependent, Duplicate, Control or Sub-Legal Entity, where this has been defined in the relation ( RELATION ) record. For every relationship, relationship direction can be defined (for example, related as other, related as parent, or related as child). For example, the relationship between Parent Company and ‘Subsidiary Of’ is mapped to Control. When the user enters the party ID in the group, the system automatically checks the associated relationships and populates the corresponding relation types that fits the mapping.
- All direct and indirect relationships of that type are retrieved.
- The user can then remove customers or parties that need not be included in the group by marking them as excluded.
- The user can add additional customers that are not added automatically to the group. It is also possible to re-include customers who were excluded by unmarking them.
- A customer group can be completely closed.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

This section covers the configuration of customer group purpose and customer relationship group.


##### Customer Group Purpose

Multiple customer grouping types can be defined in the system that are used for different purposes (for example, OPERATIONAL) and/or group types (for example, HouseHold). The group purpose contains the rules about the following:

- Where the customer group can be used
- How customers and parties in the group can be stored.

This configuration is done using the CUST.GROUP.PURPOSE application and it provides the following features:

- Capability of defining the risk purpose.
- Restricts or allows a customer to be part of a single group at any given point in time.
- Possibility to automatically update the natural relations and the group relations in a customer group based on party relationships.
- Allow specific customer types and/or person entities to be part of a group and select the group relations that can be part of a group.

The fields in CUST.GROUP.PURPOSE are explained below:

| S. No. | Field | Description |
|---|---|---|
| 1. | System Use | The Risk customer groups are used for risk purposes. Hence, it is linked to limits. The customer groups with a purpose code of risk type only can be attached to the limit structure. Only one purpose type of risk defined at any given time. |
| 2. | Unique Customer | If this field is set to Yes, the system does not allow any customers who belong to a customer group with this purpose (OPERATIONAL) to be part of another customer group. |
| 3. | Update Group Relation | If this field is set to Yes, the system automatically converts the real life relation and creates a new technical relationship between two customers in the CUSTOMER.GROUP record based on the group relationship mapping. If this field is set to No, then the system does not automatically upload the Relationship field in the CUSTOMER.GROUP record. |
| 4. | Update Relation | If this field is set to No, then the system does automatically upload the Relationship field in the CUSTOMER.GROUP record. If this field is set to Yes, the system automatically uploads the Relationship field in the CUSTOMER.GROUP record based on pre-defined party relationships. |
| 5. | Cust Sub Group | This field indicates if a customer can belong only to one or multiple sub-groups at any given moment in time. Unique: The system validates and allows a customer to be part of only one sub-group. Multiple: The system allows a customer to be part of multiple sub-groups. None: The system does not allow any customer to be part of a sub-group and any sub-group to be defined. |
| 6. | Group Type | The values for the group type are defined using the EB.LOOKUP application. Group types can take the values like HouseHold or Corporate. The DEFAULT group type is released by Temenos and is used to define a generic setup for the group purpose when specific Group Type validations are not required. If the user enters a Group Type in the CUSTOMER.GROUP record that is not defined this field (for example, MARKETING), the system looks for DEFAULT group type. If it exists, the system uses this to apply the filtering rules and gives an override to the user stating that the system has used the DEFAULT group type rules. If DEFAULT is not defined, then the system displays an error. |
| 7. | Allow Grp Relation | This field is enabled only when Update Group Relation is marked as Yes. It indicates the group relations that are allowed to be part of a customer group with a specific Group Type . |
| 8. | Allow Relation | This field is enabled only when the Update Relation field is set to Yes. It indicates the real relations that are allowed to be part of a customer group with a specific Group Type . |
| 9. | Sector | It represents the customer sectors that are allowed in a customer group for a specific Group Type . For example, HouseHold allows individuals only and Corporate allows corporate customers only. |
| 10. | Allow Cust Type | This field indicates the customer types that are allowed in a customer group for a specific Group Type (for example, Bank Customer, Bank Customer-KYC Investigate, Nordea Party and so on). |
| 11. | All Pers Ent Status | Indicates the allowed person entity’s statuses in a customer group for a specific Group Type (for example, Party). |
| 12. | Validation Rtn | The bank admin can attach a locally created routine for complex rules to be used when a customer group is created for a particular Group Type . |
| 13. | Aggregated Relation | This field represents the aggregated relation codes and each code must be a valid code in the RELATION application. Aggregated Relation field indicates the relation types that are allowed for aggregation. The bank admin can specify the aggregated relation types that must be one of the allowed relations for the respective group as shown in the following example. |

> **⚠️ Note:** The minimum configuration should be based on group type for generic conditions selected in Group Type .


##### Customer Relationship Group

The CUSTOMER.REL.GROUP application is used to create a customer relation group where multiple relationships can be linked together.

For example, an Ultimate Holding Company may have multiple Associate Holding companies linked to it. In such instances, a group can be created to show the multiple relationships.

A CUSTOMER.REL.GROUP record will be created for Micro Computers Ltd and this will be added to the CUSTOMER.RELATIONSHIP records that are created for this entity as shown in the following example.

### 19.43  Enterprise Customer Management


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *Enterprise Customer Management is part of the Banking Framework suite of products. The Enterprise Customer Management features provide the following functionality:*
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

Enterprise Customer Management is part of the Banking Framework suite of products. The Enterprise Customer Management features provide the following functionality:

- It enables the Temenos Transact CUSTOMER to be accessed and utilised by external (non- Temenos Transact ) systems, where Temenos Transact acts as a service provider. Services provided are as follows: Separate Temenos Transact CUSTOMER and customer-related tables from the rest of Temenos Transact and the ability to enable Temenos Transact CUSTOMER to be launched in a stand-alone mode. A list of service operations that are accessible to other systems enabling maintenance of their customer records within Temenos Transact . A 360-degree view of a customer including the products that are maintained through external systems (non- Temenos Transact ). Minimum data quality assurance by validating if duplicate customers are being entered into the customer database. The ability to merge customer records (for example, when banks merge, duplicate customers should be identified and merged). The ability to ensure that service operations released are in line with BIAN (Banking Industry Architecture Network).
- It enables Temenos Transact to access and utilise an external (non- Temenos Transact ) system, where Temenos Transact acts as a service consumer. This has the following benefits: Removes any direct access to customer and related tables from Temenos Transact . Provides a common interface (adaptor) in place of direct access. Provides a framework through which a request can be sent to an external system and a response provided.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

The following 'Web Service' operations associated with PW activity and EB service operations are pre-configured and available in Temenos Transact as a service provider.

| Web Service | Operations | Operation Description | PW Activity | EB Service |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Activate Customer Service | Activate Service | To change the Customer Type from prospect to active | WS.BF.UPDATE.CUSTOMER.SERVICE | ACTIVATE.CUSTOMER.SERVICE |
| Update Customer Preference | Update Customer Preference | To update the Customer Contact Preferences | WS.BF.UPDATE.CUST.PREFERENCE | UPDATE.CUSTOMER.PREFERENCE |
| Get Related Parties | Get Related Parties | To find the related Customers for a particular Customer by giving the either the Customer ID or Legal ID | WS.BFGET.RELATIONS | FIND.RELATES.PARTIES |
| Find Customer Relation | Find Customer Relation | To find the relation between two customers by giving both Customer IDs | WS.BF.FIND.CUST.RELATION | FIND.CUSTOMER.RELATION |
| Get Customer by Legal Id | Get Customer by Legal Id | To find the Customer by giving the Legal ID-Legal Document Name value | WS.BF.FIND.CUSTOMER.BY.LEGAL.ID | GET.CUSTOMER.BY.ID |
| Get Carrier Address | Get Carrier Address | To display all the Addresses of a particular Customer for a particular Channel | WS.BF.GET.CARRIER.ADDRESS | GET.CARRIER.ADDRESS |

### 19.44  Int Holidays Market Rates


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *Temenos Transact allows market interest and foreign exchanges to be recorded. Rates are typically provided by a rate supplier (for example, Reuters) and are specified for a number of rest periods.*
> 
> **Key Fields:** *PI Country*, *Rest Date*, *Rest Period*, *Spot Date*
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

Temenos Transact allows market interest and foreign exchanges to be recorded. Rates are typically provided by a rate supplier (for example, Reuters) and are specified for a number of rest periods.

A rest period is associated with a premium or discount that is applied when a transaction with the specified maturity period is performed. For example, the market provides a three months or six months LIBOR interest rate. Similarly, the rest date calculation too considers the holiday records for the transaction currency and base currency of the country.

Transaction initiation date will be the current bank day (for example, 16th Nov, 2013 Monday).

Spot date = T+2 = 18th Nov, 2013 Wednesday.

If rest period is one day.

Then, rest date is 19th Nov, 2013 Thursday.

Temenos Transact uses this rate information to calculate the actual rate to be used in transactions and subsequent revaluation. If an exact period match is found, interpolation is used to obtain the correct rate.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

The ST.RATE.PARAMETER application enables an option to provide the required base country and accordingly, the combined holiday definition can be referred to decide the rest dates in FORWARD.RATES and PERIODIC.INTEREST application. Once this parameter is setup, the system ignores the base (local) currency of the country that has been defined in the COMPANY record.

This parameter is a one-time setup. Modification to the same is restricted since it involves financial risk.


#### 🔧 Working With

The feature applies to both the PERIODIC.INTEREST and FORWARD.RATES application to build the Rest Date field.

> **⚠️ Note:** Spot date calculation is not applicable for PERIODIC.INTEREST .

Base country for FORWARD.RATES and PERIODIC.INTEREST can be defined differently in ST.RATE.PARAMETER application. However, the sensitivity should also be acknowledged since PERIODIC.INTEREST application is used by other applications like LD, MM and defining a different base country may affect the existing contracts.

Once the base country for FORWARD.RATES in ST.RATE.PARAMETER application is defined, and if the PERIODIC.INTEREST application is used for building the forward rates for any particular currency, then the Rest Period and Rest Date fields in the PERIODIC.INTEREST application is reflected in the FORWARD.RATES application for that particular currency. However, the system displays an override message while using (creating or modifying) the PERIODIC.INTEREST application.

### 19.45  Interest Accrual


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *The EB.ACCRUAL.PARAM application is used to amend the standard accrual calculations performed by Temenos Transact , which can be invoked in applications such as Load and Deposits (LD), Syndicated Loans (SL) and Payment Due (PD).*
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Accrual Data*, *Accrual Id*, *Accrual Param*, *Amort Api*, *Calc Start Date*, *Cr Account*
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

The EB.ACCRUAL.PARAM application is used to amend the standard accrual calculations performed by Temenos Transact , which can be invoked in applications such as Load and Deposits (LD), Syndicated Loans (SL) and Payment Due (PD).

Decisions, such as whether to include the first or last day, and the impact of principal increases or decrease, together with the option to have user routines called, allow this to be very flexible for bespoke accrual scenarios.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

The amount of interest which gets accumulated on the loan since the last interest payment date is the accrued interest. This is the interest earned but not received. The accrued interest calculation is a part of Temenos Transact system.

> **⚠️ Note:** Changing the days which are included in interest calculation process, can have an effect on the amount of interest calculated and the settings should be checked thoroughly before using it.

The following are the three methods of calculating interest accrual used in Japan:

- Ryoha

Interest is earned on the first and last day of the period. Principal repayment and decreases are effected in interest calculations on the next calendar day after the repayment or decrease. Principal increases and decrease take effect for interest purposes on the day of the increase.

- Kataha-End

Interest is earned for the last day of the period but not the first day. Principal repayment and decreases take effect in the interest calculations the next calendar day after the repayment or decrease. Principal increases take effect for interest purposes on the day of the increase.

- Kataha-Start

This is the current default option supported by Temenos Transact contracts. Interest is earned for the first day of the period but not the last day. Principal repayment, decrease and increase all take effect for interest purposes on the day of the movement.

The EB.ACCRUAL.PARAM records must be entered for each of the above interest calculation methods. The relevant EB.ACCRUAL.PARAM record is selected based on the settings in:

- The Accrual Param field in LD.LOANS.AND.DEPOSITS and PD.PAYMENT.DUE
- The Accrual Id field on SL.LOANS


##### Configuring Soft Accounting for AA Arrangement Contracts

The EB.ACCRUAL application uses the Temenos Transact Soft Accounting framework to generate the entries for AA Arrangement contracts. The following records are released to support the EB.ACCRUAL accounting for AA Arrangement.

| Application | Record |
|---|---|
| AC.EVENT | CHARGE-ACCRUAL-ADJ CHARGE-ACCRUAL-AMORTISE CHARGE-PL-REVESE.TO.SUS CHARGE-ACCRUAL-RESUME CHARGE-ACCRUAL-REVERSE CHARGE-ACCRUAL-SUS-REVERSE |
| AC.POSTING.DETAIL | CATEG-ACCR SPEC-ACCR STMT-ACCR |
| AC.ALLOCATIN.RULE | CHARGE-ACCRUAL |

The following screenshots show the different setups for each Event Type defined in the CHARGE-ACCRUAL record in AC.ALLOCATION.RULE :


#### 🔧 Working With

The Amort Api field in the EB.ACCRUAL.PARAM application provides the ability to call a local routine to calculate the daily amortisation amount for non-straight line methods as shown in the following.

- For rule of 78 calculation when the daily amount decreases over the calculation period.
- If the charge is cancelled, the amount refunded is less than it would be with a straight line calculation method.

The EB.ACCRUAL table stores the details of individual charge or commissions, which are being accrued or amortised. It is normally updated through a forward accounting entry, which stores additional data related to the accrual process in the multi-valued Accrual Data field. The following fields are populated from an API defined in the underlying EB.ACCRUAL.PARAM.

- The Calc Start Date field contains the start date used to calculate the accrual based on the date decided by the user. For example, if a 15 day grace period is allowed from the loan date.
- The Cr Account field is the internal account to which the amount amortized is posted to on a daily or weekly or monthly basis.

### 19.46  Interest Basis


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *Interest basis refers to the methods of calculating interest. It can be set as a default value at the transaction level or allow users to select manually.*
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Compound Type*, *Compound Yield Met*
>

#### 📖 Introduction

Interest basis refers to the methods of calculating interest. It can be set as a default value at the transaction level or allow users to select manually.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

Temenos Transact supports various INTEREST.BASIS as shown in the below table.

| Key | Days/Numerator | Description of Use |
|---|---|---|
| A | 360/360 | This method is used when each month is considered to have 30 days for the numerator and the denominator will also be 360. Sub-divided into methods A1 and A2. |
| A1 | 360/360 | Similar to A. Refer the examples below for deviation from A. |
| A2 | 360/360 | Similar to A1. Refer the examples below for deviation from A1. |
| A3 | 360/360 | Similar to A1. Refer the example below for deviation. |
| B | 366/360 | This method is used when the exact number of days is considered in respect of the numerator while the denominator will be 360. |
| C | 366/366 | This method is used when the exact number of days is considered in respect of the numerator while the denominator will be 365 in a non-leap year and 366 in a leap year. |
| C2 | 366/366 365/365 | Similar to C. Refer the example below for deviation. |
| D | 360/366 | This method is used when each month is considered to have 30 days for the numerator while the denominator will be 365 in a non-leap year and 366 in a leap year. |
| E | 366/365 | This method is used when the exact number of days is considered in respect of the numerator while the denominator will be 365. |
| E1 | 365/365 | This method is used when the 29th day of February, in case of leap year is ignored and it is considered to be a non-leap year. The total number of days in the year which is represented in the denominator is considered as 365. |
| F | 360/365 | This method is used when each month is considered to have 30 days for the numerator while the denominator will be on a 365 basis. Subdivided into methods F1 and F2. |
| F1 | 360/365 | Similar to F. Refer the examples below for deviation from F. |
| F2 | 360/365 | Similar to F1. Refer the examples below for deviation from F1. |
| G | 366/364 | This method is used when the exact number of days is considered in respect of the numerator while the denominator will be 364. |
| H | 360/356 | Hirja method – This is similar to 360/360, but the day calculations use the 360 year (30 days per month) only the denominator is changed to 356 instead of 360. |
| S | Note 1 | Special (special interest basis). |
| W | 252/252 | This method is used when interest calculation is done considering the exact number of working days in a month. The total number of days in the year, which is represented in the denominator is considered as 252. |
| W1 | 21/252 | This method is used when interest calculation is done considering the number of working days in a month to be always 21 days. The total number of days in the year, which is represented in the denominator is considered as 252. |
| A4 | 30/360 | This method is similar to other existing 30/360 basis, in addition it also caters to February month end, where each month is considered to have 30 days for the numerator while the denominator will be 360 for both leap and non-leap years. |

> **⚠️ Note:** Basis S is the special interest basis. This is used to allow the interest amount to be entered manually. The amount entered is checked against the nominal rate entered to avoid errors in amount, it is checked against a tolerance. Conventions are when actual dates are used. The convention in Temenos Transact is that the number of days in the year is calculated taking into account whether the year is a leap year or not. The leap year need not be straddled by the start or end date. If the start date is in a leap year and the end date is in the following year, then the number of days is calculated as 366 for the days in the leap year, plus 365 for the days in the following year.


#### 🔧 Working With

A1, A2 and F1, F2 are the sub-options of the 360/360 and 360/365 bases respectively. The detail of the method for treating each month as 30 days differs slightly as described below:

- In the options A, B, C, D, E, F, and G (as specified in the above table) the number on the left (days) represents the number of days basis for multiplying on the top line of the interest calculation. The number on the right (numerator) is the basis for dividing on the bottom line of the interest calculation and represents the number of days in the year.

If interest basis B (366/360) is selected, then the interest is calculated as:

Principal Amount * Rate * (366/360)

Where, 366 represents the interest calculated for the actual number of days in the month and 360 represents that each month is treated as 30 days when calculating interest.

In months with 31 days, the 30th day is ignored. In February, either the last or the penultimate day is counted as three days (or two days in a leap year) depending upon which 30-day rule is chosen.

- Methods A1 and F1 are same as A and F respectively. Under these methods, the additional interest earned in February is calculated on the last day (that is, 28th or 29th).
- Methods A2 and F2 calculate the additional interest earned in February on the penultimate day (that is, 27th or 28th).
- Method C2 is used in securities, when the start and end dates for a coupon period falls on different years, the coupon period must be split accordingly and interest must be calculated separately for each year. If the coupon period falls on a leap year, it must be considered as 366 and if the coupon period falls on non-leap year, it must be considered as 365.
- Method E1 is a comparison of E1 to other interest basis.
- Basis 366/365 – Days between February 15th and March 15th are 29 days in year 2008 and 28 days in 2009.
- Basis 360/365 – Days between February 15th and March 15th are 30 days in year 2008 and 30 days in 2009.
- Basis 365/365 – Days between February 15th and March 15th are 28 days in year 2008 and 28 days in 2009.

In a leap year, the INTEREST.BASIS is chosen as E1 and the interest is calculated as:

Principal*ROI*365/365

Where, 365 in the numerator represents the actual number of days in all the other months other than February and the number of days in February is considered as 28 ignoring the last day. Under this method, leap or non-leap year makes no difference in interest calculation.

| Dates | A | B | C | D | E | F | G | A2 | F2 | A4 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 01 Jan 1999 - 31 Mar 1999 | 89 | 89 | 89 | 89 | 89 | 89 | 89 | 89 | 89 | 90 |
| 01 Jan 2000 - 31 Mar 2000 | 89 | 90 | 90 | 89 | 90 | 89 | 90 | 89 | 89 | 90 |
| 01 Dec 2000 - 30 Jun 2001 | 209 | 211 | 211 | 209 | 211 | 209 | 211 | 209 | 209 | 210 |
| 01 Dec 1999 - 30 Jun 2000 | 209 | 212 | 212 | 209 | 212 | 209 | 212 | 209 | 209 | 210 |
| 27 Feb 1998 - 31 Mar 1998 | 33 | 32 | 32 | 33 | 32 | 33 | 32 | 33 | 33 | 30 |
| 27 Feb 2000 - 31 Mar 2000 | 33 | 33 | 33 | 33 | 33 | 33 | 33 | 33 | 33 | 30 |
| 28 Feb 1998 - 31 Mar 1998 | 32 | 31 | 31 | 32 | 31 | 32 | 31 | 30 | 30 | 30 |
| 29 Feb 2000 - 31 Mar 2000 | 31 | 31 | 31 | 31 | 31 | 31 | 31 | 30 | 30 | 30 |


##### Hirja Basis - 'H'

The rules that govern the interest basis for H (30/356) are explained below. For two dates (Y1,M1,D1) and (Y2,M2,D2),

- If D1 is 31, the user should change this to 30.
- If D2 is 31 and D1 is 30, the user should change D2 to 30.

Then, the date difference is calculated as

((Y2-Y1)*360)+((M2-M1)*30)+(D2-D1).

The denominator used is 356.

The below examples illustrates, that by using this new interest basis the calculations performed by the system results in the higher calculation of charges. This is caused as a result of using a lower denominator, that is, 356.

01 Jan 2003 - 31 Dec 2003 359 days (11*30+29)

100,000 / 356 x 6% x 359 = SAR 6,050.56

01 Jan 2003 - 01 Jan 2004 360 days (1*360)

100,000 / 356 x 6% x 360 = SAR 6,067.42

01 Jan 2003 - 25 Dec 2004 714 days (1*360+11*30+24)

100,000 / 356 x 6% x 714 = SAR 12,033.71


##### Interest Calculation for the Brazilian Market

The following are the two INTEREST.BASIS methods used for calculations in the Brazilian market:

- W (252/252)
- W1 (21/252)

For calculating the Brazilian yield compound interest, the INTEREST.BASIS , W or W1 should be used in conjunction with the Compound Yield Met field in the following parameter applications:

- GROUP.CREDIT.INT
- GROUP.DEBIT.INT
- ACCOUNT.CREDIT.INT
- ACCOUNT.DEBIT.INT

The Compound Yield Met field is set to Yield and the Compound Type field is set to DAILY in the GROUP.CREDIT.INT record (as shown in the below screenshot).

##### Interest Basis W1 (21/252)

The interest basis W1 is calculated using the formula described above, with the following exceptions:

- The numerator is the number of business days, considering current company holiday record, between the start and end dates. If there are less than 21 business days in a month, it should be considered as 21 days.
- If there are more than 21 business days in month, the system accrues up to the 21st business day only, no more accruals takes place for the remaining working days in the month.

This means that n in the formula is always 21 (with an exception as described below).

> **⚠️ Note:** If a new account is opened during the middle of the month, the number of working days preceding the account opening date in the period is deducted from the calculation. For example (y is the number of days in period before the account is opened). The system capitalises for (21-Y) days.

##### Securities and Interest Basis

Interest basis C and D used in SC follow the rules illustrated below:

- SEC.TRADE uses 366 days in the denominator when required. If a bond pays two coupons of 10% a year on the 20th of December and 20th of June. The nominal amount of 1 Million was being traded on the 20th of March 2000. This results in the following calculations for the coupon element of the consideration:
- Nominal is 1,000,000.
- Rate is 10%.
- Number of days is 91 (11+31+29+20).
- Basis denominator is 365.

Then interest is calculated as:

1,000,000 x 0.10 x 91/365 = 24,931.50

- Nominal is 1,000,000.
- Rate is 10%.
- Number of days is 183 (11+31+29+31+30+31+20).
- Basis denominator is 365.

Then interest is calculated as:

1,000,000 x 0.10 x 183/366 = 50,000.00


##### Interest Basis G used in Securities

For instruments that are issued with coupon dates that occur at set intervals (number of days), these instruments always pay on the same day of the week.

If a bond is issued with a two year life (728 days, 2 x 52 x 7) and is paid twice a year. Each period is of 182 days (26 weeks x 7 days per week); a year is always 364 days. For such bonds, each coupon period is an exact multiple of seven days.

> **⚠️ Note:** When this interest basis is selected, the number of payments must be a divisor of 52 (weeks in a year), that is, 1, 2, 4, 13, 26 or 52.

> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

A loan can be created with a fixed rate, floating rate, periodic rate or a risk-free rate.

- Fixed Rate – The interest rate does not change during the life cycle of the contract.
- Floating Rate – This indicates a market floating rate which varies over time, for example, prime rate.
- Periodic Rate – This indicates time based interest rates which vary based on the tenure of the loan, for example, London Interbank Offered Rate (LIBOR).
- Risk-free Rate – The Risk-Free Rates (RFRs) are backward-looking rates and are traditionally fixed in arrears at the end of a given interest or coupon period.

Based on the business application, an RFR interest calculation can use different methods, which includes:

- Simple or compounded average daily rates using simple amounts.
- Simple daily rates using amounts compounding.

In case of instruments where the principle is unlikely to change within the ’coupon‘ period, use the average daily rates approach. Using this method, averaged rate is calculated on each business day until a final rate is calculated and applied.

If the principal is likely to change half way through the interest calculation period, the recommended method is using the normal daily rate where the compounding formula is applied to the principal amount.

There are several market conventions for using Risk-Free Rates in contracts. In Temenos Transact, the conventions of plain arrears, lookback, lockout and lookback with lockout are covered and an API is developed to calculate average RFRs for a given interest period based on the required market convention and other conditions set by each module that uses Risk-Free Rates .

The PERIODIC.INTEREST application is used to store interest rates for forward-looking time periods. This application is enhanced to support Risk-Free Rates, which are:

- Based on actual transaction data
- Backward-looking
- Overnight
- Published with a delay
- Lack term structure and credit risk elements
- Single rates, that is, there are not any bid and/or offer rates


#### ⚙️ Configuration

The BASIC.RATE.TEXT application defines the descriptions of the BASIC.INTEREST and PERIODIC.INTEREST rates. This application enables the user to identify each interest rate easily. Each description must be defined before creating rates records for the corresponding ID in the BASIC.INTEREST rate application. It is used as the enrichment to the corresponding ID when it is displayed or printed during Temenos Transact processing. The user can define up to 9999 descriptions.

The following screenshot shows the description of Loan Base Rate in BASIC.RATE.TEXT application:


#### 🔧 Working With

This topic explains the workflow of interest related reference application in Temenos Transact . The four major rates defined are as follows:

- Fixed Rate
- Floating Rate
- Periodic Rate
- Risk-free Rate


##### Fixed Rate

The fixed rate is the rate agreed with the borrower at the time of loan creation and it does not change during the life cycle of the loan. The fixed interest rate agreed with the borrower is defined in the loan contractual agreement. Floating rates and periodic rates are stored in centralised core application, so that market rate changes can be realised on all affected loans instead of the need for a manual intervention on each individual loan.


##### Floating Rate

The floating rate fluctuates according to the market movement. The frequently used floating rates, for example, base rate, prime rate, and overnight rate are defined in the BASIC.INTEREST application for each currency. The BASIC.INTEREST application stores the interest rates which are applicable across loans regardless of the loan duration. The rates in this application may be updated automatically through external feeds.

The interest conditions can be linked directly to a basic interest record in this application, rather than defining the interest rate details on each transaction record.

When a rate change takes place, only the BASIC.INTEREST record defined in this application should be updated with the new rate(s) and the effective date. This automatically updates all the transaction records, which are tied to that rate.


##### Periodic Rate

The PERIODIC.INTEREST application defines, for each currency, interest rates for any time period desired by the user for example, 10 days, 15 days, and 30 days. For each period defined by the user, both a bid and offer rate can be entered. Interest rates can also be defined by amount slabs, so a different rate can be entered for ranges from USD1 to 10,000 and between USD10,000 to 25,000.

The PERIODIC.INTEREST application is used by applications such as FOREX to default interest rates on forward contracts using the interest revaluation method or the Money Market (MM)/Lending Deposits (LD) applications to perform automatic rollovers.

The Last Wrkng Day field is set to instruct the system to check whether the current system date is the final working day of the month. If this is the case, when the rest period is defined as number of months, the system looks for the final working day of the appropriate month, rather than selecting the equivalent working day.

If February 26

is the last working day in February and having a rest period of 1M, the system finds the final working day in March, rather than simply selecting the 26

March or the nearest next working day.

It is possible to hook an API to apply rates or spreads based on user-specific criteria through the Local Routine field that enables the core routine to be overridden. Negative interest rates can also be input in the PERIODIC.INTEREST application. The Application field is used to specify the application ID(s) that can use negative interest rates.

The following screenshot shows the Bid Rate and Offer Rate fields:

It is possible to modify the Rest Period fields, Amt , Bid Rate and Offer Rate field of existing PERIODIC.INTEREST records of a past date. The use of such modified records is application dependent. Whenever a PERIODIC.INTEREST record of a past date or processing date is modified and authorised, the ID of such records are written in the PERIODIC.RATE.CHANGE application. The ID of this application is the processing date.

To create a PERIODIC.INTEREST record with interest rates expressed in number of days greater than 31D, the Rest Period field must be set with the values expressed only in days and up to three digits as shown in the below screenshot.

The system does not allow the Rest Period field to have values greater than 31D and the values expressed in months or years in the same record. If the values in months or years have to be used, then the record can hold the values expressed in days only up to 31D.


##### Risk-free Rate

The PERIODIC.INTEREST application supports Risk-Free Rates. Risk-Free Rates are overnight, backward-looking rates derived from actual market data for a given business day. They are published on each business day with a delay (that is, a rate published this business day is effective for the previous business day). These rates do not have a term structure (they are overnight rates published on each business day) and credit risk element.

The PERIODIC.INTEREST application stores overnight Risk-Free Rates in the following fields:

- Rfr Rate – Stores the overnight Risk-Free Rate for the given PERIODIC.INTEREST record.
- Rfr Date Recd – Stores the date on which the overnight Risk-Free Rate is received.

ID of a given Risk-Free Rate PERIODIC.INTEREST record holds the effective date (the date for which the rate is applicable).

When there is a Risk-Free Rate stored in a given PERIODIC.INTEREST record, the Amount , Bid Rate and Offer Rate fields are not required. The overnight Risk-Free Rates are published as a single rate with no Bid or Offer options.

The fields used for forward-looking terms are not allowed. The fields such as Rest Period , Rest Date , Days Since Spot , Build Fwd Rate , Int Tolerance , Max Int Rate and Use Last Wrkng Day are disabled accordingly.

The RFR interest calculation is performed using two different methods such as Rate Compounding and Amount Compounding depending on the setup in the relevant business application. In case of the Rate Compounding, the system calculates the average compounded rate for the period.

Results of the RFR calculation are recorded in the ST.RFR.CONTRACT.DETAILS and ST.RFR.DETAILS tables in Temenos Transact.


##### Market Rate Text

The MARKET.RATE.TEXT application contains the descriptions of tradable interest rates that are recognised by SWIFT.

Each description is used as the enrichment to the corresponding ID when it is displayed or printed during Temenos Transact processing. The Rate Text and Swift Code Words fields are used to populate the values in Tag 14 F in SWIFT MT 340, 360 and 361 messages. The Rate Text defined should be as guided by the SWIFT standards.

If the FLOATING RATE option is chosen as OTHER in the sequence C, the SWIFT standards expect the user to provide additional information in Tag 37N of MT360 and MT361 messages. Temenos Transact is enabled to auto default the additional information which includes a code word 'FROP' that is part of SWIFT.CODE.WORDS application.

#### Product Configuration

The following system-wide applications help in grouping the customers and defining rules for the group based on the business purposes, like defining customer group specific charges and tax.

- CONDITION.PRIORITY
- XXX.GEN.CONDITION and XXX.GROUP.CONDITION, where XXX refers to the business application.
- APPL.GEN.CONDITION


##### Condition Priority

The purpose of the CONDITION.PRIORITY application is to specify, for certain applications, which data elements in other reference applications can be specified to determine condition groups. CONDITION.PRIORITY records can be created with the following IDs:

- ACCOUNT
- FIDUCIARY
- FUNDS.TRANSFER
- FX.MARGIN
- LETTER.OF.CREDIT
- SC.MANAGEMENT
- SC.SAFEKEEPING
- SC.TRADING
- STATEMENT
- TAX
- POR.TRANSACTION

CONDITION.PRIORITY is a CUS level application. Records of this application can be shared between companies, which share the same customer company, or there could be company-specific CONDITION.PRIORITY records by suffixing a hyphen and a Company Code in the ID.

For the

application, it is possible to have a specific record for the Company DE0010001 with the ID ACCOUNT-DE0010001.

The (parameters) records without a Company ID suffixed is applicable to the Master Customer Company (specified as Customer Company in the COMPANY application) as well as to Companies that do not have their own CONDITION.PRIORITY records.

An existing CONDITION.PRIORITY record cannot be modified. However, it is possible to specify parameters that are applicable in future (after the COB processing on a specified date, which can be either the processing date or any future date) by creating CONDITION.PRIORITY records by suffixing a hyphen and a date after the company code in the ID.

The record with ID ’ACCOUNT--20040702’ (with a null Company ID for the customer company) is applicable to the Master Customer Company and the record with ID ‘ACCOUNT-DE0010001-20040702’ is applicable to the Company DE0010001, both records to be effective after the COB processing on 2nd July 2004. The date specified can either be the processing date or it could be a future date.

It is possible to specify the priority items (fields) using the Priority Item field. This is a multi-valued field which defines the order in which fields are used, when matching conditions against values specified in the XXX.GEN.CONDITION records.

- Fields from CUSTOMER application can be specified in all CONDITION.PRIORITY records.
- Fields from ACCOUNT application can be specified only in the CONDITION.PRIORITY records related to ACCOUNT or STATEMENT.
- Fields from SEC.ACC.MASTER can be specified only in the three CONDITION.PRIORITY records related to Wealth application (with IDs SC.MANAGEMENT, SC.SAFEKEEPING and SC.TRADING).

The priority items specified in the CONDITION.PRIORITY records are defaulted as the field names in the corresponding XXX.GEN.CONDITION records.

While determining the condition groups of applications, the priority of the data items (specified as Priority Item ) is determined by their relative position in the CONDITION.PRIORITY record.

For each priority item specified in CONDITION.PRIORITY , users can also specify a validation, which ensures that a value entered for a priority item (in XXX.GEN.CONDITION applications) exists as a record ID in another table. This can also be used to display an enrichment when the value is entered.

In the

record for

, the

CATEGORY’ can have a validation specified in the

DESCRIPTION’. In this case, when a value for the CATEGORY is entered in

, the value entered should be a valid record ID in the

application, and the value of the

field in that

record will be displayed as an enrichment.


##### Parameters and Rules for Groups

The XXX.GEN.CONDITION applications provide the parameters to calculate the default groups for some applications. The priority data items, which are used in the XXX.GEN.CONDITION tables, are defaulted from the corresponding CONDITION.PRIORITY records.

The XXX.GEN.CONDITION applications and the corresponding CONDITION.PRIORITY records from which the priority data items are defaulted are listed below:

| XXX.GEN.CONDITION Applications | CONDITION.PRIORITY record ID from which priority data items are defaulted |
|---|---|
| ACCT.GEN.CONDITION | ACCOUNT |
| FD.GEN.CONDITION | FIDUCIARY |
| FT.GEN.CONDITION | FUNDS.TRANSFER |
| LC.GEN.CONDITION | LETTER.OF.CREDIT |
| SCPM.GEN.CONDITION | SC.MANAGEMENT |
| SCSK.GEN.CONDITION | SC.SAFEKEEPING |
| SCTR.GEN.CONDITION | SC.TRADING |
| STMT.GEN.CONDITION | STATEMENT |
| TAX.GEN.CONDITION | TAX |
| FX.GEN.CONDITION | FX.MARGIN |
| PP.GEN.CONDITION | POR.TRANSACTION |

The parameters specified in FD.GEN.CONDITION , FT.GEN.CONDITION , LC.GEN.CONDITION , SCPM.GEN.CONDITION , SCSK.GEN.CONDITION , SCTR.GEN.CONDITION , TAX.GEN.CONDITION , and PP.GEN.CONDITION are used to default the condition groups in the CUSTOMER.CHARGE application.

The parameters specified in ACCT.GEN.CONDITION are used to default the account group ( Condition Group ) in ACCOUNT , while those specified in STMT.GEN.CONDITION are used to default the frequency in ACCOUNT.STATEMENT .

For each XXX.GEN.CONDITION application, there is a corresponding XXX.GROUP.CONDITION application (except for STMT.GEN.CONDITION ) to define the various parameters for each group. The following XXX.GROUP.CONDITION applications exist:

- ACCT.GROUP.CONDITION
- FD.GROUP.CONDITION
- FT.GROUP.CONDITION
- LC.GROUP.CONDITION
- SCPM.GROUP.CONDITION
- SCSK.GROUP.CONDITION
- SCTR.GROUP.CONDITION
- TAX.TYPE.CONDITION
- FX.GROUP.CONDITION

All the XXX.GEN.CONDITION and XXX.GROUP.CONDITION applications referred here are of the FTD level, which may be company specific or shared between companies depending on the configuration of Default Finan Com or Spcl Fin File fields in the COMPANY record.

If the FTD type files for the Company DE0010001 are unique, then the

records for the Company DE0010001 can have the data items defaulted from the

record with ID as ‘ACCOUNT-DE0010001’ if that record exists, else from the default

record with ID as ‘ACCOUNT’.

While defining CONDITION.PRIORITY records to be applicable in future, it is possible to specify which XXX.GEN.CONDITION and XXX.GROUP.CONDITION records need to be retained, by specifying their IDs in the Gen Cond Keep and Group Cond Keep fields respectively. During COB processing on the specified date, these XXX.GEN.CONDITION records are automatically modified with priority data items applicable for the new structure, by retaining existing priority data items and their values. New priority data items are updated with null values.

Further, in conjunction with dated CONDITION.PRIORITY records, it is also possible to specify dated XXX.GEN.CONDITION records, which can become effective in future. Such XXX.GEN.CONDITION records are defined by suffixing a hyphen with a date (either processing date or a future date) in the ID. Priority data items in these records are defaulted from the corresponding dated CONDITION.PRIORITY records. These record IDs must not be defined as retention record IDs in the Gen Cond Keep field of CONDITION.PRIORITY .

After COB processing on the specified date, the dated XXX.GEN.CONDITION records replace the corresponding records without a date in the ID.

Those XXX.GEN.CONDITION records that are not included in the Gen Cond Keep field of the corresponding dated CONDITION.PRIORITY record or those records that do not have a corresponding dated XXX.GEN.CONDITION record are dropped after the COB processing on the specified date.

With the exceptions described below, future dated XXX.GROUP.CONDITION can be created with an ID of the format ‘xxx-Date’, provided the ID is not already specified in the Group Cond Keep field of the corresponding dated CONDITION.PRIORITY record. After COB processing on the specified date, the dated XXX.GROUP.CONDITION records replace the corresponding records without a date in the ID.

There is an exception to the above referred functionality (which existed before the CONDITION.PRIORITY application has been enhanced to accept dated records). The ID format of the SCPM.GROUP.CONDITION and SCSK.GROUP.CONDITION applications is ‘xxx.date’ (both parts mandatory and connected by a dot) to allow definition of parameters, which applies on various dates. The first part of the ID is validated against the first part of the corresponding XXX.GEN.CONDITION records. When the records in these applications are entered, there is no validation against the CONDITION.PRIORITY records.

The XXX.GROUP.CONDITION records whose IDs are not included in the Group Cond Keep field of the corresponding dated CONDITION.PRIORITY record, or which do not have a corresponding dated XXX.GROUP.CONDITION record (suffixed to the ID with a hyphen and date), will be dropped after the COB processing on the specified date. However, customer-specific XXX.GROUP.CONDITION records with ID format as ‘C-Customer ID’ is not dropped after COB processing.

For Payments, the parameters and conditions applicable for a group of customers is defined in PP.CLIENT.CONDITIONRECORD application. Please read Introduction to Client Conditions for more details.


##### Parameter to Default Groups UsingTemenos TransactRoutine

The APPL.GEN.CONDITION application is used to define group conditions for contracts based on a combination of decisions and calls to locally developed subroutines. For example, it allows specific tax codes to be applied to particular types of contract for particular types of customer.

There is one record per application for which many sets of group conditions can be defined. User must ensure that multiple set of groups are defined correctly, as the first set of conditions that pass the validation checks result in that contract group code being applied.

A Temenos Transact subroutine, APPL.GRP.CONDITION can be called to evaluate the current contract record using relevant APPL.GEN.CONDITON . It returns the first group code where all decision checks evaluate to true.

The MM.MONEY.MARKET and LD.LOANS.AND.DEPOSIT applications call the evaluation routine automatically. Other applications can call the evaluation routine from VERSION routines to update local reference fields with the relevant group code.

The subroutine processes these decisions and updates the Contract Group field in the application record whenever the contract is changed. If changes to the contract cause the conditions to break, then a new Contract Group code is generated, which results in a different tax code being applied. A default group code can be defined as the last group code without associated conditions, if required. TAX.TYPE.CONDITION allows the Contract Group code to be linked to the allocation of specific tax codes.

### 19.49  Other Core


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *The following are other core reference tables that are used by various business applications across Temenos Transact :*
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Account Mask*, *Alt Error Cd*, *Error Sol*, *GB Error Info*, *Id Length*, *Id Start*, *Local Ref*, *Max Length* ... +1 more
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

The following are other core reference tables that are used by various business applications across Temenos Transact :

- ASCII
- AUTO.ID.START
- COMPANY
- Local Reference


#### ⚙️ Configuration

There is no specific configuration for this feature as they are used as reference tables in other Temenos Transact applications.


#### 🔧 Working With

This topic details the workflow of other core reference tables in Temenos Transact .

Temenos Transact uses IN2 routines to handle the characteristics of fields, the data the system accepts and the options available to users for any fields using a particular IN2 routine. For example, an IN2 routine handling amounts need to cater for numbers, decimals, codes for millions, thousands and so on. An IN2 routine handling freeform text is completely different.

The ASCII.VAL.TABLE and ASCII.VALUES applications are used to control the characters allowed in a field associated with certain IN2 routines, this is usually done by specifying the permitted ranges, but individual values outside the ranges can be added as well.

While the supplied values are suitable for most customers, there are circumstances where a bank may wish to block certain characters or allow others that are normally considered as blocked. This can range from applications, which interface to external systems and the characters allowed there are more restrictive or have special meaning. Banks that wish to allow non SWIFT characters in mainstream applications where the users tend to prevent their usage or even due to the characters used in other languages.

The ASCII.VAL.TABLE is used to define which ASCII (American Standard Code for Information Interchange) characters must be used for the validation against any IN2 routine defined on the ASCII.VALUES application. The IN2 routines are used to validate the entry to particular fields. The format of the ASCII.VAL.TABLE allows any combination of ranges or single values of ASCII codes to be defined.

> **⚠️ Note:** The users must be careful when modifying the values allowed by the system, particularly when using SWIFT type fields, as this may cause unexpected results by allowing non-standard characters to be entered.

The ASCII.VALUES application is used to define ASCII value codes and ranges that may be used by particular IN2 routines that validate entry to particular fields.

Standard applications are provided for each IN2 routine, but there is also a provision for user-definable applications at a language and application level. Therefore, different applications may be setup for particular languages and applications. The application level definitions may be further sub-divided into different applications for different languages.


##### Automatic ID Generation

Temenos Transact can generate the ID of certain business applications automatically, based on the previous record ID and a user defined set of criteria. In order to utilise this feature, the following applications should be configured:

The AUTO.ID.START application is used to store or define the parameters for generating the ID for one or more applications. The ID of this application can be any relevant name such as contracts or accounts. The details in the record are multi-valued, so that the user can set the criteria for more than one application at a time. In theory, the user could use just the one record to pre-set all the applications the user wishes to control. But during process, there may be times when the user wants to reset the ID starting point of one or more applications so that individual or grouped records may be more beneficial.

ID generation can be a simple Julian date generation for contracts, a number for a CUSTOMER record, an ACCOUNT number (simple or based on an algorithm to prevent records having id’s too similar), an ID based upon the users department and even a complex unique ID to prevent duplication in large systems.

Although the ID of AUTO.ID.START can be anything, it is recommended that meaningful names are used to ensure that the current settings for an application can be seen readily.

The ID of many applications is in the style XXYYDDDNNNNN or XXXXXYYDDDNNNNN such as LD0712300001, where:

- XX or XXXX (or in some applications XXXXXX) is an application identifier.
- YYDDDD is the julian date (year and day number).
- NNNNN is the sequence number.

Though it is simple to input and remember, the usage of such sequential IDs creates problems in larger institutions where a high transaction throughput is required together with minimal transaction processing time. This method finds the last number used from the LOCKING table, generate the next number and locks it until the transaction is completed. It thereby imposes a bottleneck in the ID generation. If this is acceptable, then the basic IDs can be used. If faster response time and multi-threading is used to generate large volumes of transactions, then the ID generation should use the UNIQUE.ID settings as detailed below.

To use unique ID other than the standard julian date based records, the Unique No, Base Table and Id Length fields are used.

- Unique No – Holds the value Yes or Null.
- Base Table – Indicates a set of characters that can be used in the ID and it should have more than 10 characters set
- Id Length – Indicates the length of the ID allowable under selected circumstances (must be more than 11 characters).

This method of generating the ID removes the requirement for reading and locking a record in the LOCKING table. Instead an ID is generated and checked for exclusivity on the application, (checks the live, unauthorised and history files where applicable). If the ID is exclusive, then a ID is available to use, if not then the user can generate the next and test for exclusivity again. To provide more exclusive ID, the Base Table field can be updated with selected alpha or numeric characters (vowels are excluded to avoid embarrassing letter combinations being generated). If the Base Table field is left empty, then both zero and vowels are excluded, again to avoid embarrassing combinations.

In using the Unique No field, the user needs to consider the number of transactions per day and peak throughout.

A simple setup which uses a five digit sequence number appended to the standard application identifier and julian date may be acceptable in smaller institutions generating a few thousand deals, per application, per day. Larger transaction volumes make this choice impractical and therefore a more randomised ID structure is beneficial.

> **⚠️ Note:** After input or modification of the AUTO.ID.START and/or COMPANY record settings, the user must log out for the settings to take effect (as they are read at login time and stored in memory).

When using the Base Table settings (other than blank), it is recommended to ensure that the Id Length field is set to a pre-defined value. The use of these fields on standard applications without understanding, the possible impact can conflict with existing ID validation in the application or for SWIFT compliancy.

At each COMPANY level, the generation of new IDs is initially set in the Pgm Auto Id field, by entering the application name and an optional parameter. The optional parameter informs the system if the ID for the application must be generated automatically and that the user cannot enter one manually. This is done by appending M to the application in Pgm Auto Id field.

- To use the next ID option in ACCOUNT , but also allow manual generation: PGM.AUTO.ID ACCOUNT
- To permit only auto generation of next ID: PGM.AUTO.ID ACCOUNT


##### Duplicate Contract Checking

You can check the occurrence of duplicate contracts within the system. This setup is controlled using the following applications.

- EB.DUPLICATE
- EB.DUPLICATE TYPE

The EB.DUPLICATE.TYPE application acts as a parameter. It allows the definition of selected fields to check against a given application for the occurrence of any duplicate contracts.

The application in which the duplicates checks are supposed to be performed should first be defined in the Application field in the EB.DUPLICATE.TYPE application. A specific field (or fields) from the STANDARD.SELECTION record for that application (although at the moment duplicate checking is only used with funds transfer) can then be input to fields. Temenos Transact then checks for the occurrence of any duplicate contracts within the application against the fields defined.

The Purge Days field on this application defines the number of days the record of any duplicate contracts found remains on the EB.DUPLICATE table.

After authorisation, the Application field in the EB.DUPLICATE.TYPE record becomes No Change. It is however possible to change the value in Fields.

If the fields are changed, a record for that EB.DUPLICATE.TYPE has already been found, and is subsequently held on the EB.DUPLICATE table, then the old fields are not removed from the EB.DUPLICATE record. Therefore, it is recommended that new EB.DUPLICATE.TYPE records must be created instead of changing existing ones.

The EB.DUPLICATE table stores the records of all duplicate contracts, in accordance with the criteria defined on the parameter EB.DUPLICATE.TYPE application.

The duplicate FT contracts matching the criteria is listed under the Trans Ref field.

The period for which the duplicate contract record remains on this application is defined in the Purge Days field in EB.DUPLICATE.TYPE . In this example, the override indicates the possible duplicate deal. The following example shows the screens of a possible duplicate of FT transaction and update to the EB.DUPLICATE table.

The following screenshot shows the EB.DUPLICATE application:

| Linked App Field Condval | Value against which the application data needs to be compared |

##### Increasing the Length of ID and Field Attributes

The EB.OBJECT application is used to set the values for standard fields across Temenos Transact where they are being modified from the original settings.

An example of this is the use of extended account numbers. Since account number fields are used across Temenos Transact , it takes a considerable effort to modify each and every usage of an account field by application.

Using EB.OBJECT , the user can set the values to be used across the system and instruct the core IN2 routines to utilise the new settings from one central application.

> **⚠️ Note:** If extended account numbers should be used, the user must update the Account Mask field held in the COMPANY record as well. The AUTO.ID.START application must have its ‘ACCOUNT.NUMBER’ record amended, so that the Id Start field has the same number of characters as the Account Mask and the Max Length field in EB.OBJECT .

The user must also ensure to change the account number field length on any Enquiry or Report so that the extended account number fits.

The TRANSACTION application contains the information about all the transaction codes, which may be used within Temenos Transact , for each application. For example, if the transaction code is associated with a debit entry or a credit entry, it can be used in the DATA.CAPTURE application.

These codes contain and identify the important processing conditions, which are defaulted by the applications, if no other input has been entered at the transaction level. For each transaction code, it is possible to define when required, the different types of charges applicable to the specific transaction. Banks may charge their customers for services like standing orders, use of cash dispensers, and issuance of cheques and so on. This application allows the identification of these charges at the transaction level. Then, any of these charges can be processed by the Interest and Charge system.

A new data record for TRANSACTION has been released in EB.OBJECT where transaction codes up to 9999 can be created. This record allows the new range of transaction codes to be used in all applications.

Up to 999 transaction codes can be entered into the system. This can be extended to 9999 records, If a bank requires additional codes, an EB.OBJECT record should be defined for TRANSACTION with the Max Length field set to 4 (as shown in the below screenshot).

Once defined, the transaction codes may be created with ID up to four digits.

> **⚠️ Note:** When the transaction code application is configured to accept more than three digits, any enquiry or report that is in process should be amended to allow up to four characters.

The length of the amount field has increased from 15 (13+2) digits up to a maximum of 25 digits. The amount specified in EB.OBJECT includes the number of decimals, however excludes negative and positive signs, commas and periods from the digit count.

The following screenshot shows the EB.OBJECT application with Max Length Field set to a maximum length of 18:

The

with 18 digit (16 integers +2 decimals) amount for a USD currency and JPY currency.

> **⚠️ Note:** Number of decimals for USD and JPY currency is two.


##### Service to link PW and TWS Composer

The EB.SERVICE records create a link between the activities in PW (process workflow) and the TWS composer, so an automated activity or set of activities can be processed through a web service.

Most of the processing is based on user defined activities and localised code.


##### Error Messages

The EB.ERROR application defines Temenos Transact application errors in multiple languages. This table holds all the error messages which gets displayed whenever any event causes an error in any Temenos Transact application.

Error messages that have been defined on the application can be setup to contain the background information about the error message and the necessary steps has to be taken to resolve the problem. This information is displayed together with the error message at the time the error message is triggered. Background information comments can be set-up in the GB Error Info field.

Any comments on procedures for resolving the problem can be added into the Error Sol field. The Alt Error Cd field reduces the duplication of common error messages. It contains the ID of an alternative error record in the EB.ERROR application. Only the record ID and the Alt Error Cd fields should be defined, if this field is used. All the details for the error message are retrieved from the alternative error message record.

Errors can be configured to behave and appear differently depending on the channel that is used to access Temenos Transact . For example, a call centre or internet user may access Temenos Transact through different channels and can therefore be presented with a different type of override and error message.


##### Local Reference Table

It is possible to create user-defined fields (also known as local reference fields) in certain core applications of Temenos Transact to cater to local customisations. The following application are used to create the local reference fields:

Local elements may be defined for applications that have a Local Ref field (for example, the CUSTOMER application) and enables the user to create additional input fields that may be needed to meet local requirements.

A local reference field record named CUSTOMER.SEGMENT is created in

application and it must be linked to the

application.

This application allows the specific details of such fields to be defined:

- Including the name of the input field.
- The minimum and maximum number of characters.
- The type of characters.
- All possible input values.
- Whether the input is to be validated against the ID of another application.

Once the local field definitions are made in LOCAL.TABLE the next step is to specify where the fields are added and their inter-relationship with other local fields (if any). This is set in the LOCAL.REF.TABLE application. On authorising the record, the system updates the relevant STANDARD.SELECTION for the application and internal dictionary for that application.

The following screenshot shows the

application, linking the local table items to the

application.

Up to 999 elements may be specified for each application that allows the Local Ref fields. The Local Table No field is the local field reference from LOCAL.TABLE application, which defines the field characteristics. It is possible to link one or more fields into related groups which expand as a set using the Sub Assoc Code field (as shown in the above screenshot).

Temenos Transact may allow the usage of single, multi-value and sub-value fields but since the local fields are all in one position (field) on the application, these are demoted to single and multi-value only. It is not possible to construct a sub-value local field with the same operation as a standard in the Temenos Transact sub-value fields.

### 19.50  Person Entity Closure and Purge


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *The PERSON.ENTITY application captures the details of the person or entity. It is also used to capture the parties associated with other customers and potential prospects. It can be used to convert the person or entity into a prospective or an active customer.*
> 
> **Applications:** `CUSTOMER`, `PERSON.ENTITY`, `ST.CUSTOMER.CLOSURE`, `ST.CUSTOMER.EXIT.STATUS`
> 
> **Key Fields:** *'Allow Remove Exit Status'*, *Exit Status*, *Exit Status.*, *Person Entity Closure.*, *Purge Date*, *Request status*, *Status*, *status*
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

The PERSON.ENTITY application captures the details of the person or entity. It is also used to capture the parties associated with other customers and potential prospects. It can be used to convert the person or entity into a prospective or an active customer.

Read Customer Based Tables to know more information on PERSON.ENTITY .

This feature allows the user to specify whether the PERSON.ENTITY associated with the exited customer must be retained or closed once the customer role ends.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

There are no specific configuration to be setup at feature level. The parameter tables are setup at implementation stage.


#### 🔧 Working With

The user can close the customer using ST.CUSTOMER.CLOSURE or CUSTOMER , depending on the need to perform pre-closure checks on non-financial customer data. In both the cases, the user can decide whether the associated PERSON.ENTITY must be retained or closed after the customer role ends.


##### Exit initiated through CUSTOMER

When the customer exit is initiated through CUSTOMER and if an associated record exists in PERSON.ENTITY , a warning message is displayed while committing the CUSTOMER , as shown – ‘There is a person or entity linked to the CUSTOMER . Please update status in the linked PERSON.ENTITY ’.

The customer exit process continues after the warning is acknowledged. The system updates Exit Status in the CUSTOMER record if there is no pending financial obligation for the customer.

Once the customer exit is authorized, the user must manually update Status of the associated PERSON.ENTITY to ‘Active Ex-Customer’ or ‘Ex-Customer’.

- 'Active Ex-Customer' - Enables the user to maintain or edit the details of PERSON.ENTITY for other non-customer roles like Legal Solicitor, Director of an Entity, Auditor, and so on.

- 'Ex-Customer' - Indicates that the exited customer is not maintained for other non-customer roles and is purged after the exited customer record is purged.


##### Exit initiated through ST.CUSTOMER.CLOSURE

When the customer exit is initiated using ST.CUSTOMER.CLOSURE , the user updates the decision to retain or close the associated PERSON.ENTITY (if any) in the Person Entity Closure.

The user can indicate the decision to mark the associated PERSON.ENTITY as,

- ‘Yes’ – to mark the Status of PERSON.ENTITY as ‘Ex-Customer’, indicating that the PERSON.ENTITY are not maintained for non-customer role and amendment to the details is not possible.
- ‘No’ – to mark the Status of PERSON.ENTITY as ‘Active ’, indicating that the PERSON.ENTITY is maintained for non-customer roles and the user can amend the details, if required.

A sample customer closure request with Person Entity Closure as No is shown below:

When the ST.CUSTOMER.CLOSURE is processed by the CUSTOMER.CLOSURE service,if the closure request is approved, the service updates the Exit Status in the CUSTOMER and the status of PERSON.ENTITY based on the decision captured on the closure request.

Later on, when the bank end the relationship with the non-customer person or entity the user can change the Status from Active to Ex-Customer.


##### Reopening PERSON.ENTITY if CUSTOMER is reopened

The user can re-open an exited customer if 'Allow Remove Exit Status' in ST.CUSTOMER.EXIT.STATUS is enabled for the respective Exit Status.

- When Exit Status in the closed CUSTOMER record is cleared, the system updates Status of the linked PERSON.ENTITY to Active.

- When Customer exit is processed through ST.CUSTOMER.CLOSURE the user can change the Request status to Reopened. The Customer Closure service removes the Exit Status, Exit Reason, and Exit Date in both ST.CUSTOMER.CLOSURE and CUSTOMER . The Customer Closure service automatically updates the Status of the associated PERSON.ENTITY to ‘Active.’


##### Purging the PERSON.ENTITY to history

PERSON.ENTITY includes records linked or not linked to any customer.

- The PERSON.ENTITY records linked to a customer which have the Status as ‘Ex-Customer’ are purged to history when the associated customer is purged into history.
- The PERSON.ENTITY records not linked to any customer are purged to history when their Status is set to 'closed' and the bank runs the CUSTOMER.CLOSURE service.


##### Archiving the PERSON.ENTITY purged to history

The closed PERSON.ENTITY can be archived from history using the Transact Standard archival or Data Lifecycle Management (DLM) archival.

To archive the data to a read-only database, the DL product must be licensed. Otherwise, the data records are moved to the $ARC file through the standard archival method.

The closed PERSON.ENTITY and the related data records in history can be archived based on the Purge Date defined in the ARCHIVE for PERSON.ENTITY .

In the sample screenshot shown below, the Purge Date in ARCHIVE is defined as ‘01/JUN/2024’. When the user runs ARC.GENERIC (archival service) on ‘01/JUN/2024’, the files mentioned in the Arc File name that were moved to history before ‘01/JUN/2024', are archived.


#### 📋 Tasks

There are no Tasks available for Person Entity feature.


#### 📊 Outputs

There are no Outputs available for Person Entity feature.


> **Related Applications:** `CUSTOMER`, `PERSON.ENTITY`, `ST.CUSTOMER.CLOSURE`, `ST.CUSTOMER.EXIT.STATUS`
