### 20.8  Overdraft Protection and Shared Balances


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *This section explains about the Overdraft Protection and Shared Balances.*
> 
> **Applications:** `AC.ACCOUNTING.PARAM`, `AC.CASH.POOL`, `AC.CP.GROUP.PARAM`, `AC.CREDIT.CHECK`
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Balance To Use*, *Drop Credit Reservations*, *Main Master*, *No Hierarchy Reqd*, *Reserve Sweep Projections*, *Shared Balances*, *Sweep Debit Reservations*
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

This section explains about the Overdraft Protection and Shared Balances.


##### Overdraft Protection

Temenos Transact Overdraft Protection (ODP) is the functionality that enables banks to extend the option to their customers of authorising debit transactions even when there are insufficient funds in their checking account or corporate cash pool. This feature mitigates overdraft fees by automatically transferring funds from linked funding accounts such as Current or Checking Accounts, Lines of Credit, Savings, or Deposit Accounts.

The ODP conducts real-time balance checks and reserves the available funds on the funding accounts, that is, when a customer initiates a transaction that overdraws the checking account or the cash pool, the system assesses the available funds across connected funding accounts, places a lien on the available funds to extent of funds required to cover the overdraft on the transaction account as a part of the online transaction processing, ensuring customers are informed about their current balance status and potential overdraft situations.

However, the actual movement of funds from the funding account to the cash pool or the checking accounts is managed by the standard Temenos sweeping functionality provided by the Cash Pooling module. The ODP sweeps are run during the Transact COB.

The table below explains the types of funding accounts that supports ODP.

| Funding Accounts | Accounts Belong to | Pre-requisites in Accounts |
|---|---|---|
| Savings Accounts | Arrangement Accounts (AR) Product Line | Follow Component-based credit check processing |
| External Line of Credits | External Accounts (XP) Product Line | Configure Commitment Balance and Drawings Balance types |
| Investment Accounts | Arrangement Accounts (AR) Product Line | Configure Memo or Internal balance types Follow Component-based credit check processing |
| Line of Credits | Arrangement Loans (AL) Product Line | Configure Commitment Balance and Drawings Balance types |

> **⚠️ Note:** The primary role of ODP sweep projections is to prevent the overuse of balances on Funding Accounts, especially when the same funding source is linked across multiple ODP sweeps covering multiple checking accounts or cash pools. The availability of funds for direct withdrawal from funding accounts depends on the balance rules defined within the funding arrangement. These rules determine how funds are allocated and utilized across different accounts or cash pools, thus impacting the potential for direct fund withdrawal in various scenarios.


###### ODP from Multiple Sources

ODP facilitates funding from multiple sources. For example, checking an account that receives funding from both a savings account and a line of credit account for ODP in Retail. Similarly, an investment account and a line of credit account for ODP in Corporate funds a cash pool. Moreover, the same funding account can provide funds for multiple cash pools, or the same savings account can fund more than one checking or current account.


###### Real-time Sweep Projections

When the checking account or cash pool groups lack sufficient balance to cover a debit transaction, the system automatically considers the funds available in linked accounts. It reserves these funds as sweep projections before allowing the system to post the transaction thereby reducing the risk of funds being withdrawn from the linked accounts.


###### Real-time Adjustment of Sweep Projections

This ensures a dynamic response to changes in the checking account or cash pool groups. When the account receives funds, the system automatically drops or adjusts any sweep projections against the linked accounts. This allows the customer to access the funds in the linked accounts promptly, offering flexibility and efficient fund utilisation.


##### Shared Balances

Available funds across a cash pool of accounts can be maximised in Transact by the consolidation of account balances within and across sweep groups. When consolidated, surplus funds from one account can be used by the system to offset the deficits of another account. For example, the system automatically checks the consolidated balance from the cash pool compared to checking the individual account which may hold insufficient funds to execute, for example, a maintenance sweep. By consolidating balances, it provides corporate entities the ability to benefit from an available pool of cash resources, increasing financial control and better liquidity management.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

This topic covers the system-level and product-level configurations required for enabling Overdraft Protection (ODP) and Shared Balances features.


##### Enabling ODP for Retail Accounts

As a prerequisite, to enable ODP for Retail accounts like checking or current accounts, set-up a sweep group by defining Shared Balances as Accounts and No Hierarchy Reqd as Yes in AC.CP.GROUP.PARAM .

- It is not mandatory to define Main Master .
- When Balance To Use is not defined, by default the configurations defined at the level of Sweep Type take precedence.
- The sweep group is a one-time definition, that is, when a customer links another checking or current account to funding accounts for ODP, the sweeps can be defined under the same sweep group.

The checking or current accounts must be included in a maintenance style sweep using AC.CASH.POOL in order to link one or more funding accounts, such as a savings account or a line of credit.


##### Enabling ODP for Cash Pools

As a prerequisite, to enable ODP for Corporate cash pools, set-up a sweep group by defining Shared Balances as Pool Balance in AC.CASH.POOL .

- It is mandatory to define Main Master .
- When Balance To Use is not defined, by default the configurations defined at the level of Sweep Type take precedence.
- Each cash pool requires a separate sweep group.

The Main Master account of the cash pool must be included in a maintenance or a surplus or two-way style sweep using AC.CASH.POOL in order to link one or more funding accounts, such as an investment account or a line of credit.

Read the Sweep Setup section for more information on the creation and maintenance of sweeps.


##### Enabling Real-time Sweep Projections

By default, the system allocates the funds on the linked accounts against the overdraft allowed on the transaction accounts as a part of ODP. To disable the allocation of funds on the linked accounts, the user must set Reserve Sweep Projections as Disable in AC.ACCOUNTING.PARAM .


##### Enabling Overdraft Protection for Debit Holds or Reservations

To enable the Overdraft Protection feature for Debit Holds or Reservations, the user must set Sweep Debit Reservations to any of the values in AC.ACCOUNTING.PARAM as given below.

- Active – Funds are reserved on the funding account for the Active Debit Reservations, that is, the reservations with a start date as the current day or less than the current day.
- All – Funds are reserved on the funding account for all Debit Reservations including future-dated debit reservations.
- None (default) – No funds are reserved on the funding account as sweep projections.

If the user modifies the configuration, the same is applied for subsequent debit holds/reservations.

> **⚠️ Note:** Sweep Debit Reservations can be set as Active or All only if Reserve Sweep Projections is not set as Disable.


##### Drop or Adjust Sweep Projections Against the Credit Holds or Reservations

To enable the system to automatically drop or adjust sweep projections against the credit holds or reservations posted to the checking account, the user must set Drop Credit Reservations in AC.ACCOUNTING.PARAM as any of the below values.

- Active – Sweep projections on the funding account are dropped or adjusted only against the active credit reservations posted to the sweeping account. Active refers to the reservation with the start date as the current date.
- All – Sweep projections on the funding account are dropped or adjusted against the credit reservations posted to the sweeping account including future-dated credit reservations.
- None (default) – Sweep projections on the funding account are not dropped or adjusted based on the credit reservations posted to the sweeping account.

If the user modifies the configuration, the same is applicable only for subsequent credit holds/reservations.

> **⚠️ Note:** Drop Credit Reservations can be set as Active or All only if Reserve Sweep Projections is not set as Disable.


##### Credit Check Configuration for Enabling Overdraft Protection

Temenos Transact allows the bank to define a group of balance components using AC.CREDIT.CHECK to determine the funds available on the account, that are used in the funds check process. To consider funds available in the linked accounts during the funds check process on the checking accounts, the SWEEP component must be included in the credit check balance components group. Read Balance Components – AC.BALANCE.COMPONENT and Configuring the Available Balance – AC.CREDIT.CHECK to learn more about including the SWEEP component.

The user must link the credit check group created using AC.CREDIT.CHECK to respective transaction activities by configuring the accounts product conditions as shown below.


##### Shared Balances

The Shared Balances field in the AC.CP.GROUP.PARAM application determines if the account balances for a sweep group are consolidated. When used together with the Balance To Use field, it specifies to the system which balance type and amount the system should check and use for sweeping purposes.

When Shared Balances is set to Yes:

- The available balances of all accounts within the cash pool sweep group are consolidated.
- The consolidated balance is considered by the system, in the case, of overdrawn accounts during the execution of a maintenance sweep.

> **⚠️ Note:** The Balance To Use field must be set to Working.

When Shared Balances is set to Partial:

- The available balances of all accounts within the cash pool sweep group are consolidated
- The consolidated balance is considered by the system, in the case, of overdrawn accounts during the execution of a maintenance sweeps.

> **⚠️ Note:** The Balance To Use field can be set to any value other than Working.


#### 📋 Tasks

There are no Tasks available for Overdraft Protection and Shared Balances feature.


#### 📊 Outputs

Temenos Transact Overdraft Protection (ODP) is the functionality that enables banks to extend the option to their customers of authorising debit transactions even when there are insufficient funds in a checking account or corporate cash pool.


##### Enquiries and Reports

This section allows the user to view the below enquiries and reports.

Shared Account .

This enquiry displays information about the list of accounts that have shared balances. The user can execute the enquiry without query parameters or restrict results by entering a Group ID.

Sweep Movements .

This enquiry displays information about the list of sweep movements in a group.

Projected Sweep Movements .

This enquiry displays information about projected sweep movements.


##### SWIFT Messages

NA


##### Advices

NA


##### Alerts

NA

### 20.9  Sweep Groups


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *Sweep Groups are a set of linked accounts, belonging to the same customer in retail contexts or representing a cash pool of parent company or subsidiary accounts in corporate scenarios. These groups are designed to help financial institutions to efficiently sweep funds between accounts or entities f...*
> 
> **Applications:** `AC.CASH.POOL`, `AC.CP.GROUP.PARAM`, `EB.CONTRACT.BALANCES`
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Balance
 Routine*, *Balance
 To Use*, *Currency*, *Hierarchy Reqd*, *Main
 Group ID*, *Main
 Master*, *Main Group ID*, *Main Master* ... +6 more
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

Sweep Groups are a set of linked accounts, belonging to the same customer in retail contexts or representing a cash pool of parent company or subsidiary accounts in corporate scenarios. These groups are designed to help financial institutions to efficiently sweep funds between accounts or entities for the purposes of balance sharing, cash pooling or both.

In the Transact Sweeping Foundation, financial institutions can organise sweep groups into one of two structures, flat or hierarchical, to determine the transfer of funds between sweep and linked accounts. For example, a typical scenario in retail banking may involve the transfer of funds from a savings account to a checking or current account, which involves only two accounts and as such would be considered as a flat structure. However, this differs for corporate scenarios where a bank may have 4-5 company subsidiaries with their own set of cash pools linked to a parent company’s treasury account. In such cases, a hierarchical structure may dictate the direction of the allocation of funds to ensure that liquidity is managed across all entities involved.

The table below provides a visual representation of how accounts can be organised in a sweep group:

| Sweep Group Structures | Description | Visual Representation |
|---|---|---|
| One to one | One account linked to another account. For example, a retail customer checking / current account linked to a savings account |  |
| One to Many | One account linked to more than one account to define a sweep group. For example, a customer checking / current account linked to a savings account and a line of credit. |  |
| Main and Subgroups | A cash pool of accounts split into sweep groups. For example: Main Group – the primary group of accounts (for example, parent company accounts) that can be split into more than one subgroup. Sub group – a subset of accounts (for example, subsidiary company accounts) linked to an account(s) within the main group |  |


##### Main Master

When a hierarchical structure is required, especially in the case of corporate cash pools, financial institutions can define a Main Master account in the system. This account is situated at the top of the sweep group hierarchy, such as a high-interest or treasury account, in which linked account balances at the subgroup or main group level are either concentrated to or used as a source of funds to be drawn upon to cover deficit accounts.

- The definition of a Main Master account is only required for corporate cash pools where a hierarchical structure is required.
- Only those with a POFULL license subscription will have access to define sweep group hierarchies and define Main Master accounts. For users without a POFULL license, defining the Main Master is neither required nor possible.


##### Sweep Group Hierarchy

In Transact, sweep rules are applied based on the group hierarchy. If, for example, certain sweeping rules are set at main group level, these are set as default and applied to lower levels of the group hierarch, ensuring a consistent and prioritised execution of sweeps.

There may be a limited number of circumstances where sweep rules defined on a sweep may differ to the sweep group, for example, sweep suspensions. In such cases, the sweep group rules take precedence, if the associated configuration settings are defined.


##### Sequencing

When main and subgroups are involved, multiple sweep transactions can be run to facilitate liquidity requirements across multiple cash pool of accounts. The system can be manually instructed to run sweep transactions in a specific sequence within a sweep group with each sweep transaction given a sequence number. The higher the number, the lower the account in the group hierarchy, meaning that the sweep will be run first. This helps to ensure that certain accounts within the cash pool are sufficiently funded to cover credit and/or debit transactions.

Alternatively, the system can auto-generate the sequence of which sweeps are run first, which in the standard Temenos implementation is based on the creation order of sweep records in the group.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

Sweep groups are defined using the AC.CP.GROUP.PARAM application which captures basic details for both main groups and subgroups.

The table below details the necessary configurations in the AC.CP.GROUP.PARAM application:

| Fields | Description |
|---|---|
| Sub Group | Indicates if AC.CP.GROUP.PARAM record is a subgroup of a main group. If yes, the Main Group ID field must be populated with a valid AC.CP.GROUP.PARAM ID. |
| Main Group ID | The AC.CP.GROUP.PARAM record that the subgroup record is to be linked with. Applicable if the AC.CP.GROUP.PARAM record is a subgroup. |
| Main Master | Indicates the top-level account in the sweep group hierarchy. This account may determine certain settings that are applied to linked accounts, for example, currency denomination. Read Main Master for more information. |
| Shared Balances | Specifies whether the balances in the accounts within a sweep are grouped or not for overdraft checking for maintenance sweeps. Available options are: Yes Partial No |
| Sequencing | Determines whether the sequence of how of sweep records within the sweep group hierarchy should be processed should be automatically generated by the system or user-defined. Read Sequencing for more information. |
| Balance To Use | Specifies the balance the system should use to determine the available account balance for sweep calculations. Applied across all sweeps within a sweep group. The user can either define their own local routine to calculate the balance or use one of the several balances from the EB.CONTRACT.BALANCES record of the account to use: Ac.Balance.Type Booked Including Reservations Booked Less Locked Booked With Fwd Less Locked Online Actual Online Cleared Value Dated Working Working Less Locked Amt Read Defining Account Balance To Use for more information. |
| Balance Routine | Specifies the local routine to be used to calculate the balance for sweeping. Applicable when the user selects User Defined in the Balance To Use field. The local routine defined is checked against the rule supplied in AC.CASH.POOL . The PGM.FILE contains a record of this routine with its name and the type as ‘S’ |
| Currency | The defaulted currency of the account defined in the Main Master field. |
| Hierarchy Reqd | Defines if a hierarchical group structure should be setup for the record. If yes, the Main Master field is mandatory. |
| Sweep Reserve Condition | Calculates the debit holds and credit holds when Balance To Use is set as ‘Booked Including Reservations’. The available options are: Lock Funds Date Credit Reserve Date |

Read Sweep Setup for more information on how sweep group records created in AC.CP.GROUP.PARAM are used in the setup of sweep transactions.


#### 🔧 Working With

This section explains the working of Sweep Groups.


##### Main Sweep Group and Subgroups

To setup a sweep group, the user must create a valid AC.CP.GROUP.PARAM record. A Main Master account is given in the Main Master field to support the setup of a hierarchical structure.

To create a subgroup, the Sub Group field should be set to Yes and the Main Group ID field must have a valid Group ID.

> **⚠️ Note:** The AC.CP.GROUP.PARAM record for the Main Group must be created prior to creating the sub group record.


##### Sequencing

The user has the option to manually sequence the order in which sweep transactions are processed for a cash pool group or allow the system to automatically determine sequencing.

When the Sequence field is set to Auto in the AC.CP.GROUP.PARAM application, automatically processes sweeps in the group from the bottom-up. As a result, the user cannot edit the Sequence field in AC.CASH.POOL .

However, when the Sequence field is set to Manual, the user can input a sequence number in the AC.CASH.POOL . A higher sequence number means that the sweep for that account in the AC.CASH.POOL record is processed first.


#### 📋 Tasks

There are no Tasks available for Sweep Group feature.


#### 📊 Outputs

Sweep Groups are a set of linked accounts, belonging to the same customer in retail contexts or representing a cash pool of parent company or subsidiary accounts in corporate scenarios.


##### Enquiries and Reports

This section allows the user to view the below enquiries and reports.

Cash Pool Groups .

This enquiry displays information about cash pool groups. The user can execute the enquiry without query parameters or restrict results by entering a Group ID.

Cash Pool Group Links .

This enquiry displays information about cash pool group links. The user can execute the enquiry without query parameters or restrict results by entering a Group ID.

Shared Account .

This enquiry displays information about the list of accounts that have shared balances. The user can execute the enquiry without query parameters or restrict results by entering a Group ID.

Group Position .

This enquiry displays information about the group position along with the individual account balances.

Sweep Movements .

This enquiry displays information about the list of sweep movements in a group.

Interest Statement for Master Account .

This enquiry displays information about the accumulated interest for the Master Account in a cash pool group.

Interest Statement for Sub Account .

This enquiry displays information about the accumulated interest for a sub account within a cash pool group.

### 20.10  Sweep Reversals


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *When a sweep transaction is executed in the prior day COB process, and the bank requires the sweep transaction to be reversed (for example for legal or fraud-related purposes), the system offers the capability for all sweeping transactions within a particular sweeping group to be reversed (for examp...*
> 
> **Applications:** `AC.CASH.POOL`, `AC.CP.GROUP.PARAM`, `REV.GROUP.CP`
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Group ID*
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

When a sweep transaction is executed in the prior day COB process, and the bank requires the sweep transaction to be reversed (for example for legal or fraud-related purposes), the system offers the capability for all sweeping transactions within a particular sweeping group to be reversed (for example, funds swept to a checking or current account from a savings account is returned back the savings account).

> **⚠️ Note:** Intra-day sweeps cannot be reversed.

Based on the sweeping rules defined, the system re-executes the sweep transactions in the next scheduled COB process, unless intra-day sweeps have been defined.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

The REV.GROUP.CP application reverses sweep transactions for a specific sweep group that has been run during the most recent COB process.

The Group ID field in REV.GROUP.CP specifies the sweep group ID from the AC.CP.GROUP.PARAM application, identifying sweep transactions that need to be reversed.


#### 🔧 Working With

To reverse sweep transactions for a specific group from the most recent COB process, the user must provide a valid AC.CP.GROUP.PARAM ID record for the sweep group in the REV.GROUP.CP application, to initiate the sweep reversals.

> **⚠️ Note:** The system continues to run sweeps for the group in future COB processes, as per the sweeping rules, unless the user has suspended or cancelled the sweep.

| Sweep Record | Sweep Account | Rule | Link Account | Minimum Amount | Maximum Amount | Sequence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 184375 (Account Balance: 1,000 USD) | Maintenance | 105461 (Account Balance: 2,000 USD) | 300 USD |  | 10 |
| 2 | 105461 (Account Balance: 2,000 USD) | Surplus | 163290 (Account Balance: 500 USD) |  | 1,500 USD | 5 |


#### 📋 Tasks

There are no Tasks available for Sweep Reversals feature.


#### 📊 Outputs

There are no Outputs available for Sweep Reversals feature.

### 20.11  Sweep Setup


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *Temenos Transact Sweeping Foundation provides banks the ability to automatically transfer funds from one account or cash pool to another.*
> 
> **Applications:** `AC.ACCOUNT.SWEEP.ERROR`, `AC.ACCOUNT.SWEEP.HIST`, `AC.CASH.POOL`, `AC.CASH.POOL.HIST`, `AC.CP.GROUP.PARAM`, `AC.SWEEP.CONDITIONS`, `AC.SWEEP.TYPE`, `ACCOUNT` ... +8 more
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Acct
 Mode*, *Acct Mode*, *Aggregate
 Balance*, *Aggregate Balance*, *Balance Routine*, *Balance To Use*, *Blocking Date*, *Cashflow Amount* ... +61 more
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

Temenos Transact Sweeping Foundation provides banks the ability to automatically transfer funds from one account or cash pool to another.

To setup a sweep instruction, there must be a sweep account, link account(s), and a pre-determined set of rules. Based on a set of pre-determined rules, sweep instructions are executed to facilitate surpluses and deficits between accounts.

Transact supports four sweep types:

- Maintenance Sweep
- Surplus Sweep
- Two-Way Sweep
- Cash-Flow Sweep


##### Maintenance Sweeps

Maintenance Sweeps ensures a target balance is maintained for accounts such as checking / current accounts or corporate cash pools. This functionality allows both individual retail customers and corporate organisations to optimise their cash flows by automatically transferring funds between accounts, ensuring effective liquidity management for day-to-day transactions.

The system monitors the balance in the checking or operational account at pre-determined intervals. When the balance falls below the minimum target balance, the system sweeps from the linked account to restore the target balance. By doing so, this helps the bank and its customers to maintain sufficient funds for daily transactions.

For retail banking, maintenance sweep helps a bank and its customers to meet minimum balance requirements and minimise account fees, reducing the prevalence of using available overdraft limits on an account.

For corporate banking, maintenance sweeps ensures that accounts within cash pools remain adequately funded, leveraging surplus funds from treasury, investment, or other corporate accounts to optimise returns.


##### Surplus Sweeps

Surplus sweeps, enable banks to automatically transfer surplus funds to a concentration account to optimise cash utilisation and generate greater cash returns.

The system monitors account balances at specific intervals and when the account balance exceeds a pre-defined threshold, the system automatically transfers excess funds into a linked account. This ensures that funds can reap higher interest gains in other accounts such as individual savings for retail customers or investments for corporates.


##### Two-Way Sweeps

Two-Way Sweeps allow funds to be both transferred to and drawn from linked accounts. It combines the functionality of both the maintenance and surplus sweep, enabling funds to be swept to maintain balances when there is a shortfall and sweep surplus funds to higher interest accounts to ensure an optimal balance.


##### Cash Flow Sweeps

Cash Flow Sweeps offer similar functionality to Two-Way sweeps; however, banks have the option to restrict the level of funds swept to and from accounts or within a corporate cash pool.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

This section details the configuration involved in the Sweep Setup.


##### Sweep Rule Setup

To create sweep rules for different sweep types, the AC.SWEEP.TYPE application is used to create the rules for sweep types. Multiple AC.SWEEP.TYPE records can be created with different rule combinations for each sweep type.

The user can use either pre-defined sweep types available in Transact or define their own in AC.SWEEP.TYPE .

> **⚠️ Note:** A valid AC.SWEEP.TYPE record must be available prior to creating any AC.CASH.POOL or AC.CP.GROUP.PARAM records.

The table below details the necessary configurations in the AC.SWEEP.TYPE application.

| Field Names | Description |
|---|---|
| Sweep Style | Defines the sweep rule type for sweep instructions. Transact provides several available options including: Maintenance Surplus Two-Way Cashflow Read Introduction to Sweep Setup for more information. |
| Cr Txn Code , Dr Txn Code , Ret Cr Txn Code , Ret Dr Txn Code | Defines the transaction code to be used for debit and credit sweeps. For maintenance sweeps, only Cr Txn Code and Dr Txn Code are required to be populated. For surplus, two-way and cash flow sweeps, Ret Cr Txn Code and Ret Dr Txn Code are also required. |
| Use Limits | Instructs the system to check if an overdraft limit is attached to an account. Read Overdraft Limits for more information. |
| Prioritise OD | Determines the priority of overdrawn accounts when funds are swept if more than one linked account is involved. Helps to offset overdrawn account balances to zero before executing sweep instructions for other linked accounts. If set to No, then funds are all swept into the first link sweep instruction If set to Yes, then funds are swept first to the overdrawn account to offset the balance to zero. |
| Return At Sod | Instructs the system to return funds swept during the prior day COB, to the originating account during the next day Start of Day (SOD) process. |
| Balance To Use | Specifies the balance the system should use to determine the available account balance for sweep calculations. The user can either define their own local routine to calculate the balance or use one of the several balances from the EB.CONTRACT.BALANCES record of the account to use: Ac.Balance.Type Booked Including Reservations Booked Less Locked Booked With Fwd Less Locked Online Actual Online Cleared Value Dated Working Working Less Locked Amt Read Defining Account Balance To Use for more information. |
| Restrict Sweep | Instructs the system to stop or override a sweep based on posting restriction rules set on the CUSTOMER or ACCOUNT record. Read Posting Restrictions for more information. |
| Acct Mode | Identifies the accounting mode used for sweep execution. Transact provides the following available options: SAO SNP Read Partial Sweeps for more information. |
| Sweep Reserve Condition | Calculates the debit holds and credit holds when the Balance To Use field is set as Booked Including Reservations. Transact provides the following available options: Lock Funds Date Credit Reserve Date Read Defining Account Balance To Use for more information. |
| Partial Transfer | Determines whether the sweep should be executed in the case of insufficient funds to debit the sweep account. Read Partial Sweeps for more information. |

The AC.SWEEP.CONDITIONS application is used to store the conditions to be applied to a sweep types before sweep execution.

The conditions set by the user in the AC.SWEEP.CONDITIONS record are applied to the AC.SWEEP.TYPE record to which it is attached to. The sweep conditions defined are applicable to sweep records using the specific sweep type. The record ID is a free text-CCY-Date and supported in the local currency only.

The table below details the necessary configurations in the AC.SWEEP.CONDITIONS application.

| Fields | Description |
|---|---|
| Sweep Type | The sweep type for which the conditions are to be applied to. |
| Max Contribution Amount | Indicates the maximum amount that can be invested in the Investment account on a given day across all the customers participating in the investment. Sum of all the investment amount across all the customers in an investment account on a given day should be less than or equal to the maximum contribution amount. |
| Min Contribution Amount | Indicates the minimum amount that can be invested in the Investment account on a given day across all the customers participating in the investment. Sum of all the investment amount across all the customers in an investment account on a given day should be greater than or equal to the minimum contribution amount. |
| Max Redemption Amount | Indicates the maximum amount that a customer can withdraw from an investment account on a given day. |
| Min Redemption Amount | Indicates the minimum amount that a customer can withdraw from an investment account on a given day. |
| Max Sweep Amount | Indicates the maximum amount that can be swept at a time from the current account to the investment account. |
| Min Sweep Amount | Indicates the minimum amount that can be swept at a time from the current account to the investment account. |
| Sweep Unit Amount | Holds the unit amount in terms of which the sweep must happen. |
| Min Max Amount Currency | Indicates the Currency of the Maximum and Minimum Sweep Amount. |
| Maximum Amount | Controls the maximum amount that can be in place on the account. Only applicable for the following sweep types: Surplus Two-Way Cashflow The value given is defaulted in the Maximum Amount field in the AC.CASH.POOL record. |
| Minimum Amount | Controls the maximum amount that can be in place on the account. Only applicable for the following sweep types: Maintenance Two-Way Cashflow The value given is defaulted in the Minimum Amount field in the AC.CASH.POOL record. |


##### Sweep Setup

The AC.CASH.POOL application records the sweeping rules for a set of sweep instructions, which the system checks prior to the sweeping of funds between accounts (or a cash pool of accounts).

The record ID is denoted by an account number and in which the sweeping instructions apply to. Sweep instructions for one or more linked accounts can be setup on the same record by the user with each consisting of its own specific set of rules on the same record.

- A valid AC.CP.GROUP.PARAM record must be set up for corporate cash pool sweep groups before creating a sweep in the AC.CASH.POOL application.
- For the setup of retail sweeps, a AC.CP.GROUP.PARAM record is automatically generated by the system when the user commits the AC.CASH.POOL record.

The table below details the necessary configurations in the AC.CASH.POOL application.

| Field Names | Description |
|---|---|
| Group ID | The AC.CP.GROUP.PARAM record that the AC.CASH.POOL ID account number belongs to |
| Sub Group | If applicable, The AC.CP.GROUP.PARAM subgroup record that the AC.CASH.POOL ID account number belongs to |
| Main Master | The top-level account defined in the main or subgroup AC.CP.GROUP.PARAM record which linked account balances are either pooled to or pooled from. Read Sweep Groups for more information. |
| Sequence | Indicates the order position number that the AC.CASH.POOL sweep record is processed within the sweep group. Read Sequencing for more information. |
| Link Account | The account number that has a relationship with the Sweep Account and where funds are either swept to the account (surplus sweep) or from the account (maintenance sweep) or both. |
| Rule | The sweep type associated with the AC.CASH.POOL record and occurs between the sweep account and the link account. The sweep type must be first defined as a record in AC.SWEEP.TYPE (for example, maintenance, surplus, two-way and so on.) |
| Frequency | Instructs the system how often the sweep instructions are executed. Transact provides the following options: BSNSS (Business Days) WEEK1 (Weekly) M0101 (Monthly) M0331 (Quarterly) Defined (Specific Recurrence) |
| Minimum Amount | The minimum account balance to be maintained within an account. If the account balance falls below this figure, the sweep instruction is triggered to transfer funds from the linked account. Only applicable for the following sweep types: Maintenance Two-Way Cash Flow |
| Maximum Amount | The maximum account balance that should be held within an account. If the account balance falls below this figure, the sweep instruction is triggered to transfer funds from the Link Account. Only applicable for the following sweep types: Surplus Two-Way Cash Flow |
| Rule Priority | The priority level that a specific link sweep instruction has other links if more than one sweep instruction is triggered on the same day. |
| Return Rule Priority | The priority level that a specific link surplus sweep instruction has other links if more than one sweep instruction is triggered on the same day. Only applicable for the following sweep types: Surplus Two-Way |
| Aggregate Balance ; Cashflow Amount | The Aggregate Balance and Cashflow Amount fields control the amount of funds that can be taken from a higher-level account in the group hierarchy. |

> **⚠️ Note:** Most fields in AC.CASH.POOL application are multi-valued, meaning several rules can be applied for different linked accounts.


#### 🔧 Working With

The AC.SWEEP.TYPE application is used to create sweep types. These can be pre-defined (in-built Temenos Transact offering) or user-defined with different rule combinations.

For each sweep type, the user must capture at a minimum:

- Sweep Style
- Frequency
- Sweep Account
- Link Account
- Minimum Amount / Maximum Amount (dependent on sweep type)


##### Creating Maintenance Sweeps

Maintenance Sweeps are used to ensure that the account balance of a sweep account is maintained above a specified threshold. A user can define this threshold in the AC.CASH.POOL application.

When the account balance drops below this threshold, funds are automatically debited from the link account and credited to the sweep account to restore the balance.

To setup a maintenance sweep record, Sweep Style , which determines the type of sweep to be set up, is set to Maintenance.

- A maintenance sweep record is created in AC.CASH.POOL for Account B (Sweep Account) and Account A (Link Account).
- Account A has a credit balance of 500 USD and Account B has a balance of zero.
- The Rule field is set as Maintenance and the Minimum Amount field is set to 200.
- During COB, the system checks the balance of Account B. As the balance of Account B has fallen below the minimum amount of 200, the system automatically sweeps funds of 200 USD from Account A and credits Account B.


##### Creating Surplus Sweeps

Surplus Sweeps are used when excess funds above a certain threshold for an account are transferred to another account. A user can define this threshold in the AC.CASH.POOL application.

When the account balance exceeds the threshold, surplus funds are automatically debited from the sweep account and credited to the link account.

To setup a surplus sweep record, Sweep Style is set to Surplus.

- A surplus sweep record is created in AC.CASH.POOL for Account A (Link Account) and Account B (Sweep Account).
- Account A has a debit balance of 100 USD and Account B has a credit balance of 500 USD.
- The Rule field is set as Surplus and the Maximum Amount field is set to 200.
- When the balance exceeds the maximum amount of 200, during the COB process, the system automatically sweeps surplus funds of 300 USD from Account B and credits Account A.


##### Surplus Sweep for Interest Benefit

If the Return At Sod field is set to Yes in the AC.SWEEP.TYPE record, the funds are automatically returned to the account during Start Of Day (SOD) processing, making funds available.

- A surplus sweep record is created in AC.CASH.POOL for Account A (Link Account) and Account B (Sweep Account).
- Account A has a debit balance of 100 USD and Account B has a credit balance of 500 USD.
- The Rule field is set as Surplus and the Maximum Amount field is set to 200.
- The Return At Sod field is set to Yes.
- When the balance exceeds the maximum amount of 200, during the COB process, the system automatically sweeps surplus funds of 300 USD from Account B and credits Account A.
- At the end of the COB process, the balance for Account A and B are 200 USD credit.
- When the SOD process is executed at the start of the next day, the system automatically sweeps the initial 300 USD swept during the prior day COB process from Account A and credits back to Account B.
- This results in a debit balance of 100 USD for Account A and a credit balance of 500 for Account B.


##### Creating Two-Way Sweeps

To create a Two-Way Sweep record, the user must set Sweep Style to Two-Way and set transaction codes for Cr Txn Code , Dr Txn Code , Ret Cr Txn Code , Ret Dr Txn Code fields.

- A two-way sweep record is created in AC.CASH.POOL for Account B (Sweep Account) and Account A (Link Account).
- The Rule field is set as Two-way, the Minimum Amount field is set to 250 and the Maximum Amount field is set to 200.
- Account A has a current credit balance of 1,200 USD and Account B has a debit balance of 400 USD.
- During COB processing, the system first check accounts that require a minimum balance to be maintained. Account B has fallen below its minimum balance of 250 USD (maintenance sweep). The system automatically sweeps 650 USD in funds from Account A to Account B.
- The system then performs a secondary check for accounts that have a funds surplus (during the same COB process). As the balance for Account B is within the minimum and maximum amounts, the system performs no surplus sweep.
- If during the next day, 200 USD in credit transactions are made to Account B resulting in a balance of 450 USD. This results in the account balance exceeding the maximum.
- During COB processing, the system first checks if a maintenance sweep is required.
- If no maintenance sweep is required, the system performs the secondary surplus sweep check. Account B has surplus funds of 150 USD. The system automatically sweeps the 150 USD from Account B to Account A.
- At the end of COB, Account A has a credit balance of 300 and Account B has a credit balance of 300 USD.


##### Creating Cash Flow Sweeps

To create a Cash Flow Sweep record, the user must set Sweep Style to Cashflow.

The user can restrict the amount of funds swept between accounts within a corporate cash pool by entering a value in the Cashflow Amount field in the AC.CASH.POOL record.

- A sweep group record is created in AC.CP.GROUP.PARAM with Account A defined as the Main Master account.
- A cash-flow sweep record is created in AC.CASH.POOL for Account B (Sweep Account) and Account A (Link Account).
- Account A has a current credit balance of 1,200 USD and Account B has a balance of zero.
- The Rule field is set as Cashflow and the Cashflow Amount field is set as 100,000 USD, establishing a cash flow limit.
- Account B is credited with 50,000 USD. The system automatically sweeps 50,000 USD to Account A during COB.
- The next day, the Aggregate Balance field is 50,000, meaning the available funds that can be used is 150,000 USD (Cashflow Amount + Aggregate Balance) to cover shortfalls.
- A debit transaction of 200,000 USD is made to Account B resulting in an overdraft balance of 200,000 USD.
- Although Account B has an overdraft balance of 200,000, the system can only sweep up to the cash flow limit set which is 150,000 USD.
- The next day, the Aggregate Balance field is -100,000 USD. The available funds are maxed out, meaning no more funds can be taken until further transfers have been made to the higher-level account, which in this case is Account A.
- The Cashflow Amount field remains at 100,000 USD.


##### Creating Multi-currency Sweeps

Banks that engage with individual and corporate customers that conduct international transactions can use the Transact Sweeping Foundation module provides functionality to setup funds to be swept between linked accounts denominated in different currencies, for example, USD, GBP, and JPY.

At the time of execution, the system converts funds using the most appropriate exchange rate between the Mid, Buy or Sell rate from the CURRENCY table based on the value defined in the Exchange Rate Type field of AC.CP.GROUP.PARAM application.

The spread that needs to be applied on the exchange rate is defined in the Exchange Rate Spr field in the AC.CP.GROUP.PARAM application, which is defaulted in the same field in the AC.CASH.POOL application record. The user can amend the defaulted value.

Market exchange profit for the spread amount is calculated and accounted into the PL category defined in the POMKKEXCHPFT of ACCOUNT.CLASS application. The details of exchange rate, spread, market exchange profit, and so on are updated in the AC.CASH.POOL.HIST record.

When a sweep is reversed, the exchange rate used at the time of sweep execution is used at the time of reversal.

| Account | Currency | Main Master Account | Account Balance |
|---|---|---|---|
| 513983 | GBP | Yes | 600 |
| 263919 | USD | No | 400 |
| 629461 | EUR | No | -200 |


##### Intra- and Inter-Bank Account Sweeping

Sweeps transactions can be setup between Transact accounts and external accounts held in other core banking systems within the bank’s infrastructure or with another financial institution.

This functionality supports the automatic sweeping of funds without manual intervention and when executed, a payment order is generated for the sweep amount.

When sweep transactions are sent to an external account, the system retrieves the details about the beneficiary and settlement from the BENEFICIARY table. The user should define the account held with the other financial institution and related details in the BENEFICIARY table, before setting up the external sweep.

> **⚠️ Note:** Internal Wash Accounts must be defined for external sweep transactions to be processed by using the Po Wash Categ field in the AC.SWEEP.TYPE application. This enables the user to define the Beneficiary ID in the AC.CASH.POOL application.

The Payment Product field in the AC.CASH.POOL application allows the user to select the payment method. When executing a sweep, the system identifies the sweep as an external payment and triggers production of the payment order, based on the information defined in the BENEFICIARY table and the Payment Product field.

| Sweep Record | Sweep Account | Rule | Link Account | Maximum Amount | Frequency | Beneficiary ID | Pref Pymt Product |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 824736 (Account Balance: 300 USD) | Surplus | 915382 (Account Balance: 400 USD) Memo Type Account | 200 USD | BSNSS (every business day) | 749264 | ACSWEEP |


##### Sweep Charges

For individual or corporate cash pool group sweeping, various charges can be collected for various sweeping activities, for example, for sweep execution.

> **⚠️ Note:** Current PO functionality does support sweep charging, however, it is recommended for users to use the Activity Charges feature in the Retail Accounts (AR) module.

To setup a sweep charge, the user must populate the following fields in the AC.CASH.POOL application:

- Charge Code
- Charge Amount
- Tax Amount
- Charge Account

The values entered in these fields are cleared by the system on authorisation, to enable the user to collect charges for any subsequent events such as sweep suspension and cancellation.

- The user must enter in the Charge Code field a valid record ID of FT.COMMISSION.TYPE
- When flat or fixed amount is not defined in a FT.COMMISSION.TYPE record, the user enters a value in the Charge Amount field.
- Charge or fee collected for setting up a sweep is a flat amount.

To collect sweep charges for successful sweep transactions, the Sweep Chg Code field in the AC.CP.GROUP.PARAM application must have a valid record ID from FT.COMMISSION.TYPE . For corporate cash pool groups, this is defaulted for every sweep record defined under the group in AC.CASH.POOL application.

The user can define the charge amount to be collected in the Sweep Chg Amount field. Otherwise, the system calculates the charge amount based on the sweep amount and the conditions defined in FT.COMMISSION.TYPE .

- When the default sweep charge is defined at the sub group level, the condition defined at the subgroup level overrides the conditions defined at the group level.
- The sweep charge amount collection mode for successful maintenance sweeps is debit plus charge.
- The sweep charge amount collection mode for successful surplus sweeps is credit less charge.

If sweep charges are to be waived, the user can set the Waive Charges field to No in the AC.CASH.POOL application.


##### Overdraft Limits

When accounts have insufficient funds available, pre-approved overdraft limits provide additional source of funds to cover short-term cash shortfalls, unexpected debit transactions or manage temporary liquidity issues.

Sweeps setup in the system can use or disregard overdraft limits attached to an account, if the account becomes overdrawn. Banks can setup sweeps to consider overdraft limits attached to link account(s), increasing available funds, or disregard the limit, only considering the balance of the account.

This can differ depending on the scenario. For example, a sweep group of 2-3 customer accounts may consider the full overdraft limit attached to a checking / current account. However, for sweep groups involving multiple cash pool of accounts in a corporate scenario, the use of overdraft limits may be up to a sanctioned amount to ensure that limits are not exceeded.

Read Account Limits for more information about Account Limits and Overdrafts.

The Use Limits field in AC.SWEEP.TYPE application allows the system to check if an overdraft limit is linked to the sweep account and can be utilised to cover the need for additional funds.

When Use Limits is set as:

- Yes - The system includes the overdraft limit amount (or up to the sanctioned limit) in the calculation of the total account balance available for sweeping.
- No – The system does not consider the overdraft limit attached to the link account and executes the sweep per the sweeping rules.

| Sweep Instruction | Sweep Account | Rule | Link Account | Maximum Amount | Overdraft Limit Attached |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Account 231849 (Account Balance: 400 USD) | Maintenance | Account 183173 (Account Balance: 150 USD) | 200 USD | Yes – 100 USD |


##### Partial Sweeps

The Partial Transfer field in AC.SWEEP.TYPE application allows the user to set whether the system should make a partial transfer when there are insufficient funds in the linked accounts, instead of not executing the sweep transaction whenever limitations exist. For example, because of a maximum concentration cap or insufficient available funds.

> **⚠️ Note:** The Partial Transfer field is not available for retail account sweeping.

The user can allow overdrafts on the account using the Acct Mode field, which are not Memo type.

When the Acct Mode field is set as:

- Sao – The system accepts any overrides encountered whilst executing a sweep transaction and the sweep is executed. This includes if an account is attached to an overdraft limit that can be used for sweeping purposes. Successful sweeps are stored in AC.ACCOUNT.SWEEP.HIST .
- Snp – The system rejects any overrides encountered whilst executing a sweep transaction, resulting the sweep not being executed. This may be due to an insufficient account balance or an account level restriction, for example, locked amounts or posting restrictions. Details of rejected sweeps are stored in AC.ACCOUNT.SWEEP.ERROR .

This is applied for both maintenance and surplus sweeps, irrespective of the options selected in the Partial Transfer field.

| Sweep Instruction | Sweep Account | Rule | Link Account | Minimum Amount | Rule Priority | Overdraft Limit Attached |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Account 583863 (Account Balance: -600 USD) | Maintenance | Account 378224 (Account Balance: 400 USD) | 0 USD | 2 | No |
| 2 | Maintenance | Account 261833 (Account Balance: 400 USD) | 0 USD | 1 | Yes – 700 USD |  |


##### Defining Account Balance To Use

When calculating the amount to be swept to or from an account, the system enables banks to select which account balance is used, with consideration for the accounting mode set for sweeps and any locked amounts on the involved accounts.

Locked amounts can be excluded from the sweeping account and the sweep is executed by split per value date. When processing the sweep, the system considers the locked amount and the remaining amount is swept to the master account with split per value date. The locked amount is maintained in the respective account sweep history, regardless of the sweeping process. It considers the current date locked amount for the current value dated transactions.

History of locks on the sweeping account is maintained for a defined period. The standard setup allows such history to be maintained up to 30 calendar days. While processing the sweep, the system considers the history of the locked amount on the sweep account.

| Balance Type | Description |
|---|---|
| Online Cleared | The account balance that represents funds from all cleared transactions that are available for withdrawal and use during the day. This includes transactions where the exposure date is realised as of Start of Day (SOD) and excludes those with an exposure date in the future. |
| Online Actual | The account balance that represents funds from all cleared and uncleared transactions that are available for withdrawal and use during the day. This includes authorised transactions where the exposure date is realised, as of Start of Day (SOD) or are future-dated. |
| Working | This account balance represents the current funds cleared and available in an account. This includes any pending or unauthorised debit transactions and excludes pending or unauthorised credit transactions. It shows the lowest balance available compared to the actual balance that may be available for withdrawal and use. Critical for online sweeps, as at eod, any unauthorised transactions are placed on hold and the working balance is adjusted accordingly. |
| Working Less Locked | This account balance represents the working balance, less any locked amounts on the sweep account. |
| Booked Including Reservations | This balance is the online actual balance plus any debit holds/reservations and credit holds or reservations. The debit and credit holds are considered based on the configuration done in the multi-valued Sweep Reserve Condition field in the AC.CASH.POOL application, which allows the user to select: Lock Funds Date - indicates only Active* debit reservations or debit-locked events are considered for calculating the available or usable balance of the sweeping account. Credit Reserve Date – indicates only Active* credit reservations or credit-locked events are considered for calculating the available or usable balance of the sweeping account. When the Sweep Reserve Condition field is not configured then the maximum of debit holds and minimum of credit holds are considered for the sweeping account. Sweep Reserve Condition can only be configured if the Balance To Use field has the option Booked Including Reservations. |
| Booked Less Locked | This balance is the online actual balance less all locked amounts posted to the account. |
| Booked with Fwd Less Locked | This balance is the online actual balance with the inclusion of future credit and debit balance projections less all locked amounts posted to the account. |
| Value Dated | This account balance represents the current funds cleared and available in an account after excluding any future- dated FT, teller, or DC entries. It is used when back-value dated adjustment is required. This option is only available for legacy (AC) and Arrangement accounts. |
| Ac.Balance.Type | This balance is used for the settlement of contracts created using the Arrangement Architecture (AA) in Temenos Transact. |
| User Defined | This balance is defined by the user for sweeping purposes (based on the bank’s requirement). A local routine is used to calculate the balance to be moved. The balance supplied by the routine is checked against the rule specified in the AC.CASH.POOL application. The local routine is specified in the Balance Routine field. There is a record in the PGM.FILE with the name of the routine and the type as S. |

##### Posting Restrictions

Posting of sweep transactions can be configured to be restricted at account or customer level.

When the Restrict Sweep field is set to Null or No, the system ignores any posting restrictions set on the account or customer record and executes the sweep, per its rules.

When the Restrict Sweep field is set to Yes, the system stops the sweep process based on the following conditions:

- When a POSTING.RESTRICT record with Restriction Type field set to All or Debit is attached to the Customer whose account is to be debited or to the debit account itself in the sweep process.
- When a POSTING.RESTRICT record with Restriction Type field set to All or Credit is attached to the Customer whose account is to be credited or to the credit account itself in the sweep process.
- When the account in a sweep process is attached to a SEC.ACC.MASTER record, which is blocked (the Blocking Date field is set to a value), the system stops the sweep from the date specified in the Blocking Date field.
- If the Debit Restrict field is set to Yes in the ACCT.GROUP.CONDITION record of an account which is to be debited in the sweep process.


#### 📋 Tasks

There are no Tasks available for Sweep Setup feature.


#### 📊 Outputs

Temenos Transact Sweeping Foundation provides banks the ability to automatically transfer funds from one account or cash pool to another. To setup a sweep instruction, there must be a sweep account, link account(s), and a pre-determined set of rules. Based on a set of pre-determined rules, sweep instructions are executed to facilitate surpluses and deficits between accounts .

Sweep History .

This enquiry displays information about the history of all sweeps that have occurred.

Group Position .

This enquiry displays information about the group position along with the individual account balances.

Sweep Movements .

This enquiry displays information about the list of sweep movements in a group.

### 20.12  Sweep Suspensions and Cancellations


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *In Transact, banks can suspend sweep instructions between the sweep and link account or a cash pool of accounts within a sweep group. Sweeps can be either temporarily suspended until a defined end date or indefinitely, without deleting the sweep record from the system.*
> 
> **Applications:** `AC.CASH.POOL`, `AC.CP.GROUP.PARAM`
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Link Susp End Date*, *Link Susp Start Date*, *Link Sweep Cancel Date*, *Susp End Date*, *Susp Sign*, *Susp Start Date*, *Suspend Indefinite*, *Sweep Cancel Date*
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

In Transact, banks can suspend sweep instructions between the sweep and link account or a cash pool of accounts within a sweep group. Sweeps can be either temporarily suspended until a defined end date or indefinitely, without deleting the sweep record from the system.

For a given sweep, the system also provides the ability for banks to cancel specific sweep instructions between the sweep account and link account where there may be multiple sweep instructions, or all sweep instructions associated to a sweep account to be cancelled.

The table below shows the key highlights of sweep suspensions and cancellations.

| Sweep Suspensions | Sweep Cancellations |
|---|---|
| Applies to an entire sweep group including main groups and subgroups or to a specific subgroup. Applies to both existing sweep transactions and those created within the suspension period for a sweep group. Can be configured to take immediate effect or a scheduled date in the future. | Applies to all sweep instructions or a specific sweep instruction on the sweep record. Can be configured to take immediate effect or a scheduled date in the future. |


#### ⚙️ Configuration

This section details the configurations involved in processing sweep suspensions and cancellations.


##### Sweep Suspensions

Sweep suspensions can be set at different levels within Transact to determine if sweeps should be executed during COB (or intra-day) based on the configuration settings for Susp Start Date , Susp End Date and Suspend Indefinite fields in either AC.CP.GROUP.PARAM or AC.CASH.POOL applications.

If there is an active suspension at a higher level in the hierarchy, any sweep instructions defined lower in the hierarchy are also suspended. For example, if the current system date falls between Susp Start Date and Susp End Date on the main AC.CP.GROUP.PARAM record, no sweeps will be executed for the entire sweep group until the suspension end date.

The user can configure the temporary suspension of all sweeps for a cash pool of accounts within a sweep group using the Susp Start Date and Susp End Date fields on the group’s AC.CP.GROUP.PARAM ID record:

- Susp Start Date - The date from which sweep execution for all sweep records within a sweep group are suspended from. Sweep transactions are suppressed in the system meaning no funds are swept from/to any accounts during COB (or intra-day if setup). This restriction is applied to: Existing sweep records defined in the sweep group. New sweep records created by the user during the active suspension period.
- The Susp Start Date field can only be set for the current system date or a date in the future. When set as the current date, sweep(s) are suspended as soon as the AC.CP.GROUP.PARAM record is committed. When set for a future date, sweep(s) are suspended at the start of that day.

- Susp End Date - The date up to and including, which sweep execution for all sweep records within a sweep group are suspended until. The Susp End Date field can only be set for the current system date or a date in the future. When set as the current date, sweeps are released from suspension as soon as the AC.CP.GROUP.PARAM record is committed. The execution of sweeps is resumed in the next scheduled sweep (intra-day or eod). When set for a future date, the suspension is lifted at the start of that day.

> **⚠️ Note:** If the Susp End Date field is left blank, the suspension is only active for one day before sweeps are resumed.

The user can configure a temporary suspension for a specific sweep using the Susp Start Date and Susp End Date fields on the AC.CASH.POOL record. When set, this applies to all sweep instructions on the record.

For a temporary suspension for a specific link sweep instruction, the following fields are set:

- Link Susp Start Date – the date from which sweep execution between the sweep account and a specific link account is suspended from. The system continues to execute other sweep instructions on the sweep record.
- Link Susp End Date – the date, up to and including, from which the sweep execution between the sweep account and a specific link account are suspended until.

Indefinite sweep suspensions can be configured through one of two methods:

- To suspend all sweeps within a sweep group (i.e. across a cash pool of accounts) indefinitely, set the Suspend Indefinite field to Yes in the AC.CP.GROUP.PARAM application.
- To suspend a specific sweep instruction indefinitely, set the Suspend Indefinite field to Yes in AC.CASH.POOL record.

> **⚠️ Note:** The Suspend Indefinite field can only be set when a suspension end date has not defined.

To remove the sweep suspension before the end date, the user should:

- Update the Suspend Indefinite field to blank.
- Remove the values for Susp Start Date and Susp End Date .

> **⚠️ Note:** If no suspension end date is set, the system automatically lifts the sweep suspension after one day.


##### Sweep Cancellations

Sweep cancellations are configured in the AC.CASH.POOL application. The user can specify if a specific sweep instruction or all sweep instructions on a sweep record should be cancelled using the following fields:

- Sweep Cancel Date – the date from which all sweep instructions on a sweep record are cancelled. The sweep record becomes inactive, and no further sweeps are executed.
- Link Sweep Cancel Date – the date from which the sweep execution is cancelled for a specific sweep instruction between the sweep account and the link account. The system continues to execute other sweep instructions on the sweep record.


#### 🔧 Working With

This section details the processes involved in sweep suspensions and cancellations.


##### Temporary Sweep Suspensions

A sweep record can be suspended temporarily by specifying dates within the Susp Start Date and Susp End Date fields.

The examples below shows the process of sweep suspensions.

| Sweep Instruction | Sweep Account | Rule | Link Account | Maximum Amount | Frequency | Susp Start Date | Susp End Date |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 829462 (Account Balance: 1,000 USD) | Surplus | 238138 (Account Balance: 500 USD) | 700 USD | Daily (every business day) | 07/11/1900 | 21/11/1900 |

| Sweep Instruction | Sweep Account | Sweep Type | Link Account | Min. Amount | Max. Amount | Rule Priority | Link Susp Start Date | Link Susp End Date |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 273926 (Account Balance: 1,300 USD) | Maintenance | 173926 (Account Balance: 2,500 USD) | 1,500 USD |  | 1 | 01/06/1900 | 03/06/1900 |
| 2 | Surplus | 826491 (Account Balance: 1,900 USD) |  | 2,000 USD | 2 |  |  |  |


##### Indefinite Sweep Suspensions

When the Suspend Indefinite field is set to Yes, sweeps are suspended indefinitely until a suspension end date is set by the user to remove the suspension.

| Sweep Instruction | Sweep Account | Sweep Type | Link Account | Min. Amount | Max. Amount | Rule Priority | Link Susp Start Date | Suspend Indefinite |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 273926 (Account Balance: 1,300 USD) | Maintenance | 173926 (Account Balance: 2,500 USD) | 1,500 USD |  | 1 |  |  |
| 2 | Surplus | 826491 (Account Balance: 1,900 USD) |  | 2,000 USD | 2 | 02/06/1900 | Yes |  |


##### Sweep Suspension Based on Account Blocking (Debits/Credits)

The user can restrict a sweep by blocking the posting of any credits or debits to the sweep account, affecting any sweep instructions on the AC.CASH.POOL record.

When the Susp Sign field is set as:

- Cr – the sweep is blocked from posting credits to the sweep account
- Dr – the sweep is blocked from posting debits to the sweep account

> **⚠️ Note:** The Susp Start Date and Susp End Date (optional) fields are also set.

| Sweep Instruction | Sweep Account | Sweep Type | Link Account | Min. Amount | Max. Amount | Rule Priority |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 273926 (Account Balance: 1,300 USD) | Maintenance | 173926 (Account Balance: 2,500 USD) | 1,500 USD |  | 1 |
| 2 | Surplus | 826491 (Account Balance: 1,900 USD) |  | 2,000 USD | 2 |  |


##### Sweep Suspension Cancellations

Individual or group sweep instructions can be set to cancel from a specified date in the system by the user. When either the Sweep Cancel Date or Link Sweep Cancel Date field is set in the AC.CASH.POOL record, no further sweeps for sweep instructions on the record (or a specified link sweep instruction) are executed by the system beyond this date.

> **⚠️ Note:** The system cancels the sweep instructions upon the cancellation date and moves to history.

- A surplus sweep instruction was setup between Account 538482 (Sweep Account) and Account 272463 (Link Account) on 6th June.
- On 14th August, the user sets the Sweep Cancel Date field to 1st September in the AC.CASH.POOL record and commits the record.
- On 31st August, during COB, the system checks the rules of sweep instruction and executes, if required.
- On 1st September, the sweep cancellation date takes effect. The record in AC.CASH.POOL becomes inactive and moves to history.


#### 📋 Tasks

There are no Tasks available for Sweep Suspensions and Cancellations feature.


#### 📊 Outputs

In Transact, banks can suspend sweep instructions between the sweep and link account or a cash pool of accounts within a sweep group. Sweeps can be temporarily suspended until a defined end date or indefinitely, without deleting the sweep record from the system.


##### Enquiries and Reports

This section allows the user to view the below enquiries and reports.

Suspended Sweeps .

This enquiry displays information about sweeps that are currently suspended.
