**Interest Basis**

| Key | Days/Numerator | Description of Use |
|---|---|---|
| A | 360/360 | This method is used when each month is considered to have 30 days for the numerator and the denominator will also be 360. Sub-divided into methods A1 and A2. |
| A1 | 360/360 | Similar to A. Refer the examples below for deviation from A. |
| A2 | 360/360 | Similar to A1. Refer the examples below for deviation from A1. |
| A3 | 360/360 | Similar to A1. Refer the example below for deviation. |
| B | 366/360 | This method is used when the exact number of days is considered in respect of the numerator while the denominator will be 360. |
| C | 366/366 | This method is used when the exact number of days is considered in respect of the numerator while the denominator will be 365 in a non-leap year and 366 in a leap year. |
| C2 | 366/366 365/365 | Similar to C. Refer the example below for deviation. |
| D | 360/366 | This method is used when each month is considered to have 30 days for the numerator while the denominator will be 365 in a non-leap year and 366 in a leap year. |
| E | 366/365 | This method is used when the exact number of days is considered in respect of the numerator while the denominator will be 365. |
| E1 | 365/365 | This method is used when the 29th day of February, in case of leap year is ignored and it is considered to be a non-leap year. The total number of days in the year which is represented in the denominator is considered as 365. |
| F | 360/365 | This method is used when each month is considered to have 30 days for the numerator while the denominator will be on a 365 basis. Subdivided into methods F1 and F2. |
| F1 | 360/365 | Similar to F. Refer the examples below for deviation from F. |
| F2 | 360/365 | Similar to F1. Refer the examples below for deviation from F1. |
| G | 366/364 | This method is used when the exact number of days is considered in respect of the numerator while the denominator will be 364. |
| H | 360/356 | Hirja method – This is similar to 360/360, but the day calculations use the 360 year (30 days per month) only the denominator is changed to 356 instead of 360. |
| S | Note 1 | Special (special interest basis). |
| W | 252/252 | This method is used when interest calculation is done considering the exact number of working days in a month. The total number of days in the year, which is represented in the denominator is considered as 252. |
| W1 | 21/252 | This method is used when interest calculation is done considering the number of working days in a month to be always 21 days. The total number of days in the year, which is represented in the denominator is considered as 252. |
| A4 | 30/360 | This method is similar to other existing 30/360 basis, in addition it also caters to February month end, where each month is considered to have 30 days for the numerator while the denominator will be 360 for both leap and non-leap years. |

### Framework - TSF (TSF)


**NSF ExceptionProcessing**

| Field Name | Description |
|---|---|
| Settle Type | The possible values in the field are: PTL (Payed Through Limits) – Account balance including transaction amount is within the limit available at the time of posting the entry. POL (Payed Outside Limit) – Either account balance including transaction amount is in excess of the limit available at the time of posting the entry or the limit is not applicable (Opt-Out) for the respective debit transaction or activity. SET (Automatic Settlement) – Force settled with NSF. This debit transaction or activity is forced to be settled at the activity class definition. |
| Expiry Days | Indicates the cut-off period for manual decision making. This is the number of days within which the bank user should either approve or reject the NSF item and negotiate the NSF fee or charge. If the decision is not actioned manually, the default decision (if defined in the NSF parameter) applies on the COB of the expiry date of the NSF exception item. |
| Def Fund Decision | Hold the value approved or rejected. |
| Fund Decision Upd | Hold the value system or manual, to indicate the fund decision update. |
| Fund Deci Approve Act; Fund Deci Rej Act; Rev Approve Act; Rev Rej Act | Arrangement activity to be triggered for the default decision processing for fund approval/rejection or reversal approval/rejection. |
| Charge Negotiable | Hold the value YES or NO, to indicate if the NSF fee or charge is negotiable. |
| NSF Decision Hook | Configure the user exit routine to overrule the rule-based NSF decisioning of account transactions. |
| NSF Start Balance | Indicates the starting balance that must be used when calculating the accounts available balance used for the NSF evaluation process. It belongs to a set of associated fields. The allowed values are: Open.booked Open.valued If there is no value defined, Open.valued is the default value. |
| NSF Balance Type | Defines the inclusion of active debit holds and active credit holds in the available balance calculation during the NSF Evaluation process. It belongs to a set of associated fields. The allowed values are: Lock.funds Credit.reserve If there is no value defined, the available balance is calculated by including all the balance components. |
| NSF Lock Reserve Condition | The allowed values are: Lock.funds.date - Includes active debit locked events Credit.reserve.date - Includes active credit locked events. If there is no value defined for the associated balance type, the system refers the definition in AC.ACCOUNTING.PARAM . |
| NSF Process Type | The allowed value is: Exclude.return - Excludes the debit transaction amount from calculating the running balance when the default decision of the entry is set as RETURN or REJECT. |

**NSF ExceptionProcessing**

| Field Name | Description |
|---|---|
| Grace Period Type | Indicates the balance cure method applied when Grace Period functionality is enabled. The supported values are: Full – The account must have an available balance and tolerance greater or equal to 0 for the NSF charges to be waived. Partial – Each NSF exception is evaluated to determine if the positive movement of the available balance is sufficient to cover that item. |
| Grace Start Balance | Indicates the starting balance used for calculating the accounts available balance (used for grace period waiver). The allowed values are: Actual.booked - Indicates the account’s booked balance for today. A transaction is considered booked once it is completed and the balances are updated. Transactions with a forward processing date (for example, non-stop transactions entered at the close of business) are not included in this balance until the bank’s system date matches the processing date of the transaction. Actual.value - Indicates the account’s value-dated balance for today, which is used for interest calculation. Transactions with a forward value date are not included in today’s value-dated balance until the specified value date arrives. If the balance is not defined, then Actual.value is considered as the default value. |
| Grace Balance Type | Indicates the debit locked events and credit locked events are included when calculating the account available balances used for grace period waiver. The supported values are Lock.funds and Credit.reserve. The user can select one or both the options. |
| Grace Locked Reserve Condition | Indicates if current day’s active locked events should be used or if the maximum or minimum amounts should be used when debit locked events and credit locked events are included in the account available balance calculation. The supported values are Lock.funds.date and Credit.reserve.date. The user can select one or both the options. If the field is left blank for the associated Grace Balance Type , then the system uses the setting defined in Lock Reserve Condition in AC.ACCOUNTING.PARAM as default. |

**Sweep Groups**

| Fields | Description |
|---|---|
| Sub Group | Indicates if AC.CP.GROUP.PARAM record is a subgroup of a main group. If yes, the Main Group ID field must be populated with a valid AC.CP.GROUP.PARAM ID. |

| Balance To Use | Specifies the balance the system should use to determine the available account balance for sweep calculations. Applied across all sweeps within a sweep group. The user can either define their own local routine to calculate the balance or use one of the several balances from the EB.CONTRACT.BALANCES record of the account to use: Ac.Balance.Type Booked Including Reservations Booked Less Locked Booked With Fwd Less Locked Online Actual Online Cleared Value Dated Working Working Less Locked Amt Read Defining Account Balance To Use for more information. |
| Balance Routine | Specifies the local routine to be used to calculate the balance for sweeping. Applicable when the user selects User Defined in the Balance To Use field. The local routine defined is checked against the rule supplied in AC.CASH.POOL . The PGM.FILE contains a record of this routine with its name and the type as ‘S’ |
| Currency | The defaulted currency of the account defined in the Main Master field. |
| Hierarchy Reqd | Defines if a hierarchical group structure should be setup for the record. If yes, the Main Master field is mandatory. |
| Sweep Reserve Condition | Calculates the debit holds and credit holds when Balance To Use is set as ‘Booked Including Reservations’. The available options are: Lock Funds Date Credit Reserve Date |

**Sweep Groups**

| Sweep Group Structures | Description | Visual Representation |
|---|---|---|
| One to one | One account linked to another account. For example, a retail customer checking / current account linked to a savings account |  |
| One to Many | One account linked to more than one account to define a sweep group. For example, a customer checking / current account linked to a savings account and a line of credit. |  |
| Main and Subgroups | A cash pool of accounts split into sweep groups. For example: Main Group – the primary group of accounts (for example, parent company accounts) that can be split into more than one subgroup. Sub group – a subset of accounts (for example, subsidiary company accounts) linked to an account(s) within the main group |  |

**Sweep Setup**

| Field Names | Description |
|---|---|
| Sweep Style | Defines the sweep rule type for sweep instructions. Transact provides several available options including: Maintenance Surplus Two-Way Cashflow Read Introduction to Sweep Setup for more information. |
| Cr Txn Code , Dr Txn Code , Ret Cr Txn Code , Ret Dr Txn Code | Defines the transaction code to be used for debit and credit sweeps. For maintenance sweeps, only Cr Txn Code and Dr Txn Code are required to be populated. For surplus, two-way and cash flow sweeps, Ret Cr Txn Code and Ret Dr Txn Code are also required. |
| Use Limits | Instructs the system to check if an overdraft limit is attached to an account. Read Overdraft Limits for more information. |
| Prioritise OD | Determines the priority of overdrawn accounts when funds are swept if more than one linked account is involved. Helps to offset overdrawn account balances to zero before executing sweep instructions for other linked accounts. If set to No, then funds are all swept into the first link sweep instruction If set to Yes, then funds are swept first to the overdrawn account to offset the balance to zero. |
| Return At Sod | Instructs the system to return funds swept during the prior day COB, to the originating account during the next day Start of Day (SOD) process. |
| Balance To Use | Specifies the balance the system should use to determine the available account balance for sweep calculations. The user can either define their own local routine to calculate the balance or use one of the several balances from the EB.CONTRACT.BALANCES record of the account to use: Ac.Balance.Type Booked Including Reservations Booked Less Locked Booked With Fwd Less Locked Online Actual Online Cleared Value Dated Working Working Less Locked Amt Read Defining Account Balance To Use for more information. |
| Restrict Sweep | Instructs the system to stop or override a sweep based on posting restriction rules set on the CUSTOMER or ACCOUNT record. Read Posting Restrictions for more information. |
| Acct Mode | Identifies the accounting mode used for sweep execution. Transact provides the following available options: SAO SNP Read Partial Sweeps for more information. |
| Sweep Reserve Condition | Calculates the debit holds and credit holds when the Balance To Use field is set as Booked Including Reservations. Transact provides the following available options: Lock Funds Date Credit Reserve Date Read Defining Account Balance To Use for more information. |
| Partial Transfer | Determines whether the sweep should be executed in the case of insufficient funds to debit the sweep account. Read Partial Sweeps for more information. |

**Sweep Setup**

| Fields | Description |
|---|---|
| Sweep Type | The sweep type for which the conditions are to be applied to. |
| Max Contribution Amount | Indicates the maximum amount that can be invested in the Investment account on a given day across all the customers participating in the investment. Sum of all the investment amount across all the customers in an investment account on a given day should be less than or equal to the maximum contribution amount. |
| Min Contribution Amount | Indicates the minimum amount that can be invested in the Investment account on a given day across all the customers participating in the investment. Sum of all the investment amount across all the customers in an investment account on a given day should be greater than or equal to the minimum contribution amount. |
| Max Redemption Amount | Indicates the maximum amount that a customer can withdraw from an investment account on a given day. |
| Min Redemption Amount | Indicates the minimum amount that a customer can withdraw from an investment account on a given day. |
| Max Sweep Amount | Indicates the maximum amount that can be swept at a time from the current account to the investment account. |
| Min Sweep Amount | Indicates the minimum amount that can be swept at a time from the current account to the investment account. |
| Sweep Unit Amount | Holds the unit amount in terms of which the sweep must happen. |
| Min Max Amount Currency | Indicates the Currency of the Maximum and Minimum Sweep Amount. |
| Maximum Amount | Controls the maximum amount that can be in place on the account. Only applicable for the following sweep types: Surplus Two-Way Cashflow The value given is defaulted in the Maximum Amount field in the AC.CASH.POOL record. |
| Minimum Amount | Controls the maximum amount that can be in place on the account. Only applicable for the following sweep types: Maintenance Two-Way Cashflow The value given is defaulted in the Minimum Amount field in the AC.CASH.POOL record. |

**Sweep Setup**

| Field Names | Description |
|---|---|
| Group ID | The AC.CP.GROUP.PARAM record that the AC.CASH.POOL ID account number belongs to |
| Sub Group | If applicable, The AC.CP.GROUP.PARAM subgroup record that the AC.CASH.POOL ID account number belongs to |
| Main Master | The top-level account defined in the main or subgroup AC.CP.GROUP.PARAM record which linked account balances are either pooled to or pooled from. Read Sweep Groups for more information. |
| Sequence | Indicates the order position number that the AC.CASH.POOL sweep record is processed within the sweep group. Read Sequencing for more information. |
| Link Account | The account number that has a relationship with the Sweep Account and where funds are either swept to the account (surplus sweep) or from the account (maintenance sweep) or both. |
| Rule | The sweep type associated with the AC.CASH.POOL record and occurs between the sweep account and the link account. The sweep type must be first defined as a record in AC.SWEEP.TYPE (for example, maintenance, surplus, two-way and so on.) |
| Frequency | Instructs the system how often the sweep instructions are executed. Transact provides the following options: BSNSS (Business Days) WEEK1 (Weekly) M0101 (Monthly) M0331 (Quarterly) Defined (Specific Recurrence) |
| Minimum Amount | The minimum account balance to be maintained within an account. If the account balance falls below this figure, the sweep instruction is triggered to transfer funds from the linked account. Only applicable for the following sweep types: Maintenance Two-Way Cash Flow |
| Maximum Amount | The maximum account balance that should be held within an account. If the account balance falls below this figure, the sweep instruction is triggered to transfer funds from the Link Account. Only applicable for the following sweep types: Surplus Two-Way Cash Flow |
| Rule Priority | The priority level that a specific link sweep instruction has other links if more than one sweep instruction is triggered on the same day. |
| Return Rule Priority | The priority level that a specific link surplus sweep instruction has other links if more than one sweep instruction is triggered on the same day. Only applicable for the following sweep types: Surplus Two-Way |
| Aggregate Balance ; Cashflow Amount | The Aggregate Balance and Cashflow Amount fields control the amount of funds that can be taken from a higher-level account in the group hierarchy. |

**Sweep Setup**

| Balance Type | Description |
|---|---|
| Online Cleared | The account balance that represents funds from all cleared transactions that are available for withdrawal and use during the day. This includes transactions where the exposure date is realised as of Start of Day (SOD) and excludes those with an exposure date in the future. |
| Online Actual | The account balance that represents funds from all cleared and uncleared transactions that are available for withdrawal and use during the day. This includes authorised transactions where the exposure date is realised, as of Start of Day (SOD) or are future-dated. |
| Working | This account balance represents the current funds cleared and available in an account. This includes any pending or unauthorised debit transactions and excludes pending or unauthorised credit transactions. It shows the lowest balance available compared to the actual balance that may be available for withdrawal and use. Critical for online sweeps, as at eod, any unauthorised transactions are placed on hold and the working balance is adjusted accordingly. |
| Working Less Locked | This account balance represents the working balance, less any locked amounts on the sweep account. |
| Booked Including Reservations | This balance is the online actual balance plus any debit holds/reservations and credit holds or reservations. The debit and credit holds are considered based on the configuration done in the multi-valued Sweep Reserve Condition field in the AC.CASH.POOL application, which allows the user to select: Lock Funds Date - indicates only Active* debit reservations or debit-locked events are considered for calculating the available or usable balance of the sweeping account. Credit Reserve Date – indicates only Active* credit reservations or credit-locked events are considered for calculating the available or usable balance of the sweeping account. When the Sweep Reserve Condition field is not configured then the maximum of debit holds and minimum of credit holds are considered for the sweeping account. Sweep Reserve Condition can only be configured if the Balance To Use field has the option Booked Including Reservations. |
| Booked Less Locked | This balance is the online actual balance less all locked amounts posted to the account. |
| Booked with Fwd Less Locked | This balance is the online actual balance with the inclusion of future credit and debit balance projections less all locked amounts posted to the account. |
| Value Dated | This account balance represents the current funds cleared and available in an account after excluding any future- dated FT, teller, or DC entries. It is used when back-value dated adjustment is required. This option is only available for legacy (AC) and Arrangement accounts. |
| Ac.Balance.Type | This balance is used for the settlement of contracts created using the Arrangement Architecture (AA) in Temenos Transact. |
| User Defined | This balance is defined by the user for sweeping purposes (based on the bank’s requirement). A local routine is used to calculate the balance to be moved. The balance supplied by the routine is checked against the rule specified in the AC.CASH.POOL application. The local routine is specified in the Balance Routine field. There is a record in the PGM.FILE with the name of the routine and the type as S. |
